He says the second beast causes people to keep worshiping the first beast, and that “he deceives by great wonders,” “brings down fire from heaven,” and has an idol made of the first beast. He says “he gives life to that idol” and “causes that idol to speak,” and notes the Bible says “an idol is nothing” and those who follow idols “become just like them.”
What makes the second beast different from the first? (Revelation 13:12–15)

So this guy has all the power of the first beast to speak, but he causes, and he causes people to worship the first beast. Well, the first, the people are already worshiping the first beast, and this guy pops up and says, continue worshiping the first beast. And the people who worshiped the first beast also worshiped what? Satan. So he says, continue on as you are. So what makes the second beast different from the first beast? Well, he deceives by great wonders. He brings down fire from heaven. He has an idol made of the first beast. He gives life to that idol. He causes that idol to speak. Now that’ll get your attention. Pretend this is an image of Mary or Buddha or whatever you want it to be. The Bible says an idol is nothing. It has eyes but it can’t see, it has ears it can’t hear. It says it’s powerless, and that’s the fact. People who follow them, the Bible says, become just like them. They can’t see, they can’t hear. Okay, but this guy makes this beast come to life, this, this idol. Now I’m sorry, the idol is living, and not only living, this idol now speaks. Now, how, you know, that would get your attention. I’m surprised that they haven’t come up with the theory of building an idol over in Palestine yet, not just a temple. You guys missed that.
What makes the second beast different from the first? (Revelation 13:12–15)

Revelation 13:12-15: And he exercises all the authority of the first beast in his presence, and causes the earth and those who dwell in it to worship the first beast, whose deadly wound was healed. He performs great signs, so that he even makes fire come down from heaven on the earth in the sight of men. And he deceives those who dwell on the earth by those signs which he was granted to do in the sight of the beast, telling those who dwell on the earth to make an image to the beast who was wounded by the sword and lived. He was granted power to give breath to the image of the beast, that the image of the beast should both speak and cause as many as would not worship the image of the beast to be killed. Psalm 115:4-8: Their idols are silver and gold, The work of men’s hands. They have mouths, but they do not speak; Eyes they have, but they do not see; They have ears, but they do not hear; Noses they have, but they do not smell; They have hands, but they do not handle; Feet they have, but they do not walk; Nor do they mutter through their throat. Those who make them are like them; So is everyone who trusts in them. 1 Corinthians 8:4: Therefore concerning the eating of things offered to idols, we know that an idol is nothing in the world, and that there is no other God but one.
Does he say prophecy needs a rebuilt temple? (Acts 17:24)

He says people expect an idol and temple in Palestine, and tells of Christians who tried to burn down the “temple of Omar” and a Jewish sect that “already has a temple in boxes.” He says “the focus is on what? A natural temple,” that God does not dwell in temples made with hands, and that “God doesn’t need our help making things come to pass.” His accounts have not been verified here.
Does he say prophecy needs a rebuilt temple? (Acts 17:24)

We always try to make our theories work. You know, there was some Christians who tried to burn down the temple of Omar, that Muslim temple, so that the temple they wanted to be built could be built there. Don’t you... you didn’t know that? You guys are illiterate. Do you know that a church, a certain Jewish sect, I [unclear] which one it is, it already has a temple in boxes, and they’re ready to put it up as quick as they can destroy the Muslim temple? You didn’t know that either. You see, the focus is on what? A natural temple. And God says, what? I don’t dwell in temples made with hands. And see, they’re trying to make things come to pass. How many, you know, God doesn’t need our help making things come to pass. He’s perfectly capable of doing it, and just involve us. Hallelujah. So that’s why I’m wondering, you know, when are they going to build an idol over there and expect some antichrist to come along and make it talk?
Does he say prophecy needs a rebuilt temple? (Acts 17:24)
Acts 17:24: God, who made the world and everything in it, since He is Lord of heaven and earth, does not dwell in temples made with hands.
Has an idol ever come to life? (Revelation 13:14–15)

He says “nowhere in history do we find an idol talking and an idol coming to life,” and that this beast “gets the attention through supernatural power,” unlike the first beast’s “verbal attacks.” He says the Bible gives no time limit for this second beast.
Has an idol ever come to life? (Revelation 13:14–15)

Now, all through history this has never happened. Nowhere in history do we find an idol talking and an idol coming to life. Believe me, it would be in the record books, that would make Josephus, and, man, they’d have it in there. Am I right? And the Bible says an idol is nothing. But he gets the attention through supernatural power. This guy has supernatural power. This group has what? Supernatural power. The other people just had what? Blasphemy, words they spoke. Well, they, they just use verbal attacks. What are they doing in America right now? The verbal. But this one has supernatural power. Wow. And not only can he speak, he can do something, and there’s no time given here. We got a problem.
Has an idol ever come to life? (Revelation 13:14–15)

Revelation 13:14-15: And he deceives those who dwell on the earth by those signs which he was granted to do in the sight of the beast, telling those who dwell on the earth to make an image to the beast who was wounded by the sword and lived. He was granted power to give breath to the image of the beast, that the image of the beast should both speak and cause as many as would not worship the image of the beast to be killed.
Why does he say the three-and-a-half-year charts are a problem?

He says the second beast rises after the first beast’s three and a half years with the same power, so “we really got a problem here” fitting three and a half years into “our little charts.” He says “stick with the Bible,” that “everyone that has predicted this stuff has failed so far,” and tells of the Y2K scare, saying “nothing happened.”
Why does he say the three-and-a-half-year charts are a problem?

It doesn’t say this beast is around for three and a half years. After the three and a half years period is over, here we got another beast rising with the same power, the first beast who lasted for three and a half years. We really got a problem here. Do you see the problem, trying to make three and a half years work into our little charts? Hallelujah. Church, don’t get wrapped up in that nonsense. Stick with the Bible. Everyone that has predicted this stuff has failed so far, and it’s been going on for almost 2,000 years. Every millennium, everybody thought the second coming was here, and the last one they thought the second coming was here. My church asked me to teach on the Y2K problem and the end time. You know, we’re supposed to, everything was supposed to shut down and cars crash because lights don’t work anymore, and we get flooded because the gates of the dams don’t work anymore, and all the, man, and Christians went out and bought into that, and they bought storage food and light, uh, uh, flashlights and all this stuff, and I go, “Folks, it ain’t going to happen.” I had two things going for me: I knew the scriptures, and I used to work in the computers. I know a computer does nothing. Nothing comes out except what you put into it. And so my scientific knowledge with my Bible knowledge just confirmed that nothing’s going to happen, and guess what? Nothing happened. Now, in third world countries when I went preaching, and I told them Jesus wasn’t coming in the year 2000, and wasn’t going to come for 13 or more years after the year 2000, they got mad at me. See, we want him to come so desperately, we want him to fit into our agenda. Let, let me give you a theory. You ready for a theory? A Kincer wild imagination theory. I mean, everybody else is throwing them out. Three and a half years.
Does he say it could be 1,000 years before Jesus returns? (2 Peter 3:8)

He offers what he calls a “wild imagination theory”: “suppose that 1,000 years from now the world is still going on and Jesus hasn’t come,” since “a thousand years is as a day.” He says “the Bible plainly says nobody” knows when, and asks, “are we going to quit fantasizing and start living in the present generation.”
Does he say it could be 1,000 years before Jesus returns? (2 Peter 3:8)

Suppose that 1,000 years from now the world is still going on and Jesus hasn’t come. Have you got that? A thousand years is as a day, and a day is as a thousand years. Now what are the theory people going to be preaching 1,000 years from now? These three and a half years is a thousand years, is a day, we’re at the 3,000th year, just 50 more years and it’s going to happen. And the Bible plainly says nobody what? Knows when. Are we going to quit fantasizing and start living in the present generation and be who we are supposed to be and identify what’s going on in our time? Amen. Now that was a good preaching.
Does he say it could be 1,000 years before Jesus returns? (2 Peter 3:8)

2 Peter 3:8: But, beloved, do not forget this one thing, that with the Lord one day is as a thousand years, and a thousand years as one day. Matthew 24:36: “But of that day and hour no one knows, not even the angels of heaven, but My Father only.
What does he say the number 666 means? (Revelation 13:16–18)

He gives “another great theory of mine”: the first six is not believing God created the earth in six days, the second is not worshiping on the seventh day (“they don’t go to church”), and the third is people who “don’t want to work six days.” He says it is “as good as theirs,” that “we have been failing with the 666 for 2,000 years,” and that the book “doesn’t tell us.”
What does he say the number 666 means? (Revelation 13:16–18)

Those that didn’t worship the idol are killed. You can’t buy or sell without the mark, 666. You want to hear another great theory of mine? Mine’s as good as theirs. They can’t back their... I, I at least gave you some scriptures. 666, you ready for this? Okay, the people that follow Satan, the people that blasphemed God, they do not believe that God created the earth in six days. First six. They will not worship God on the seventh day, God rested. They don’t go to church, they don’t believe in God. Second six. And you’re wondering what the third six is? Six days shall you work, and if you don’t work you neither should eat. All this welfare stuff, all this health program stuff, all these goodies. You see, a lot of people don’t want to work six days. See, that’s... are you there? Hey, they like to draw welfare. That’s the third six. It’s the number of who? Amen. And it’s humans that think this way. My theory of 666 is just as good as theirs. I got scripture to back mine up. They have to say it’s Hitler because his name spells out 666, adds up to 666. You know, they get their little alphabet calculator going, and Hitler, 666. Listen, the Catholic Church summed up Luther at 666. Did you know that? Yeah. See, we’re ignorant of this stuff. This is not new. We have been failing with the 666 for 2,000 years. We haven’t figured it out, and I submit to you, it doesn’t tell us.
What does he say the number 666 means? (Revelation 13:16–18)

Revelation 13:16-17: He causes all, both small and great, rich and poor, free and slave, to receive a mark on their right hand or on their foreheads, and that no one may buy or sell except one who has the mark or the name of the beast, or the number of his name. Genesis 2:2: And on the seventh day God ended His work which He had done, and He rested on the seventh day from all His work which He had done. Exodus 20:9: Six days you shall labor and do all your work, 2 Thessalonians 3:10: For even when we were with you, we commanded you this: If anyone will not work, neither shall he eat.
When did the last days begin, and can we know when Jesus returns?

He says “we’re not allowed to add to the word,” and that “shortly” in Revelation 1 and 22:6 was true “since Christ ascended.” He says the last days began at Pentecost, so “we have been living in the last days for 2,000 years” and may be for “another thousand,” and that people said Christ was coming in 1960 and later years. He says we can know “what’s happening in our generation,” like the virgins who were “awake and ready.”
When did the last days begin, and can we know when Jesus returns?

He says, “He who has wisdom.” I tell you, I don’t have it. I can’t, all the wisdom I got from the scriptures, and I can’t find it revealed anywhere. Have you? And we’re not allowed to add to the word, so we can’t make up our own definition of this thing. Hallelujah. And remember, Revelation 1 and Revelation 22:6, the beginning of the book and the end of the book, it says what? These things will happen. Say it: shortly. Now, when I told you they were happening since Christ ascended, was that shortly? Yes, it was then, and it is what? Now. “In the last days I’ll pour out my Spirit on all flesh.” When did the last days start? Day of Pentecost, when he poured out his Spirit on all flesh. We have been living in the last days for 2,000 years. What if we’re going to be living for another thousand? Oh my God, you’re kidding. I, I ain’t saying it’s going to happen, but folks, they didn’t think we would be here in 1960. They said he was coming in 1960, 1962, I lived through this mess, 1964, 1968, 1982, you know. And our generations might be here another thousand years from now, and he’s still not come, because no one what? Knows. But we do know what’s happening in our generation, because the virgins with the lights, the, you know, they had lamps, they had light in them, that, you know, and there was one virgin, with of the virgins, that what? Didn’t even go to sleep. They were awake and ready and knowing what was happening, and that’s what he’s talking about in Revelation, overcomers being that virgin.
When did the last days begin, and can we know when Jesus returns?

Revelation 13:18: Here is wisdom. Let him who has understanding calculate the number of the beast, for it is the number of a man: His number is 666. Revelation 1:1: The Revelation of Jesus Christ, which God gave Him to show His servants—things which must shortly take place. And He sent and signified it by His angel to His servant John, Revelation 22:6: Then he said to me, “These words are faithful and true.” And the Lord God of the holy prophets sent His angel to show His servants the things which must shortly take place. Acts 2:17: ‘And it shall come to pass in the last days, says God, That I will pour out of My Spirit on all flesh; Your sons and your daughters shall prophesy, Your young men shall see visions, Your old men shall dream dreams. Matthew 25:1-13: “Then the kingdom of heaven shall be likened to ten virgins who took their lamps and went out to meet the bridegroom. Now five of them were wise, and five were foolish. Those who were foolish took their lamps and took no oil with them, but the wise took oil in their vessels with their lamps. But while the bridegroom was delayed, they all slumbered and slept. “And at midnight a cry was heard: ‘Behold, the bridegroom is coming; go out to meet him!’ Then all those virgins arose and trimmed their lamps. And the foolish said to the wise, ‘Give us some of your oil, for our lamps are going out.’ But the wise answered, saying, ‘No, lest there should not be enough for us and you; but go rather to those who sell, and buy for yourselves.’ And while they went to buy, the bridegroom came, and those who were ready went in with him to the wedding; and the door was shut. “Afterward the other virgins came also, saying, ‘Lord, Lord, open to us!’ But he answered and said, ‘Assuredly, I say to you, I do not know you.’ “Watch therefore, for you know neither the day nor the hour in which the Son of Man is coming.
How does Satan disguise himself as an angel of light? (2 Corinthians 11:14–15)

He says “Satan himself is transformed into an angel of light,” and that those who follow him “come at you like their ideal is good.” He gives atheists, humanists and freethinkers as people “disguised as angels of righteousness” who say “they’re lying to you, they’re deceiving you, we got the truth.” He ends the virgins illustration with “I’m awake, I know what’s happening.”
How does Satan disguise himself as an angel of light? (2 Corinthians 11:14–15)

Not the one that ran out of oil, not the ones that had oil, been the ones that said, “Come on, man, I’m awake, I know what’s happening.” Satan himself is transformed into an angel of light. “Therefore it is no great thing if his ministers also be transformed as the ministers of righteousness.” Scripture, right? Supernatural. We’re going to show you supernatural. This beast works supernaturally, got it? Satan, you know, they don’t come at you as, as evil, they come at you like their ideal is good. Don’t atheists believe they are right? Don’t they tell everybody like they really know what’s right? And the humanist, the freethinker, yeah. See, they’re disguised as angels of righteousness, of right. They’re not going to come out and say, “I’m lying to you, man.” No. They’re going to be saying that church, man, they’re lying to you, they’re deceiving you, we got the truth.
How does Satan disguise himself as an angel of light? (2 Corinthians 11:14–15)

2 Corinthians 11:14-15: And no wonder! For Satan himself transforms himself into an angel of light. Therefore it is no great thing if his ministers also transform themselves into ministers of righteousness, whose end will be according to their works.
Should we follow signs and wonders? (Deuteronomy 13:1–3)

He reads that if a prophet gives “a sign, a wonder” and says “let’s go after and serve other gods,” “you shall not listen to them.” He says he went to a revival in Lakeland, Florida, and “it was the biggest gimmick I ever seen in my life” because “they were focusing on miracles that weren’t happening.” This is his opinion and has not been verified here.
Should we follow signs and wonders? (Deuteronomy 13:1–3)

Okay. Now, “If there arise among you a prophet that gives you a sign, a wonder,” an amazing thing, a supernatural act, “and then they say, let’s go after and serve other gods, you shall not listen to them.” Now, why were people running down to Lakeland, Florida, for this revival thing that was supposed to happen, and the pastors here in [unclear] were seeking God for the same visitation that was in Lakeland, Florida? I went down there, and it was the biggest gimmick I ever seen in my life. And what was the gimmick? They were focusing on miracles that weren’t happening. Nothing was happening, and they were saying it happened, much less if they can make one or two happen. Are you out there, church?
Should we follow signs and wonders? (Deuteronomy 13:1–3)

Deuteronomy 13:1-3: “If there arises among you a prophet or a dreamer of dreams, and he gives you a sign or a wonder, and the sign or the wonder comes to pass, of which he spoke to you, saying, ‘Let us go after other gods’—which you have not known—‘and let us serve them,’ you shall not listen to the words of that prophet or that dreamer of dreams, for the LORD your God is testing you to know whether you love the LORD your God with all your heart and with all your soul.
What power did the sorcerers of Egypt really have? (Exodus 7–8)

He says the sorcerers “never had any power till Moses showed up,” and then God gave them “limited authority, limited supernatural power.” They could copy a sign but not undo it, because “they can’t do any more than God lets them do,” and “the sorcerers could not create life.”
What power did the sorcerers of Egypt really have? (Exodus 7–8)

“The sorcerers of Egypt also did like manner with their enchantments, but could not make lice,” saying, “This is the finger of God.” You see, the sorcerers of Egypt never had any power till Moses showed up. They weren’t down there turning water to blood, they weren’t down there turning their rod to a snake, they weren’t down there bringing frogs out of the river. When Moses showed up, God gave them limited authority, limited supernatural power. And so when Pharaoh said, “Okay, magicians, sorcerers, you change your rod into a snake,” well, they didn’t need any more snakes, they needed to change Moses’s snake back to a rod. So they threw down their rod and it turned to a snake, and guess what? Moses ate them all. They didn’t have any rod to turn back. Are you there? See, they had limited supernatural power. When Moses poured the water out and it became blood, Pharaoh said, “Okay, you sorcerers, do that.” So they poured water out, became blood. They didn’t need any more blood, they needed the water, the blood changed back to water. See, God gave them limited supernatural power. What they really needed was to overpower Moses and turn the blood back to water. This is what you got to remember. And then Moses brought up frogs, and Pharaoh said, “Okay, sorcerers, bring up...” Well, they don’t want any more frogs. Frogs! So the sorcerers put out their staff, and here comes more frogs. The thing, they didn’t need more frogs, they needed the other frogs removed, but they couldn’t do it. Why? They can’t do any more than God lets them do. And God says, “Okay, you want more frogs? Okay, we’ll give you more frogs. You think there’s power in your sorcery? Go ahead.” But when they came to the [unclear], where they created something out of nothing, God says, “This is as far as you go,” and the sorcerers could not create life.
What power did the sorcerers of Egypt really have? (Exodus 7–8)

Exodus 7:11-12: But Pharaoh also called the wise men and the sorcerers; so the magicians of Egypt, they also did in like manner with their enchantments. For every man threw down his rod, and they became serpents. But Aaron’s rod swallowed up their rods. Exodus 8:18-19: Now the magicians so worked with their enchantments to bring forth lice, but they could not. So there were lice on man and beast. Then the magicians said to Pharaoh, “This is the finger of God.” But Pharaoh’s heart grew hard, and he did not heed them, just as the LORD had said.

He says the idol that comes to life “has got to be a ventriloquist somewhere,” and that the sorcerers had “supernatural power to deceive people.” Citing Acts 16:16, he says the girl with a spirit of divination “had limited supernatural ability,” and that he knew a person at a revival who told people their addresses “had a familiar spirit.” He asks whether people “just fall for every little prophetic word of knowledge.” This is his account and has not been verified here.

And that’s why this idol that comes to life has got to be a ventriloquist somewhere, just throwing things out. Hallelujah. Isn’t this wonderful? Isn’t this book great? And the sorcerers, they got the boils, they got the hell, they got everything rained down upon them, they couldn’t stop it. Why? They have limited power, but they did have supernatural power to deceive people. Okay, Acts 16:16: “A girl possessed with a spirit of divination met us, who brought her masters much profit by fortune telling.” You see, she had limited supernatural ability. And I was in a church meeting in Alabama, not a church meeting, but a revival meeting, where somebody came in, and they had a, someone there that’s supposed, supposed to be able to see, have this word of knowledge and all that, and they were telling people their addresses and so forth, and I quickly, I quickly, because I’d been in the book, I’d been a prayer, I’d been a seeker, I quickly knew that person had a familiar spirit. Limited knowledge, and the knowledge did them no good. So they know where I live, so what? You can find where I live in the phone book. What I need is I need a source of power to live in this life for Christ and do what’s right. I don’t need you telling me my phone book, and whether I got a pack of cigarettes in my back pocket or not, or, you know, this limited, not, that doesn’t do me any good. That fools the idiots, but it doesn’t fool those that are written in the Lamb’s Book of Life. Hallelujah. And I dared that one. I was sitting there daring her to come to me. I kept my eye right on her. She was a black preacher man. I just kept my eye right on her. I dare you to come over to me, and she knew better than come over to me. She knew I was different. She knew she’d have been in big trouble. Do they know they’ll be in big trouble if they come to you, or you just fall for every little prophetic word of knowledge that comes by? You know, when a prophet has got to say, “I see...” And, and, uh, “cars, I see rivers.” Don’t give me that. “I see cars and river” stuff. Tell me exactly what you see. Am I going to die in a car accident, or am I going to get a new car? Just let it, you know, give with a program. Amen. Yes. And, uh, don’t ask me if Rebecca’s my wife. Tell me she’s my wife, then I’ll know you’re a prophet. Are you out there, church? And us Spirit-filled people have got to get the program, they got to get with the program. We’re one of the worst for this nonsense, and it’s no wonder people have gotten a bad name by being filled with the Holy Ghost, because us Spirit-filled people have made some stupid things out of it that just turn people off. But the word stands sure, it’s still good. Amen.
Acts 16:16: Now it happened, as we went to prayer, that a certain slave girl possessed with a spirit of divination met us, who brought her masters much profit by fortune-telling.
Who was Simon the sorcerer, and what is the end goal? (Acts 8:9)

Reading that Simon “used sorcery and bewitched the people of Samaria,” he says the people said he was the power of God, and the power of sorcery “comes from the kingdom of darkness.” He says “just because someone can do some kind of supernatural thing, and it’s limited, you don’t fall for it,” and asks, “what’s their message? What’s their end goal?”
Who was Simon the sorcerer, and what is the end goal? (Acts 8:9)

Hallelujah. Simon, in Acts 8:9, “used sorcery and bewitched the people of Samaria, giving out that himself was some great one, to whom they all,” how many? All “gave heed, from the least to the greatest, saying, This man is the power of” Satan? No. Who do they say he was? “The power of God.” And who does the scripture say this power of sorcery comes from? The kingdom of darkness, church. Are you there? See, just because someone can do some kind of supernatural thing, and it’s limited, you don’t fall for it. What’s their message? What’s their end goal? And in Lakeland, Florida, they had their end goal as some woman angel. Nowhere in the Bible is there a woman angel. In fact, angels don’t have sex, they’re just spirits. They don’t have a penis, they don’t have a vagina, they’re just spirits. What I mean, he uses “he” so we can understand. Ain’t that right?
Who was Simon the sorcerer, and what is the end goal? (Acts 8:9)

Acts 8:9-11: But there was a certain man called Simon, who previously practiced sorcery in the city and astonished the people of Samaria, claiming that he was someone great, to whom they all gave heed, from the least to the greatest, saying, “This man is the great power of God.” And they heeded him because he had astonished them with his sorceries for a long time.
Who does he say will not worship the beast?
He says “those in the Book of Life” won’t worship, and “all the earth worships” except “the ones written in the Book of Life, the ones that got born again.”
Does he say joining a church makes you saved?

He says “churches just put people on the roll book, they just want attendance,” but “Jesus said you got to be born again of the word and the Spirit.” He asks, “how are they going to get birthed in the word if we don’t preach the word?”
What does he say “the patience and the faith of the saints” is?
He says “they’re going to stick with Jesus no matter what,” and that “they are patiently waiting for Jesus to fulfill his word in them and in the world.”
Does he say Christians will be raptured out of difficulty?
He says no: “they’re still here,” and “we don’t have to get raptured out.” He says “Jesus is big enough to keep us in any kind of difficulty of this world.”
What does he say the word “Christian” means?
He says “Christian means I came from Christ, I follow Christ, I act like Christ,” and “there’s a big difference between a believer and a Christian.”
What does he mean by the “assembly line”?

He says “we got to move on down the assembly line,” and “the great master assembly man puts us together.” He says “don’t disqualify yourself because you got some faults,” because “the master craftsman will get the parts and get everything in you.”
What does he say the Bible says about idols?
He says “an idol is nothing. It has eyes but it can’t see, it has ears it can’t hear,” and that “people who follow them … become just like them.”
Does he say end-time predictions have been reliable?
He says no: “Church, don’t get wrapped up in that nonsense. Stick with the Bible. Everyone that has predicted this stuff has failed so far.”
What does he say about the Y2K scare?

He says he told people “it ain’t going to happen,” because “a computer does nothing” except what is put into it. His “scientific knowledge with my Bible knowledge just confirmed that nothing’s going to happen, and guess what? Nothing happened.”
When does he say the last days started?
He says “day of Pentecost, when he poured out his Spirit on all flesh,” and “we have been living in the last days for 2,000 years.”
Does he say we can know when Jesus is coming back?
He says no: “no one” knows. He recalls that “they said he was coming in 1960, 1962” and later, and says “our generations might be here another thousand years from now.”
What does he say the sorcerers of Egypt really needed to do?
He says “what they really needed was to overpower Moses and turn the blood back to water,” but they could not, because God gave them only “limited supernatural power.”
What does he say about someone telling people their addresses?

He says “you can find where I live in the phone book,” and “I need a source of power to live in this life for Christ and do what’s right.” He says “limited knowledge” like that “doesn’t fool those that are written in the Lamb’s Book of Life.” This is his account.
What does he say about vague prophetic words?
He says “tell me exactly what you see,” not general words about cars and rivers. He says “us Spirit-filled people have got to get the program,” because “we’re one of the worst for this nonsense.”

items.d: In this third lesson, Pastor David G. Kincer teaches from Revelation 14 that the 144,000 with the Lamb on Zion are the church, written with God’s name as overcomers, and that “virgins” means spiritual purity…
p: In this third lesson, Pastor David G. Kincer teaches from Revelation 14 that the 144,000 with the Lamb on Zion are the church, written with God’s name as overcomers, and that “virgins” means spiritual purity kept through repentance. He covers first fruits, servants, brethren and remnant, the gospel harvest, the two harvests, and why he says we are to fear God, ending that the church, not the beast, is the powerful one.
Who are the 144,000 with the Lamb on Mount Zion? (Revelation 14:1, 3:12)

He says “Zion is the church,” so the 144,000 with the Lamb are the people of God, and that he has “no idea what 144,000 is” beyond 12 times 12. Reading Revelation 3:12, he says the overcomer gets God’s name written on him, that we overcome “by our faith in Jesus Christ,” and “we have the name of God written on us” if we pursue God as overcomers.
Who are the 144,000 with the Lamb on Mount Zion? (Revelation 14:1, 3:12)

Now let’s get to the people of God. I like this part of Revelation here: 144,000 with the Lamb on Zion, Revelation 14. Zion is what? Yeah, Hebrews 12 and other places, Zion is the church. So here is 144,000 with the Lamb. There are two tribes missing, one tribe is mentioned twice in the listing. All right, and you know God don’t make those kind of mistakes. So obviously he’s not interested in 12 tribes, is he? And he’s really not interested in 144,000. I have no idea what 144,000 is, except, you know, 12 times 12 is 144 and 120,000, you know. And they have their Father’s name written in their forehead. Okay, well, this is a no-brainer. We know Zion is the church, we know the Lamb, Jesus, is why we are saved, isn’t that right? Jesus dying on the cross, we know that. And all of us, what, have to believe in the Lamb, ain’t that right? Now, if we can get the name of God on our forehead, we got it. Revelation 3:12, remember this teaching, very first, second one, first, first or second one: “He who overcomes, I will make him a pillar in the temple of my God.” Now, who’s the temple of God? The people, the believers. “And he shall go out no more. I will write on him the name of my God.” Wow. This 144,000 had what written on them? The name of God. I have written on me, if I’m an overcomer. And how do we overcome? By our faith in Jesus Christ. “He that overcometh the world.” Are we overcomers of the world? Are we destined to do that? Do we give up because we haven’t quite made it yet? No, man, we’re on the assembly line, just hang tight, the thing’s coming. Hallelujah. “And the name of the city of my God.” What’s the city of God? The church, the New Jerusalem, “which comes down out of heaven from my God, and I will write on him” what? “My new name.” Are you there, church? Now, if we’re pursuing God to be overcomers and conquerors in this life, we have the name of God written on us. Hallelujah. We are Zion, we are the church.
Who are the 144,000 with the Lamb on Mount Zion? (Revelation 14:1, 3:12)

Revelation 14:1: Then I looked, and behold, a Lamb standing on Mount Zion, and with Him one hundred and forty-four thousand, having His Father’s name written on their foreheads. Hebrews 12:22: But you have come to Mount Zion and to the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem, to an innumerable company of angels, Revelation 3:12: He who overcomes, I will make him a pillar in the temple of My God, and he shall go out no more. I will write on him the name of My God and the name of the city of My God, the New Jerusalem, which comes down out of heaven from My God. And I will write on him My new name. 1 John 5:4: For whatever is born of God overcomes the world. And this is the victory that has overcome the world—our faith. Revelation 21:2: Then I, John, saw the holy city, New Jerusalem, coming down out of heaven from God, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband.
What is the new song, and are the 144,000 literal Jewish virgins? (Revelation 14:3–4)

He says the new song is ours, citing the psalm “He hath put a new song in my heart” and “psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs.” He says “there isn’t some 144 Jews over there in Palestine that God is going to raise up to be virgins,” that God “is interested in the whole world,” and that the first thing is to “get redeemed, repent, and get saved.” He says “there’s nothing wrong with getting married and having sex in marriage,” so “it can’t be this virgin thing.”
What is the new song, and are the 144,000 literal Jewish virgins? (Revelation 14:3–4)

Hallelujah. Now, he says they had a new song. Well, what does the Psalm say? “He hath put a new song in my heart, a song of praise unto my God, and many shall see and turn and put their trust in the Lord.” It says over and over, sing unto the Lord a new song. In Ephesians it says speak and sing to yourself as “psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs.” New songs, we are the ones that have the new song. Are you getting this? Say, “Oh me,” or “Amen.” You see, there isn’t some 144 Jews over there in Palestine that God is going to raise up to be virgins. They don’t even believe in Christ. And that’s what these theory people, they try to make their theories come to pass. God is interested in the whole world, he’s not willing that any should perish, isn’t that right? Now, let’s continue. “Redeemed from the earth.” I don’t even have to show scripture, that we all know we’ve been redeemed by the blood of the Lamb, right? Every one of us. Okay, so see, it’s still us. The first thing we got to do is get redeemed, repent, and get saved. Ah, here we are. They’re virgins. They’re virgins, and it plainly says they’re virgin, never knew a woman, that’s what it says. Okay. And they follow the Lamb. Okay, hallelujah. Well, that leaves out Peter, John, King David, Job, Noah, and the God that wrote the book in the very beginning of the book said it is good for a man to leave his mother and father and cleave to his wife. There’s nothing wrong with getting married and having sex in marriage. God can’t contradict his word, so it can’t be this virgin thing. Are you out there?
What is the new song, and are the 144,000 literal Jewish virgins? (Revelation 14:3–4)

Psalm 40:3: He has put a new song in my mouth— Praise to our God; Many will see it and fear, And will trust in the LORD. Ephesians 5:19: speaking to one another in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing and making melody in your heart to the Lord, 2 Peter 3:9: The Lord is not slack concerning His promise, as some count slackness, but is longsuffering toward us, not willing that any should perish but that all should come to repentance. Revelation 14:3-4: They sang as it were a new song before the throne, before the four living creatures, and the elders; and no one could learn that song except the hundred and forty-four thousand who were redeemed from the earth. These are the ones who were not defiled with women, for they are virgins. These are the ones who follow the Lamb wherever He goes. These were redeemed from among men, being firstfruits to God and to the Lamb. Genesis 2:24: Therefore a man shall leave his father and mother and be joined to his wife, and they shall become one flesh.
What does he say it means to be a “spiritual virgin”? (2 Corinthians 11:2, Isaiah 54:5, Revelation 19:7)

He says Paul’s words to the Corinthians, “I’ve espoused you to one husband, to present you as a chaste virgin,” mean “the absence of sin, the absence of walking in darkness and disobeying God,” not “fleshly virginity.” He says “I become a spiritual virgin” through Christ’s blood and “I maintain that through the principle of repentance.” He cites Isaiah 54:5 and Revelation 19:7 and says “adulthood is 20 years old,” telling young people to “hang tight.” These are his views.
What does he say it means to be a “spiritual virgin”? (2 Corinthians 11:2, Isaiah 54:5, Revelation 19:7)

I mean, how many of you are going to be willing to become an overcomer by not having sexual relationships while here on earth? No hands are jumping up. You know, you wanted to get married, you wanted to have kids, am I right? Who put that in you? Your Creator. And then he’s going to punish you because you’re not a virgin? It doesn’t make sense. But this does, are you ready? “I’ve espoused you to one husband, to present you as a chaste virgin.” To who? Who’s he talking to? The Corinthian believers. I’m preaching to you and I’m praying with you and, and, and we’re working together that you become this pure, chaste virgin that Jesus is looking for. He’s not talking about fleshly virginity there. He’s talking about the absence of sin, the absence of walking in darkness and disobeying God. You young’uns getting this? Hallelujah. “You should be married.” Romans 7:14: “You should be married to another, even to him,” should be capitalized, that’s Jesus, “who is raised from the dead.” We should be married to who? Jesus, who is raised from the dead, and he marries what? Virgins. How do we become virgins when we were sinners? His blood. His blood cleanses from what? All sin. I become a virgin, I become a spiritual virgin, and I maintain that through the principle of repentance. If I mess up, I repent and I am restored back to what? Being a spiritual virgin. Now, this makes sense. Isaiah 54:5: “Your Maker, your Husband, the Lord of hosts is his name, your Redeemer.” See, the Redeemer and the Husband, it’s all one package. Hallelujah. Revelation 19:7: “The marriage of the Lamb is come, and his wife,” his what? “Wife has made herself ready.” That’s us. We’re ready, Lord. We’re mature. Men marry mature women, and women marry mature men. We don’t marry kids. Sex with kids and all that’s out in the Bible, that’s ridiculous. “Sex by eight or you’re too late” is just ridiculous. Are you with me? And adulthood is 20 years old. You young ones, look at me, the Bible says adulthood is 20 years old. How old? 20. You hang tight to your 20 and you’ll live a life that’s right. Hang tight and live right. Don’t you get to be 14, you got breasts sticking out, and you know, you got pubic hair and so forth, and you think, “Man, I’m more grown.” No, you’re not. Wait till you’re 20. Hang in there. Yes, that’s a good place for a hallelujah.
What does he say it means to be a “spiritual virgin”? (2 Corinthians 11:2, Isaiah 54:5, Revelation 19:7)

2 Corinthians 11:2: For I am jealous for you with godly jealousy. For I have betrothed you to one husband, that I may present you as a chaste virgin to Christ. Romans 7:4: Therefore, my brethren, you also have become dead to the law through the body of Christ, that you may be married to another—to Him who was raised from the dead, that we should bear fruit to God. 1 John 1:7: But if we walk in the light as He is in the light, we have fellowship with one another, and the blood of Jesus Christ His Son cleanses us from all sin. Isaiah 54:5: For your Maker is your husband, The LORD of hosts is His name; And your Redeemer is the Holy One of Israel; He is called the God of the whole earth. Revelation 19:7: Let us be glad and rejoice and give Him glory, for the marriage of the Lamb has come, and His wife has made herself ready.”
Who are the first fruits, and how is the church presented without blemish? (1 Corinthians 15:20, James 1:18, Ephesians 5:27)

He says “just because you got the equipment doesn’t mean you’re capable of using it yet,” then that the first fruits are “we are, the church,” citing 1 Corinthians 15:20 and James 1:18. He says the church is “an overcomer in this world in spite of the beast,” and reading Ephesians 5:27 he says the blood keeps us “faultless before Christ as long as we admit our sin and we keep going to him.”
Who are the first fruits, and how is the church presented without blemish? (1 Corinthians 15:20, James 1:18, Ephesians 5:27)

He said, “Well, he gave me this equipment, surely I got to use it.” Don’t you dare. He gave you hands, but don’t drive a car at nine. Right? Amen. Hallelujah. Yeah. Yeah. Just because you got the equipment doesn’t mean you’re capable of using it yet, and using it rightly. Hallelujah. Now, he says these are the first fruits, no deceit or faults in them. These are the first fruits. 1 Corinthians 15:20: “Christ has risen from the dead and become the first fruits of them that slept.” James 1:18: “Of his own will begat he us with the word of truth, that we should be a kind of first fruits of his creation.” So who are the first fruits? We are, the church. These people are missing the whole focus of Revelation, that is, the church is an overcomer in this world, in spite of the beast, in spite of Satan, and everything that comes against us, we are overcomers. And that’s why we’re here today. Our forefathers overcame, not all of them. They handed this stuff down to us. Ephesians 5:27: “Present the church to himself, the bride, a glorious church with no spot, no wrinkle, no blemish, but holy.” What’s he going to present to himself? This first fruit people that are without blemish, no faults. Why are we have no faults, even though we have faults? The blood. And we’re on the assembly line, we’re following Christ, and the blood covers us, the blood keeps cleansing us, the blood keeps keeping us a virgin, a spiritual virgin for Christ, faultless before Christ, as long as we admit our sin and we keep going to him. We’re on the assembly line, he keeps changing us. And if you don’t change, you’re going to burn.
Who are the first fruits, and how is the church presented without blemish? (1 Corinthians 15:20, James 1:18, Ephesians 5:27)

1 Corinthians 15:20: But now Christ is risen from the dead, and has become the firstfruits of those who have fallen asleep. James 1:18: Of His own will He brought us forth by the word of truth, that we might be a kind of firstfruits of His creatures. Ephesians 5:27: that He might present her to Himself a glorious church, not having spot or wrinkle or any such thing, but that she should be holy and without blemish.
What does he say about hell and the church prevailing? (Matthew 16:18)

He says “the people want to laugh at the Bible … they’re going to burn,” and reading Matthew 16:18 he says “we’re supposed to be overcoming the gates of hell.” Of people who claim hell is just the grave, he says “they’re lying to you,” because “there’s a power in hell” and the church prevails against it. These are his views.
What does he say about hell and the church prevailing? (Matthew 16:18)

The people want to laugh at the Bible and all that, they’re going to burn. Matthew 16:18: “The gates of hell shall not prevail against” what? The church. See, we’re supposed to be overcoming the gates of hell. And these people that say that, “Oh, hell isn’t like that, it isn’t a place of the fire, and it isn’t a place, it’s just a place where you go and you’re in the grave,” they’re lying to you. It says the church does not prevail against hell. What good does it do to prevail against someone that’s dead and has no life after that? There’s a power in darkness, there’s a power in hell, there’s a power in that judgment, and the church, what? Prevails against it. We overcome it. Okay, the saints are likened to servants in Revelation, the brethren, the remnant, and the bride. The servant does things out of duty.
What does he say about hell and the church prevailing? (Matthew 16:18)
Matthew 16:18: And I also say to you that you are Peter, and on this rock I will build My church, and the gates of Hades shall not prevail against it.
What are the servants, the brethren, the remnant and the bride? (Revelation 12:11, 12:17)

He says servants “just do it because it’s their duty,” the brethren “overcome Satan by the blood of the Lamb,” and the remnant “keep the commandments of God and follow Christ.” He says Satan “makes war with those that believe, even do something about it,” and the bride is last.
What are the servants, the brethren, the remnant and the bride? (Revelation 12:11, 12:17)

They don’t feel like it, they don’t want to, they just do it because it’s their duty, and all of us are to be servants. Then there’s the brethren. The brethren are a little different. They overcome Satan “by the blood of the Lamb, and they loved not their life unto death, and the word of their testimony.” The brethren are [unclear], they overcome Satan, they don’t let sin and Satan rule and control their life. Are you there? The remnant are they that, what? Keep the commandments of God and follow Christ. That’s us. We’re supposed to keep the commandments of God and follow Christ, isn’t that right? We’re supposed to go from believer to servant to discipleship to being brethren to being the remnant. That he makes war with the remnant, you know why? Because they keep the command. He’s not interested in people that just believe and don’t follow Christ. Satan makes war with those that believe, even do something about it. So if you don’t have problems in your life, it’s a good chance you’re not much, a, you’re not, you haven’t gone past the servanthood.
What are the servants, the brethren, the remnant and the bride? (Revelation 12:11, 12:17)

Revelation 12:11: And they overcame him by the blood of the Lamb and by the word of their testimony, and they did not love their lives to the death. Revelation 12:17: And the dragon was enraged with the woman, and he went to make war with the rest of her offspring, who keep the commandments of God and have the testimony of Jesus Christ.
What is the harvest where the gospel is preached to all nations? (Revelation 14:6–7)

He says the saints are still here and the gospel is preached “to all nations, saying, fear God, praise and worship God, the judgment is come.” He says “nothing has happened like this in history” as the emphasis on praising and worshiping Jesus, and that people in many churches cannot hide behind “I was raised this way.” He says he will show who Babylon is “without leaving the book of Revelation.” He also names churches and denominations; see the editor note.
What is the harvest where the gospel is preached to all nations? (Revelation 14:6–7)

In fact, if you don’t do things just because it’s your duty, you’re probably just a weak wimp believer. You haven’t gotten out of the baby crib yet. Could that be an amen? And then the bride. Oh, the bride prepared for her husband. Okay, last but not least, the harvest. The gospel is preached. See, the saints are still here, right? We just found out the saints are still here, and the gospel is being preached by who? The saints, the people of God. God’s wrath and God’s judgment and the harvest. Here we go. The gospel is preached. It says there to all nations, saying, “Fear God, praise and worship God, the judgment is come.” Okay, and nothing has happened like this in history like our generation, where there’s an emphasis on praising and worshiping Jesus Christ. The Baptists are doing it now. Catholics have a separate group in the back room that are doing it. They’re praising and worshiping God. Why? God said this would happen before he would come. Hallelujah. And you don’t have to, you can sit there like a dodo bird and go, “Well, you know, I was raised this way, and I’m shy, and I was, you know, born a Baptist, I’ll die a Baptist,” or whatever. I just told you the Baptists are being converted to the Bible. They’re praising and worshiping and singing choruses, and the judgment has come. All right, and what do we preach? We preach to fear God, turn from your sins, praise and worship him, follow him, pray and seek him, for there’s a judgment coming where you’re going to be accountable for what you say and do. Now, here’s God’s wrath, judgment: Babylon has fallen. We’ll be getting into that very clearly. I’m going to show you clearly who Babylon is from the Bible without leaving the book of Revelation. That sound fair? So see, this is like the old series, you know, they, they ended it with a what’s going to happen next. Everybody’s got Babylon this and Babylon that. The Bible plainly tells us who Babylon is, Revelation does: the beast worshipers, and those that have the Mark.
What is the harvest where the gospel is preached to all nations? (Revelation 14:6–7)

Revelation 14:6-7: Then I saw another angel flying in the midst of heaven, having the everlasting gospel to preach to those who dwell on the earth—to every nation, tribe, tongue, and people— saying with a loud voice, “Fear God and give glory to Him, for the hour of His judgment has come; and worship Him who made heaven and earth, the sea and springs of water.” Revelation 14:8: And another angel followed, saying, “Babylon is fallen, is fallen, that great city, because she has made all nations drink of the wine of the wrath of her fornication.”
What does he say the two prophets and “limited supernatural power” are? (Revelation 11)

He says the beast worshipers are being challenged by the saints and by “two prophets who have supernatural powers” who counteract the second beast, “a display of full supernatural power against a display of limited supernatural power.” Of the two witnesses killing people with fire from their mouths, he says “I highly doubt that’s really what he’s talking about.”
What does he say the two prophets and “limited supernatural power” are? (Revelation 11)

I mean, you got to remember, we just left two prophets that were calling down fire from heaven and tormenting mankind. We got these supernatural people doing super... we got two supernatural powers working against each other here. Are you, are you there? Do you remember the two witnesses, the two prophets, that tormented people on earth for three and a half years, bringing fire? They would kill them with fire from their mouth. We’ve never seen that, and I highly doubt that’s really what he’s talking about. Are you there? So the beast worshipers, they that worship the beast, they are being challenged by the word of God from the saints of God who won’t worship the beast. At the same time they’re getting a challenge, and not only are they challenging, when this supernatural beast comes up, these two prophets who have supernatural powers are counteracting the supernatural power of the second beast, if you can read it right. And it’s a display of full supernatural power against a display of limited supernatural power. Hallelujah.
What does he say the two prophets and “limited supernatural power” are? (Revelation 11)
Revelation 11:5: And if anyone wants to harm them, fire proceeds from their mouth and devours their enemies. And if anyone wants to harm them, he must be killed in this manner.
What is the patience of the saints, and which group do you want to be in? (Revelation 13:10, 14:12)

He says the beast worshipers “enter into eternal torment,” and “this is the patience of the saints”: the saints are “patiently waiting for God to remove these people” and “turn the table on them.” He asks which group you want to be in, the one that takes 666 and “can buy and sell,” or the one that says “I’m following Christ,” even if we do not have “full victory” now.
What is the patience of the saints, and which group do you want to be in? (Revelation 13:10, 14:12)

And they’re going to enter into eternal torment, not just tormented now while they’re here on earth, they’re going to go into the torment, the hell fire and brimstone and all that. And then he comes up and says, “This is the patience of the saints.” They that lead into captivity shall, what, go into captivity. They that kill with the sword shall be killed with the sword. And so the saints are just patiently waiting for God to remove these people, this beast, and put them into captivity, and these that want to use force to get their way, they go, they’re just waiting for God to turn the table on them. Are you there? Now, which group you want to be? You want to be the one that takes the 666 and you can buy and sell and go on through life, and then when you’re confronted with Jesus Christ, you’re in trouble? Or you want to be one that says, “I’m following Christ, I’m following what’s right, and yes, it may look bleak for us now, and we may not have full victory and full control over everything in this earth, but it’s coming”?
What is the patience of the saints, and which group do you want to be in? (Revelation 13:10, 14:12)

Revelation 13:10: He who leads into captivity shall go into captivity; he who kills with the sword must be killed with the sword. Here is the patience and the faith of the saints. Revelation 14:12: Here is the patience of the saints; here are those who keep the commandments of God and the faith of Jesus.

He says “there’s two harvests”: the harvest of the earth, which is “us” (“the dead in Christ will rise”), and then “the wrath of God’s wine press.” He says the wrath, the second coming and the day of judgment are “all one package.”

And everyone with the mark’s in serious trouble. Ain’t that what it says? Man, don’t get me no more, I don’t even want to get close to the kingdom of Satan. Then there’s two harvests. He says the harvest is ripe. The angel says, “Put in your sickle and reap the harvest, for the harvest is ripe.” It’s ready. Isn’t that what Jesus said? “Look upon the fields, for they are white, ripe for the harvest.” And here comes the harvest of the earth. That’s us, folks. That’s us, those of us who are, and the dead in Christ will rise. That’s us. We’re going to be harvested. And oops, and then there is a second harvest. Ain’t that cute? And then there is the wrath of God’s wine press, where the blood went up to the horses’ bridles. I mean, here we got the wrath, judgment, it’s eternal, they’re going to be tormented, and it’s at the same time, the day of wrath, the second coming, the day of judgment, all one package.

Revelation 14:14-16: Then I looked, and behold, a white cloud, and on the cloud sat One like the Son of Man, having on His head a golden crown, and in His hand a sharp sickle. And another angel came out of the temple, crying with a loud voice to Him who sat on the cloud, “Thrust in Your sickle and reap, for the time has come for You to reap, for the harvest of the earth is ripe.” So He who sat on the cloud thrust in His sickle on the earth, and the earth was reaped. John 4:35: Do you not say, ‘There are still four months and then comes the harvest’? Behold, I say to you, lift up your eyes and look at the fields, for they are already white for harvest! Revelation 14:19-20: So the angel thrust his sickle into the earth and gathered the vine of the earth, and threw it into the great winepress of the wrath of God. And the winepress was trampled outside the city, and blood came out of the winepress, up to the horses’ bridles, for one thousand six hundred furlongs.

He says this message “scared me to come to Jesus,” and that “we are to be afraid of God,” which he explains as to “respect him” and “be scared of him.” He cites “fear the one who is able to cast your soul into hell,” and says a ruler who heard Paul preach on righteousness and judgment “trembled, but he would not change his life.”

And I don’t know about you, but I’m glad this kind of message scared the hell out of me. It scared me to come to Jesus, and I found out Jesus was real. And these people that want to diminish the Bible by saying, “You’re just putting fear in people.” We are to be afraid of God. We are to respect him, and we are to be scared of him. It says, “Fear the one who is able to cast your soul into hell.” Don’t fear the one that can just hurt you physically. They can take away your job, they can take away your income and ability to buy and sell. Fear him who has the power to cast you into hell. And we’re supposed to tremble. Didn’t Herod tremble when Paul preached to him of righteousness and the judgment to come? He trembled, but he would not change his life. And the church needs this message to cause God to move people to tremble and be afraid of God.

Matthew 10:28: And do not fear those who kill the body but cannot kill the soul. But rather fear Him who is able to destroy both soul and body in hell. Acts 24:25: Now as he reasoned about righteousness, self-control, and the judgment to come, Felix was afraid and answered, “Go away for now; when I have a convenient time I will call for you.”
What does he say the final judgment is like? (Revelation 20–21)

He says everyone stands before God “on your own merit,” “weighed in the balance,” by “what you did with the word of God and how you lived your life.” He says judgment on earth is “temporary to get your attention,” while the final judgment is eternal, with “a new earth and a new heaven” for the righteous and “a lake of fire” for the unrighteous. These are his statements about eternal punishment.
What does he say the final judgment is like? (Revelation 20–21)

On that day, one day you got to stand before, young people, you got to stand before God. Old people, nobody can stand there with you. Not your husband, not your wife, not your, your parents. You are there on your own merit. You’re going to be weighed in the balance, and it’s not your opinions, it’s going to count. It’s what you did with the word of God and how you lived your life, and did you admit you were wrong when you made mistakes. It’s a serious thing, and this judgment is eternal. Judgment down here is temporary to get your attention, but this judgment is eternal. Young people, there is a lake of fire. There is a new earth and a new heaven where the righteous live in, and a lake of fire where the unrighteous live in for eternity. And it says they are tormented forever before the throne and before the Lamb. They see Jesus up there, they see God up there, and yet they’re down there tormented in the flame of the lake of fire, and they can look up and see us blessed and rewarded, and that’s double torment.
What does he say the final judgment is like? (Revelation 20–21)

Revelation 21:1: Now I saw a new heaven and a new earth, for the first heaven and the first earth had passed away. Also there was no more sea. Revelation 20:14-15: Then Death and Hades were cast into the lake of fire. This is the second death. And anyone not found written in the Book of Life was cast into the lake of fire. Revelation 14:10: he himself shall also drink of the wine of the wrath of God, which is poured out full strength into the cup of His indignation. He shall be tormented with fire and brimstone in the presence of the holy angels and in the presence of the Lamb.
Who does he say the two beasts are, and will wickedness grow? (Matthew 13:30)

He says people who follow Satan “are the children of Satan” and people who follow God “are the children of God,” so “the beast can simply be people who carry out Satan’s actions and will and purposes in this life.” Reading “let both grow together until the harvest,” he says wickedness will grow and so will righteousness, “so don’t get rattled by it.”
Who does he say the two beasts are, and will wickedness grow? (Matthew 13:30)

Now, I told you who the two beasts were from the book of Revelation. We know that the Bible says that people who follow Satan are the children of Satan, and the people that follow God are the children of God. And so the beast can simply be people who carry out Satan’s actions and will and purposes in this life, and the people of God are those that do the opposite. And though we may make mistakes, we have a God that forgives and keeps us going, whereas the people of wickedness just keep, what, getting more wicked. Isn’t that what it says in the parable? “Let both grow together until the harvest.” So see, wickedness is going to grow, and so is righteousness. Isn’t that good news? God promised we would grow in righteousness, and he says the wicked are going to grow in wickedness, so don’t get rattled by it. We are destined to be overcomers if we pursue God.
Who does he say the two beasts are, and will wickedness grow? (Matthew 13:30)

1 John 3:10: In this the children of God and the children of the devil are manifest: Whoever does not practice righteousness is not of God, nor is he who does not love his brother. Matthew 13:30: Let both grow together until the harvest, and at the time of harvest I will say to the reapers, “First gather together the tares and bind them in bundles to burn them, but gather the wheat into my barn.” ’ ”
Why does he say we should publicly acknowledge Jesus? (Matthew 10:32–33)

He says “if you don’t publicly acknowledge him, he won’t acknowledge you.” He says God has chosen “these simple, humble acts,” such as worshiping, coming to church, raising hands and telling coworkers “I’m a Jesus boy,” to bring us to himself, and that God uses that “humiliating act” “to strengthen you and develop you and mature you.”
Why does he say we should publicly acknowledge Jesus? (Matthew 10:32–33)

Amen. How many will raise your hand, “Jesus, I’m on your side”? Yes. You got to pu... see, if you don’t publicly acknowledge him, he won’t acknowledge you. Ain’t that right? And these simple, humble acts is what God has chosen to bring us to himself and touch us with his supernatural power. It’s in that act of humiliation, humbling yourself to worship and pray, humbling yourself to come to church, humbling yourself to raise your hands and sing unto him, humbling yourself to say “I’m a Jesus boy” to your fellow workers. That’s what God uses, that humiliating act, to strengthen you and develop you and mature you. Hallelujah. So in the book of Revelation, who is the powerful one, the beast or the church? The church.
Why does he say we should publicly acknowledge Jesus? (Matthew 10:32–33)

Matthew 10:32-33: “Therefore whoever confesses Me before men, him I will also confess before My Father who is in heaven. But whoever denies Me before men, him I will also deny before My Father who is in heaven.
In Revelation, who is the powerful one, the beast or the church? (Romans 4:21)

He asks who the powerful one is in the book of Revelation and answers “the church.” He says God has “the power to perform what he promised,” and “we know he has the power to keep me … to mature me,” so “we patiently wait for him to do it.” He attributes the “power to perform” words to Paul’s letter to the Galatians; see the editor note.
In Revelation, who is the powerful one, the beast or the church? (Romans 4:21)

Hallelujah. Now, does God have power to back up what he said? Does he? Yes. That’s what Paul wrote to the Galatians. Faith in God is faith that says God has the power to perform what he promised. God, and that’s the patience of the saints. We know he has the power to do that. We know he has the power to keep me. We know he has the power to mature me. We know he has the power to overcome the principalities and powers of this life. We know that, and so we patiently wait for him to do it.
In Revelation, who is the powerful one, the beast or the church? (Romans 4:21)
Romans 4:21: and being fully convinced that what He had promised He was also able to perform.
What does he say Zion is?
He says “Zion is the church,” citing Hebrews 12, and later “we are Zion, we are the church.”
What does he say is written on the 144,000?
He says it is “the name of God,” and ties it to Revelation 3:12: “He who overcomes, I will make him a pillar in the temple of my God… I will write on him the name of my God.”
What does he say we should do if we have not yet overcome?
He asks, “Do we give up because we haven’t quite made it yet?” and answers, “No, man, we’re on the assembly line, just hang tight.”
What does he say the new song is?
He says “we are the ones that have the new song,” and points to the psalm’s “new song in my heart” and “psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs.”
Does he say the 144,000 must be physical virgins?
He says no: “God can’t contradict his word, so it can’t be this virgin thing,” since God said it is good for a man to leave his mother and father “and cleave to his wife.”
What does he say “chaste virgin” means?
He says Paul is “not talking about fleshly virginity,” but “the absence of sin, the absence of walking in darkness and disobeying God.”
What does he say the marriage of the Lamb is?
Reading Revelation 19:7, “the marriage of the Lamb is come, and his wife” “has made herself ready,” he says “that’s us. We’re ready, Lord. We’re mature.”
Who does he say the first fruits are?
He says “we are, the church,” and that the church is “an overcomer in this world in spite of the beast, in spite of Satan.”
How does he say we can be without fault when we still have faults?
He says “the blood keeps cleansing us,” keeping us “faultless before Christ as long as we admit our sin and we keep going to him,” and that “if you don’t change, you’re going to burn.”
Why does he say Satan makes war with the remnant?
He says “he’s not interested in people that just believe and don’t follow Christ,” and “Satan makes war with those that believe, even do something about it.”
What does he say about believers who do nothing out of duty?
He says “if you don’t do things just because it’s your duty, you’re probably just a weak wimp believer,” who “haven’t gotten out of the baby crib yet.”
What does he say we preach in light of the judgment?

He says “we preach to fear God, turn from your sins, praise and worship him, follow him, pray and seek him,” because “there’s a judgment coming where you’re going to be accountable for what you say and do.”
Who does he say can stand with us before God?
He says “nobody can stand there with you,” not a husband, wife or parents: “you are there on your own merit.”

items.ser: Why Jesus Is Important to All
tg: Why Jesus Is Important to All
p: The message defines a disciple as someone disciplined who follows Jesus’ teaching and does the Father’s will. From the rich man and Lazarus it teaches that hell is real, success won’t get you to heaven, and repentance is the key; Paul’s words to Felix on righteousness, self-control and judgment are the message the world needs. It closes with Job’s steps and forgiving those who wronged us.

Maybe differently: imagine Jesus Christ is your King walking into the room, with all glory and majesty belonging to Him.

items.d: Pastor David G. Kincer compares how the four gospels begin. Mark opens with John the Baptist preaching repentance at the Jordan without a building or band. Luke writes an orderly account, Matthew traces Jesus…
p: Pastor David G. Kincer compares how the four gospels begin. Mark opens with John the Baptist preaching repentance at the Jordan without a building or band. Luke writes an orderly account, Matthew traces Jesus to David and Abraham, and John declares the Word made flesh. God the Father imparts belief, and believers bear fruit as He prunes them.
The beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ, the Son of God; a messenger prepares the way.

items.d: Continuing on the first commandment, Pastor David G. Kincer studies Balaam, the sorcerer hired to curse Israel. God turned the curse into blessing and spoke truth through him, but Balaam’s counsel led Israel…
p: Continuing on the first commandment, Pastor David G. Kincer studies Balaam, the sorcerer hired to curse Israel. God turned the curse into blessing and spoke truth through him, but Balaam’s counsel led Israel into immorality and idolatry. Jesus warned Pergamos about the doctrine of Balaam. The lesson: take counsel from God’s word, and God works through his people, whom he never abandons.

And uh he says this is the great and the first commandment. All right, there were a lot more than seven churches in Asia. But he picked these to teach us. And he said to the Ephesus church, I have this against you. Uh you have left your first love. Now what’s the first love? Love God with all your heart, with all your soul, with all your understanding. And so I made a statement. For the past 50 years, the success of the American church has been increasingly measured by the second commandment, love your neighbor as yourself, and not the first and great commandment to love God with all your being.
