He says humanist billboards put “In Good We Trust” against “In God We Trust,” yet leaders since the French Revolution—Mao, Pol Pot, Stalin—killed twenty-some million. Claiming never to lie, steal, or sexually sin is self-deception; even Christians work at being good and make mistakes.
What does he say about “In Good We Trust” and mass-killing leaders?

In Matthew 19:17 there is none good but God. Ecclesiastes 7:20, there’s not a just man on earth who does good and does not sin. Yet you humanists have this billboard around the nation: In Good We Trust—on our quarter instead of In God We Trust. You have more than three leaders, nations, that have killed 20 and some million people since the French Revolution—Mao of China, Pol Pot of Cambodia, and Stalin of Russia. That’s not good. Again you are—good without God, millions are—and what you’re telling us is you never lie, you never steal, you never commit sexual immorality, you don’t mistreat people, you don’t hate people. You are deceiving yourself. Even us Christians are trying and working at being good people. We make mistakes.
What does he say about immigration, work, and “something for nothing”?

He cites one law for citizen and stranger (Numbers 15:16), labor as God’s gift (Ecclesiastes 3:13), and if you don’t work you don’t eat—against a billboard blaming capitalism and a manifesto guaranteed salary. Promoting something for nothing is like false religion promising heaven with no obligation to do good.
What does he say about immigration, work, and “something for nothing”?

Numbers 15:16, there’s one law and one custom for citizens of a nation and the stranger that comes into a nation. Ecclesiastes 3:13, all must eat, drink, enjoy the good of his labor—must labor; it is a gift of God. And the Bible says if you don’t work you don’t eat. Yet you have a billboard that says we don’t have an immigration problem, we have a capitalism problem, because in your manifesto you said that you want to guarantee a yearly salary, minimum salary, to everyone in the nation—when the Bible says that the poor work for wealth, field droppings, corners of the field left for them, or they had to beg, or they had to sell themselves to someone in the nation for six years. When you promote something for nothing you’re just like false religions that promote eternal life without any obligation to do good. And a lot of religions are promoting something for nothing—all I got to do is believe in Jesus or believe in Allah or believe in something, and everything’s going to be okay, I’m going to go to heaven, and I don’t have to do good and I don’t have to do righteous. That is something for nothing.
What does he say about immigration, work, and “something for nothing”?

Numbers 15:16: One law and one custom shall be for you and for the stranger who dwells with you.’ ” Ecclesiastes 3:13: and also that every man should eat and drink and enjoy the good of all his labor—it is the gift of God.
How can God’s people, humanists, and the wicked grow together?

First, neither humanists nor God-followers may lie or harm others physically, financially, mentally, or spiritually. Second, when either hurts others they must be punished or corrected as criminals, and if they will not change, separated from society.
How can God’s people, humanists, and the wicked grow together?

Now how can God’s people and humanists and the wicked grow or increase together? We’re going to summarize it. How can this possibly work out? Okay, we’ve given you the steps. We’re going to sum those steps. First of all, humanist nor God followers may lie to other people or do harm to other people physically, financially, mentally, or spiritually if we’re going to grow together and work together as a community, as a nation. Neither humanists that don’t believe in God nor God followers that believe in God have an excuse to hurt other people. All right. Secondly, when humanists or God followers hurt others they must be punished. You know, just because you’re a believer in Christ does not give you permission to hurt others, and because you don’t believe in God doesn’t give you permission to hurt others. And when we do we need to be punished or corrected for the wicked behavior, as we are no longer just believers or non-believers but we are criminals—and criminals need to be corrected, punished, and if we don’t change our harmful ways we need to be separated from society.
What three choices does he sum up at the end?

Remember God cannot lie, God is love, love does no harm (Romans 13:10); laws should protect citizens from harm. Manifesto agrees “short of harming others.” Three choices: follow Jesus and don’t harm; reject Jesus and don’t harm (humanist); or follow/reject but hurt others—criminal wickedness requiring punishment. We must do good, not only talk.
What three choices does he sum up at the end?

Now we’ve got to remember and recall that God cannot lie, that God is love, and love does no harm to a neighbor. And in Romans 13:10 it says love fulfills the law. Every law written should be written to protect its citizens from harm, both from government and other citizens—and that’s the kind of laws that work. We got to remember these things, these high priorities. Next is we got to remember in the Humanist Manifesto they said, short of harming others, individuals should be permitted to express their likings and pursue their lifestyles as they desire. But the key is short of harming others. They agree with the Bible that they believe is a myth—we don’t have a right to hurt others. So we can unite around good, around not hurting others, and live amongst each other though one of us believes in God and the other doesn’t. So summing it up, there’s three choices: follow Jesus, the Bible, and don’t harm others; reject Jesus, the Bible, and don’t harm others—that would be the humanist; and number three, follow or reject Jesus in the Bible but we hurt others by criminal wicked behavior requiring punishment. In summation, we cannot just talk about doing good—we must do good.
What three choices does he sum up at the end?
Romans 13:10: Love does no harm to a neighbor; therefore love is the fulfillment of the law.
What does Matthew 13:30 say about good and wicked growing together?
Let both grow together until the harvest at the end of the world.
What third discernment does Malachi 3:18 add?
Discern between the righteous and the wicked, and between one who serves God and one who does not.
What Manifesto phrase does he say is the key to living together?
Short of harming others—individuals may pursue lifestyles, but evil must still be punished, corrected, or removed.
What Bible verse does he pair with humanist “do good”?
Galatians 6:10—as we have opportunity let us do good to all people.
Did Thomas Jefferson say Christianity has no redeeming feature?
He says humanist billboards claim that quote, but Jefferson never said it—a blatant lie.
Does he say the Bible calls itself a book of faith or of truth?
He says the Bible never says it is a book of faith; it says it is a book of truth (John 17:17).
What scientific claims does he say the Bible made early?
Earth as a sphere hung on nothing, the water cycle, and ocean currents before science knew them—and commands not to kill, steal, or do immoral sex.
Which leaders does he cite against “good without God”?
Mao of China, Pol Pot of Cambodia, and Stalin of Russia—killing twenty-some million since the French Revolution.
What does Numbers 15:16 say about citizens and strangers?
One law and one custom for citizens and the stranger who comes into the nation.
What is his final line on talking versus doing good?
In summation, we cannot just talk about doing good—we must do good.

items.t: Clash of the Horns and Carpenters Part 1
items.d: Zechariah saw four horns that scattered Judah—kingdoms empowered by spiritual forces. God sends carpenters, builders who terrify the horns. Daniel, Esther and John the Baptist stood firm; religious leaders…
items.ser: Clash of the Horns and Carpenters · 1
tg: Clash of the Horns and Carpenters
p: Zechariah saw four horns that scattered Judah—kingdoms empowered by spiritual forces. God sends carpenters, builders who terrify the horns. Daniel, Esther and John the Baptist stood firm; religious leaders opposed Jesus despite His signs. In Christ, Satan has no more authority.
The powers that scattered Judah—four kingdoms in Daniel 7, with spiritual forces behind them.

Zechariah 1 verse 18 through 19, it says, “I lifted up my eyes.” This is Zechariah, and I saw four horns. I said unto the angel that talked with me, “What are these horns?” The angel answered and said, “These horns have scattered Judah, Israel, and Jerusalem.” When he talks about Zion, Judah, Jerusalem, he’s talking about his church. Now, if you remember in our teaching in Daniel, Daniel chapter 2, the statue, the golden head was the king of Babylon, the Babylonian empire. The silver chest and arms was the Persian empire, the king. The brass waist and thighs were the kingdom of Greece, and the iron was Rome, and the feet and the legs were still Rome, but it was a divided Rome. Jesus had come and messed up their whole theology. All right, mixed people. Also, in Daniel 7, you remember the lion was Babylon, the bear was Persia, the four-headed leper was Greece, and the beast that was unlike all the other beast was the Roman empire that followed. Okay, so there were four horns, four kings, four nations, Gentile nations that tried to scatter Israel, God’s people. Got it? Now, we also got to remember in Daniel that there were spiritual powers behind these nations. Okay? In Daniel 10:20, the heavenly messenger said, “Now will I return to fight with the prince of Persia.” Now, he wasn’t returning to fight with Cyrus or one of the Darius or one of those Persian kings, he was going to fight with the spirit behind those kingdoms and those kings. And then he says, “When I’m done with the prince of Persia spiritually, I’m going to deal with the prince of Greece, the supernatural source power behind the kingdom of Greece.” Okay? So, there’s two things. We got the natural kingdom down here that is actually carrying out things that hurt God’s people, scatter God’s people, and prevent God’s people from serving God and and and the promotion of His kingdom. And then we got the spirit behind them. And the Bible says in Ephesians, “We wrestle not against flesh and blood, but with what?” Yeah, principalities and powers and spiritual wickedness in high places. See, heavenly places, spiritual places. And we got to remember that. We’re in a spiritual war. All right? Now, verse 20 says, “The Lord showed me four carpenters.” Four craftsmen, skilled laborers, craftsmen. And I says, “What are these What are these guys for? What do these guys do?” And he says, “These are the horns which have scattered Judah so that no man did lift up his head, but these four carpenters are come to fray or put them in fear, and cast out the horns of the Gentiles, which lift up their horn over the land of Judah to scatter it. Now, what is Judah in the New Testament? The church. What is Zion in the New Testament? The church. What is Jerusalem in the New Testament? The church. See, all these things were written for us to learn. Now, 2 Chronicles 24:12 tells us they hired carpenters to repair the house of God. So, what does a carpenter do? He works on God’s house. Got it? Simple. Now, who’s working on God’s house during these four kingdoms? All right. Going back to this picture of the four kingdoms, we have Daniel. Daniel was there interpreting dreams, interpreting visions.

Zechariah 1:18-19: Then I raised my eyes and looked, and there were four horns. And I said to the angel who talked with me, “What are these?” So he answered me, “These are the horns that have scattered Judah, Israel, and Jerusalem.” Daniel 7:3: And four great beasts came up from the sea, each different from the other. Ephesians 6:12: For we do not wrestle against flesh and blood, but against principalities, against powers, against the rulers of the darkness of this age, against spiritual hosts of wickedness in the heavenly places.
Daniel kept praying in the lions’ den; Esther, raised by her uncle, had a purpose.

He was thrown into the lions’ den because he prayed and wouldn’t stop praying. And God closed the mouth of the lions. Daniel was there to interpret the writing on the wall and tell the king of Babylon that he was going to die that night and Persia was going to take over and it happened right after he got through. See, he actually put the kingdom of Babylon and Persia in fear. He actually brought those kingdoms down because he was a carpenter building God’s house and building God’s people. Amen. Now, we got the three Hebrew children, remember? The king made a idol and said everybody’s got to worship it at the sound of the music and these three guys said, “We’re not worshipping your idol. It’s against our God.” They said, “Well, we’re going to throw you into the fiery furnace.” He said, “Go ahead and throw us into the fiery furnace. We’re not worshipping your God.” Well, he threw them into the fiery furnace, we all know, and there were four people in the fiery furnace, and one of them was the son of God, Jesus Christ himself. And then they came out of the fiery furnace without even a smell of smoke on them, let alone damaged physically. And then the king changed the laws of the land because of these carpenters that had a mind to build God’s people. Hallelujah. Okay, the third one is we have Esther and Mordecai. Esther married this heathen king following the advice of her uncle. Her parents had obviously killed in the captivity. And she and her uncle were taken captive. He raised her and God had a purpose for her marrying this heathen king to save Israel from the bad man, the bad people, Haman. And uh then she did all that. Haman was hung. And Mordecai was given the king’s ring, made the second in command of the kingdom just overnight, just like that. See, can God do a quick work? Yeah, he did it there. And then the king said, “You write the laws the way you want.” And so Mordecai wrote the laws, sealed it with the king’s thing, and the people of Israel got God’s people defending themselves and survived this extermination that Haman had planned. You see? See, they were carpenters. Then you have Ezekiel. Ezekiel prophesied. He was taken captive in the third captivity. And he was prophesying all this time to the people of God. All right. And he was carried away at one point back to Jerusalem, where the Jewish leaders were telling the people that they weren’t going to go into a third captivity and leading the people astray. And Ezekiel was sent to minister to God’s people’s leaders who were telling the people wrong. And when they rejected his message, as we will find in Ezekiel when we study it, God slew one of the leaders. Backed up the message of Ezekiel. And so, yes, it’s not just the Gentiles that can scatter God’s people.

Daniel 6:10-22: Now when Daniel knew that the writing was signed, he went home. And in his upper room, with his windows open toward Jerusalem, he knelt down on his knees three times that day, and prayed and gave thanks before his God, as was his custom since early days. Then these men assembled and found Daniel praying and making supplication before his God. And they went before the king, and spoke concerning the king’s decree: “Have you not signed a decree that every man who petitions any god or man within thirty days, except you, O king, shall be cast into the den of lions?” The king answered and said, “The thing is true, according to the law of the Medes and Persians, which does not alter.” So they answered and said before the king, “That Daniel, who is one of the captives from Judah, does not show due regard for you, O king, or for the decree that you have signed, but makes his petition three times a day.” And the king, when he heard these words, was greatly displeased with himself, and set his heart on Daniel to deliver him; and he labored till the going down of the sun to deliver him. Then these men approached the king, and said to the king, “Know, O king, that it is the law of the Medes and Persians that no decree or statute which the king establishes may be changed.” So the king gave the command, and they brought Daniel and cast him into the den of lions. But the king spoke, saying to Daniel, “Your God, whom you serve continually, He will deliver you.” Then a stone was brought and laid on the mouth of the den, and the king sealed it with his own signet ring and with the signets of his lords, that the purpose concerning Daniel might not be changed. Now the king went to his palace and spent the night fasting; and no musicians were brought before him. Also his sleep went from him. Then the king arose very early in the morning and went in haste to the den of lions. And when he came to the den, he cried out with a lamenting voice to Daniel. The king spoke, saying to Daniel, “Daniel, servant of the living God, has your God, whom you serve continually, been able to deliver you from the lions?” Then Daniel said to the king, “O king, live forever! My God sent His angel and shut the lions’ mouths, so that they have not hurt me, because I was found innocent before Him; and also, O king, I have done no wrong before you.”
Builders who terrify the horns so they can’t lift their heads—Jesus came to build His church.

And cause them not to be able to lift up their head. Lift up your head is a is a is a phrase in the Bible where we worship, we serve, we acknowledge God up in heaven. Lift up your head to the coming king. See? And uh they don’t like us serving God. They don’t like us teaching the Bible. And so, Ezekiel was that fourth carpenter. Okay? Now, let’s go. Remember? He told us in Romans 15:4, all things written before time was written for our admonition, our learning, upon whom the ends of the world have come. 1 Corinthians 10:11, all things happened to them that were written for our admonition upon whom the ends of the world are come. So, what do we learn? What do we learn from this story? This illustration, God put Israel through this to teach us something. So, how many are ready to learn something? Hallelujah. Now, so we go to the days of Jesus when Jesus came to build the church. See, he come to restore. Elijah came to restore all things. Did you know that? And John the Baptist, Elijah was going to come. The spirit of Elijah was in John the Baptist to restore all things. So, John the Baptist started preaching repentance and Jesus was coming and all this stuff. And he was going to restore and build his church. Jesus come to build his church. So, what do we learn by looking at Zechariah? All right. What are the horns that scattered and oppressed God’s people that were prophesied to happen by Ezekiel? I mean by Zechariah. Okay. Civil leaders. You got the Roman Empire. You know, they killed Christians. They put them in the arena. They put the lions on them. They persecuted Christians. They had their armies destroy the temple and all the rest. Herod had every child from 2 years old to uh and down killed because he wanted to kill Jesus. He heard there was a baby Jesus born a uh a a spiritual king and he didn’t want anybody king but him and so he had all the 2-year-olds down, but Jesus had moved down to Egypt by that time. You see. Pilate wound up giving the command to kill Jesus. The second Herod killed John the Baptist. See, they opposed God’s people in the midst of this time of restoration. Jewish leaders, the Pharisees, the Sadducees, and Caiaphas, the high priest, they all opposed Jesus and those that followed him. Their doctrines were horrible the Bible says. Jesus said beware of their these people’s doctrines. Doctrines are important. See, your doctrine affects your thinking and your thinking affects your behavior. So, doctrine is very important. He said these people are hypocrites. Jesus said they were hypocrites.

Zechariah 1:20-21: Then the LORD showed me four craftsmen. And I said, “What are these coming to do?” So he said, “These are the horns that scattered Judah, so that no one could lift up his head; but the craftsmen are coming to terrify them, to cast out the horns of the nations that lifted up their horn against the land of Judah to scatter it.” Matthew 16:18: And I also say to you that you are Peter, and on this rock I will build My church, and the gates of Hades shall not prevail against it.
They say and do not; spiritual forces worked behind them; faith is conviction of His truth, not opinion.

They say and they do not. They don’t even do what they say to do. He said they’d make two times the child of hell. They convert people to the religion, their way, and they make them two times more the child of hell than they are. So, where were the Pharisees, Sadducees going? To hell. Were they believers? Yes. Were they followers? No. You see, there’s a difference between a believer and a Christian. A Christian follows. They may make mistakes, but they get up, dust themselves off, and get going again. A believer just believes anything they believe is okay because they believe it. But a Christian believes what God said to believe. Can I hear an amen? Hallelujah. I had to tell somebody this week. You know, you’re not a you’re not you’re not a Christian, you’re a believer. And you’re you’re a believer because you are for this law that the Bible is against. You are a believer. You just believe you think God’s going to honor everything you believe. But a Christian follows the word and they won’t vote for or approve of things that the Bible doesn’t approve of that’s a Christian. Even at the cost of being persecuted, mocked, and rejected by those around them. Jesus said the father of these people was Satan himself. You see, the supernatural force behind the religious Pharisees and Sadducees was Satan himself. See, just like Daniel showed us that there was a spiritual force behind these four kingdoms. There is a spiritual force behind people that opposed Jesus and his truth. Are you there? And that’s what we as a church and as an individual Christian have to learn to focus on, the power behind the people that are opposing. Cuz if we can break the power behind them, we can win the people. So, we don’t have to get mad at people. See? Now, then there’s the Jewish scribes. They were professional interpreters of the Bible. They’re the one writing the books of the day, positive thinking, possibility thinking, purpose-driven thinking, prosperity thinking, faith thinking. They were the ones that were making all the money. Telling people what the Bible said because the people were too lazy to read the book and find out what God said. Hallelujah. And this is what Jesus said about them. He says, “These scribes have omitted the weightier matters of the law, judgment, God’s going to judge us, folks. People are saying, “Don’t judge, don’t judge.” God says, “You better be preaching judgment because I am judging.” See, and mercy. The mercy here is in the context that he will save and forgive the sinner that will repent, his mercy. You see, so they won’t be judged. And then faith is the conviction of truth. Not the conviction of your opinion. See? Faith is you’re convinced of his truth that you can repent, his mercy will forgive you and cleanse you, and you will escape the judgment. That’s the weightier matters of the law. And what do people not want us to talk about today? The judgment. Don’t judge. Judge not that you be not judged. Jesus said, “That’s the heavy stuff of the scriptures. That’s the important stuff.” Now, not only did Jesus say that, but he said that or the people said the scribes, when they speak, they don’t speak with authority. When Jesus speaks, he speaks with authority. In other words, Jesus, when he spoke, he came across that he had the right to say it. Heaven backed him up. But when the scribes talked, why? They were teaching their own opinion. So there was no power in what they said. How many of you heard ministers preaching there’s no power behind what they’re saying? Absolutely. How many of you spoken things that there was no power behind what you said? Because it was your opinion. They were sign seekers. Now, he was healing the dead, casting out demons, I mean, raising the dead, casting out demons, healing the sick, walking on water, calming the storm, and they want a sign. How do we know you’re the son of God?
Matthew 23:3: Therefore whatever they tell you to observe, that observe and do, but do not do according to their works; for they say, and do not do.
Despite many signs, they feared Him; Bible morality is the entrance to the kingdom.

Show us a sign. My goodness, he The Bible says he did so many signs that the heavens couldn’t contain the books that would be written of what he did. And what he spoke. But see, and uh they just want to justify their own opinions and the way they live. He also said that the Bible also says he mocked Jesus, made fun of Jesus, and they were displeased with people following and worshipping Jesus. You see, they don’t like it when you separate yourself to really live for Christ. See, and the more you separate yourself to Christ, the more people are not going to like you, including your family. And this is where a lot of Christians cannot overcome. They want everybody to like them, and they want to serve Jesus. Well, my friend, when you read the book, the more you follow Jesus, the more people don’t like you. Why? Because you expose them. And they don’t like it. So, they’ll call you a holy roller or religious idiot or whatever. Are you hearing me? And these were the ones that people went to to find out what the scriptures said. They feared Jesus. See, they were afraid of him. Just like it said over there. That these carpenters come to put them in fear. Okay? They feared Jesus. They said he cast out demons by Beelzebub, the chief of devils. And then they killed Jesus because they were afraid of him. They didn’t like people following him. They wanted people to follow them. They made their money off people following them. And then, we have the pagan religious leaders. Rome was is was built around paganism, idolatry. Uh Caesars were considered gods and to be worshipped. And they tried to kill Paul. You see, these are the four horns that opposed the building of the church. Are you with me? And see, he gave us the perfect illustration over there in Zechariah. See? Now, Luke 20:46, Jesus said, “Beware of the scribes.” In Luke 11:44, “Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, you hypocrites.” In Matthew 5:20, we get the summation of it all. “Except your righteousness exceeds the righteousness of the scribes and the Pharisees, you shall in no way, no case, enter the kingdom.” Did you hear that? He didn’t say, “Except your faith exceed.” He didn’t say, “Except your belief exceed.” He didn’t say, “Except your grace exceed.” He said, “Except your standard of living, doing right, exceeds the scribes and the Pharisees, you can’t get into the kingdom because they’re not getting into the kingdom.” Now, how many of that’s that’s just clear? That’s just plain. And how many American Christians have been brainwashed into believing because they believe in Christ, they’re automatically going to heaven? No accountability. So, Bible morality is the entrance into the kingdom of God. Can I hear an amen? Amen. Along with believing in Jesus, there’s no there’s no other way. Jesus is the way. But we got to put some action behind it. Now, the craftsmen, who are the craftsmen? We found out who the horns were that were opposing the building and the restoration of God’s people. Now, who are the craftsmen that are going to put these these opposers in fear and cast their power out over the people. See? Their influence over the people. Okay? You got John the Baptist and you got Jesus. Both of them were filled with the Holy Spirit. This is very important. Both of them preached the word. Not their word, God’s word. And that word was repent and bring forth fruit worthy of repentance. That was their message. Repent and what? Bring forth fruit worthy of repentance. Not just turn, not just in your mind say I’m wrong, but you what? Start doing right. And it takes a while for some of us to overcome. It’s okay. God We’re in a growing session. But we should be growing, shouldn’t we? Yes. Yeah. See, so a lot of people think because they cried the altar and they feel bad because they’re doing wrong that oh, I’ve arrived. No, you arrive when you stop doing wrong.
What did John the Baptist do?
No miracles—he told Herod what he did was wrong and was beheaded; in Christ, Satan has no more authority.
What did John the Baptist do?

Amen? Now, John did no miracles. Now, this is important, too, because I got saved in Pentecostal church, Assembly of God, and the Pentecostals really pushed, “Man, if you want to reach the world, you got to have miracles.” And uh Oral Roberts was saying, “A miracle a day, expect a miracle every day.” And my goodness, it’s a guilt trip on you if you’re going to preach the gospel, you got to have some kind of performance to back it up, to prove to the people, you know, and man, I I couldn’t do any miracles. I’d preach my heart out, but I wasn’t doing any miracles. I was trying. I was trying to do what my leaders told me to do, but nothing was happening. Now, people were getting saved. People were turning their life around, but I wasn’t doing any miracles. And finally, God had to awaken my brain, my spiritual brain, and say, “Son, it’s okay not to do miracles. John the Baptist didn’t do any, and he brought a multitude of Israel to God.” Hallelujah, just preaching repentance. So, I got out of that guilt trip. Now, Jesus did miracles. They rejected John, who didn’t do miracles. They rejected Jesus, and he did do miracles. Herod, the Bible says, feared John. Now, what do we read over there? That the carpenters would what? Put him in fear. And here, Herod is afraid of John, just like Zacharias said. And John, when Herod came to his meeting, John looked at Herod and says, “It’s not lawful for you to have your brother’s wife.” Cuz Herod had divorced his wife and stole his brother’s wife, married her, and came down there to Jerusalem to uh in Judah reign and rule. And Herod said, “What you did is wrong.” Herod And Herod didn’t repent. He cut John’s head off. And then this is why I was talking to someone just yesterday. And this is why they don’t want to really live the Bible and speak the Bible because they don’t want the repercussions. That’s exactly what they told me. “If I do what you’re telling me to do people aren’t going to like me and I can pay a price for that. I I’m not going to do that.” And I go, “Yeah, that’s the problem with the American Christians. We don’t want to put our life on the line. We don’t want our family disliking us or our friends disliking us or people on the job disliking us. We’re trying to please everybody but God. Can I hear an amen?” Cost him. He was martyred. Jesus the Bible said had no sin. That’s why he became the perfect sacrifice. Pilate, the Bible says, was afraid of Jesus when he heard who Jesus was when they told him who Jesus said he was, the Son of God. He got afraid. But he still ordered Jesus to be crucified. So he martyred Jesus and in martyring Jesus Jesus through his death destroyed the power of Satan. See, there’s that supernatural power behind these forces. See, he destroyed in his death Satan’s power. See, when when you come to Christ, Satan no more has any authority over you. Do you understand that? He can’t follow you and bother you. He can tempt you and test you. That’s his job. But he can’t possess you, you know, he can’t do anything to you because his power has been destroyed, rendered powerless over people that follow Jesus because Jesus has all the authority. So, we can’t blame Satan. Now, there’s the apostles. 12 of them and then 90 more that we know of they weren’t apostles, but 90 other followers that preached the gospel. They were taught by Jesus for 3 and 1/2 years. How many of you know that would be a good idea? Is for a minister to seriously get 3 and 1/2 years in the Bible before they start opening their big mouth. Personally taught by Jesus Christ and his word. Then, as the Bible says in Luke 24, he opened their understanding. After he rose from the grave, he had been teaching them 3 and 1/2 years, but it wasn’t until the he rose from the grave that he give them the understanding of what he had been teaching. What’s my point? My point is you can hear me preach every Sunday. You can read your Bible all through the week. You can hear people on the radio, but until he opens your understanding, you’re not going to get it. And he opens our understanding little by little, line upon line, precept on precept. I hear Christian talking way above their experience level. Like they’ve experienced it when they haven’t passed level one yet. You’re You’re going to get level 12 until you pass level one.
What did John the Baptist do?
Mark 6:18: Because John had said to Herod, “It is not lawful for you to have your brother’s wife.”
Why was Daniel thrown to lions?
How many signs did Jesus do?
So many they couldn’t be contained.
Does Satan have authority over believers?

items.t: Clash of the Horns and Carpenters Part 2
items.d: Spirit-filled carpenters preached and Felix trembled. Modern horns include false religion, fascism and nationalism, America’s inconsistent equality, liberalism, hedonism, denominational splits and evolutionary…
items.ser: Clash of the Horns and Carpenters · 2
tg: Clash of the Horns and Carpenters

Filled with the Holy Ghost, they preached; Felix trembled; scattered believers kept their character.

p: In “Conference Report,” a Vine Cluster Church member, asked by Pastor David G. Kincer to be a witness, reports what he heard at a pastors’ conference: calls to preach righteousness without fear, stories of believers attacked for their convictions, and a plea for the church to unite and get involved. Pastor Kincer then closes, saying the church cannot justify silence and that America needs a message of hope, illustrated by David and Goliath and by Paul at Corinth.

p: Ezra responded to the people’s sin by tearing his garment in grief. Nehemiah asked about the afflicted remnant. Programs can’t restore—unless the Lord builds the house, we labor in vain. Jesus came to proclaim liberty and make us trees of righteousness; every generation can be restored.
He tore his garment and sat astonished—megachurches wouldn’t survive such honesty.

Here’s Ezra’s implosion response. Check this out. I love this. Ezra, when he heard this, he tore his garment, plucked his hair out, plucked his beard. Ah, you guys. Stunned. He fell to his knees. Lifted up his hands toward heaven and prayed. Ashamed. He asked God to forgive these people that mingled with the heathen, that got intimate with their sins and did the abominations they were doing. He is asking forgiveness for other people. Wouldn’t that be a novelty in America that we actually come together? Wouldn’t it be something that the mega churches actually came together on Sunday morning and they knelt on their knees and they cried out for the sins of America instead of the upbeat music and they all the little flattering things they do to make everybody feel like they’re on a high-tech uh media source. I tell you right quick, they wouldn’t be a media uh a mega church anymore because the people that go to those churches don’t go to break the hold of sin on America. They go to get flattered. They go to get inspired. They want to hear the music of the day. Just put Christian words in it. They want, you know, entertainment. They want famous athletes coming in and saying what great Christians they are and all this stuff. Am I right? Yeah. In fact, most little churches wouldn’t last if they actually came and just sought God for the condition of the nation and the people around them. Think about it. One man started praying. One man just like Ezra. One man started studying the word, doing the word, and preaching the word, and he wound up with 3,000 people plus children coming to Jerusalem with him. One man here, we got one man who fell on his knees, began to pray, and the next thing you know, there’s a great congregation of men, women, and what? Children. There’s no nurseries back then. There’s no children’s church programs back then. They had to bring their kids with them. They had children under control. And folks, they’re coming to a prayer meeting. This mad man’s down here pulling out his hair, pulling out his beard, crying out to God to forgive the Levites, the priest, and the people of Israel for their sins. He’s out in public. It’s raining. The next thing you know, somebody sees him and they, oh my God. Yes. They get down on their knees. They begin to cry out. Somebody else comes along. The word gets out. items.d: In “Cruel and Unusual Punishments,” Pastor David G. Kincer quotes the Supreme Court’s 1958 “evolving standards of decency” line, reviews U.S. penalties (prison, parole, probation, restitution, fines, death)…
items.ser: Clarity on Crucial Choices · Full sermon
p: In “Cruel and Unusual Punishments,” Pastor David G. Kincer quotes the Supreme Court’s 1958 “evolving standards of decency” line, reviews U.S. penalties (prison, parole, probation, restitution, fines, death), and contrasts Bible restitution, stripes, limited servitude, refuge cities and death for murder—with no OT prisons. He argues some modern sentences are unusually light for violent crimes named in the transcript, and from 1 Timothy and Deuteronomy that punishment should be public so others fear and turn from evil.
What did the Supreme Court say about cruel and unusual punishment in 1958?

He quotes that the Eighth Amendment must draw its meaning from the evolving standards of decency of a maturing society, and tells of a half-day deserter who lost citizenship—the Court called that cruel and unusual for that crime.
What did the Supreme Court say about cruel and unusual punishment in 1958?

Today we’re going to look at the issue of the Eighth Amendment of the Constitution: what is cruel and unusual punishment? What is cruel and unusual punishment that the Constitution says we cannot punish people with? The Supreme Court in 1958 made this statement: the Eighth Amendment must draw its meaning from the evolving standards of decency that mark the progress of a maturing society. A soldier had deserted for half a day, came back, turned himself in; he was sent to the brig, he was discharged with an undesirable discharge, and then they took his citizenship away. And the Supreme Court said no—the Eighth Amendment—that is cruelty and that is an unusual severe punishment for that crime. So remember they said this statement: the Eighth Amendment must draw its meaning from the evolving standards
What punishments does he say America uses?
He lists prison (about 2.3 million), parole (800,000+), probation (2.5 million), restitution (which he doubts is really collected), and community service at a charity for so many hours.
What punishments does he say America uses?

of a progressing mature society. In America we have several punishments. We have prison, and we have 2.3 million people in prison, and we have eight-tenths of a million—800,000 or more—on parole from prison. And then we have the probation: you know, first-timer, we’ll put you on probation, you know, you just check in with us and be a nice guy. Two and a half million are on probation in America. Then you have restitution. And honestly, all the people I know, I have never heard one of them thieves having to pay back even what they stole plus the loan added to it, so I don’t know about this one, but they say it’s a law. Community service: so you pick your charity, you did a bad thing like some famous people do, so you pick a charity and you go work in that charity for so many hours—that is your punishment.
How often is the death penalty used, in his figures?

He puts a question mark on it: 15,000 murders in 2014 and only 35 executions—doesn’t sound carried out in a progressive mature society. Bible civil penalties he lists: restitution, fines, and at most 40 stripes.
How often is the death penalty used, in his figures?

Then you have fines where you pay a dollar amount for your punishment and then you’re just free to go. And then you have the death penalty—and I got a question mark there, because there were 15,000 murders in 2014 and only 35 people were executed with the death penalty. Doesn’t sound like it’s carried out in this progressive and a decent mature society. Civil punishments in the Bible: we have restitution; you have fines when you have a dispute with your neighbor, an argument or a court contest over something, and the loser has to pay a fine; and then you have beatings of 40 at the most stripes, okay.
Does Bible “servitude” mean slavery, in his teaching?

He says no: debtors hired themselves out up to six years to pay bills—not slavery. Refuge cities protected accidental killers from the avenger of blood until trial. Courts could beat bullies (39 stripes to stay under 40).
Does Bible “servitude” mean slavery, in his teaching?

So everybody beat 39 times so they didn’t go over the mark. And that was over a physical dispute: you’re a bully, you’re going around beating up 11-, 12-, 13-, 14-year-old guys and you’re 18, 19, 20, or your threesome in your little group is beating up people in the community—then the courts can beat you. All right. Servitude is very misunderstood in the Bible. Everybody that attacks the Bible says that slavery—that is not slavery. That is: you went into debt, or you had a bad business adventure, you couldn’t pay your bills, so you went and hired yourself out to someone for six years, or in that period of six years, to pay off that debt. It couldn’t last any more than six years, so it’s not slavery at all. Refuge cities were for people who accidentally killed someone: your axe handle, your axe flew off and hurt your neighbor and killed him, and so you could run to the city of refuge so the avenger of blood, the family, couldn’t come and kill you until you had a trial and found innocent.
What counts as cruel and unusual in the Bible?

He says the OT has no prison sentences—dealt with that day. Cruel examples: death for theft, death without trial by a mob, and torture (totally forbidden). Jail today is like a city of refuge until trial.
What counts as cruel and unusual in the Bible?

And then you had murder and you had the death penalty. And over here we have little symbols of that: death penalty was carried out by stoning or a sword; this is the whipping lash; and a jail is our city of refuge today—you go to jail to protect you from people and protect society from you until you’ve had a trial and found guilty. There are no prisons in the Old Testament laws—no prison sentences at all. Everything was dealt with that day, at that time, at that moment, and done and decided. So cruel and unusual punishment in the Bible would be death for a theft: you kill a person because they steal your horse—the Bible would say that was cruel and unusual punishment for that crime. Death without a trial: the mob, they accuse you of something, they think you’re guilty, and they just take you and they hang you and they stone you—that’s cruel and unusual in the Bible. Torture is totally forbidden in the Bible—no torture at all. False witness:
What happened to false witnesses, and what modern cases does he raise?

False witnesses received the penalty they sought for the accused. He then turns to on-screen modern crime cases (named in the transcript) that he says show offenders back in society harming the innocent.
What happened to false witnesses, and what modern cases does he raise?

they were examined, and if they were found to be a false witness, what they’ve brought that person to court for was done to them. If they brought that person to court to be stoned, then they were stoned. So you didn’t want to get in that court as a false witness. Now, cruel and unusual punishment—up on your screen is John Cooey. He’s age 46. He’s been arrested 24 times for drug violations. He’s a habitual user of crack cocaine. He’s been arrested for burglary, concealed weapons, disorderly intoxication, disorderly exposure, disorderly conduct under the influence of alcohol and drugs, driving. He committed fraud. He had some insufficient funds. He was charged with larceny, and his driver’s license had been suspended for 99 years. He had been arrested twice for fondling and abusing children, sexually abusing children. Okay. He was high on cocaine one day. He goes into the trailer in the same park and gets this girl out, age nine, Jessica.
Why does he ask why offenders were back in society?

After describing violent crimes against children and teens (details in the transcript), he asks why the offender was free to harm an innocent girl, and notes another offender got probation then short sentences after repeat rapes.
Why does he ask why offenders were back in society?

Takes her to his trailer where his sister and her lover lived—and you can see all three of them are on drugs. I mean, come on, anybody can tell something’s wrong there. And he rapes this nine-year-old girl, tore her vagina from the rape, put her in a closet to stay there all day without food till he got home. And my point is this: why was he back in society to harm this innocent girl? Secondly, we got Josh up there. He got a teenage girl drunk, 13 years old, intoxicated, and raped her, and he was given probation. Two years later, after he got off probation, he got a 14-year-old girl drunk and raped her, and he served one year.
What sentences does he call unusual for the crime?

He says three years for a pattern of getting girls drunk and raping them is an unusual punishment for a very bad crime, and the cruelty falls on the victim—including one buried alive (case named in the transcript).
What sentences does he call unusual for the crime?

Well, after he got out, he got a 16-year-old girl drunk and raped her, and unbelievably he got three years in prison. He was sentenced at three years in prison. I tell you that is an unusual punishment for a very bad crime. And the cruelty is to the young girl who lost her life. He took her and he put her in plastic bags and buried her alive. That was John Cooley. He buried her alive. Melinda Loveless—she’s 16 years old. She is a homosexual lady teenager. And she loved the girl
What other violent cases does he cite as under-punished?

He recounts a jealous teen torture-murder over a same-sex relationship and a rape-mutilation case that received eight years (names and details in the transcript), asking if that is maturing-society decency.
What other violent cases does he cite as under-punished?

up on your screen there, Shanda. And they had sexual relationships. That girl was 12 years old. Melinda is 16 years old. Well, Shanda switched partners and went to have sex with a 14-year-old girl, and Melinda got jealous, talked to her friends into luring her out of her home at midnight, took her to a place and beat her with her fist, beat her with a tire iron, shoved that tire iron up her anus, beat her over the head some more, tried to choke her—this was over an eight-hour period—tried to choke her to death. She passed out and then came back. They beat her more with the tire iron.
Is light sentencing the “decency” of a maturing society?
He asks whether treating the criminal with such decency that serious crime has no real penalty is the direction the Court says we are heading, and notes one victim survived after hikers found her.
Is light sentencing the “decency” of a maturing society?

And then she went home and her parents were there, with this girl in the trunk of her car out in the yard, and finally put gasoline on this girl and burned her to death. She died from the burning. Lawrence Singleton. Mary Vincent was having car trouble. This guy stopped and offered her a ride to the gas station and so forth, took her to a secluded place, raped her repeatedly, and then took an axe and cut off her arms. And he got eight years. Now, for that kind of cruel crime, is this the decency of a maturing society?
What is the Bible purpose of punishment?
From 1 Timothy 5:20, rebuke sinners before all that others may fear. From Deuteronomy 17:12, put away evil so all hear and fear and do no more presumptuously.
What is the Bible purpose of punishment?

Is this the direction we’re going, where the criminal is treated with such decency that there is no real penalty for a serious crime? Is this—for the Supreme Court says we are heading—two hikers came by. She was walking with her hands up trying to keep the bleeding down. Just happened two hikers came by and took the girl to the hospital, and she’s alive today. Purpose of punishment: 1 Timothy 5:20, them that sin rebuke before all, that others also may fear. Deuteronomy 17:12: you shall put away the evil from Israel; all the people will hear and fear and do no more presumptuously.
What is the Bible purpose of punishment?

1 Timothy 5:20: Those who are sinning rebuke in the presence of all, that the rest also may fear. Deuteronomy 17:12: Now the man who acts presumptuously and will not heed the priest who stands to minister there before the LORD your God, or the judge, that man shall die. So you shall put away the evil from Israel.
What does he call cruel and unusual punishment today?

From Deuteronomy 19:19 he says punishment should be publicized to deter. Cruel and unusual, to him, is authorities not punishing and publicizing, not informing citizens of destructive results, and missing morals and self-control—the puzzle piece—not decency.
What does he call cruel and unusual punishment today?

So penalizing is for deterring crime. Deuteronomy 19:19: put evil away from your midst, and those that remain shall hear and fear and shall from henceforth commit no more such evil. Punishment is to be publicized, to be public, to cause those that are coming up behind to stay away from a life of crime. Now, cruel and unusual punishment is civil authorities not discouraging future criminals by punishing present criminals and publicizing it; civil authorities not informing uninformed citizens of immoral behaviors’ destructive and life-ending results; and the conclusion that no morals, no knowledge of morals, lack of self-control is the missing social puzzle piece in America. And it is not decency when we do not punish the criminal for the proper crime.

Deuteronomy 19:19: then you shall do to him as he thought to have done to his brother; so you shall put away the evil from among you.

He says torture is totally forbidden in the Bible—no torture at all.

p: A heavenly messenger came to Daniel after a 21-day delay caused by the prince of Persia. God declares, delays to work in us, then delivers. Our weapons are spiritual—prayer, not self-help books. The disciples waited ten days before the Spirit came.
A heavenly being with a message—all visitations come with a message.

A certain man clothed in linen, a belt of gold, a body of beryl, a stone, when it’s pure, it’s crystal clear. The face was as lightning, his eyes of fire, arms and feet like polished brass, and the voice of his words was like the voice of a multitude. Now, how many of you know, if you’ve seen something like that, it would stop you in your tracks? Uh it would get your attention, yeah. Lightning face and all this stuff. Wow. Nowhere in the Bible is another creature described like this. But I’ll tell you one thing, that would get my attention really quick. And so, this guy comes and he says to Daniel, he has a message. All visitations from God have a message. If you see an angel, I’m interested in the message, not your vision of an angel. I’m interested in what God’s got to say, and if it doesn’t line up with things, I don’t know. From the first day that you set your heart to understand, the guy said, “From the first day you set your heart to understand and to discipline or chasten yourself before God, this is what this guy’s words were. From the very first day you started to discipline yourself and lift up your voice in prayer, he said, ‘Your words were here, heard from the very first day. And I am come for your words.’ Hallelujah. What brought this heavenly being? Daniel disciplined himself, setting aside some time, disciplining his body to pray and seek God audibly speaking. None of this thinking stuff, but audibly speaking prayers. And he heard him from the first day. Okay? Now, if that’s true, if God heard him the first day, why did it take 21 days for the message to get there? We call it the promise, the problem or the preparation, and the provision. You see, from the time you get a promise or a potential from God, you can be something in God. There has to be a preparation. There is going to be problems. We want to name it, claim it, ask it, receive it, bamboo jumbo, popcorn, did it dot. But a lot of times we need preparation. And if we don’t need preparation, like Daniel, he didn’t need any preparation, it was a delay. So, we call it the declaration, the delay, and then the delivery. And Christians don’t like that. God promises things in the Bible that we know are our But then God delays doing it, and we try to make it work on our own strength, and it won’t work.

items.d: In “Deflective Defective Disciples Part 1,” Pastor David G. Kincer says many of Jesus’ disciples in John 6 left because they wanted what they could get rather than what they could give, and he applies that to…
p: In “Deflective Defective Disciples Part 1,” Pastor David G. Kincer says many of Jesus’ disciples in John 6 left because they wanted what they could get rather than what they could give, and he applies that to prosperity preaching and other teaching he calls fractured. He plays recorded clips of public figures and ministers speaking about heaven, other religions and sin, and responds to them. He ends with the phrase “my faith,” saying the Bible uses it with works and with the faith of Jesus, and that our faith must be in Jesus Christ and his word, not in a group.
Why did many of Jesus’ disciples leave him?

Pastor Kincer says these were disciples who did not believe: they were disciplined to follow Christ to a certain degree, but they left when it came down to God being involved, and to accountability and responsibility. He says Jesus told them you cannot decide to serve God on your own, since the Father and the Spirit must be involved in your salvation, and it is not about joining a church or being a Jew, Protestant or Catholic.
Why did many of Jesus’ disciples leave him?

But this morning we’re going to talk about some deflective, defective disciples. Not everybody in the Bible turned out to be heroes. Deflective, defective disciples. They deflected because they had a defect. A disciple is one that’s disciplined, a pupil of Christ, a follower of Christ. And in John 6 we find him talking to what he called disciples, and he said, “There are some of you that believe not.” These are disciples that believe not. “For Jesus knew from the beginning who believe not and who should betray him.” Wow, powerful statement. “No man,” Jesus said, “can come unto me except it were given unto him by my Father.” Jesus said, listen, you can’t decide to serve God on your own. Me and my Father have to be involved in your conversion, in your salvation. It’s not joining a church, or being a Jew, or being a Protestant, or being a Catholic. Jesus said my Father has to be involved. The Spirit of God has to be involved. That’s why the Bible says you must be born again of the Spirit and of the word. Well, the disciples didn’t like this statement. Okay, now these are disciples. They’re disciples that didn’t believe. See, they were disciplined to follow Christ to a certain degree, but “from that time many of his disciples went back and walked no more with him.” They left him. And they were called disciples, but when it come down to God being involved, and accountability and responsibility, they left Jesus. And we’re going to show you what was really in their heart here.
Why did many of Jesus’ disciples leave him?

John 6:64-66: But there are some of you who do not believe.” For Jesus knew from the beginning who they were who did not believe, and who would betray Him. And He said, “Therefore I have said to you that no one can come to Me unless it has been granted to him by My Father.” From that time many of His disciples went back and walked with Him no more.
What does “Lord, to whom shall we go?” mean?

He says Jesus asked the twelve whether they would also go away, and he says that is what God is saying to the churches in America today: will you stop walking with me and join your little clique? He says Peter and the others answered that there is nowhere to go, because Jesus has the words of eternal life, and he says eternal life is to know God and Jesus Christ, not just live forever.
What does “Lord, to whom shall we go?” mean?

Here Jesus is. Then Jesus said to the twelve apostles, “Will you also go away?” Right now they’re the twelve disciples, apostles. Later they said, “You going to leave also?” And that’s what God is saying to the churches in America: Are you people going to leave me? Are you going to stop walking with me? You’re going to join your little clique and take your little clique and go out and think you got something? Are you going to stop walking with me? And they said, “Lord, to whom shall we go? You have the words of eternal life.” Now, as a young Christian this scripture just jumped right out at me, really did. There’s nowhere to go. Jesus has the words of eternal life. And remember, a couple weeks ago we learned that eternal life is to know God and Jesus Christ, not just live forever. And then the disciples, his twelve disciples, replied and said, “We believe and we know that you are that Christ, the Son of the living God.” You see, they had experienced that dimension of God being involved in their salvation. It wasn’t a little hand-me-down Christianity: my parents were Christians, so I’m a Christian. Hallelujah.
What does “Lord, to whom shall we go?” mean?

John 6:67-69: Then Jesus said to the twelve, “Do you also want to go away?” But Simon Peter answered Him, “Lord, to whom shall we go? You have the words of eternal life. Also we have come to believe and know that You are the Christ, the Son of the living God.” John 17:3: And this is eternal life, that they may know You, the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom You have sent.
Are we following Jesus for what we can get or for what we can give?

He says the fractured followers were after what they could get from following Jesus, not what they could give to him, and a lot of Christians are the same. He says what God wants us to give him is a Bible morality lifestyle, living right and stopping sinning, and that praise and prayer are wonderful but what he wants from you is to live right.
Are we following Jesus for what we can get or for what we can give?

Now, so that you understand why these disciples left, we’re going to go back to the early part of the scripture. And I’m going to make this statement: these fractured followers were after what they could get from following Jesus, not what they could give to Jesus. And a lot of Christians are only out for what they can get from God and not what they can give from God. And what God wants you to give him is a Bible morality lifestyle: living right, stop sinning. Hallelujah, that’s what he wants out of you. Oh, praise is wonderful and prayer is wonderful, but what he wants out of you is you to live right. That’s what he wants you to give him back. Doesn’t matter if you’re a Catholic or a Jew or a Protestant or whatever. And we only want what we can get.
Is prosperity preaching what Jesus taught?

He says the crowd followed Jesus in John 6 for signs and then for free food, and Jesus said so plainly, and he says that is where prosperity, positive-thinking and similar preaching comes in today. He says Jesus wants us to give him Bible morality and self-control, not these approaches, and he recalls an emphasis on miracles in earlier decades that made a sick person feel faithless.
Is prosperity preaching what Jesus taught?

And so, you know, the prosperity people come in. Like today, in John 6:2, this is the multitude, this is the disciples that were following him. They followed him in John 6:2 because they saw his signs which he performed on those who were diseased. They wanted to show— you know, Oral Roberts back in the old days: “Expect a miracle every day.” The emphasis was on a miracle. You couldn’t go through a day without a miracle. God help you if you were sick and God never healed you, because during the ‘50s, during the ‘60s, in the Spirit-filled world there was such an emphasis on divine healing that, man, if you’d got sick you were just a faithless, weak, worthless person. See, are we— we want what we can get out of God. And Jesus said it plainly. Okay, then later, in verse 26, he says, “You don’t seek me now because you see the signs and wonders and miracles. Now you seek me, you follow me, because I fed you with the loaves and the fishes and you were filled.” You want free food. Now you don’t want a show anymore, you want free food: what we can get out of God. And this is where your prosperity preaching today comes in: today’s faith and grace camps, prosperity, psychotherapy, Purpose— Purpose Driven, possibility thinking, positive thinking, and prophecy— one-on-one independent individual prophecy. We got all the— all these P’s. And they’re fractured followers. They are deflecting from Christ because they have a de— defect in them. They’re wanting something instead of giving him something. Can I hear an amen? And that’s where we’re at in America, and America needs to hear this message, and you need to get it out to them. Now, Jesus wants us to give to him Bible morality, not grace and faith, or prosperity, positive, purpose, possibility, psychotherapy, reparative therapy. There’s no reparative therapy in the Bible. In the Bible it’s self-control: just stop what you’re doing. Hallelujah. Now, I’m going to give you some examples of some deflective, defective ministers. All right, these are their statements.
Is prosperity preaching what Jesus taught?

John 6:2: Then a great multitude followed Him, because they saw His signs which He performed on those who were diseased. John 6:26: Jesus answered them and said, “Most assuredly, I say to you, you seek Me, not because you saw the signs, but because you ate of the loaves and were filled.
Is a Mormon a true Christian?

He plays a recorded clip in which a speaker says he is not the one to judge the little details and believes Mormons are Christians. He then says he phoned the headquarters of the Mormon church and was told Jesus Christ is not God and did not exist until Mary, which he says is not what the Bible teaches. He asks whether Christ cares what you believe or that you believe what he believes.
Is a Mormon a true Christian?

[Recorded clip begins.] And what about Mitt Romney? And I got to ask you the question, because it is a question, whether it should be or not, in this campaign: Is a Mormon a true Christian? Well, in my mind they are. Mitt Romney has said that he believes in Christ as his Savior, and that’s what I believe. So, you know, I’m not the one to judge the little details of it. So I believe they are. And, you know, Mr. Romney seemed like a man of character and integrity to me, and I don’t think he would— anything would stop me from voting for him, if that’s what I felt like. So, for instance, when people start talking about Joseph Smith, the founder of the church, and the golden tablets in upstate New York, and God assumes the shape of a man, do you not get hung up in those theological issues? I probably don’t get hung up in them, because I haven’t really studied them or thought about them. And, you know, I just try to let God be the judge of that. I mean, I don’t know. I certainly can’t say that I agree with everything that I’ve heard about it, but from what I’ve heard from Mitt, when he says that Christ is his Savior, to me that’s a common bond. [Recorded clip ends.] So I personally talked with headquarters of the Mormon church this week. I didn’t act like I was somebody else; I just personally called them, and I said, I want some questions answered, and they answered them. I said, is Jesus Christ God? And they said no. I said, is Jesus Christ eternal, without a beginning and without an end? And they said no, Jesus Christ is only the Son of God, and he didn’t exist until Mary. Now, how many you know the Bible teaches he existed before Mary? [Clip replayed:] He believes in Christ as his Savior, and that’s what I believe. So, you know, I’m not the one to judge the little details of it, so I believe they are. I’m not the one to judge them. I believe— say that statement: I believe, I believe. Who cares what he believes? See, when he says that Christ is his Savior, to me— is— does Christ care what you believe, or does he care that you believe what he believes? Yeah.
Does 1 Corinthians 15 teach three kingdoms after death?

He says the Mormon church told him there are three places to go when you die, tied to the sun, moon and stars, and he says there is nothing in 1 Corinthians 15 that says the sun, moon and stars are kingdoms. He says he was told that their modern prophets taught it.
Does 1 Corinthians 15 teach three kingdoms after death?

Now, they also told me that there were three places to go when you die. I said, really? Is a certain type of people going to hell? And they said no. And 1 Corinthians 15: there’s the sun, moon and stars, the terrestrial, the celestial, and the— they got a new word, terrestrial, telestial. They created a new word. And they said the sun, moon and the stars: the first kingdom after you die is where people that believe God and follow God and do good go. The second one is where people that can change later, and then the third one is for people that just resent God, and, you know, and all this. I said, man, that sounds like Catholicism. I said, you know, I happen to know 1 Corinthians 15. I happen to know it by heart, and there is nothing in 1 Corinthians 15 that says that the moon and sun and the stars are kingdoms. They said, oh no, no, he says our modern prophets told us that. I go, really? I go, who are your modern prophets telling you this? He said, Joseph Smith. I go, okay, all right. Now, folks, that’s from the horse’s mouth. That’s from Utah.
Does 1 Corinthians 15 teach three kingdoms after death?

1 Corinthians 15:40-41: There are also celestial bodies and terrestrial bodies; but the glory of the celestial is one, and the glory of the terrestrial is another. There is one glory of the sun, another glory of the moon, and another glory of the stars; for one star differs from another star in glory.

He calls what he has just described fractured philosophy, taking the Bible and making it be what they want it to be, and says Mormons are not going to heaven. He also says a well-known Christian preacher who does not know this has not studied it, and he calls that sad.

Okay, now, is that fractured philosophy? Yes. Biblical? Yeah, it is. You see, they are— they are taking the Bible and making it be what they want it to be. And so, no, Mormons aren’t going to heaven. Joel Osteen’s out of his mind. He is a Christian preacher, and he doesn’t know that, and he hadn’t studied it, and yet he’s got— he’s the biggest church in America. It’s sad. Are you with me? It’s very sad.
Do works matter if you believe in Christ, and what about people of other religions?

He plays a recorded clip in which a speaker says a believer will have some good works, calls it a cop-out to say you are a Christian but never do anything to help, and says he is very careful about saying who would and wouldn’t go to heaven. The speaker speaks of the sincerity of people of another religion he saw in India.
Do works matter if you believe in Christ, and what about people of other religions?

Now, let’s go on. [Recorded clip begins.] Who said your record don’t count? You either believe in Christ or you don’t. If you believe in Christ you are going to heaven; if you don’t, no matter what you’ve done in your life, you ain’t. Yeah, it— I don’t know. There’s probably a balance between— I believe you have to know Christ, but I think that if you know Christ, if you’re a believer in God, you’re going to have some good works. I think it’s a cop-out to say, well, I’m a Christian but I don’t ever do anything to help. What if you’re Jewish or Muslim and you don’t accept Christ at all? No, I— I just— I’m very careful about saying who would and wouldn’t go to heaven. I don’t know. I think only God— you believe you have to believe in— I believe they’re wrong. Well, I don’t know if I believe they’re wrong. I don’t know if I believe they’re wrong. I spent a lot of time in India with my father, and, you know, I don’t know all about the religion, but I know they love God, and I don’t know, I’d have to— you know, I’ve seen their sincerity, so I don’t know. I don’t know. [Editor’s note: about 20 seconds of this stretch have no captions.]
Is there only one way to God, or are there many paths?

He plays a recorded exchange in which a questioner says being gay is a gift from God, one speaker says there are millions of ways to be a human being and many paths to God, and another replies there is one way and only one way, Jesus. A panelist answers that there are many paths to Jesus and that everybody is going to heaven. He presents these as examples of deflective, defective ministers.

Hey, glad to have you. Hello, Oprah! Awesome to have you. We love you, we pray for you. Joel Osteen’s church. Oprah brought a friend with her today. He’s an entrepreneur, an actor, just— Tyler Perry is with us as well. Mr. Tyler Perry. All right, what’s your question for our spiritual panel? I’m a thirty-three-year-old guy. I grew up in a rural part of Alabama, and I happen to be gay, and the troubling part of our culture, which is largely anti-gay— being gay is a gift from God. Being gay is a gift from God. But our culture doesn’t understand that, and consequently the culture sends messages that you ought to isolate it, that you ought to isolate, that you ought to isolate. Well, you’re the first minister I ever heard say being gay is a gift from God. I can say now here human beings make is believing that there is only one way to live, and that we don’t accept that there are diverse ways of being in the world, that there are millions of ways to be a human being, and many ways— no, but many paths to what you God, and her path might be something else, and when she gets there she might call it the light, but her loving and her kindness and her generosity brings her— if it brings her to the same point that it brings you, it doesn’t matter whether she called it God along the way or not. Well, I believe, Oprah, that there— I believe that Jesus is the way to the one God, but I believe there are many paths to Jesus. So are gay people also included? Absolutely.
