Ecclesiastes 8:11: Because the sentence against an evil work is not executed speedily, therefore the heart of the sons of men is fully set in them to do evil. Ecclesiastes 8:12-13: Though a sinner does evil a hundred times, and his days are prolonged, yet I surely know that it will be well with those who fear God, who fear before Him. But it will not be well with the wicked; nor will he prolong his days, which are as a shadow, because he does not fear before God. Psalm 73:17: Until I went into the sanctuary of God; Then I understood their end.
Why does God correct his people?
He says God corrects his people because he loves them, just as parents correct children and a husband and wife correct each other. He says love is the reason for correction.
Why does God correct his people?

Okay, and so correction is important, and we dealt with correction of sin last week. And here in Revelations 3:19 it tells us why God corrects us, what kind of attitude he has. As many as I love, Jesus said, I rebuke and chasten, I, I correct. Be zealous therefore and repent. As many as I love. Why does he correct his people? Because he loves them. Why does a parent correct their children? Because they love them. If you don’t correct them, you’re what? Not loving them. Why does a husband and wife correct each other? Because they love each other, and they want the marriage to be solid and strong and the family to be strong. So love is the reason for correction. You see, do we get this?
Why does God correct his people?
Revelation 3:19: As many as I love, I rebuke and chasten. Therefore be zealous and repent.
What is the difference between God rebuking and chastening us?

He says rebuke is verbal, telling a fault to convince, and God comes verbally first. Chasten means to train up and educate by discipline or punishment. He says God’s Word can correct us so that we do not need to be punished.
What is the difference between God rebuking and chastening us?

Now, rebuke. He says, I rebuke. Rebuke is to tell a fault, to convince. So the first source of his correction is to verbally come and say you’re messing up. He’s going to verb... that’s what parents do. Son, you can’t do that. You cannot stick your finger in an electric socket. It’s going to straighten your hair. It’s going to knock you 15 feet. It’s verbal. Son, you cannot go out and play in the street. The cars are going to smash you. You know, it’s verbal. And so God comes, comes verbally first. How many are glad of that? Yeah. How many would like a hearing ear to hear God verbally? Yeah, yeah. And then he says, I will chasten, I will correct you. The word chasten is to train up, educate by discipline or punishment. Let me say it again. Chasten here is different than rebuke. Rebuke is verbal. Chasten is to train up and educate by discipline, by punishment. Say I do something that makes your life uncomfortable, and then you will straighten up. So in this verse we see there are two ways God corrects his people, besides, as we taught last week, our sin corrects us and our backslidings correct, correct us. Here God gets involved and corrects us verbally. He tells us we’re wrong, and this is why we need to assemble in Bible studies and, and church. Uh, we need to forget about the miracles and the flattering prophecies and the tongues and interpretation, and we need to go for the Word, because his Word will correct us. And I would rather be corrected by the Word of God than having him to come and punish me in some way, amen, because when God punish me, it also has a tendency to affect other members of my family or those around me. So it’d be better just to listen to the Word.
What is the difference between God rebuking and chastening us?
Revelation 3:19: As many as I love, I rebuke and chasten. Therefore be zealous and repent.
How can God correct us when we ignore his Word?

He says God can remove his presence and correct by things like disease, war, famine, floods, earthquakes and fire. He gives depression as an example, saying King Saul had a depressed, angry spirit come upon him because of his sins and God was correcting him.
How can God correct us when we ignore his Word?

Physical punishment. The Bible says he gives you what you want, but he’ll send leanness to your soul. He can remove his presence, like King David said, not, don’t take your presence from me. If you haven’t touched his presence in a while, it could be, and it obviously is, God is saying you need to correct something in your life. He can correct by disease, war, famine, acts of God, acts of God, or floods, earthquakes, fire, hell from heaven and all that stuff. Depression. King Saul was a, had a depressed, angry spirit come upon him because, because of his sins, and God was correcting him. And I know Christians that are depressed all the time. They never know how to smile. They’re grumpy, they’re grouchy, and they’re angry and they’re violent. King Saul tried to kill his own son because his son disagreed with him, the anger, the lashing out. You can’t stand yourself. Saul couldn’t stand it, and he would, would bring in a musician to bring peace to himself, and people around him couldn’t stand it. And so God uses these things to correct us. Are you out there? We just need to what? Recognize it, get the problem solved and move on.
Who does God use to correct us?

He says God will not use an audible voice from heaven but will use people: the parent, a friend, the church, the Bible and civil authorities. He says God gave parents the responsibility to train up a child, and quotes Colossians 3:20 about obeying parents in the Lord.
Who does God use to correct us?

Now, how does God carry these things out? Well, he’s going to speak to you through the parent, through a friend, through a church. The Bible is not going to be an audible voice from heaven: David, stop it. He’s going to come and he’s going to use people. So we have the parent, the friend, the church, the Bible, and civil authorities that are verbally going to correct us. Now, if you’re a child this morning and listening to this lesson, God gave parents the responsibility to train up the child in the nurture and the admonition of the Lord, including punishment. Even a grown-up child may need verbal correction or advice from a parent. The sad thing is that some parents never let their kids grow up. They’re 30 years old and the parents are still telling them what to do, and uh, God help you if you got one of those parents. The Bible says in Colossians 3:20, to obey your parents in the Lord.
Who does God use to correct us?
Colossians 3:20: Children, obey your parents in all things, for this is well pleasing to the Lord.
What if my parent is not a good parent?
He says that not every parent is a good example, and gives 2 Chronicles 22:3 where a mother was her son’s counselor to do wickedly. He says the child is then at the mercy of that parent until grown.
What if my parent is not a good parent?

In 2 Chronicles 22:3, what if the parent is not a good parent? You see, it’s great that parents are given the responsibility to train up and be an example to the children. It’s great. Man, I wish it was that easy, but what if the parent isn’t a good example? What if the parent aren’t good parents? And in 2 Chronicles 22:3 it says, his mother was his counselor to do wickedly. See, his own parent gave him bad advice and was a bad example. You see, the child in this case is at the mercy of the [unclear] till they grow up and can think [unclear].
What if my parent is not a good parent?
2 Chronicles 22:3: He also walked in the ways of the house of Ahab, for his mother advised him to do wickedly.
How does the Lord take up children whose parents forsake them?

He says the Lord takes them up through the church: the church gets the message out to children, brings them in, and teaches them what is right and wrong. He tells of a time he dealt with two sisters, where the one who took her children to church had children who knew what was wrong.
How does the Lord take up children whose parents forsake them?

But the Bible says in Psalms 27:10, when my parents forsake me, when they turn their back on me, the Lord will take me up. Now, how does the Lord take them up? The parent, the church. See, the church has got to wake up to what it really is. You know, we are here to get the message out that there’s a better way to live, and we’re here to get the message out to children that there’s a better way to live. And so when the children hear, they come to church, you go out and you bring them in, and they come to church and they hear what is right and wrong, and then they go home and they know something’s wrong here. There was a, some years back I dealt with two sisters. They married two brothers, and both brothers were bad brothers. They were drinkers and horrible sexual permissiveness and everything else. But one of the sisters went to church and took the children to church, so when this father approached the 16-year-old daughter of his in the kitchen and grabbed her, and she knew that that was wrong and fought off, that. But the other sister, who didn’t go to church, and of course neither of the men went to church, they didn’t know what was right and wrong, and they just thought, you know, well, this is this is life, and they gave in and had a child by the father and didn’t learn the years later that that’s wrong. You see, the church is important. Church, you are important to get the word out what is right and what is wrong, to save children from bad homes and to give parents in bad homes an opportunity to change their life. Amen. Are you with me? And if we, and, and it’s the Word that’s going to do that. We got to get the Word out. You got to be able to, you guys have got to learn, you are a witness of God’s Word. You can share the Word with people, and we’ve got to go out to the highways and the hedges and compel them to come in. They’re not going to come knocking on the door.
How does the Lord take up children whose parents forsake them?

Psalm 27:10: When my father and my mother forsake me, Then the LORD will take care of me. Luke 14:23: Then the master said to the servant, ‘Go out into the highways and hedges, and compel them to come in, that my house may be filled.
Why must Christians go out and find people instead of waiting for them to come?

He says people are not going to come knocking on your door, so we must go find them where they are and invite them to hear the Word of God. He says that Word will change their life if they want change and receive it.
Why must Christians go out and find people instead of waiting for them to come?

They’re not going to come knocking on your house and go, hey, hey, hey, uh, can you tell me how to find Jesus or improve my life or whatever? No, you got to go knock on their door. You got to go find them where they’re at. You got to invite them to hear the Word of God and touch God, and that Word then will change their life if they want change and receive it. It’s amazing how we help the homeless, how we help the addicts, the dropouts, and defend the rights of adults in America to live as they please, but won’t stand up for the rights of innocent children that these same adults are hurting, abusing, sexing, neglecting and raising up wrongly. And the church has lost its fight in America.
What does he say about runaway youth in America?

He says the church used to speak out on righteousness and sin but now offers psychology and feel-good messages. He cites figures on teenage runaways being abused and says 1.6 million young people 18 and under run away every year in America.
What does he say about runaway youth in America?

In the ‘90s the church spoke out openly for righteousness and justice, but after the ‘90s you don’t hear the church speaking out on righteousness and sin. You hear psychology and feel-good messages, and God, you know, want you, you self-esteem, God wants you to have self-esteem. Well, my, you know, come on, church, we need the teaching of God’s Word, amen, in right and wrong. The United States Department of Health and Human Services said 46% of teenage runaways 18 and under are physically abused, [unclear]% were sexually abused, that’s why they ran away, 38% was emotionally abused: you’re no good, you’re worth, you’ll never amount to anything, uh, no interaction, the kid just left alone. 60%, 66% of runaways had an alcohol parent, two-thirds of runaways were running from alcohol and the abuse and the problems that come with it. 25% are running from those parents who abuse drugs. That’s 91% of runaways in America, or throwaways, are drug and alcohol related. Are you there? And the church wants to argue about whether Jesus drank or didn’t drink. Folks, there’s something wrong in America. Now listen. You say, well, so what? Well, there’s 1.6 million 18 and under running away every year in America.
Where is the church when young people are on the streets?

He asks whether the church cares or only wants to enjoy the presence of God, and says no one is addressing the problem. He says these young people are exposed to sex trafficking and survival sex, and says the church is silent.
Where is the church when young people are on the streets?

In 10 years that’s 16 million. Obama never addresses it, the Democrats never address it, the Republicans aren’t addressing it, no one is addressing it, and the church is silent. And yet we worry about the war in Iraq, and we worry about the border, and we worry about all a lot of these things, abortion and so forth, and yet 1.6 million of our young people are out on the streets every year. Does the church care, or do we just want to come in and enjoy the presence of God and hear an inspirational message and hear about us sending mission money to the mission field and feeding the [unclear] down here and the [unclear] that drops out and [unclear] and everything we are? Where is the church in this thing? These kids are exposed to sex trafficking. They’re actually being sold for sex, sex for survival. They have sex just so somebody will give them a roof to be under and some food. And we’re talking about kids from 10, 11 up to 18 years old. One mother sold her own child for sex in South Carolina. All this sexual promotion in America, and if it feels good, do it. The mentality is, you know, sex is the thing, and sex is okay, and we, and we sell our kids. There’s some wrong when a mother who has a God-given protection button in her, you touch that kid, man, you just caught a tail of a wild cat, and that is changed and neutralized to where have my daughter, have my son, give me a hundred bucks. Are you there? And what is the church saying? We’re saying nothing. Either they get HIV and they get viral diseases and they go into prostitution, and it’s just embarrassing. It’s shameful what is happening to 1.6 million youth every year. And some of these kids are thrown out by their parent. They don’t want them anymore, they’re just in the way, and other ones are running away.
What does he say is the source of America’s problems?

He says the source of America’s problems right now is the home, and that no one is addressing it. He says the church is here to be a source to straighten out troubled homes and to comfort and encourage neglected children and youth.
What does he say is the source of America’s problems?

Matthew 10:36, Jesus said, a man’s enemies will be those of his own household, and that is exactly what’s happening in America. The source of America’s problems right now is the home, and no one is addressing it, and the church, in my research, including this one, has not stood up publicly and declared that this is wrong. What politician running for office hammers about these issues? None. See, they want the right for women to have abortion, they’ll hammer, you know, environmental issues, they hammer all kinds of things, and no one is going to the rescue of these innocent kids being thrown out or running away from abusive homes. The church is there. We are here. We’re not just people here to come in and sing songs and enjoy the blessings of God, but we’re here to be a source to straighten out troubled homes and comfort and encourage [unclear] neglected children, neglected youth, and we should be going out of our way to do that. We should have time to do that. Can I hear an amen?
What does he say is the source of America’s problems?
Matthew 10:36: and ‘a man’s enemies will be those of his own household.’
How can a church work together as a team?

Using a football team as his picture, he says every player must know the role, the part and the goal, and that the church must agree to work as a team to get the Word of God out to homes and children. He says it is nothing for God to save by many or by few.
How can a church work together as a team?

You see, to do that we got to become a team. They’ve been talking about teams on Friday, you got to join the team. We’re having Super Bowl today, and every player has to play as this team player. They got to know their role, they got to know their part, they got to know the goal. The goal is to get that football in the end zone, and whatever it takes to get it there, we got to work as a team to do it. We got to protect our quarterback, we got to block for our runner. Are you there? The quarterback can’t go out there and hack the ball to himself and then throw it to himself. And church, look at you. You can decide today to be a team, because the Bible says it’s nothing for God to say by many or by few. But the key is we got to agree to work as a team and set a goal to get the Word of God out to these homes and get these, the Word out to these children and bring them in. That bus should be full of kids, because in no area have I been that there is such a high percentage of troubled homes in [unclear]. And I’ve ministered in a lot of areas in California. There’s a lot of troubled homes out there, messed up homes, parents who don’t know what they’re doing, they’re just self-centered, selfish, and accidentally had kids.
How can a church work together as a team?

1 Samuel 14:6: Then Jonathan said to the young man who bore his armor, “Come, let us go over to the garrison of these uncircumcised; it may be that the LORD will work for us. For nothing restrains the LORD from saving by many or by few.”
How can a friend correct us, and what about bad friends?
He says a good friend will correct you when you are wrong, and a Bible friend will verbally correct you. A worldly friend who seduces you into things against God’s word will lead you astray.
How can a friend correct us, and what about bad friends?

Now then, we got the friend, a friend, a close acquaintance, they can correct us. A man sharpens the countenance of his friend, Proverbs 27:17. See, as iron sharpens iron, we sharpen the countenance, the conscience, see, the person of our friend, and a good friend will do that. A good friend will correct you when you’re wrong. But what if that friend is not a good friend? Psalms 41:9, my own familiar friend in whom I trust, who ate my bread with me, has lifted up his heel against me. And a lot of your acquaintances are trying to lure you and seduce you into doing things that are against God’s word. We don’t have to go to church, it’s okay to drink and [unclear], they are seducing it. These kind of friends aren’t Bible friends. A Bible friend will verbally correct you. A worldly friend will lead you astray.
How can a friend correct us, and what about bad friends?
Proverbs 27:17: As iron sharpens iron, So a man sharpens the countenance of his friend. Psalm 41:9: Even my own familiar friend in whom I trusted, Who ate my bread, Has lifted up his heel against me.
What does Jeremiah 5 say God will not do?
In the passage he reads, God says that even in those days of judgment, “I will not destroy you completely.” He says that is because God’s ultimate plan is to restore.
What is the goal of God’s correction?
He says God’s ultimate plan is to restore, and that God corrects so that we can go on, just as a parent corrects the problem rather than throwing the child out.
Should we measure ourselves by unbelievers?

He says no: do not measure yourself by unbelievers, but realize the fear of the Lord is to depart from evil. He says if we live a life of righteousness and repent when we do wrong, God will do good to us.
Why do a husband and wife correct each other?
He says a husband and wife correct each other because they love each other and want the marriage and the family to be strong.
What two ways of correction does he find in Revelation 3:19?
He says that in this verse there are two ways God corrects his people: rebuke, which is verbal, and chastening, which is to train up and educate by discipline or punishment.
Why would he rather be corrected by God’s Word than by punishment?
He says he would rather be corrected by the Word of God than have God punish him, because when God punishes, it also has a tendency to affect other members of his family or those around him.
What does he say we need instead of miracles, flattering prophecies and tongues?
He says we need to forget about the miracles and the flattering prophecies and the tongues and interpretation and go for the Word, because his Word will correct us.
What does he say about depression and correction?

He says King Saul had a depressed, angry spirit come upon him because of his sins and God was correcting him. He says he knows Christians who are depressed all the time and recommends that we recognize the problem, get it solved and move on.
Does God speak to us with an audible voice from heaven?
He says it is not going to be an audible voice from heaven. He says God will come and use people to correct us verbally.
What does he say about parents and grown children?
He says even a grown-up child may need verbal correction or advice from a parent, but that some parents never let their kids grow up.
What does he say about the church speaking out in America?

He says that in the ’90s the church spoke out openly for righteousness and justice but after that you hear psychology and feel-good messages. He says the church needs the teaching of God’s Word in right and wrong.
What does he say the church is here for?

He says we are not just people here to come in and sing songs and enjoy the blessings of God, but are here to be a source to straighten out troubled homes and comfort and encourage neglected children and youth.
What makes a friend a Bible friend?
He says a Bible friend will verbally correct you, while a worldly friend will lead you astray.

items.d: In “God’s Correction Tactics Part 2,” Pastor David G. Kincer says God’s correction comes by his Word and, when it is ignored, by punishment, and that the goal is the peaceable fruit of righteousness (Hebrews…
p: In “God’s Correction Tactics Part 2,” Pastor David G. Kincer says God’s correction comes by his Word and, when it is ignored, by punishment, and that the goal is the peaceable fruit of righteousness (Hebrews 12). He uses Ezekiel 14, Isaiah 29:6 and 1 Corinthians 11:30, and Ezra’s request to God as a pattern for accepting correction and asking God to keep his promises. He closes with Proverbs 13:24 and 19:18 on prompt discipline.
Why is it important to find a good moral church?

He says preachers and churches are not always good, and that a church which stands for morality is the church that will have an effect for good on homes, the community and the world. He says a church that flatters you and lets you live the way you want is not a good church.
Why is it important to find a good moral church?

And then you got the church. But we know from the newspapers and the Bible that preachers and churches aren’t always good. Churches have been caught molesting children, taking the money, preaching bad doctrines, both in the Bible and in our everyday newspapers. So, finding a good moral church is important, isn’t it? A church that stands for morality. You may not like to hear the preaching, but let me tell you, that’s the church that is going to have an effect for good on the homes and the community and in the world. Could that be true?
Why can we always trust the Bible when we cannot always trust people?

He says you cannot always trust a friend, a spouse, church leaders or a parent, but you can always trust the Bible because it does not change. He says the Bible will keep you sound, keep correcting you and keep making you wiser, and that it is the foundation of correction.
Why can we always trust the Bible when we cannot always trust people?

Amen. A church that flatters you and lets you live the way you want is not a good church. And so when the ministers goes a muck, what does a person do? Well, then they go to the Bible. You can’t... the Bible stands strong. It’s our standard. And if you don’t twist it and turn it to your own convenience, that word will always keep you sound. Hallelujah. It will always be correcting you. It will always keep making you wiser. And do you realize that only 15%, 15% of Christians read their word? And that is the foundation of correction. You can’t always trust your friend. You can’t always trust your spouse. You can’t always trust the church leaders. You can’t always trust a parent. But you can always trust the Bible. Hallelujah. It doesn’t change. And it is sad when we do not read that seriously and objectively every day. How many of you read your Bible through last year? You see what I mean? And we’re in a church that pushes reading the word all the time, and we can’t find time to read the word. And we can find time to watch TV, go to movies, and do all kinds of things, but we can’t find time to read the book that is a sound source for us to be corrected by God.
What saves a person when God sends judgment?

Reading Ezekiel 14, he says Noah, Daniel and Job would only save themselves by their righteousness, not by faith, grace, miracles, worship, prayer, the ark or prosperity. He says you can have miracles and not be righteous.
What saves a person when God sends judgment?

Hallelujah. How do you know preachers are preaching the right thing if you don’t get to the book and find out? And that’s what the Bible said. The acts of God were also used to correct, and punishment. Correction by punishment in Ezekiel 14:21 sums it up. When I send my painful judgments upon Jerusalem, war, famine, beast, and epidemic diseases, if Noah, Daniel, and Job were there, they would only save themselves by their what? You notice the word faith is not there. You will notice the word grace is not there. Hello, are you out there? Do you notice the word miracles are not there? We got miracles in our church. You can have miracles and not be righteous. Hallelujah. Worship is not there. Some people, that’s all they want to do is just focus in on worship. That’s just one aspect. The word prayer is not there. Are you getting the message? Daniel was a prayer. Daniel had miracles. Daniel had visions. But it wasn’t his prayers, his visions, and his miracles that would save him. What was it? What was it? His righteousness. Noah built a boat. My goodness, what a feat he did. He had a huge building. Miraculous. Oh man, how awesome. But it wasn’t the ark that saved him. Are you there, church? It wasn’t his faith that saved him. It was his righteousness. Hallelujah. Job was wealthy, prosperous. So was Daniel. But it wasn’t their prosperity that saved him. It was their righteousness. Do you get it? Correction by punishment. God can bring a war. And I don’t care how great we are right now in, in the world, in our arms.
What saves a person when God sends judgment?

Ezekiel 14:14-21: Even if these three men, Noah, Daniel, and Job, were in it, they would deliver only themselves by their righteousness,” says the Lord GOD. “If I cause wild beasts to pass through the land, and they empty it, and make it so desolate that no man may pass through because of the beasts, even though these three men were in it, as I live,” says the Lord GOD, “they would deliver neither sons nor daughters; only they would be delivered, and the land would be desolate. “Or if I bring a sword on that land, and say, ‘Sword, go through the land,’ and I cut off man and beast from it, even though these three men were in it, as I live,” says the Lord GOD, “they would deliver neither sons nor daughters, but only they themselves would be delivered. “Or if I send a pestilence into that land and pour out My fury on it in blood, and cut off from it man and beast, even though Noah, Daniel, and Job were in it, as I live,” says the Lord GOD, “they would deliver neither son nor daughter; they would deliver only themselves by their righteousness.” For thus says the Lord GOD: “How much more it shall be when I send My four severe judgments on Jerusalem—the sword and famine and wild beasts and pestilence—to cut off man and beast from it?
Does God use war and disease to correct a nation?

He says God can bring a war, and that if God decides this nation is going down, it will go down. He says “this HIV thing is obviously a visitation from God” and that new sexually transmitted diseases are God saying the sexual revolution is not the way to go.
Does God use war and disease to correct a nation?

If God decides this nation’s going down, folks, we’re going down. See, the Bible says, “Some trust in chariots, some in horses, armaments, but we will remember the name of the Lord our God.” Now, we got to have arms, but let me tell you, we got to have God. And this HIV thing is obviously a visitation from God. We didn’t have it before, before. It came from a source of sin. It’s obvious God is trying to adjust. All these new sexually transmitted diseases that we never heard of before, 30-some new ones, are God saying sexual revolution is not the way to go.
Does God use war and disease to correct a nation?
Psalm 20:7: Some trust in chariots, and some in horses; But we will remember the name of the LORD our God.
What are the acts of God that correct people?

He says acts of God are flood, fire from heaven and hell, and reads Isaiah 29:6, where the Lord of hosts visits with thunder, earthquake, a great noise, storm, tempest and devouring fire. He says the reason is to get you to correct yourself.
What are the acts of God that correct people?

And America just keeps pumping medicine into them and hanging on to these ideas and not recognizing, even mocking when somebody, and I heard ministers get on TV at these news, uh, talk shows and say that’s God’s judgment, and they were laughed at and mocked at. And one was a woman pastor that did an excellent job, and they just ridiculed her. And that was on Fox News. Did one of the best jobs I ever heard. Acts of God are flood, fire from heaven, and hell. In Isaiah 29:6 it says, “You shall be visited of the Lord of hosts with thunder and earthquake and a great noise, and a storm and a temp, tempest, and a flame of devouring fire.” Why?
What are the acts of God that correct people?
Isaiah 29:6: You will be punished by the LORD of hosts With thunder and earthquake and great noise, With storm and tempest And the flame of devouring fire.
Does 1 Corinthians 11:30 say believers are sick because of God’s correction?

He reads that many are weak and sick among you, and many asleep, and says God is talking to the church. He says some believers are weak, sick or dead before their time because they did not discern the Lord’s body, and that God corrects by punishment.
Does 1 Corinthians 11:30 say believers are sick because of God’s correction?

To get you to correct yourself. Colossian, 1 Corinthians 11:30, for this reason, many are weak and sick among you, and many asleep. He’s talking to the church. Some of you believers are weak, weak in your mind, weak in your emotion, weak in your spirit. Some of you are sick and some of you are dead before your time because you did not discern the Lord’s body. You are the body of Christ. His body died for our sins. We are the body of Christ. And so God corrects by punishment. What’s the goal of correction? Hebrews 12:9, our fathers of our flesh corrected us and we gave them respect.
Does 1 Corinthians 11:30 say believers are sick because of God’s correction?
1 Corinthians 11:30: For this reason many are weak and sick among you, and many sleep.
What is the goal of God’s correction according to Hebrews 12?

items.d: God’s goal is that we know and love Him, and that His church be established high in His ways. Saul half-obeyed and rejected correction; David and the sinful woman repented and were forgiven; Judas loved money.…
p: God’s goal is that we know and love Him, and that His church be established high in His ways. Saul half-obeyed and rejected correction; David and the sinful woman repented and were forgiven; Judas loved money. Love God first and accept His correction.

items.t: God’s Identity for His People - June 11, 2023
items.d: We are made in God’s image, male and female, and the family illustrates Christ’s relationship with His church. Anyone can be a fellow heir; our identity is shown in faithfulness, knowing God, letting our light…
p: We are made in God’s image, male and female, and the family illustrates Christ’s relationship with His church. Anyone can be a fellow heir; our identity is shown in faithfulness, knowing God, letting our light shine and being called out of darkness into His marvelous light.

items.d: In Part IV of “God’s Magnifical House,” Pastor David G. Kincer says the church must be built by the Bible pattern so the fame and glory of Jesus fill the nations, and that every believer is invited to be a…
p: In Part IV of “God’s Magnifical House,” Pastor David G. Kincer says the church must be built by the Bible pattern so the fame and glory of Jesus fill the nations, and that every believer is invited to be a priest. He gives four responsibilities of a priest from Deuteronomy 10:8, Numbers 16:9 and Hebrews 9, and says that through the blood of Jesus every believer can enter the holy of holies, minister to the Lord, hear his voice and have the Scriptures opened.
What does “the Lord’s house shall be exceedingly magnifical” mean?

He reads 1 Chronicles 22:5 that the Lord’s house would be magnifical, of fame and of glory throughout all countries, at a time when people did not know about other continents but God did. He says the fame was fulfilled in Luke 5:15, when great multitudes came to hear Jesus and be healed.
What does “the Lord’s house shall be exceedingly magnifical” mean?

We’re going to be talking about the magnifical church this morning and just a brief review. First Chronicles 22:5. The Lord’s house shall be exceedingly magnifical. Of fame. And of glory throughout all countries all nations. Now you’ve got to remember at this time they didn’t know there was nations in South America South Africa North America. They didn’t know that as human beings God did and God had a big plan way back there. The fame was fulfilled we saw in Luke chapter 5 verse 15 so much the more went there a fame abroad of Jesus great multitudes came together to hear him and to be healed of their infirmities they came to hear his word not just for a miracle not everybody needs a healing but they need to hear the word and so we see it fulfilled then we must remember.
What does “the Lord’s house shall be exceedingly magnifical” mean?

1 Chronicles 22:5: Now David said, “Solomon my son is young and inexperienced, and the house to be built for the LORD must be exceedingly magnificent, famous and glorious throughout all countries. I will now make preparation for it.” So David made abundant preparations before his death. Luke 5:15: However, the report went around concerning Him all the more; and great multitudes came together to hear, and to be healed by Him of their infirmities.

He says David gave Solomon the pattern by the Spirit, and “we cannot build the church our own way we’ve got to follow the Bible pattern.” He says the apostles turned their known world upside down, and Haggai 2:9 says the glory of the latter house shall be greater than the former.

And First Chronicles 28:11 David gave to Solomon the pattern of all he had by the spirit we cannot build the church our own way we’ve got to follow the Bible pattern and if we follow the Bible pattern then the fame will go to all nations Acts 17:6 these that have turned the world upside down are come here. Speaking of the apostles. Who went out preaching to the known world at that time the known world these like I said they didn’t know there was islands in the sea they didn’t know north and South America were around and they didn’t know anything about South Africa the southern part of africa and so they turned their known world upside down just like God said the glory and the fame would go to all countries now Haggai 2:9 says the glory of this latter house this last day house shall be greater than the former now if God through Jesus and the apostles could turn that world that known world upside down manifest his glory manifest his fame.

1 Chronicles 28:11: Then David gave his son Solomon the plans for the vestibule, its houses, its treasuries, its upper chambers, its inner chambers, and the place of the mercy seat; Acts 17:6: But when they did not find them, they dragged Jason and some brethren to the rulers of the city, crying out, “These who have turned the world upside down have come here too. It’s also about the people that come in they need to be showed where the bathrooms are see they need to be told what to expect when they get to that altar and how that lamb is to be sacrificed they have to be instructed they have to be in order they have to be take a number who’s next yeah. Only one lamb could be sacrificed at a time on that altar are you there. And so you know they had to take care of the people when they come sick babies what are they going to do just say well you know it’s your problem no they had to have a first aid station had to take care of sick people sick babies whatever.
Do priests also take care of God’s house and the people who come?

Numbers 16:9: Is it a small thing to you that the God of Israel has separated you from the congregation of Israel, to bring you near to Himself, to do the work of the tabernacle of the LORD, and to stand before the congregation to serve them;
Can every believer enter the holy of holies?

He says only the high priest went into the holy of holies once a year, but Jesus is our high priest, entered once by his own blood, and the veil was torn from top to bottom. He says from Hebrews 10:19 that now we all can go in by the blood of Jesus, hear him speaking to us, have the Scriptures opened and see the change in our lives.
Can every believer enter the holy of holies?

And some of these people that come to God’s house are tough to deal with they are tough. But God invites them all in so what are you going to do is the priest. The fourth one Hebrews 9:7. Unto the second part of the temple went the high priest alone. Once every year. Not without blood which he offered for himself his own sins and for the sins of the people the mistakes of the people one time a year and I have the diagram of Solomon’s temple Moses’s tabernacle Herod’s temple they’re all the same you have the holy place and I don’t have anything there because I don’t want you focusing in on the holy place it’s a holy of holies once a year the priest you see these fancy clothes he wears. Those clothes every one of them has a meaning speaks of a truth speaks of a doctrine he would come in once a year. And there was the. Ark of the covenant with the mercy seat on top and the cloud of his presence visible presence of God at night a cloud turned to a fire. Visible. Audible. Presence of God in that holy place but only the high priest could go in not the other priests and he could only go in once a year. Now beside that ark of the covenant. Is a scroll with the scriptures God told Moses to put the scroll the scriptures beside the ark of the covenant and let me tell you folks there is nothing more illuminating. In the scriptures than reading it in the presence of God. That’s when you get illuminated Jesus Christ of course is our high priest for our sin Hebrews 9:11 Christ the high priest of good things to come by a greater and more perfect tabernacle. Not made with hands God is not interested in natural buildings he’s interested in living people. By his own blood he entered one time into the holy place. Having obtained. Eternal redemption for us he didn’t have to keep offering himself every year one time he gave us eternal redemption. Wow wow that is so powerful okay. Now. When Jesus died you see this little lightning bolt here. He rent the veil separating the holy place from the holy of holies he rented in two from top to bottom so that people knew it wasn’t a man or human that did it because this curtain was way up there they couldn’t reach it but when Jesus died God rent the curtain in two from top to bottom signifying that now not just the high priest can go in we all can go in. Now this is a powerful understanding. If you can catch it. Hebrews 10:19 having therefore for this reason brethren boldness to enter into the holiest by the blood of Jesus by a new and living way so I can come in. To the presence of God hear his voice and see the result not just the cloud but I can see the fruit in my life I can see the fruit in your life you see. The visible results of the presence of God you see the change in the attitude you see the change in the talk how many you know we need that more than we need walking on water. And see this isn’t just for J.B. Fireball that’s the name I use for the mighty man of God full of faith and power the hour and everybody’s following him and whatever he says they do no. You can go in to Jesus Christ yourself in the holy of holies and hear him talking to you and have the scriptures. Open to you. Yeah give God a clap offering that’s powerful. But we have been so brainwashed that we look for some superwoman or some superman to lead us and guide us and hand walk us and feed us and give us a bottle and you know psychoanalyze our emotional levels and whatever when we have been invited in as priests to come into Jesus by the blood of Jesus and by his blood alone. And there he will speak to us and he will change us and we will see the change.
Can every believer enter the holy of holies?

Hebrews 9:7: But into the second part the high priest went alone once a year, not without blood, which he offered for himself and for the people’s sins committed in ignorance; Hebrews 9:11-12: But Christ came as High Priest of the good things to come, with the greater and more perfect tabernacle not made with hands, that is, not of this creation. Not with the blood of goats and calves, but with His own blood He entered the Most Holy Place once for all, having obtained eternal redemption. Hebrews 10:19: Therefore, brethren, having boldness to enter the Holiest by the blood of Jesus,
Can a priest or minister forgive sins?

He says we do not go into the holy of holies to redeem sin, because nobody can forgive sin but Jesus Christ, no matter what mighty man of God you follow. He says we go in to minister directly to him, hear his voice and have the Scriptures opened in his presence.
Can a priest or minister forgive sins?

Hallelujah very powerful. So ministering into him really becomes important lifting your hands singing praying kneeling doing these things is what he asked us to do to come into his presence that’s the protocol see it’s humbling. Now we don’t go into the holy of holies to redeem sin. Nobody can forgive sin but who Jesus Christ I don’t care what kind of mighty man of God you’re following he can do nothing for you let me tell you only Jesus can do anything. And he does them through ministries and he does them through the goofiest ministries because he loves people but it’s Jesus that does this stuff we can go into the holy of holies not to forgive sins the Catholics are all wrong that priest cannot absolve you from sin only Jesus can. Yeah I have to call it like it is I love the Catholics I love the people but let me tell you you can’t violate God’s word you’ve got to build it by the pattern you got to go to Jesus he is the only one on that has authority to forgive sin on earth that’s what the Bible says. I mean we can forgive other people’s offenses toward us but he can wash the sin away deliver you from that sin set you free and give you life. Not to redeem sins but to minister directly unto him hear his voice and have the scriptures open to us in his presence remember. The scroll of the scriptures was right beside the ark and the Bible says spiritual things are revealed by the spirit if you really want to get the word opened up to you come into his presence. Open that book and he will open your understanding he’ll speak to you in a still small voice.
Did the apostles fulfill the fame of God’s house?
He says the apostles turned their known world upside down, but they did not know about North and South America or the southern part of Africa, so the glory has not yet filled every nation.
Has the whole earth been filled with the glory of the Lord yet?
He says if you know your history it has not happened; it happened in the book of Acts to the known world, but we have not seen it fill every nation, so we have something powerful to look forward to.
Is the church in America holy and without blemish?
He says no, because public opinion and public policy say everything is okay and much of the church, not all of it, just goes along with it.
Why did Israel say they would die if God spoke to them?

He says Amos shows they carried idols for forty years in the wilderness, so they knew that if they went up God would expose them; they wanted the land of promise but not a personal encounter with God.
What does the word “bless” mean when priests bless the Lord?
He says it has a threefold meaning: to kneel, to praise or brag about God, and to adore him.
What does he say separates Christians from other religions?
He says we do things because Jesus said to do them and we do them in his name; we follow Jesus, not other religious founders.
Why does he say to praise God now while you are alive?
He says it is no good to wait till you’re dead, because the Bible says the dead praise not the Lord.
Does God say the same thing to every church?
He says what God is saying in one church would be entirely different from another because the people and their level are different, so we should not try one method for everybody.
How does he say ministers should be sent out?
He says it would be nice if ministers were sent out by the Holy Ghost instead of by seminars and Bible colleges, and not just to make it an occupation.
Do women have a place in the kingdom?
He says the women brought Jesus food and drink, washed his clothes and ministered to him of their substance, so he questions people who say women don’t have a place in the kingdom.
Is giving part of ministering to the Lord?
He says giving to Jesus and to the church to get the word out and help people grow is part of ministering to the Lord, and that mentality changes the attitude you give with.
What happened when the veil of the temple was torn?
He says when Jesus died God tore the curtain from top to bottom, too high for a man to reach, signifying that now not just the high priest but all of us can go in.
Where does he say the Scriptures are opened to us?

He says the scroll of the Scriptures was beside the ark, and if you really want the word opened to you, come into his presence, open the book and he will open your understanding in a still small voice.

items.d: In Part III of “God’s Magnifical House,” the speaker takes 1 Chronicles 22:5 and says the church must be built by God’s pattern. He says the glory came into the temple when the people praised God, that God’s…
p: In Part III of “God’s Magnifical House,” the speaker takes 1 Chronicles 22:5 and says the church must be built by God’s pattern. He says the glory came into the temple when the people praised God, that God’s house is now people as living stones, and that music, thanksgiving and participation are sacrifices to him. He closes with the power of the gospel over human intellect and the claim that miracles are for the church today.
What does 1 Chronicles 22:5 say the Lord’s house will be?

He reads that “the lord’s house shall be exceedingly” magnifical, “of fame and glory throughout all countries,” and recalls that earlier parts covered the fame of Jesus and the apostles. He says “miracles should be a normal part of the magnifical church,” pointing to Noah, the fiery furnace and Daniel.
What does 1 Chronicles 22:5 say the Lord’s house will be?

Follow in the Bible we’re going to 1 Chronicles 22:5. Now remember we talked about the fame and the honor of Jesus fulfilling this prophecy. We talked about the fame and the honor of the twelve apostles and the early church fulfilling this prophecy. It says the lord’s house shall be exceedingly magnifical. Of fame and glory throughout all countries throughout all countries not just the Jewish nation but every nation and I will therefore now make preparation for it we saw how miracles should be a normal part of the magnifical church. See God created everything out of nothing Enoch didn’t die miracles have been going on ever since God began creation Noah and seven others were saved from the flood with the animals the [unclear] swam in the Bible the fiery furnace didn’t burn the three Hebrew Hebrew children need the neither did the lions eat Daniel Jesus and his apostles did miracles and healings consistently.
What does 1 Chronicles 22:5 say the Lord’s house will be?

1 Chronicles 22:5: Now David said, “Solomon my son is young and inexperienced, and the house to be built for the LORD must be exceedingly magnificent, famous and glorious throughout all countries. I will now make preparation for it.” So David made abundant preparations before his death.
Why does he say the Bible can’t be reduced to the one word “faith”?

He says many Christians “have reduced the Bible to one word and that word is faith,” but “we can’t reduce the Bible down to one word of faith it’s just part of God’s word.” He says believing without repenting, confessing and being water baptized is “something for nothing,” which he calls “a welfare mentality” that “cripples the power of the Bible.”
Why does he say the Bible can’t be reduced to the one word “faith”?

We also found that it is built by foreigners aliens illegals or other words not so perfect individuals. [unclear] Being we’re not so perfect along with God’s chosen people. Now many Christians and denominations today. Have reduced the Bible to one word and that word is faith basically it is their faith but like the Muslims the Hindus the Confucius the Buddhas the animus and all the other religions. When we only have to believe and get all the rewards we’re getting something for nothing. When I don’t have to straighten my life out when I don’t have to repent when I don’t have to confess my sins and confess Jesus as God and Jesus is the savior and I don’t have to be water baptized.
Why must God’s house be built according to the pattern?

He says the temple “had to be built according to the pattern shown you on the mount,” and that David gave Solomon the pattern “by the spirit,” so “they couldn’t just do what they wanted to do.” He says “the magnifical house that God is building must be done his way.”
Why must God’s house be built according to the pattern?

What we’re saying is I’m getting something for nothing and that’s exactly what all the man-made religions offer something for nothing you just follow them and you’re in. We can’t reduce the Bible down to one word of faith it’s just part of God’s word. That’s a welfare mentality. When we want something for nothing and it cripples the power of the Bible. Now. This temple that God is talking about in first Chronicles had to be built according to the pattern shown you on the mount that’s Moses’s tabernacle and Solomon’s temple in 1 Chronicles 28:11 David gave to Solomon the pattern of all that he had by the spirit both Moses and tabernacle Solomon’s temple had to be built by the pattern that God gave they couldn’t just do what they wanted to do and we got to understand that.
Why must God’s house be built according to the pattern?

1 Chronicles 28:11-12: Then David gave his son Solomon the plans for the vestibule, its houses, its treasuries, its upper chambers, its inner chambers, and the place of the mercy seat; and the plans for all that he had by the Spirit, of the courts of the house of the LORD, of all the chambers all around, of the treasuries of the house of God, and of the treasuries for the dedicated things;
What does he say about the First Amendment and the Bible in early America?

He says the First Amendment bars Congress from setting up a religion or “prohibiting the free exercise thereof,” so “the church has a right to preach the gospel.” He says Congress “passed the law that the Bible would be printed,” sent Bibles to soldiers, and that “people are twisting the constitution to their own benefit.”
What does he say about the First Amendment and the Bible in early America?

The magnifical house that God is building must be done his way the Bible. Is twisted like our Constitution by people let’s look at the First Amendment of the Constitution all right Congress shall make no law respecting an establishment of religion they can’t set up a religion. They can’t respect one religion over another neither. Can they make a law prohibiting the free exercise thereof. Or a bridge in the freedom of speech so not only as we as united states citizen have the right to speak freely. But the church has a right to preach the gospel. Now people say that this nation was not built on christianity. But let me just remind you. That Congress. It was Congress. That passed the law that the Bible would be printed. And suggested that it be taught in schools. It was Congress that decided to pass out ten thousand bibles to the soldiers in the revolutionary war they didn’t pass out ten thousand hindu books. Or any other religious books it was the Bible it was Congress that passed a law at the same time that said we’ve got to have chaplains for every two regiment it’s got to be a chaplain those chaplains were Methodists Quakers Presbyterians Baptists. They were Muslim Buddhists. Are you there church. See we’ve got to understand people are twisting the Constitution. To their own benefit and America’s destruction just like they twist the Bible. And we have got to wake up to these things. It was Congress and and the Bible wasn’t taken out of public school and prayer wasn’t taken out of public school when I was a boy we prayed in public school and we were taught scriptures in public school and we sang songs Christian songs in public school down south in Kentucky in the Appalachian mountains. The Bible and prayer wasn’t taken out until 1962.
What does he say happened in 1962, and what does he say about “separation of church and state”?

He says “up to 1962 the Bible was an accepted book,” and that then “congress made a new religion” of secular humanism and atheism, and that “they prohibited the Bible.” He says “the church is protected from government,” and that “when you repeat a lie enough people start believing it,” as people also twist the Bible.
What does he say happened in 1962, and what does he say about “separation of church and state”?

So up to 1962. The Bible was an accepted book. And remember lawyers in the beginning of our nation up into Abraham Lincoln they had to know the Bible to become a lawyer I don’t know if you’re aware of that. And so these people that say that you know it wasn’t founded on the Bible it wasn’t founded on christianity they’re lying to you these people are lying to you. Now in 1962 Congress. Made a new religion they recognized and respected a new religion and that religion was the religion of secular humanism. And the religion of atheism the Supreme Court back then said that atheism was a religion. And the humanists say they have the new religion of secular humanism and our government which is not supposed to identify any religion they respected the atheists and the humanists and in doing so they prohibited the Bible. And those who followed the Bible. In America they threw out Jesus and the Bible do you understand that. They violated this Constitution but what did they do they twisted it they started in about 1948 twisting it and saying separation of church and state separation of church and state we got to be a government’s got to be protected from the church no it’s the opposite the church is protected from government. That’s the truth but see when you repeat a lie enough people start believing it and just like they twist the Constitution people are twisting the Bible around and we don’t have magnificent churches anymore as the prophecy said last week you go to one church and it’s different than the next church every church is different when we should be like the Toyota car when you buy it in China or you buy it in Africa or where you buy it in America it’s the same product.
What happened in 2 Chronicles 5:13 when the musicians praised God?

He says they had built the temple with the door, altar, laver, lampstand, table and ark, “but nothing had happened” until “they started praising God with musical instruments.” He says then “the house of the Lord was filled with a cloud,” and “the glory of the Lord had filled the house.”
What happened in 2 Chronicles 5:13 when the musicians praised God?

Are you with me but we have got to get the vision for God’s way God’s pattern and do it his way whether we like it or not we got to change this thing 2 Chronicles 5:13. Now remember. The temple had a door which is Jesus it had an altar. Where the blood was shed for the cleansing of sin that’s the cross it had a labor water baptism it had a lampstand it had a table communion and it had alder of incense prayer and praise and it had a holy of holies where God dwelt. But they had built all this and they put everything together. The lampstand was there the communion table was there the altar of incense was there the ark of the covenant was there the mercy seat was there the temple was built beautiful everything was great they had a magnificent natural building but nothing had happened. Nothing spiritual had happened. Then we get the 2 Chronicles 5:13 it came to pass. As the musicians and singers were as one to make one sound to be heard in praising and thanking the Lord you see it came to pass when this happened not the natural part of the building not the symbolic part of the building but when they started praising God with musical instruments. When they lifted little boys with the trumpets and the symbols and instruments of music and praise the Lord saying for he is good for his mercy endures forever then. Then. The house of the Lord was filled with a cloud so the priest could not stand to minister by reason of the cloud for the glory of the Lord had filled the house of God the presence of God came and filled the house of God and the ministers. Could minister anymore because God himself was ministering. And that really intimidates a lot of ministers and a lot of song leaders. When God shows up. It intimidates them it threatens them because they got to do their show you know they got to put on their their finest.
What happened in 2 Chronicles 5:13 when the musicians praised God?

2 Chronicles 5:13-14: indeed it came to pass, when the trumpeters and singers were as one, to make one sound to be heard in praising and thanking the LORD, and when they lifted up their voice with the trumpets and cymbals and instruments of music, and praised the LORD, saying: “For He is good, For His mercy endures forever,” that the house, the house of the LORD, was filled with a cloud, so that the priests could not continue ministering because of the cloud; for the glory of the LORD filled the house of God.
Why does he say ministers must step aside when God shows up?

He says that when God filled the temple “the priest could not stand to minister” and “God himself was ministering,” which “intimidates a lot of ministers and a lot of song leaders” and “ministers won’t step aside for God to touch people today.” He says “you can build crystal cathedrals… but that thing is nothing until God shows up.”
Why does he say ministers must step aside when God shows up?

Presentation but when God comes up we don’t need you my friend. And ministers won’t step aside for God to touch people today. But the key here they had everything the door the labor the water baptism Jesus is the way the truth and the life the door they had everything in the tabernacle but the glory but the presence and when they begin to praise and sing and minister unto him then God came and filled the temple. And the ministers had to step aside. Hallelujah. Now folks that’s when it became a magnifical house when the magnifical one came. You can have nice furnishings all you want you can build crystal cathedrals and all kinds of fancy buildings but that thing is nothing until God shows up he’s the magnificent one of the magnificent house.
Is God’s house a building or people? (Romans 15:4, Acts 17:24, Hebrews 3:6, 1 Peter 2:5)

He says the tabernacle “built and written about so we could learn from it,” and that God “does not dwell in temples made with hands.” He says “we are the house of God we are the temple of God… human beings not mortar but people,” and “living stones” in “spiritual house.”
Is God’s house a building or people? (Romans 15:4, Acts 17:24, Hebrews 3:6, 1 Peter 2:5)

Hallelujah. Very powerful. After. Following the pattern God came including. Praise and worship unto him. Romans 15:4 says things written the fourth time were written for our learning who’s learning hours. This tabernacle was built and written about so we could learn from it. First Corinthians 10:11 these things happen to them as examples. And they were written for our admonition upon whom the ends of the ages have come are we in the end of the ages yeah acts tells us we’re in the end of the last days we’re in the last days we’ve been in the last days since that day. So we got to learn God’s magnifical house. In Acts 17:24 is not a natural building at all. God as the scriptures say does not dwell in temples made with hands he’s quoting out of Isaiah. God never intended to dwell in a man-made building. Do you understand that. When he did this in Solomon’s temple he never intended. For that to be his dwelling place or Moses’s tabernacle. In Hebrews 3:6 Christ the son over his own house whose house are who we are the house of God we are the temple of God that’s what God was trying to teach us how to be a magnifical house of God human beings not mortar but people that’s all we see in first Peter 2:5 you as living stones are built up a what spiritual house a spiritual temple God is interested in people and he wants us to be magnifical.
Is God’s house a building or people? (Romans 15:4, Acts 17:24, Hebrews 3:6, 1 Peter 2:5)

Romans 15:4: For whatever things were written before were written for our learning, that we through the patience and comfort of the Scriptures might have hope. 1 Corinthians 10:11: Now all these things happened to them as examples, and they were written for our admonition, upon whom the ends of the ages have come. Acts 17:24: God, who made the world and everything in it, since He is Lord of heaven and earth, does not dwell in temples made with hands. Hebrews 3:6: but Christ as a Son over His own house, whose house we are if we hold fast the confidence and the rejoicing of the hope firm to the end. 1 Peter 2:5: you also, as living stones, are being built up a spiritual house, a holy priesthood, to offer up spiritual sacrifices acceptable to God through Jesus Christ.
What does “magnifical” mean, and why can’t the church do anything without Jesus?

He says “magnifica means excellence superior,” and the church is “supposed to be superior to every man-made ideal.” He says quoting Jesus that apart from him you can do nothing, and that “without Jesus folks we can’t do anything,” and a church isn’t built on a good worship leader, team or speaker: “Jesus is more important than the pastor… than anything.”
What does “magnifical” mean, and why can’t the church do anything without Jesus?

Magnifica means excellence superior. The church is supposed to be superior to every man-made ideal in this world. John chapter 15 verse 5 I am the vine you are the branches. If you abide in me and I abide in you. You’ll bear much fruit for without me you can do what. Nothing. You think a church is built on a good worship leader or a good worship team or a good orator. The church isn’t built on that without Jesus folks we can’t do anything. We need his glory to come and it comes when he comes it doesn’t come because you believe it came it can’t comes because it comes and you know it. Hallelujah. See Jesus is more important than the pastor than the youth leader then the church secretary then the clerk. He’s more important than anything. And without him we’re not going to excel and that’s what it says back there the glory of the Lord filled the house Jesus filled the house John 7:38 he that believes on me out of his belly shall flow rivers of life-giving water this [unclear] of the Holy Spirit which they that believe on him should receive. Same statement in John 3:16 he that believes on me shall not perish but have everlasting life same statement he that believes on me out of his belly shall flow the spirit of God the presence of God out of our innermost being so we are the temple as an individual as well as corporate. But if we don’t allow Jesus to show up we don’t allow Jesus to express himself and fill our being. We miss out on his glory. First Corinthians 6:9 your body is the temple of the Holy Ghost. Now who’s the Holy Ghost. God Jesus they’re all the same God the father God the son God the Holy Spirit it’s all God how many gods are there in christianity. One God okay. He manifested himself in that fleshly body called Jesus and you’ll see that flesh of the body when you go to heaven but it’s still God the Holy Spirit is God John 17:3 this is eternal life now everybody thinks that eternal life is just living forever but Jesus describes and gives us another definition of eternal life this is eternal life that they may what no you the only true God and Jesus Christ whom you have sent now this word no is used in the Bible as a sexual relationship all through the Bible Joseph did not know mary till after Jesus was born he didn’t have sex with mary to after Jesus was born and we are to have an intimate relationship with God he is to live in a it’s a real thing it’s not just head knowledge.
What does “magnifical” mean, and why can’t the church do anything without Jesus?

John 15:5: “I am the vine, you are the branches. He who abides in Me, and I in him, bears much fruit; for without Me you can do nothing. John 7:38-39: He who believes in Me, as the Scripture has said, out of his heart will flow rivers of living water.” But this He spoke concerning the Spirit, whom those believing in Him would receive; for the Holy Spirit was not yet given, because Jesus was not yet glorified. 1 Corinthians 6:19: Or do you not know that your body is the temple of the Holy Spirit who is in you, whom you have from God, and you are not your own? John 17:3: And this is eternal life, that they may know You, the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom You have sent.
What is the place of music, singing and praise in church?

He says “we’re not here to be entertained by music, we’re here to entertain the Lord to minister to him,” and that “you need to hear yourself saying how great he is.” He says a song service should have a song for sinners, an instructive song for babies in the faith, high praise, adoration and prayer.
What is the place of music, singing and praise in church?

It’s not intellect. God wants you to be a magnificent temple and when we come together he wants the body of Christ to be a magnifical church. Hallelujah it’s not about the Bible is not a book of faith it never says it’s a book of faith the Bible says it’s a book of truth and the Bible says it is a book that leads you to God so you can know God. And that is part of eternal life that you have a living real relationship with Jesus Christ. Music and singing a part of the New Testament pattern Ephesians 5:18 be filled with the spirit speaking to yourselves in Psalms hymns and spiritual songs singing and making melody in your heart to the Lord we’re not here to be entertained by music. We’re here to entertain the Lord to minister to him he ordained music he ordained singing he ordained praise and worship for us to minister to him does he need to be told how great he is no you need to hear yourself saying how great he is he needs nothing. But he’s given us principles we need to remind ourselves how great he is and how thankful we should be and when we sing unto him now Psalms are what they say 150 Psalms we can sing them they are songs and there are poems all right hymns is scripture put together to make a song like how great thou art see that’s a him all right Psalms 1 or Psalms 150 you know and we can sing those and we should sing those it’s the living word it’s powerful and a spiritual song. Jesus said the hour is coming and now is when they that worship the father must worship him in ones spirit in the truth you see when we transcend from the sacrifice from the mechanics to where the spirit gets involved that is when it becomes a spiritual song it’s spirit ignited and we need to make that transition. Hallelujah and that’s why we have a pause in between songs that people can lift up their song and sing and thank God their own personal self that’s why we do that so you’re not stuck with just chorus after chorus but you have some time to sing and to praise and to thank your God as an individual hallelujah. Colossians 3:16. Same thing let the word of Christ dwell in you richly let what dwell in you the word of Christ we need the word we need the spirit we need his presence we need his word not man’s word his word. In all wisdom teaching and admonishing one another in songs hymns and spiritual songs giving thanks to God now a church. A good song service. Will have a song. That touches sinners. Because the church is supposed to have sinners in it. Say that we’re supposed to welcome them. items.d: Pastor David G. Kincer teaches Isaiah 53:9–10: Jesus’ grave with the wicked and the rich, his innocence, and why it pleased God to bruise him—to see his seed. He discusses biblical hate as dislike, identifies…
p: Pastor David G. Kincer teaches Isaiah 53:9–10: Jesus’ grave with the wicked and the rich, his innocence, and why it pleased God to bruise him—to see his seed. He discusses biblical hate as dislike, identifies the seed as the children of promise and the remnant who keep God’s commandments, presents Christ as the one seed, and traces church history from the former house through the falling away and restoration to the coming latter glory.

items.t: God’s Promises to All the Acceptable 11/12/2017
items.d: Pastor David G. Kincer teaches that God has promises for “the acceptable”—those like Cornelius who fear God and do right by conscience: the Spirit poured on all flesh, the earth filled with his glory…
p: Pastor David G. Kincer teaches that God has promises for “the acceptable”—those like Cornelius who fear God and do right by conscience: the Spirit poured on all flesh, the earth filled with his glory, transformation into Christ’s image, knowing God, and wisdom from above. From Acts 19 he asks whether believers have received the Holy Ghost, urges adding virtue to faith, and teaches that any believer can lay on hands.
Like Cornelius, those who fear God, depart from evil and do right by their conscience without knowing more. He points to the innumerable multitude in heaven.

items.d: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer teaches from Isaiah 29 and 30 about God punishing His people and their opponents, and says believers must confront opposition to the Bible, drawing examples from Moses…
p: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer teaches from Isaiah 29 and 30 about God punishing His people and their opponents, and says believers must confront opposition to the Bible, drawing examples from Moses, Joshua, Daniel, Jesus and Paul and from church history and the Humanist Manifesto. He closes with God’s promise “in that day” to rebels who repent: He opens ears and eyes, answers their cry, and says “weep no more.”
What does Isaiah 29 say about God punishing His people and their opponents, and honoring Him with lips only? (Isaiah 29:1-13)

He says Isaiah 29 gives “a word about God punishing the city of God, the people of God, Jerusalem, and her opponents,” both those God used to correct His people and those who just oppose God and His people. He says those who fight God and His church are like a man who dreams he eats but wakes up still hungry, and that we can say we are believers while “the heart, the mind, the will, our actions, our attitude is removed far from God.”
What does Isaiah 29 say about God punishing His people and their opponents, and honoring Him with lips only? (Isaiah 29:1-13)

Okay, in Isaiah 29:1-17 we find God, through Isaiah, giving a word about God punishing the city of God, the people of God, Jerusalem, and her opponents: those that God used to correct his people, and those that just oppose God and his people. It says in verse one, “Woe to Ariel, the city where David dwelt.” That’s Jerusalem. Woe to Jerusalem, you will be brought down. He said in verse 7, “The multitude of the nations that fight against Jerusalem, Ariel, shall be as a dream of a night.” When a man dreams and he’s hungry and he eats, he’s thirsty and he drinks, but he wakes up, he’s still hungry and he’s still thirsty. It’s just a dream. So people that think they can fight against God and his church, they’re just it’s just a dream. It says you will be punished by the Lord who fight against Mount Zion, the church. Isaiah 29:10, “The Lord has closed your eyes, and the eyes of the prophets, and the eyes of your rulers and the seers has he covered. The vision is like words of a sealed book delivered to one who’s learned, saying, ‘Read this,’ and he says, ‘I can’t read it because it’s sealed.’ Delivered to another that’s not learned, and he says, ‘I can’t read it because I’m not learned.’” For this reason the Lord says, “As the people draw nigh to me with their mouth and their lips do honor me, but they have removed their heart far from me.” You see, yeah, we say we’re believers, yeah, we say we’re Christians, but the heart, the mind, the will, our actions, our attitude is removed far from God. “Their fear toward me is taught by the precept of men.” You see, and do we have that today, where we just teach our own doctrines, man-made doctrines, much like the Constitution of America’s interpreted for their own personal gain, so is the Bible in a generation we live in. it’s just And when people use the word “interpret,” watch out, because the Bible doesn’t need to be interpreted. The Bible interprets itself. It explains itself. You don’t have to psychoanalyze it.
What does Isaiah 29 say about God punishing His people and their opponents, and honoring Him with lips only? (Isaiah 29:1-13)

Isaiah 29:1-10: “Woe to Ariel, to Ariel, the city where David dwelt! Add year to year; Let feasts come around. Yet I will distress Ariel; There shall be heaviness and sorrow, And it shall be to Me as Ariel. I will encamp against you all around, I will lay siege against you with a mound, And I will raise siegeworks against you. You shall be brought down, You shall speak out of the ground; Your speech shall be low, out of the dust; Your voice shall be like a medium’s, out of the ground; And your speech shall whisper out of the dust. “Moreover the multitude of your foes Shall be like fine dust, And the multitude of the terrible ones Like chaff that passes away; Yes, it shall be in an instant, suddenly. You will be punished by the LORD of hosts With thunder and earthquake and great noise, With storm and tempest And the flame of devouring fire. The multitude of all the nations who fight against Ariel, Even all who fight against her and her fortress, And distress her, Shall be as a dream of a night vision. It shall even be as when a hungry man dreams, And look—he eats; But he awakes, and his soul is still empty; Or as when a thirsty man dreams, And look—he drinks; But he awakes, and indeed he is faint, And his soul still craves: So the multitude of all the nations shall be, Who fight against Mount Zion.” Pause and wonder! Blind yourselves and be blind! They are drunk, but not with wine; They stagger, but not with intoxicating drink. For the LORD has poured out on you The spirit of deep sleep, And has closed your eyes, namely, the prophets; And He has covered your heads, namely, the seers. Isaiah 29:13: Therefore the Lord said: “Inasmuch as these people draw near with their mouths And honor Me with their lips, But have removed their hearts far from Me, And their fear toward Me is taught by the commandment of men,
If there is a God, why does He allow wars and evil in the earth? (Isaiah 29:14)
