What are the signs of possessing the kingdom, and can a cross or a Bible drive out demons? (Matthew 12:28)

Now let’s look at the signs of possessing the kingdom. Now, this is important, and this is what I’ve been trying to get the church to understand for 40 years. I got this revelation in my bedroom on Warner Street in Santa Ana when I was just a couple of years old in God, and I said, “God, whatever it takes, whatever you got to do to me to reach this goal, I’m open to it.” Boy, I didn’t know what I said then, and I went through hell on earth. But this is the high mark of the calling of God, along with God’s character. Matthew 12:28: “If I cast out demons by the Spirit of God, surely the kingdom of God has come upon you.” Wow. This guy says he’s down on the church. Why? American churches don’t even believe in demons. Bill O’Reilly said there was a demon somewhere back in Ohio or someplace, and they had the priest on, and the priest said, “Yeah, I put the cross on him and, you know, he went crazy.” Church, demons are spirits. They could care the least if you touch that person with a cross, wooden, metal, plastic or whatever. In the Pentecostal realms, if you put the Bible on them, they, or they can’t say the Lord, and they go through the torch; that’s a bunch of baloney. Demons are spirits. And also in the Pentecostal world they vomit up demons; it’s really the phlegm coming out of their throat, and that’s a demon? That ain’t no demon; that’s your phlegm, you idiot. Down in Mexico they were casting out demons that came out as frogs. I said, “I don’t know what church you people are going to, but ain’t no frogs.” You read some scripture out of Revelation. Demons are spirits. Are you there? Hallelujah. You need some of these side issues sometimes. Somebody told me they took a picture of the Adam family. I immediately went home and looked on the Internet for this picture of the Adam; it’s a joke. Ain’t no picture, no Adam. Do you guys ever check things out? My goodness.
What are the signs of possessing the kingdom, and can a cross or a Bible drive out demons? (Matthew 12:28)
Matthew 12:28: But if I cast out demons by the Spirit of God, surely the kingdom of God has come upon you.
Is the kingdom in words or in power? (Luke 10:9, 1 Corinthians 4:20, 2:5)

He says the church should “heal the sick” and that “the kingdom of God is not in word but in power,” so we do not need “a lot of theology.” He tells how he led a young man of another religion to Christ in about five minutes by pointing to sin, the cross and that Jesus laid down his life, and says faith should “not stand in the intellect of men … but in the power of God.”
Is the kingdom in words or in power? (Luke 10:9, 1 Corinthians 4:20, 2:5)

Anyway, the church should be delivering people from possession and oppression of demons. Power! The church should be powerful, and this why this young person said, “I’m down on the church.” You know, he went to it, and it’s just a bunch of theology, just a bunch of rituals and routines, and no power. And yes, church, we should be people of power. Amen. Right, Luke 10:9: “Heal the sick there, and say to them, ‘The kingdom of God has come near to you.’” Heal the sick: physically sick, mentally sick, spiritually sick, emotionally sick. Jesus heals people. And people come in and we use psychology and we got these 12-step programs and seven-step programs, when the Bible says that the church can have power to heal. Are you there? And this is what we got to attain to, this is what we got to pursue: being a church that has the power. 1 Corinthians 4:20: “The kingdom of God is not in word but in power.” It’s not in speech, it’s not in words, it’s not all these words. When I led a young Muslim to Christ Friday night, I didn’t need a lot of theology. It took about five minutes. “Are you a sinner?” “No.” I said, “Well, let’s check this out. Have you murdered anybody?” “No.” I said, “Well, you’re looking good there.” I said, “Have you stole anything?” “Yep.” “Oh, really?” I said, “Have you told a lie?” “Yep.” I go, “Oh, two witnesses; you’re lying, you stole. What does that make you?” He looks at me, and someone beside me goes, “A sinner.” And then I told him the wages of sin is eternal death, eternal punishment, but there’s a higher law: Jesus Christ died on the cross. I says, “You Muslim, believe he’s just a prophet?” He said, “Yep, that’s right, we believe he was a prophet.” I said, “They’re lying to you. He’s not only the Son of God, he was God. And the Muslims are right, you can’t kill God. He had to lay down his life; that’s what Jesus said: ‘I lay down my life, ‘cause no one has authority to take it.’” And he laid it down so you could be forgiven, set free and so forth. We prayed the sinner’s prayer. Bam! Are you there? Hallelujah. And I, they don’t need to know where Cain’s wife come from and what the horns on the altar mean. Come on, they need this power of Christ touching them. God has chosen the foolishness of what? Preaching to save those that believe, and the gospel is the power of God. The gospel is Jesus’ birth, ministry, death and resurrection for you, and any of us can share that. Hallelujah. Not in words. 1 Corinthians 2:5: “Your faith should not stand in the intellect of men” (they use the word wisdom, really means intellect) “but in the power of God.” See, Calvin, St. Augustine, Wesley, the popes, Joseph Smith, Muhammad, I could care the least. I’ve read the Book of Mormon; man, I got one-third through it, and there’s so many mistakes, I go, “Any idiot can see that this just can’t be an angel. Angels don’t make mistakes like this.” Are you there? I mean, ridiculous mistakes. And I am shocked that people will read Christian books and not the Bible. I’m just shocked that authors today are better than Paul, better than Peter; it just amazing me, when these guys were connected with Christ in person. Are you there?
Is the kingdom in words or in power? (Luke 10:9, 1 Corinthians 4:20, 2:5)

Luke 10:9: And heal the sick there, and say to them, ‘The kingdom of God has come near to you.’ 1 Corinthians 4:20: For the kingdom of God is not in word but in power. 1 Corinthians 1:21: For since, in the wisdom of God, the world through wisdom did not know God, it pleased God through the foolishness of the message preached to save those who believe. 1 Corinthians 2:5: that your faith should not be in the wisdom of men but in the power of God. John 10:18: No one takes it from Me, but I lay it down of Myself. I have power to lay it down, and I have power to take it again. This command I have received from My Father.”
Why do Christians need to know the Scriptures, and what does “the power of the Lord was present to heal” mean? (Luke 5:17)

He says Jesus told the religious leaders “you are mistaken” because they didn’t know the Scriptures, and that today Christians “are passing on what these people are saying” instead of reading the Word. He says “the power of the Lord was present to heal” means it “wasn’t always there,” so “when it’s not there, we should not try to fake it.”
Why do Christians need to know the Scriptures, and what does “the power of the Lord was present to heal” mean? (Luke 5:17)

Matthew 22:29: “You are mistaken,” why? Because you don’t know the Scriptures. And this is the big problem in America: Christians are passing on what these people are saying. I try to get people to read the Word; they just won’t do it. They’ll go to a church where they don’t tell them to read the Word. “You’re going to harp on reading the Word? I’ll just leave.” What do I do? The Bible says, “Seek out of the book of the law and read,” “study to show thyself approved.” What do you want me to preach? You young people, you need to know the Scriptures. You need to start early. Remember this: we’re born by the Word and the Spirit, and the Word, his Spirit, by the way. Okay, the second reason we make [unclear] is we don’t have the power of God: the power of the name of Jesus, the power of the Holy Ghost, and the power of the Word. Luke 5:17. Okay, let me set the picture here. The lawyers, the religious leaders will come down to trap Jesus. They’re always trying to trap him, all right. And they come down, and Jesus is there, and the Bible says “the power of the Lord was” (they added this word “present”) “to heal.” All right, the power was there. So that means it wasn’t always there. And, folks, when it’s not there, we should not try to fake it, all right? So they brought in a man that was paralyzed, he couldn’t walk, four people brought him in on a stretcher, and Jesus said, “Your sins are forgiven you.” And these religious leaders and lawyers: “Hey, hey, nobody can forgive sins but God.” Well, duh! If you really knew your Bible, you’re looking at him; that’s God right there, Jesus. And so Jesus said these famous words: “Which is easier, to forgive sins or heal the sick?” Huh? Folks, both of them are supernatural. We can’t forgive sin and we can’t heal the sick, but he can do both. And so “the power of the Lord was present to heal.” That’s why we worship: to get the presence that will touch people’s minds, people’s souls, people’s spirit and change them. That’s why we want a living word, not some word from [unclear] or somebody, some book, you know. All these home Bible studies are using somebody’s book instead of the Bible book. We need the power of the Word; we need the power of the presence. And we can’t settle for anything less. And Jesus healed that paralytic man.
Why do Christians need to know the Scriptures, and what does “the power of the Lord was present to heal” mean? (Luke 5:17)

Matthew 22:29: Jesus answered and said to them, “You are mistaken, not knowing the Scriptures nor the power of God. Isaiah 34:16: “Search from the book of the LORD, and read: Not one of these shall fail; Not one shall lack her mate. For My mouth has commanded it, and His Spirit has gathered them. 2 Timothy 2:15: Be diligent to present yourself approved to God, a worker who does not need to be ashamed, rightly dividing the word of truth. Luke 5:17: Now it happened on a certain day, as He was teaching, that there were Pharisees and teachers of the law sitting by, who had come out of every town of Galilee, Judea, and Jerusalem. And the power of the Lord was present to heal them.
Why did crowds travel 60 miles to touch Jesus? (Luke 6:17-19)

He says the crowds came “to hear him” and “to be healed,” with no advertising, because “when the powers in the church, they didn’t need to advertise.” He says they “just came up and touched him,” with no healing line or fanfare, and that we can touch him today through “worship and prayer, seeking his face, fasting.”
Why did crowds travel 60 miles to touch Jesus? (Luke 6:17-19)

Now look at this powerful scripture, Luke 6:17. “A great multitude from all Judea” (60 miles away from where Jesus is at; he’s at the Sea of Galilee) “and from the sea coast of Tyre and Sidon” (these are heathen nations, heathen cities; they’re on the coast of the Mediterranean; they are 60 miles away) “came to hear him.” Folks, if they walked, it would take them two days to get there, and how did they find out where he was at? They had no TV and radio. Word of mouth, that’s right. When you got the power, when the power’s in the church, they didn’t need to advertise. God did his own advertising by healing the sick, casting out demons, saving souls, strengthening spirits, delivering minds. Amen. See, they didn’t need to sell you a Bible autographed by [unclear], or some trinket that you could put there and pray on, or some prayer cloth that cost you a hundred bucks. You could just bring a hanky out of the drawer and it works without the $100. If God’s in it, God only did that one time, and we make a rule out of it. He did it one time. A great multitude 60 miles away, folks. No air conditioning; they either walked or they rode donkeys or they rode in chariots. Most of these people are poor; they walked, it’s hot, they sat in the hot sun to what? No nursery, no children’s program, no youth program, and the multitude will sit there all day and listen to him teach. All day they came. Number one, to hear him: Jesus had something to say. Jesus had a life-changing message. He had the living Word. And to be healed of their diseases, their torments by unclean spirits, not even necessarily possessed, just oppressed and tormented, and they were what? Healed. “The whole multitude sought to touch Him, for power went out from Him and healed them all.” See, he didn’t have a healing line. He didn’t have to go through these big dramatics: “In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ of Nazareth, I pronounce your healing.” No, they just came up and touched him, touched him, touched him. No cameras, no fanfare, and the magic word is “touch.” Say “touch.” Folks, we can touch him today through worship and prayer, seeking his face, fasting. We can touch him today.
Why did crowds travel 60 miles to touch Jesus? (Luke 6:17-19)

Luke 6:17-19: And He came down with them and stood on a level place with a crowd of His disciples and a great multitude of people from all Judea and Jerusalem, and from the seacoast of Tyre and Sidon, who came to hear Him and be healed of their diseases, as well as those who were tormented with unclean spirits. And they were healed. And the whole multitude sought to touch Him, for power went out from Him and healed them all. Luke 6:19: And the whole multitude sought to touch Him, for power went out from Him and healed them all. Acts 19:11-12: Now God worked unusual miracles by the hands of Paul, so that even handkerchiefs or aprons were brought from his body to the sick, and the diseases left them and the evil spirits went out of them.
What power did the early church demonstrate, and what do we need today?

He criticizes ministers who “take credit for healings” that Jesus did, and says we are “vessels to bring God and people together.” He lists the early church’s power (a ruler struck down, deception judged, prison doors opening, a shadow healing) and says “you don’t need a lot of theology, you don’t need a lot of psychology.”
What power did the early church demonstrate, and what do we need today?

And these ministers that take credit for healings, I’ve been in a lot of healing ministers’ meetings. They take credit for something that Jesus came and did. He came and touched them and healed people, and the mighty man of God raised money saying he had the ability. Are you there? I loved it how God worked in Africa. My first visit to Africa, I’m preaching the gospel out in the church and all that, and I get done, and, you know, 15 or 30 people came up front saying, “God healed this, and God healed that, and God did this, and God did that.” And I go, “Hold it.” You know me, I’m a doubter. I go down, I start questioning. “All right, now you say God did this. Now who, who knows this was, who knows?” “Oh, I know, over here, over here.” It’s really happening. Yeah, no fanfare, no nothing. While you’re preaching, while the worship is going on, God comes and touches people, and amazing things happen. No healing line, nobody getting credit, the elders didn’t get up and put on theatrics: “Oh, hallelujah, I’m praying for you.” You know, “call the elders of the church.” Yeah, man, I’m one of them guys. Check me out, man. “De Lord!” and they’d get worse. You see, we need to touch him. And like [unclear] said, “I am a vessel that brings God and people together.” And when people touch him, things happen. I liked what he said, and that’s what we are: we are vessels to bring God and people together, and God does his work. Hallelujah. Isn’t that powerful? So we can touch him. Now, young people, I want you to know, the early church, there was a big demonstration of power. All right, Herod was killed with worms; Ananias and Sapphira died because they lied to the [unclear]. Herod, because he took the title of being a god, took the worship of being a god. The sorcerer was blinded. Philip was transported 30, 40 miles; just beam me up, beam me down. Prison doors did open all by themselves. Peter’s shadow was healing people. The fear: the outsiders feared the church, that they would not say anything against it or do anything against it. That’s the power of God. You young ones hearing this, this is what you need. You don’t need a lot of theology, you don’t need a lot of psychology, you don’t need a lot of words. We need the living Word, and we need that Holy Ghost working in the church and touching people’s lives. And we’ve gotten away from that, and this is my point to this guy. See, the church has gotten away from that, and we just do things that will bring the people in. We go to some kind of survey company and they do a survey how to build a church, and so we do these things to get people into the church, and we have 10,000 in the congregation, and they can’t handle life at all. I know, ‘cause I have to deal with them. They got no power in their life at all. They can’t even stay married. Remember Paul reasoned to Felix, the [unclear], self-control, righteousness and a judgment to come, and Felix trembled. He shook just hearing that simple message. Are you there?
What power did the early church demonstrate, and what do we need today?

Acts 12:23: Then immediately an angel of the Lord struck him, because he did not give glory to God. And he was eaten by worms and died. Acts 5:1-10: But a certain man named Ananias, with Sapphira his wife, sold a possession. And he kept back part of the proceeds, his wife also being aware of it, and brought a certain part and laid it at the apostles’ feet. But Peter said, “Ananias, why has Satan filled your heart to lie to the Holy Spirit and keep back part of the price of the land for yourself? While it remained, was it not your own? And after it was sold, was it not in your own control? Why have you conceived this thing in your heart? You have not lied to men but to God.” Then Ananias, hearing these words, fell down and breathed his last. So great fear came upon all those who heard these things. And the young men arose and wrapped him up, carried him out, and buried him. Now it was about three hours later when his wife came in, not knowing what had happened. And Peter answered her, “Tell me whether you sold the land for so much?” She said, “Yes, for so much.” Then Peter said to her, “How is it that you have agreed together to test the Spirit of the Lord? Look, the feet of those who have buried your husband are at the door, and they will carry you out.” Then immediately she fell down at his feet and breathed her last. And the young men came in and found her dead, and carrying her out, buried her by her husband. Acts 8:39-40: Now when they came up out of the water, the Spirit of the Lord caught Philip away, so that the eunuch saw him no more; and he went on his way rejoicing. But Philip was found at Azotus. And passing through, he preached in all the cities till he came to Caesarea. Acts 16:26: Suddenly there was a great earthquake, so that the foundations of the prison were shaken; and immediately all the doors were opened and everyone’s chains were loosed. Acts 5:15: so that they brought the sick out into the streets and laid them on beds and couches, that at least the shadow of Peter passing by might fall on some of them.
Is the church a one-man show? Why does he say you are important? (Acts 4, Acts 12)

He says Pentecost was “not a one-man show” but happened because “120 prayed and worshiped him,” and that in Acts 4 the whole church prayed. He says “you are important,” should make prayer and worship a priority, and should give God “one hour a day.” He ends by urging people to come to the altar “to touch Jesus.”
Is the church a one-man show? Why does he say you are important? (Acts 4, Acts 12)

And listen to this, this is what you got to get in your cranial vacuum, you ready? This is not a one-man show. God moved on the day of Pentecost because 120 prayed and worshiped him, not just Peter. God called Peter out to do the message, but it was the 120 that ushered in the baptism of the Holy Ghost. Acts chapter 4: the whole church was gathered together praying and saying, “Lord, grant unto us that signs and wonders would be done,” and God came and shook the place and granted unto them signs and wonders would be done, and they spoke the Word of God with power. You see, first the whole group prayed. See, this is a group. Are you getting this? You are important. We’re in America, we’re looking for the mighty man of God in the Baptist circles, the fundamentalist circles, the Catholics are looking for the pope and the priest, and, you know, we’re all looking for this one-man ministry thing. And all through the Bible it was the group. When Peter was in prison, he went to sleep, but the church didn’t. The church what? Prayed for him, and God came and rescued Peter. This is a corporate thing, and you are important. If you want the church to be more than just a bunch of word and a bunch of rituals and ceremonies, then you have to decide to get involved. You have to decide to make prayer a priority in your life, worship and praise a priority in your life, the Word. You need to give one hour a day to God; that’s what Jesus asked for, one hour. There’s 24; that leaves you 23. You say, “Well, I’m busy all day.” Then get up at 3:00 in the morning, seek God for an hour and go back to bed. Nobody can bother you, kids are sleeping. There is solutions for every problem that you give me. The reason I know that’s what I had to do: sometimes I had to get up in the middle of the night to get the real time in and go back to bed sometime. Hallelujah. Church, are you getting this? Do we want to be just another wordy church, rituals, routine? We got our little ceremony; we dance, we lift our hands, we shout unto God with the voice of triumph, and we have no hope in it at all. Hope is his expectation. These are scriptural things to do, but when we don’t do them with a purpose, it becomes a ceremony. Ain’t that right? It just becomes a ceremony. Now, these people traveled 60 miles to touch Jesus. Some of you only have to travel six feet to come down to the altar, humble yourself, get out of your safe zone, separate yourself from everybody around you, to touch Jesus.
Is the church a one-man show? Why does he say you are important? (Acts 4, Acts 12)

Acts 24:25: Now as he reasoned about righteousness, self-control, and the judgment to come, Felix was afraid and answered, “Go away for now; when I have a convenient time I will call for you.” Acts 4:24-31: So when they heard that, they raised their voice to God with one accord and said: “Lord, You are God, who made heaven and earth and the sea, and all that is in them, who by the mouth of Your servant David have said: ‘Why did the nations rage, And the people plot vain things? The kings of the earth took their stand, And the rulers were gathered together Against the LORD and against His Christ.’ “For truly against Your holy Servant Jesus, whom You anointed, both Herod and Pontius Pilate, with the Gentiles and the people of Israel, were gathered together to do whatever Your hand and Your purpose determined before to be done. Now, Lord, look on their threats, and grant to Your servants that with all boldness they may speak Your word, by stretching out Your hand to heal, and that signs and wonders may be done through the name of Your holy Servant Jesus.” And when they had prayed, the place where they were assembled together was shaken; and they were all filled with the Holy Spirit, and they spoke the word of God with boldness. Acts 12:5: Peter was therefore kept in prison, but constant prayer was offered to God for him by the church.
What line does he use when witnessing about the Bible?
He asks, “If there is a God, can he lie?” and when they answer no, he says the Bible is God’s Word and God can’t lie, so “God is who the Bible says he is, he’ll do what the Bible says he will do.”
Does he say James is describing something the church actually did?
No. He says James uses “if” as “an allegory, an illustration of a truth,” and “he didn’t say the church was doing this at all.”
Does he say every poor person is an heir of the kingdom?
No. He says “you’re not poor unless you meet the definition of the Bible poor,” meaning rich in faith and loving Jesus. He says “I’ve been in churches where poverty is spirituality.”
What does he say about being taken to court over your faith?

He says he has “been to court four times because of my faith” and “won all four times.” He says people with money and position oppress because the gospel “threaten them” by telling them they have to change their lifestyle.
Which name does he say to use rather than just “God”?
He says the noble name is “Jesus,” and to “be careful about using God in this generation; everybody takes God as anybody’s God,” while “that name of Jesus” separates it from all other gods.
What does he mean by positional and conditional righteousness?

He says being “righteous by the blood” is positional, and asks what good it does your family and community “if you just stay positionally righteous and you live wrong in this world.” He says “I need a God that can change my brain, change my actions, change my talk.”
What does he say the word “converted” means?

He says “it literally means to turn and change your beliefs to the one you’re turning to,” so “turn from the erroneous beliefs over who you’re following and turn to God, turn to Jesus and get his beliefs.”
What two things does he say the church needs to birth and change people?
He says “the living presence of God, the Spirit of God, and the living Word of God.”
Does he say tongues or preaching pricked hearts at Pentecost?
He says “no one got their heart pricked when they heard him speaking in tongues in their language,” but when Peter “stood up and preached Christ and crucified, then the Word pricked their heart.”
What test does he give for a spiritual experience?
He says “when it doesn’t line up to the Word, I know it’s not the Spirit of God,” and that the Word and the Spirit “agree.”
Does he say a cross or the Bible on a person drives out a demon?

No. He says “demons are spirits. They could care the least if you touch that person with a cross, wooden, metal, plastic or whatever,” and he also says putting the Bible on a person is “a bunch of baloney.”
How does he describe sharing the gospel in about five minutes?

He says he asked simple questions about murder, stealing and lying, showed that the person was “a sinner,” then said the wages of sin is eternal death “but there’s a higher law: Jesus Christ died on the cross.” He says “they need this power of Christ touching them.”
What does he say about healing lines and credit for healings?

He says Jesus did the healing and ministers who “take credit” are taking credit for something Jesus did. He says in Africa God touched people during preaching and worship with “no healing line, nobody getting credit.”
How much time does he say to give God each day?
He says to “give one hour a day to God; that’s what Jesus asked for,” and if you’re busy, “get up at 3:00 in the morning, seek God for an hour and go back to bed.”

items.d: Pastor David G. Kincer teaches the ministry of helps: the wise men financing Jesus’ flight to Egypt, deacons qualified by honest report, the Spirit and wisdom, the church’s welfare policy in 1 Timothy 5 and 2…
p: Pastor David G. Kincer teaches the ministry of helps: the wise men financing Jesus’ flight to Egypt, deacons qualified by honest report, the Spirit and wisdom, the church’s welfare policy in 1 Timothy 5 and 2 Thessalonians 3, the four men carrying the paralytic, the apostles serving the multitude, and thrifty ministers. Help begins at home; good families make a good church.
Where does the ministry of helps fit among the gifts?

God sets people in the church—Bible college or Ivy League schools can’t. He ranks the utterance ministries (apostle, prophet, teacher), then sign ministries (miracles, healings), then work ministries anyone can do—helps and governments—with tongues last. Paul the apostle still helped set up and clean up; good leaders work with the crew.
Where does the ministry of helps fit among the gifts?

We learned that God sets in the church you see you can’t go to Bible college or seminar or Princeton or Yale and call yourself a minister only God can do that and don’t get me wrong we need knowledge of the Bible but it takes God. To prepare someone and give them the abilities to do these things and then he gives us a list of these ministries these gifts. Apostle and he gives them an order the number one ranking minister is the apostle then the prophet then the teachers and we call these the teaching ministries the utterance ministries okay. Then. You got miracles and healings these are the signs the supernatural. Only God can do humans can’t do them and then you got the work ministries anybody can do that. Ministry of helps which will be talking about the day governments and then at the bottom is a variety of languages and if there’s interpretation languages tongues become a teaching part of this up here and also. Tongues are a sign for the unbeliever you see and so it becomes a supernatural thing now. The apostle did all of them Paul the apostle have worked every one just because he was an apostle he was still helping clean up have him set up he was involved okay and a good leader won’t just be standing there watching a crew work they will be working with the crew that’s the right character to have and I hear an amen yeah too many want to be the boss.
Where does the ministry of helps fit among the gifts?

1 Corinthians 12:28: And God has appointed these in the church: first apostles, second prophets, third teachers, after that miracles, then gifts of healings, helps, administrations, varieties of tongues.
How did the wise men show the ministry of helps?

They came to a house—not the manger—to worship the young child and gave gold, frankincense and myrrh. When the angel told Joseph to flee to Egypt from Herod, those gifts financed the stay until Herod died—a financial ministry of helps.
How did the wise men show the ministry of helps?

And just watch all the rest of us do work now we’re going to take a look first at the wise men these wise men there wasn’t just three of them by the way we don’t know how many there were we know there were more than two. Because it’s plural we have. Accepted the song that said we three kings of Orient are, and just accept these things as doctrine and they’re not but these wise men came to worship Jesus they traveled for two years ok and when they got to. Jerusalem. They went into a house not the manger. items.t: Historical Examples of Falling Away, Opposing God and His Church 04/15/2018
items.d: Pastor David G. Kincer gives historical examples of believers opposing what God was doing: crowds rejecting Jesus, the New Testament church and what it lacked, the falling away he dates to Constantine, and…
p: Pastor David G. Kincer gives historical examples of believers opposing what God was doing: crowds rejecting Jesus, the New Testament church and what it lacked, the falling away he dates to Constantine, and restoration movements from the 1300s through the Pentecostal outpouring, each opposed by the last. He ties the great awakenings to America’s founding and urges the church to ask for latter rain now.

items.d: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer teaches that the baptism of the Holy Ghost with power is a real experience separate from salvation and water baptism. He starts with John 7:38-39 and Jesus as the…
p: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer teaches that the baptism of the Holy Ghost with power is a real experience separate from salvation and water baptism. He starts with John 7:38-39 and Jesus as the baptizer, covers prophecy, visions and the names of the Holy Spirit, then walks through the accounts in Acts of Pentecost, the believers in Samaria, Cornelius’s household and the disciples at Ephesus. He also speaks about unity in worship, mistakes in Spirit-filled churches, and the purpose of the Spirit’s power.
What is the baptism of the Holy Ghost, and what does John 7:38-39 promise?

He says there is “an experience in God called the baptism of the Holy Ghost with power,” not just something at Pentecost, at salvation or at water baptism. He reads John 7:38-39 as a promise to believers, and says the criteria for having the Holy Ghost is “Believe. Okay, it’s not complicated.” The Spirit flows from “your belly, innermost being,” and “it’s not a ceremony, it’s not a ritual, it’s a real experience.”
What is the baptism of the Holy Ghost, and what does John 7:38-39 promise?

They told me that Holy Spirit baptism was one time on the day of Pentecost, or it was when you get saved, or it was when you got water baptized. And you people need to know how to answer this stuff, and you also need to know that there is an experience in God called the baptism of the Holy Ghost with power that is vitally important to your life, to the church life, and what God is doing in the earth. Okay, and I’m going to give you biology this morning. Are you ready? John 7:38-39. It is a promise to believers. Now, the Holy Spirit is called the Holy Ghost, Holy Spirit, Spirit of Truth, Comforter, My Spirit, and we’re going to give you the facts of the Holy Spirit. All right, nothing but facts. “He that believes on Me.” Okay, how many of you believe on Jesus? Where’s the rest of you? Huh, now. Okay, John 3:16 says, “He that believes on Me shall not perish but have everlasting life.” Same statement here, but instead of everlasting life, He says, “As the Scripture has said, out of his belly shall flow rivers of living water.” And this spake He of the Spirit, which they that believe on Him should receive, for the Holy Ghost was not yet given because Jesus was not yet glorified. He hadn’t died and risen again, and so the Holy Spirit hadn’t been poured out on all flesh yet. But what’s the criteria for having the Holy Ghost? Believe. Okay, it’s not complicated. All right, and where will we experience this Holy Ghost? Out of your belly, innermost being. You’re going to experience it in that inner man that you really are, that spirit that’s really inside that body. Let me just share with you here a minute. It said, “As the Scripture has said” in the Old Testament. In Job 32:18, Elihu said, “I am full of the matter, the spirit within me constrains me. Behold, my belly is as wine which hath no vent, it is ready to burst like new wine bottles.” See, in the Old Testament Scriptures God already said He was going to do this. All right, and it’s going to pour out of our innermost being. It’s not a ceremony, it’s not a ritual, it’s a real experience. In Isaiah 58:11: “You shall be like a watered garden and like a spring of water whose waters fail not.” Hallelujah. And so this is the promise of that in John 7:38.
What is the baptism of the Holy Ghost, and what does John 7:38-39 promise?

John 7:38-39: He who believes in Me, as the Scripture has said, out of his heart will flow rivers of living water.” But this He spoke concerning the Spirit, whom those believing in Him would receive; for the Holy Spirit was not yet given, because Jesus was not yet glorified. John 3:16: For God so loved the world that He gave His only begotten Son, that whoever believes in Him should not perish but have everlasting life. Job 32:18-19: For I am full of words; The spirit within me compels me. Indeed my belly is like wine that has no vent; It is ready to burst like new wineskins. When I spoke in Third World countries, I interpreted a lot of tongues. All right, it is a sign for the unbeliever. Doesn’t happen so much in America. And this happened in Iconium, and they so spoke that a great multitude believed. They so spoke by the Holy Ghost that a great multitude believed. How many would like to see [unclear] really get a word from the Spirit of God? Amen, yes. See, that’s our cry, that’s my cry, that we get past the form and into the force. Yes, see, we get past the fear and into the force.
Is being filled a one-time experience, and what does he mean by “great grace”? (Acts 4:33; 13:9, 52; 14:1)

Acts 4:33: And with great power the apostles gave witness to the resurrection of the Lord Jesus. And great grace was upon them all. Acts 13:9: Then Saul, who also is called Paul, filled with the Holy Spirit, looked intently at him Acts 13:52: And the disciples were filled with joy and with the Holy Spirit. Acts 14:1: Now it happened in Iconium that they went together to the synagogue of the Jews, and so spoke that a great multitude both of the Jews and of the Greeks believed.
What does Samaria show about Holy Spirit baptism being separate from believing and water baptism? (Acts 8:12-17)

He says the Samaritans believed and were baptized in water, yet when Peter and John came “as yet He was fallen upon none of them,” and then “they laid their hands on them and they received the Holy Ghost.” He says “it didn’t happen at water baptism, it didn’t happen when they believe, it happened when God made it happen,” and calls it “a different experience from salvation, a different experience from water baptism.”
What does Samaria show about Holy Spirit baptism being separate from believing and water baptism? (Acts 8:12-17)

Okay, are they already believers? Yep. Have they been water baptized? Yeah. See, it didn’t happen at water baptism, it didn’t happen when they believe, it happened when God made it happen. It happens when it happens. Acts 8:12: “When they believed Philip preaching the things of the kingdom of God,” he went down to Samaria, and the name of Jesus Christ, and miracles, “they were all baptized, both men and women.” Okay, so they believed. Okay, are they filled with the Holy Ghost? Not yet. Are they baptized in water? Yes. Are they filled with the Holy Ghost yet? No. Verse 14: Peter and John came down and prayed for them to receive the Holy Ghost, “as yet He was fallen upon none of them.” Now here they use the word “fallen.” See, come upon. “Only they were baptized in the name of the Lord.” Had they been water baptized? Had they been water baptized? The story is the story, church. Do you get it? Then they laid their hands on them and they received the Holy Ghost. A different experience from salvation, a different experience from water baptism. Already believers, they were already baptized. Okay, now separate event. You agree? Is that what the Scripture says? Yes. Say amen if you got it. Amen. All right, say it with fortitude. Amen. All right, now I believe you.
What does Samaria show about Holy Spirit baptism being separate from believing and water baptism? (Acts 8:12-17)

Acts 8:12: But when they believed Philip as he preached the things concerning the kingdom of God and the name of Jesus Christ, both men and women were baptized. Acts 8:14-17: Now when the apostles who were at Jerusalem heard that Samaria had received the word of God, they sent Peter and John to them, who, when they had come down, prayed for them that they might receive the Holy Spirit. For as yet He had fallen upon none of them. They had only been baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus. Then they laid hands on them, and they received the Holy Spirit.
What does Cornelius’s household show about the order of salvation, the Holy Ghost and water baptism? (Acts 10:44-48)

He says “everything is backwards here”: the Holy Ghost fell on people who “were unbelievers,” and “before he could have an altar call for salvation, God just filled them with the Holy Ghost.” He says the Jews with Peter “were astonished,” and that the Gentiles “spoke with tongues again and magnified God.” He gives the order: “First you got the Holy Ghost, then you got them believing, and then you got them water baptized,” and calls it “separate experience from water baptism and the salvation of your soul.” He says God did it “because He knew these dumbbells in the future would twist the Scriptures and rob people of a real experience in God.”
What does Cornelius’s household show about the order of salvation, the Holy Ghost and water baptism? (Acts 10:44-48)

Now, this one is really interesting. God really dazzles you when you come to Cornelius. All right, I mean, everything is backwards here. God just don’t fall into our little pattern all the time, and He does have a pattern, but He’s God, He can go outside His pattern. We’re not allowed to, but He’s God, He can do anything He wants when He wants. Okay, Cornelius is a Roman soldier, praying and fasting. An angel came, told him go down and get Peter to come up and preach to him. So he went down and got Peter, Peter come up and spoke, and as Peter spoke the Word of God, the Holy Ghost fell on all them which heard the Word. All these people came to Cornelius’s house. They were unbelievers. Peter had to come and preach the gospel to them. These were unbelievers, and before he could have an altar call for salvation, God just filled them with the Holy Ghost. How could He do such a thing? Because He knew these dumbbells in the future would twist the Scriptures and rob people of a real experience in God, a powerful experience in God, by their theological interpretations. And so here He really just messes everything up. They were filled with the Holy Ghost before a salvation call and before their water baptism, and they of the circumcision, the Jews that came with Peter, were astonished because on the Gentiles was poured out the gift of the Holy Ghost. They were just astonished. How can this be? You know, it’s us [unclear], no more. You know, it’s just us people, with the, we’re the people. Hallelujah. And God said He would pour out His Spirit on how many flesh? All flesh. You are a candidate for the Holy Ghost. “For they heard them speak with tongues.” Oh, tongues again. My gosh, how could God do such a thing? They spoke with tongues again and magnified God, or praised God. Remember, on the day of Pentecost they spoke the mighty works of God. Here they praise and enlarged, magnified God. Then commanded Peter that they be baptized in water in the name of the Lord. Amen. First you got the Holy Ghost, then you got them believing, and then you got them water baptized. He’s God. He had definitely, this is a what? Separate experience from water baptism and the salvation of your soul. Unbelievers, not baptized, they got the Holy Ghost.
What does Cornelius’s household show about the order of salvation, the Holy Ghost and water baptism? (Acts 10:44-48)

Acts 10:44-48: While Peter was still speaking these words, the Holy Spirit fell upon all those who heard the word. And those of the circumcision who believed were astonished, as many as came with Peter, because the gift of the Holy Spirit had been poured out on the Gentiles also. For they heard them speak with tongues and magnify God. Then Peter answered, “Can anyone forbid water, that these should not be baptized who have received the Holy Spirit just as we have?” And he commanded them to be baptized in the name of the Lord. Then they asked him to stay a few days.
What happened in Ephesus in Acts 19, and what does he say about churches that do not teach the baptism of the Holy Ghost?

He says Paul asked, “Have you people received the Holy Ghost since you believed?” and they were “in a group that didn’t teach the Holy Ghost.” He says “when you don’t teach the baptism of the Holy Ghost, you are robbing the people of a powerful experience in God that will help them in daily life.” After Paul laid hands on them, “they spoke in languages again, and they prophesied.” He says tongues are “a sign for the unbeliever, prophecy is for the believer.”
What happened in Ephesus in Acts 19, and what does he say about churches that do not teach the baptism of the Holy Ghost?

All right, now we go to Acts 19. Here Paul comes to Ephesus, and Paul says, “Have you people received the Holy Ghost since you believed?” And of course they were in a group that didn’t teach the Holy Ghost. And see, when you don’t teach the baptism of the Holy Ghost, you are robbing the people of a powerful experience in God that will help them in daily life and help us reach the world for Christ. You got that? And here’s a group that wasn’t teaching. They said, “We never heard of it.” So when Paul preached to them, they were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus. Paul laid his hands upon them, the Holy Ghost came upon them, and they spoke with tongues. Oh my God, that tongue again. That tongue just drives people nuts. They spoke in languages again, and they prophesied. They spoke by the inspiration, they did both of them. All right, so three out of five times they spoke with tongues, and we don’t know one of those times if they did or not because he didn’t say. He just didn’t say. And tongues are a sign for who? The unbeliever. Don’t forget that. Tongues are a sign for the unbeliever, prophecy is for the believer. Hallelujah.
What happened in Ephesus in Acts 19, and what does he say about churches that do not teach the baptism of the Holy Ghost?

Acts 19:1-7: And it happened, while Apollos was at Corinth, that Paul, having passed through the upper regions, came to Ephesus. And finding some disciples he said to them, “Did you receive the Holy Spirit when you believed?” So they said to him, “We have not so much as heard whether there is a Holy Spirit.” And he said to them, “Into what then were you baptized?” So they said, “Into John’s baptism.” Then Paul said, “John indeed baptized with a baptism of repentance, saying to the people that they should believe on Him who would come after him, that is, on Christ Jesus.” When they heard this, they were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus. And when Paul had laid hands on them, the Holy Spirit came upon them, and they spoke with tongues and prophesied. Now the men were about twelve in all.
What does he say about excesses and “funny things” in Spirit-filled churches, and the claim that the Holy Ghost is not for today?

He admits “us Pentecostals, we do make mistakes,” and that “babies in Christ” may “speak some silly things,” but compares them to children: “we don’t kick them out of the house and condemn them.” He says “these things hurt no one,” and asks “how does tongues hurt you?” He says teaching that the Holy Ghost “isn’t for today” hurts people because “you’re robbing them of a tremendous experience and truth in God,” and that being offended by it is “called pride.” He says “I would rather be in a Spirit-filled church with some funny things going on.”
What does he say about excesses and “funny things” in Spirit-filled churches, and the claim that the Holy Ghost is not for today?

Now, I tell these brethren, you know, us Pentecostals, we do make mistakes. Okay, we get too shaken, we slain in the Spirit, we fall for this stuff, and we even have babies in Christ that speak some silly things. Okay, me and Mr. Barnes heard some of that in one of the services. Didn’t bother us any, we just knew they were babies in Christ. And you know, children, they say strange things, and we just laugh and we don’t kick them out of the house and condemn them. These things hurt no one. I asked them, “How does tongues hurt you?” It doesn’t hurt you. There’s no physical harm, there’s no spiritual harm because somebody speaks in tongues. If somebody shakes and falls down on the ground, how does that hurt you? Why are you offended at that? That does no personal harm to you, does it? You’re only hurt because they’re not believing what you believe. That’s why you’re hurt. It’s called pride. But I said, “Now, let’s get to your end. You’re telling people that the Holy Ghost isn’t for today. That hurts them because you’re robbing them of a tremendous experience and truth in God. I said, are you over here, you’re telling them that they get the Holy Ghost when they were water baptized and they didn’t get anything. You’re robbing them. I said, who’s really doing the hurting here? You’re robbing people of an experience in God.” Amen. So we have a few funny things going on. I would, listen, I would rather be in a Spirit-filled church with some funny things going on, and believe me, I have the authority to control things. You don’t believe me, you watch funny things happen. Yeah, we don’t have to hurt people and step on them, we can just guide them. We can grow in this thing. How many, when you first got on a bicycle, didn’t crash it? Most of us wrecked the bike, don’t we? Okay, so we do some funny things with the Holy Ghost. They’re babies, we’re babies, we’re learning. Could that be an amen? Amen, yes. What we need is that power. We need that power that changes people’s life in our services.
What is Holy Spirit baptism for, and what does he challenge the church to do? (John 3:30; 1 Corinthians 14:26; John 16:13)

He concludes that the baptism of the Holy Ghost “is another spiritual miracle like salvation,” and that “you have to believe above your experience before you’re going to experience it.” He says it is “for a purpose,” not “for you to feel good,” and people need “power, freeing them from sin, Satan, and self.” He says “everything we do should be to build up the people of God,” and the church must “decrease and let God increase.” He says the Spirit “will drive you to the Word,” and “politicians need to hear the Word of God” too.
What is Holy Spirit baptism for, and what does he challenge the church to do? (John 3:30; 1 Corinthians 14:26; John 16:13)

Okay, they are believers, they are baptized. Clearly the Holy Ghost baptism is another separate experience. Amen. Now, conclusion: “Clothed with power,” “receive power,” “witnesses unto Me.” The baptism of the Holy Ghost is another spiritual miracle like salvation. Okay, the Bible says that, I don’t care what you believe, the Bible say you have to preach above your experience before you’re going to experience it. You have to believe above your experience before you’re going to experience it. Don’t take your experience and bring the Bible down to your lack of experience. You speak the Bible and He will bring your experience up to what you’re speaking and believing. Separate from water baptism and salvation, we saw it clearly, didn’t we? There’s nothing to interpret, is there? Power to speak, smite your enemies, do miracles, and win souls. Do we need that in the church at Mountainside? Yes. As John says, “I must decrease and He must increase.” How many of you realize we got to decrease and let God increase in this church? We got to get out of our opinions, we got to get out of our cultural antics, and we got to say, “God, arise,” if we want to see a visitation. And I guarantee you, when God starts moving, people will come. The Holy Ghost baptism is for a purpose, either in the assembly or individually, whether they’re filled, baptized, or the Spirit comes upon them. All right, it’s for a purpose. It’s not for you to feel good, and that’s not totally true. There are times of refreshing, you need to be refreshed, but not to where you have to roll around on the floor and shake and bake. And just that refreshing on the inner man, that strengthening in the inner man. You see, it’s for a purpose. He’s a Comforter, He’s a Spirit of Truth that teaches us all things. So I challenge this church today. People need power, freeing them from sin, Satan, and self, and they need refreshing from God. This is what I liked about the Spirit-filled churches when I went to them. You could feel God. He would penetrate your being. He would convict you that you’re wrong. I was always wrong. I hadn’t given my heart to Christ yet. I believed in God, but I wasn’t about to serve Him because I had plans, man, I had plans. But that presence comes, you can feel Him. It’s like putting gas in your tank. You know, we run out of gas, we run out of spiritual gas, we get refilled. It’s a refreshing, and people need that. And people need the Holy Ghost to convict them of sin, forgive them of sin, and cleanse them of sin, and encourage them. Remember, prophecy is for edification, exhortation, and comfort. People need that comfort, people need that building up. See, and Paul said in 1 Corinthians 14, “Let all things be done to edify.” Everything we do should be to build up the people of God, make them better people, and that’s what the ministry of the Holy Ghost is for. We’ve got to get the word out. They told me over there they send us to go to politicians, politicians is of the devil, you know, and all this stuff. I go, man, this world is still believing the lies of Satan in the garden when Satan told Jesus that all these kingdoms are given to me and I can give them to who I want. He’s lying through his teeth. The Bible plainly tells us over and over that the nations, the kingdoms, belong to the Lord. Amen. He was lying. Politicians need to hear the Word of God. Unbelievers need to hear the Word of God. Unlearned people, unlearned people, they’re believers but they’re unlearned, they need to hear this Word that God has given this church. And to whom much is given, much is required. Folks, we got to get this word out. We’ve got to buck up, we’ve got to get together and get this word out: printed, Internet, radio, TV, CD. You know, Christine and Mike were really good on a camera, I’ve noticed. They really have camera appeal. Me and Mr. Barnes, we don’t, you know, we don’t look so good on camera. And remember, the Holy Ghost will guide you into all truth. When you really get filled with the Holy Ghost, you will not only know because of the feeling. He will not allow you to be lazy in the Word of God, because it’s the Word that set you free. He will drive you to the Word, He will drive you to church to learn the Word. You will have a motivational factor in your life.
What is Holy Spirit baptism for, and what does he challenge the church to do? (John 3:30; 1 Corinthians 14:26; John 16:13)

John 3:30: He must increase, but I must decrease. 1 Corinthians 14:26: How is it then, brethren? Whenever you come together, each of you has a psalm, has a teaching, has a tongue, has a revelation, has an interpretation. Let all things be done for edification. Luke 4:5-7: Then the devil, taking Him up on a high mountain, showed Him all the kingdoms of the world in a moment of time. And the devil said to Him, “All this authority I will give You, and their glory; for this has been delivered to me, and I give it to whomever I wish. Therefore, if You will worship before me, all will be Yours.” Luke 12:48: But he who did not know, yet committed things deserving of stripes, shall be beaten with few. For everyone to whom much is given, from him much will be required; and to whom much has been committed, of him they will ask the more. John 16:13: However, when He, the Spirit of truth, has come, He will guide you into all truth; for He will not speak on His own authority, but whatever He hears He will speak; and He will tell you things to come.
What teachings does he say he was told about Holy Spirit baptism?

He says, “They told me that Holy Spirit baptism was one time on the day of Pentecost, or it was when you get saved, or it was when you got water baptized.” He says “you people need to know how to answer this stuff.”
What does he say is the criteria for having the Holy Ghost?
He asks, “But what’s the criteria for having the Holy Ghost? Believe. Okay, it’s not complicated.” He says you will experience it in “that inner man that you really are.”
Who does he say baptizes in the Holy Ghost?
He says, “Jesus is the baptizer in the Holy Ghost,” and “Jesus is the sender,” reading Luke 3:16 and Luke 24:49.
Does he say prophesying and predicting are the same thing?
No. He says “there’s a big difference when you go into predicting,” and that “prophesying for edification, exhortation, and comfort is totally different.”
What does he say the Holy Ghost is not out to do?
He says, “He’s not out to condemn you, He’s not out to punish you, He is out to change you and help you in your time of need.”
What does he say about resisting the Holy Ghost as a young man?

He says, “I believed in God, but I had plans and I had purposes, and I would just shove that Holy Ghost away. I didn’t want to be convicted.” He says that “until finally He got my attention, and it’s been a great life ever since.”
What does he say about following the song leader in worship?
He says, “If the song leader claps their hands, you clap your hands. Song leader raises the hand, you raise your hand.” He also says, “if you don’t want to lift your hands, you don’t have to.”
What does he say about faking tongues?
He says of Pentecost, “They didn’t fake it, they didn’t pretend it,” and of his early experience in Pentecostal churches that “you don’t manufacture, God does it.”
How does he say you know you have been filled with the Holy Ghost?
He says, “Believe me, you will know. It comes from your innermost being. It is a visitation of power, supernatural ability.” He adds “tongues or no tongues, you will know.”
What does he say about speaking God’s Word with confidence?
He says, “speak like it’s God’s Word. It’s truth. Don’t speak like it’s a suggestion, it’s your opinion. Speak like it is.”
What does he say grace is?
He says, “grace isn’t just favor from God,” and “grace is divine enablement. There’s power in grace.”
What order does he give for Cornelius’s household?
He says, “First you got the Holy Ghost, then you got them believing, and then you got them water baptized.”
What bicycle illustration does he use?

He asks, “when you first got on a bicycle didn’t crash it? Most of us wrecked the bike, don’t we?” and says, “we do some funny things with the Holy Ghost. They’re babies, we’re babies, we’re learning.”
What does he say about politicians and the Word of God?
He says the Bible “plainly tells us over and over that the nations, the kingdoms, belong to the Lord,” and “politicians need to hear the Word of God. Unbelievers need to hear the Word of God.”

items.d: Pastor David G. Kincer walks through the first Holy Spirit events of the New Testament—John filled from the womb, Mary, Elizabeth, Zacharias, Simeon and Anna, and Jesus baptized in the Spirit and led into…
p: Pastor David G. Kincer walks through the first Holy Spirit events of the New Testament—John filled from the womb, Mary, Elizabeth, Zacharias, Simeon and Anna, and Jesus baptized in the Spirit and led into testing. He explains blasphemy against the Holy Spirit, teaches that Christ’s blood can cleanse even it (Paul in 1 Timothy 1:13), and what Hebrews 6 falling away really means.
What does John the Baptist teach about waiting on the Spirit?

Luke 1:15: John would be filled with the Holy Spirit from his mother’s womb, yet thirty years passed before he ministered. You can’t manufacture a move of the Holy Spirit; respond when he moves, and if it takes days or years, hang in there.
What does John the Baptist teach about waiting on the Spirit?

So in this third section we’re going to take a look at the first four usages. Of the Holy Spirit four events and we start with the first one in Luke 1:15 John shall be filled John the baptist shall be filled there’s that verb again with the Holy Spirit from his mother’s womb now from the mother’s womb till when he began to preach there were 30 years that went by before he ever ministered before he ever fulfilled God’s goal for him and remember there were 400 silent years between the Old Testament prophets and the New Testament we have no record of God doing and saying anything for 400 years remember Solomon had a visitation of God and then he didn’t have another one for 13 years Moses when he went up to the mountain when he first got there he had to wait 7 days before God came and began to speak to him there’s nothing wrong with waiting on the Lord to move you can’t you can’t manufacture a move of the Holy Spirit you’ve got to respond when he moves and if it takes 7 days or 10 days or 30 years or whatever just hang in there be filled with the Holy Spirit now speaking of John
What does John the Baptist teach about waiting on the Spirit?
Luke 1:15: For he will be great in the sight of the Lord, and shall drink neither wine nor strong drink. He will also be filled with the Holy Spirit, even from his mother’s womb.
Who is least and who is greatest in the kingdom?

John did no miracle, yet none was greater, and the least in the kingdom is greater than he. Matthew 5:19: whoever breaks the least commandments—the baby doctrines of Hebrews 6 like repentance, baptisms and laying on of hands—and teaches others to break them is least. The greatest do and teach righteousness.
Who is least and who is greatest in the kingdom?

and the Bible says that John did no miracle John did not speak in tongues John was never slain in the spirit John did no miracle but the Bible. Says that there was no greater prophet than John the baptist in other words he was equal to Isaiah Jeremiah Ezekiel amos Daniel David Adam all these prophets Moses John the baptist was equal to just as great even though there were no miracles done through his ministry but the most important thing here is Jesus goes on and says the least in the kingdom of God is greater than John the baptist wow the least so who are the least in the kingdom of God Matthew 5:19 tells us he that breaks the word the least of the commandments of God and teaches of other people to break them is the least in the kingdom. And the least in the kingdom is greater than John the baptist because they’re in the kingdom of God and the kingdom of God come to us through Jesus Christ but he also said they that do the greatest. Commandments and teach the greatest commandments and is servant of all is the greatest in the kingdom so the least commandments are the baby doctrines in Hebrews 6. Repentance from dead works faith toward God baptisms of water baptisms of the Holy Spirit baptism of the body of Christ laying on of hands resurrection of the dead and eternal judgment which is the second coming what’s going to happen at the second coming so the second coming laying on of hands praying for the sick praying for each other uh water baptism Holy Spirit baptism being placed into the body of Christ faith and repentance are baby things and the least in the kingdom don’t even do those and they teach other people you don’t need to get water baptized you don’t need to get baptized in the Holy Ghost Holy Ghost is not for today miracles are not for today that is the least in the kingdom how many don’t want to be the least in the kingdom yeah they not only disbelieve God’s word but they teach others but the greatest is the mature ones and
Who is least and who is greatest in the kingdom?

Matthew 5:19: Whoever therefore breaks one of the least of these commandments, and teaches men so, shall be called least in the kingdom of heaven; but whoever does and teaches them, he shall be called great in the kingdom of heaven. Hebrews 6:1-2: Therefore, leaving the discussion of the elementary principles of Christ, let us go on to perfection, not laying again the foundation of repentance from dead works and of faith toward God, of the doctrine of baptisms, of laying on of hands, of resurrection of the dead, and of eternal judgment.
What does the Holy Ghost coming on Mary show?

The angel told Mary the Holy Ghost would come upon her and the power of the Highest overshadow her (Luke 1:35)—the Holy Ghost is the power of God. Galatians 4:19: God wants Christ formed in us spiritually. Don’t knock babies in the church, and look to Jesus the author and finisher of your faith.
What does the Holy Ghost coming on Mary show?

maturity is righteousness it says just in Hebrews 5 just before this this verses and so the greatest in the kingdom teaches righteousness and does it and so John teaches us tremendous truths the next account of the Holy Spirit is Mary the Holy Ghost told Mary I mean the angel told Mary that the Holy Ghost shall come upon you the power of the highest shall overshadow you and that which is conceived in you is of the Holy Ghost and so the power of the highest God the power of God. Is the Holy. Ghost the Holy Ghost is the power God the Holy Spirit is that part of God that is working on earth with mankind to make him successful spiritually naturally and in their family it is a thing that works with us now Galatians 4:19 says Christ be formed in you just like Christ was formed in Mary in the natural God wants to form Christ in us in the spiritual and make us the greatest in the kingdom not the least and so yes the church has babies and the early church had babies and they sinned and they had their problems but also in the church there is righteous people disciplined people mature people and those babies.
What does the Holy Ghost coming on Mary show?

Luke 1:35: And the angel answered and said to her, “The Holy Spirit will come upon you, and the power of the Highest will overshadow you; therefore, also, that Holy One who is to be born will be called the Son of God. Galatians 4:19: My little children, for whom I labor in birth again until Christ is formed in you, Hebrews 12:2: looking unto Jesus, the author and finisher of our faith, who for the joy that was set before Him endured the cross, despising the shame, and has sat down at the right hand of the throne of God.
What happened to Elizabeth and Zacharias?

When Mary greeted Elizabeth, the baby leaped for joy and Elizabeth, filled with the Holy Ghost, prophesied things not yet revealed. Zacharias, whose barren wife bore John in old age, was filled with the Holy Ghost and prophesied. Sons and daughters prophesy, so God uses women in the church while keeping structure in the home.
What happened to Elizabeth and Zacharias?

As three years or so goes by can be mature themselves so don’t knock the babies but don’t knock the church because we have babies in there that don’t obey God’s word and teach wrong look to Jesus the author and the finisher of your faith the third account is Mary went down to visit. Elizabeth who was pregnant now 6 months with John the baptist and remember the angel said he’s going to be filled with the Holy Ghost from his mother’s womb okay when Mary came in and said hi to Elizabeth the Holy Ghost came upon Mary and the baby leaped in her womb for what joy 6 months old leaping in the womb for joy you see because Elizabeth was filled with the Holy Ghost the baby is filled with the Holy Ghost just like if if you take drugs as a pregnant mother the baby’s going to get those. Drugs okay so John was filled with the Holy Ghost in the womb when his mother was filled with the Holy Ghost are you with me all. Right and she began to prophesy she began to speak she began to say things that people didn’t know see that’s prophecy that’s Revelation prophecy that’s the office of a prophet when you are declaring things that hasn’t been revealed that’s the office of a prophet and she’s a woman of all things. Prophesying the next one one is Zacharias it’s number four as it was said earlier Zacharias and his wife was old she was barren she had went past the age of being able to have children yet when the Holy Ghost came upon her restored her womb a miracle took place her womb was restored and even at an old age she birthed John the baptist got pregnant with John the baptist and Zacharias when John was born was filled with the Holy Ghost and gave a tremendous. Prophecy tremendous you can read it there in Luke and so just like the Old Testament said he’s going to pour out his spirit on all flesh your sons and daughters shall what. Prophesy is a son a male is a daughter a female your sons your females and your males will what prophesy they’re going to be filled with the Holy Spirit how can you silence women in the church when God said I’m going to pour it out on both. p: From 1 Corinthians 12:28 Pastor David G. Kincer shows God sets people in the church as he wills, ranked from apostles, prophets and teachers down to tongues. He explains the gifts of the Spirit, why the best gifts are those that edify, and why love is the more excellent way—showing what love looks like, why prophecy and tongues have not ceased, and how the fruit of the Spirit grows.
Who sets people in their place in the church?

What is the order of priority in 1 Corinthians 12:28?

First apostles (ambassadors with full authority), second prophets (who predict and are right every time), third teachers who explain the whole counsel of God, fourth miracles, then healings, helps (aides like ushers and office workers—your high calling if God set you there), governments or administrations, and diversities of tongues last.

tg: Bible Morality Banned by Wimps and Born by Warriors
p: From Philippians 3:13–14 the speaker calls hearers to forget what is behind and press to God’s top goal—loving God and neighbor (Matthew 22) and the church—by adding virtue, knowledge, self-control, patience, godliness, brotherly love, and love (2 Peter 1). items.d: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer sets Jeremiah 31 and 32 in the middle of Israel’s captivity and shows the hope God gave there: a new, everlasting covenant in which God puts His Word in our hearts…
p: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer sets Jeremiah 31 and 32 in the middle of Israel’s captivity and shows the hope God gave there: a new, everlasting covenant in which God puts His Word in our hearts, forgives, and promises to do us good. He then lays out our part, to repent, believe the gospel, confess Jesus as Lord and receive Him, and uses the butterfly and 1 John 2 to describe growing from baby to child to young man to father in Christ.
What was happening in Israel when Jeremiah 31 and 32 were written?

He says Josiah was the last good king, but his son “burned the Scriptures” and did evil before God, the first captivity came, and later the king of Babylon burned Jerusalem and destroyed the temple. He says Jeremiah 32 was written about ten years after that, and asks, “If Israel had hope, do we have hope?”
What was happening in Israel when Jeremiah 31 and 32 were written?

Okay, we’re going to go to Jeremiah chapter 31 and 32, but we want you to understand and remember when these chapters were written. Okay? You remember a few lessons ago we showed you that Josiah was the last good king of Israel. All right, looks like Israel was going to avoid the captivity and everything, because Josiah really turned to God, got the nation to turn to God, reinstituted the feast and the things of God. But then his son came on the throne. How many of you had children that didn’t follow your ways? Jehoiakim came up. He reigned 11 years, and he burned the Scriptures, just burned them, and he did evil before God. He shed innocent blood. He committed abominations. Abominations is sexual immorality, homosexuality, idolatry, stealing, murder. In Proverbs 6:17, you remember, there’s seven things that the Lord, it’s called abominations: a lying tongue, a proud look, hands that shed innocent blood, he that devises wicked imaginations, feet that are swift to running to do evil, a false witness that repeats lies and speaks lies, and he that sows division among the brethren, and there’s many others. Okay? And he committed them. He committed them all. All right, he had wars, there were famine, there were plagues, and the first captivity came at the end of his term. Then [unclear] arose, and he was king, made king by the king of Babylon, and he only lasted three months, but the Bible just summed him up and said he did evil like [unclear] did. Now it was in this condition that chapter 31 was written. Hallelujah. I mean, we got serious calamity. America’s got calamities, but nothing this bad yet. So if Israel had hope, do we have hope? If Israel would have listened to Jeremiah, 31 and 32 could have saved them a lot of pain, and so can we. Hallelujah. Then we go down to Zedekiah. He reigned 11 years, and the second captivity came in the 11th year, and this time the king of Babylon destroyed and burned the city of Jerusalem, destroyed the temple. He imprisoned the preacher of righteousness, Jeremiah, and this is when Jeremiah 32 was written, okay, about 10 years later.
What was happening in Israel when Jeremiah 31 and 32 were written?

Proverbs 6:16-19: These six things the LORD hates, Yes, seven are an abomination to Him: A proud look, A lying tongue, Hands that shed innocent blood, A heart that devises wicked plans, Feet that are swift in running to evil, A false witness who speaks lies, And one who sows discord among brethren.
What is a covenant, and who keeps God’s part of the new covenant? (Jeremiah 31:31)

He says “a covenant is a contract,” like promising a lender to pay for a house: each side does its part. Of the new covenant he says, “this is God’s covenant, this is God’s contract, and this is God’s part,” and that God does it, not any preacher.
What is a covenant, and who keeps God’s part of the new covenant? (Jeremiah 31:31)

Now you got the picture. Things are really bad here, and the people keep being bad, they keep rejecting, and God keeps giving them hope. And this is what God says as we’re coming up. Remember, the false prophets are still prophesying falsely. How many of you know we got false prophets today, false teachers teaching their own doctrine? Temple leaders, the citizens, his own hometown tried to kill Jeremiah, tried to silence the Word of God. Everybody’s wanting to kill Jeremiah. The temple leaders tried to kill him, imprison him. And if you’re going to stand up for right, people are going to dislike you, and that’s one of the reasons we don’t stand up for right, is we don’t want people not liking us. Jeremiah 31:31: “The days come.” Here’s God talking in the midst of this, and watch, this is really simple. It’s just plain, clear English. This is what God says: “I will make a new covenant,” a fresh covenant, a fresh contract, “with Israel and Judah.” A covenant is a contract. If I go to buy a house, I promise the lender that I will pay the payments, I promise the government that I will pay the taxes, and they let me buy that house, live in it. If I don’t pay the payments or I don’t pay the taxes, they kick me out. See, they do their part, I have to do my part. So this is God’s covenant, this is God’s contract, and this is God’s part. This is what God says, this is what I will do. Who will do it? God. Not the Pope, not Billy Graham, not Martin Luther, not [unclear].
What is a covenant, and who keeps God’s part of the new covenant? (Jeremiah 31:31)
Jeremiah 31:31: “Behold, the days are coming, says the LORD, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah—
Will everyone in the new covenant know God, keep His commandments, and be forgiven? (Jeremiah 31:33-34)
