How can you just be satisfied with just being a saved Christian and not know the promise of the covenant that God promised to you, if you would do these simple things: turn from your sin, confess your sin, put your trust in Jesus’s death, burial, and resurrection, confessing Him as Lord, accept Him in your life? Then He said, “I will do all these things.”
What does he say Israel’s kings did that led up to the captivities?

He says Josiah turned the nation to God, but his son “burned the Scriptures,” shed innocent blood and committed abominations, listing the seven things the Lord hates from Proverbs 6:17. He says the first captivity came at the end of that king’s term.
What is a covenant, according to this message?

He says “a covenant is a contract.” He compares it to buying a house, where you promise the lender and the government to pay, “they do their part, I have to do my part,” and says the new covenant is God’s contract with God’s part and ours.
Does he say God forgives and forgets sin?
He says God says, “I’ll forgive it, I’ll render it zero, I’ll look at it like it never happened, and I will remember your sin no more.” He asks, “If God forgives us, shouldn’t we forgive ourselves?”
What does he say the fear of the Lord is?
He says, “depart from evil and hate evil. That’s the Bible definition of the fear of the Lord.”
What does he say about denominational names on churches?

He says Paul “plainly says there is one Lord, one Savior, one body, one baptism, one church,” and that putting a name on your church building and saying what you believe “doesn’t count.” He says all of us have the responsibility to line up to Him.
Is there another covenant coming after the new covenant?
No. He says it is the “everlasting” covenant and lists the Adamic, Noah, David and Moses covenants before it: “there ain’t no other covenant coming. This is it, and this is a good one.”
Why does he say God blesses those who obey His covenant?
He says God wants to bless your finances, health and life “because He wants to get the attention of your neighbor,” so they see it pays to serve God.
He says “repent: turn from your evil ways, adultery, stealing, and turn to right ways,” leave sin behind, and “believe the gospel.”
What does he say Luke 13:5 tells us we must do?
He reads, “Except you repent, you shall all likewise perish,” and says it doesn’t say “except you get baptized” or “except you witness”; “it says except you what? Repent. You turn.”
How does he say we confess our sins?
He says “I have to admit it with my mouth” and name what is wrong, and then, citing 1 John 1:9, “He is faithful to forgive, and not only forgive, but wash it off, cleanse me of the contamination.”
Does he say a Christian becomes mature right away?
No. He says “I’m not going to be zapped,” and says old Pentecostals thought “I’m totally mature now,” but “no, no, no,” you go from glory to glory, faith to faith, and salvation to salvation.
How can you tell which stage of Christian growth you are at?

He says, “you can identify where you’re at today.” If you have habitual sin you are a baby; if you don’t know the doctrines of Christ or believe in your own doctrines, you are a child; if you know the Bible and overcome the wicked one, you are a young man; fathers know Him and can birth others.
What does he say about relying only on Jesus as Savior?

He says “the Savior stage is the stage we got to go through,” like the caterpillar hatching from the egg, “but that wasn’t the goal.” The goal is “a beautiful butterfly,” so we need Jesus as teacher and then as Lord.
How many Christians does he say can tell him what the new covenant is?
He says “most Christians cannot tell me the covenant,” and over 90% have no idea when he asks, then asks how you can live in or inherit something you have no knowledge of.

items.t: How a Tax Exempt, New Testament Church Benefits Americans
items.d: Pastor David G. Kincer contrasts the federal 501(c)(3) definition of church—building, community aid, public-policy limits and no lobbying—with the Bible’s assembly of living stones focused on Jesus’ presence…
items.ser: Clarity on Crucial Choices · Full sermon
p: Pastor David G. Kincer contrasts the federal 501(c)(3) definition of church—building, community aid, public-policy limits and no lobbying—with the Bible’s assembly of living stones focused on Jesus’ presence, prayer, praise and truth. He argues public policy that silences the church while allowing other lobbies yields destroyed lives, and that a real New Testament gathering where each brings Spirit-led speech convicts unbelievers and benefits America more than welfare programs—while tax exemption keeps government from fighting God.
How does the federal government define a church?

He says they define it as a building where people congregate for worship, marriage, burial, communion and rites, with religious history and ordained ministers, and—most importantly—people congregated to give aid to the community via 501(c)(3).
How does the federal government define a church?

I want to thank you again and offer my appreciation for joining us on another session of clarity on crucial choices. Today we’re going to discuss how a tax-exempt New Testament church benefits America and Americans. What benefit does the New Testament church have for the people of America? We’re going to take a look first at the federal government’s definition of a church—how they define it, how they see it. First of all they say it is a building where people congregate to worship, marry, bury, serve communion, do other religious rites. Is this group must have a religious history, and this congregation of people ordained ministers such as priests, rabbis or so forth. But most importantly, as I have accented, it is a people congregated to give aid to the community. Now this is found in your 501(c)(3) instructions that almost every church gets a tax exemption by filling out this tax exemption form 501(c)(3). The second thing they define a church as is a
Why did a 1938 bill say churches get tax exemption?
H.R. 1860 argued government is compensated for lost tax by benefits from promoting general welfare—community aid saves the government money.
Why did a 1938 bill say churches get tax exemption?

House of Representatives bill—H.R. 1860, 75th Congress, third session in 1938—said the exemption from taxation of money or property devoted to charitable and other purposes, the church is based on the theory that the government is compensated for the loss of tax revenue by the benefits resulting from the promotion of the general welfare. The aid that the church gives to the community saves the government taxes, and therefore the government is compensated and can give a tax exemption.

He says a tax-exempt church must serve a public purpose for all the community and not be contrary to public policy, with no political lobbying or campaign involvement under separation of church and state.

Now that’s 501(c)(3) and this bill in the 1930s give us two of the definitions. The third one is there are restrictions, controls put upon the church by the federal government. Again quoting from the 501(c)(3) application and instruction in the IRS manual: an institution is a society or organization founded for religious, educational or social purposes. So an institution, a church seeking tax exemption, must serve a public purpose—in other words it’s got to serve all the people in the community
Who does he say can lobby when the church cannot?

He lists homosexuals, transvestites, transsexuals, pedophiles, NEA, feminists, NAACP, seniors, NRA and gun-control side, pro-Israel, pro-choice and Wicca—while the church (78% of America in his figure) is silenced.
Who does he say can lobby when the church cannot?

and not be contrary to public policy. In our generation we can’t be contrary to homosexuals, the unborn, illegal aliens, the capital punishment, right to bear arms, over-taxation, witchcraft—if the community and its public policy, we cannot contest it. All right. And it says absolutely no political lobbying or no involvement in campaign, and they use the excuse of the separation of church and state with the definition of church that they have. Now who can lobby and campaign? Well, homosexuals can, transvestites—those that dress like the opposite sex—transsexuals—those that change their sex—pedophiles—those that have sex with children—the National Education Association, the feminists, the NAACP, the seniors, the NRA and the other side wanting gun control. They can lobby. Pro-Israel or Jews can lobby. Pro-choice can lobby. Wicca or witchcraft can lobby. But not the church. These other people can be involved in campaign, speak about their candidates, but not the church, who is 78% of the population of America, and they are silenced by the restriction and controls of the 501(c)(3). Now we’re going to take a look at government policy, public policy benefits. What are the benefits of this public policy that the government puts upon the community? Well, it gives freedom to make harmful choices.
What results of harmful public policy does he cite?

Destroyed lives: 50% with STDs, 26,000 homosexual AIDS deaths a year, 450,000 tobacco deaths, 88,000 alcohol deaths and millions injured—policies putting birth control and abortion above self-control.
What results of harmful public policy does he cite?

And of course the results of these kind of public policies is destroyed lives. 50% of people in America have a sexually transmitted disease. 26,000 homosexuals are killed by AIDS every year. 450,000 people die from tobacco, and only 18% of Americans smoke. 88,000 people die from alcohol-related deaths and 4 million from alcohol-related injuries are hurt, and yet only 50% of Americans drink alcohol. So the public policy and the results are disastrous. They put abortion, birth control, above self-control. Birth control—
How does he contrast same-sex marriage with science?

He says science knows marriage is man-woman producing and raising kids; homosexuals cannot have kids naturally; no homosexual gene; AIDS stats versus civil-rights framing; evolution taught, creation censored.
How does he contrast same-sex marriage with science?

we just need to control ourselves. They put women’s rights over the scientific babies’ rights. Science has declared life begins at conception, but they don’t care. They put same-sex marriage above the Bible and science marriage. Even science knows that marriage is between a man and a woman because they can produce kids and they commit to a lifetime commitment to raise those kids and protect those kids. Homosexuals cannot have kids naturally; they have to take your kids. That’s science. But who cares about science or the Bible in America today? Same-sex lifestyle instead of a scientific fact they were not born that way—science has found there’s no homosexual gene. Homosexual civil rights versus science stats: AIDS kill 26,000 a year as we said before. And they put the unprovable evolution
What is the Bible’s definition of church?

Called-out assembly of Jesus’ followers—not a building or corporation. Acts 7:48 / Isaiah 66:1: God does not dwell in temples made with hands; 1 Corinthians 3:9 and 1 Peter 2:5: people are God’s building and living stones.
What is the Bible’s definition of church?

with Bible creation censored. They don’t like any opposition. Now let’s go and look at the Bible’s definition of the church and see how the Bible defines the church. First of all the word used in the Bible for church just simply means assembling—called out to assemble together. So a church is followers of Jesus and His word that come together, that congregate together. Church has nothing to do with a physical building. It has nothing to do with a corporation. A corporation is a company or group of people authorized to act as a single unit and recognized in civil law. The church is not a corporation. It is not a physical building. Acts 7:48 says, and is quoting from Isaiah 66:1, the Most High God does not dwell in temples, buildings made with hands. In Isaiah He explains that heaven is My throne, earth is My footstool—where are you going to put Me? I’m big. And so the Bible doesn’t back up our government’s definition of a church as a building where people congregate together. People can congregate for Christ anywhere—in the park, at a home or wherever—not some special building. 1 Corinthians 3:9 makes it plain: you, the followers of Christ, are God’s building. 1 Peter 2:5: you as living stones are built up a spiritual house to offer spiritual sacrifices. It is the people coming together that God is working with to build His spiritual house. He lives in the congregation of His people, and the people come together to offer up spiritual sacrifices—
What is the Bible’s definition of church?

Acts 7:48: “However, the Most High does not dwell in temples made with hands, as the prophet says: Isaiah 66:1: Thus says the LORD: “Heaven is My throne, And earth is My footstool. Where is the house that you will build Me? And where is the place of My rest? 1 Corinthians 3:9: For we are God’s fellow workers; you are God’s field, you are God’s building. 1 Peter 2:5: you also, as living stones, are being built up a spiritual house, a holy priesthood, to offer up spiritual sacrifices acceptable to God through Jesus Christ.
Is the church mainly a charitable welfare organization?
No. From Mark 14:6 Jesus prioritized the woman’s anointing over selling perfume for the poor—Jesus is the primary focus; aid has criteria (1 Timothy 5), not just handing out stuff.
Is the church mainly a charitable welfare organization?

not carnal, not fleshly offerings to God but spiritual ones. Continuing with the Bible definition of a church: the church is not a charitable or welfare organization. And Jesus made this clear when the woman with the alabaster box came—very expensive perfume—and anointed Jesus, and Judas and some others there go, this is ridiculous, this is a waste of money, this could have been sold and given to the poor and help the poor. And what was Jesus’ reply to these people? Leave her alone. Mark 14:6: leave this woman alone; she’s done a good work for Me to anoint My body for burial. You always have the poor with you, and whenever you want to you can do them good, you can help them, but Me you don’t always have with you. So in the church Jesus is the primary and high-ranking focus of the church. The first priority of spiritual sacrifices is ministering unto the presence of Jesus—not giving medical, food or clothing to the poor. Matthew 18:20 makes it very clear: where two or three are gathered in My name—see, the gathering of the people that follow Christ and His word—I am there in the midst. The important factor, the high priority factor when a church comes together is to bring the presence of Jesus Christ. The criteria for church aid by the way is found in 1 Timothy 5:8: if anyone does not provide for his own and especially for his immediate family he has denied the faith and is worse than an unbeliever. No widow may be put on the list of widows unless she is over 60 years of age, had been faithful to her husband while he was alive and known for good deeds such as bringing up children, helping those that were in trouble and so forth. There were qualifications—not just handing out stuff. The church—continuing with the Bible’s definition of a church—we found that the church is an assembly of followers, and when they assemble together they assemble together to pray, to worship, to bless or speak good of God and one another, to thank—tell God that we appreciate Him—and to praise Jesus. So prayer, as the Bible says according to His will, is another spiritual sacrifice that we do in the church.
Is the church mainly a charitable welfare organization?

Mark 14:6: But Jesus said, “Let her alone. Why do you trouble her? She has done a good work for Me. Matthew 18:20: For where two or three are gathered together in My name, I am there in the midst of them.” 1 Timothy 5:8: But if anyone does not provide for his own, and especially for those of his household, he has denied the faith and is worse than an unbeliever.
What is the house of God for?
Mark 11:17: house of prayer for all nations, not merchandise. Hebrews 13:15 and John 4:23: continual praise and true worship; Psalm 22:3: He inhabits praises.
What is the house of God for?

Mark 11:17: My house shall be called a house of prayer for all nations—Chinese, Australia, Russians, whoever, homosexuals, humanists, atheists, all nations, all people—but you have made it a den of thieves. And to America, just like then in the New Testament time they made the house a house of merchandise. The house of God is not for making money and merchandising; it’s for prayer— very limited in American churches. Hebrews 13:15: by Jesus let us offer continually the sacrifice of praise to God, that is the fruit of our lips giving thanks to His name. See, the New Testament church is a church that comes together to boast and brag and honor Jesus Christ and thank Him for His blood and His goodness. John 4:23: true worshipers will worship the Father in spirit and in truth, for the Father is seeking such to worship Him. So when the church comes together they adore Him—not only praise Him but they adore Him, they love Him. Psalm 34:1: I will bless the Lord at all times—no matter what condition I’m in I’ll speak good of the Lord, I’ll speak good of His word, I’ll speak good of the church. His praise shall continually be in my mouth. And Psalm 22:3 says He inhabits the praises of His people.
What is the house of God for?

Mark 11:17: Then He taught, saying to them, “Is it not written, ‘My house shall be called a house of prayer for all nations’? But you have made it a ‘den of thieves.’ ” Hebrews 13:15: Therefore by Him let us continually offer the sacrifice of praise to God, that is, the fruit of our lips, giving thanks to His name. John 4:23: But the hour is coming, and now is, when the true worshipers will worship the Father in spirit and truth; for the Father is seeking such to worship Him. Psalm 22:3: But You are holy, Enthroned in the praises of Israel.
How is the church the pillar of truth and a disciple-maker?

John 8:32 and 17:17: continue in the word; 1 Timothy 3:15: pillar of truth. Matthew 28:19 and Luke 24:47: make disciples of all nations and preach repentance and forgiveness—including to atheists and humanists.
How is the church the pillar of truth and a disciple-maker?

Continuing with the Bible’s definition of a church: the fourth description of God’s church—an assembly of followers of the Bible and Jesus that speaks and lives truth. John 8:32: Jesus said if you continue in My word you are My disciples indeed, and you shall know the truth, and the truth shall make you free. Chapter 17 verse 17 of John: God’s word is truth. So the followers speak the truth—not their opinions, not psychology and philosophies but the truth. 1 Timothy 3:15: these things I write to you so you may know how to conduct yourself in the house of God. He just gave us what we’re to do when we come together. The house of God which is the church—they’re synonymous terms—the church of the living God. His presence is there when we congregate together, and the church is the pillar and support of truth. We back up truth, not opinions. We back up truth, not lies. Matthew 28:19: Jesus said go make disciples of all nations, teaching them to observe all things that I have commanded you—not only to teach them but emphasize that they practice them. And all nations includes the atheists, the humanists, the homosexuals, the hedonists, the religionists, and any nationality that you can think of. Luke 24:47: Jesus said repentance and remission, forgiveness of sins, should be preached in His name among all nations. That is a primary message of the church: that people need to turn from sin and that’s how you give forgiveness.
How is the church the pillar of truth and a disciple-maker?

John 8:32: And you shall know the truth, and the truth shall make you free.” 1 Timothy 3:15: but if I am delayed, I write so that you may know how you ought to conduct yourself in the house of God, which is the church of the living God, the pillar and ground of the truth. Matthew 28:19: Go therefore and make disciples of all the nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, Luke 24:47: and that repentance and remission of sins should be preached in His name to all nations, beginning at Jerusalem.
What speech gifts should build the church?

From 1 Corinthians 12–14 and Ephesians 5:19 he lists wisdom, knowledge, prophecy (edify/exhort/comfort), tongues with interpretation, revelation, teaching, psalms, hymns and spiritual songs—by the Spirit, not intellect.
What speech gifts should build the church?

Humanists, their followers and humanist churches don’t preach Jesus’s truth to turn immoral people to morality. Instead they teach immoral behavior is acceptable and they sentence people to preventable deaths, physical harm such as sexually transmitted diseases and other harms. And we need to preach repentance for forgiveness of sin every church. There are eight sources of speaking—and I left out prayer because most prayer is us talking to our God personally. 1 Corinthians 12:8: a gift is given to one by the Spirit the word of wisdom—it’s an ability to speak the word of wisdom. You hardly ever hear that in the church world today. Hasn’t been restored yet in my opinion. To another by the Spirit is given the word of knowledge—they actually get into the word and God opens the word up and they have knowledge of the word. To another, prophecy—and this word prophecy is edification, exhortation, comfort. It is not the office of a prophet to predict the future and it comes to pass. He’s using prophecy—speaking by the inspiration of God—to build the church. Tongues: to another tongues. And this is a big argument in America today, but tongues are Bible languages whether they are earthly or whether they’re heavenly. And Paul said if there’s no interpretation you can’t do it in the church because there’s no understanding. So he says to another’s given interpretation. Then in 14:6 he says what shall I profit you unless I speak to you either by revelation or teaching. Revelation is the uncovering of a truth revealed to you. Ephesians 5:19: speaking to yourselves in psalms, hymns and spiritual songs. See, music: hymns. Psalms is singing—singing Scripture. Hymns is a song of truth put together. And music and singing is very important. They carry a heavy weight in the New Testament church. And all this is to be done by the Spirit, not human intellect. You can’t go and get these things by human intellect. Teaching is basically what most of the church world is doing. You hardly ever hear a word of wisdom, a word of knowledge. I know what they call knowledge, but that’s not what this is. Teaching is basically what we’re doing—and they don’t even have the credentials of a teacher, they just teach. So to answer our question at the beginning: what are the benefits of a New Testament tax-exempt church service?
What speech gifts should build the church?

1 Corinthians 12:8: for to one is given the word of wisdom through the Spirit, to another the word of knowledge through the same Spirit, Ephesians 5:19: speaking to one another in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing and making melody in your heart to the Lord,
What should each person bring when the church gathers?
1 Corinthians 14:26: each contributes song, teaching, tongue, revelation or interpretation for edification—not primarily food, clothing, medicine or 12-step programs.
What should each person bring when the church gathers?

1 Corinthians 14:26: when you come together—see, here we are, the church comes together—each of you, see, all of us, come with something to contribute: a song, song music, maybe your instrument play, maybe you’re a singer, whatever, maybe you’re just in the congregation and you lift up your voice and sing; a teaching; a tongue, a language; a revelation. He’s given five of the eight things listed here. And the other has an interpretation—come be ready to interpret a language. And let all things be done to edification—building, encouraging the people of God. Not when you come have food for the hungry, clothing for the naked, medicine for the sick and a 12-step recovery program for those who have gone through traumatic things.
What should each person bring when the church gathers?

1 Corinthians 14:26: How is it then, brethren? Whenever you come together, each of you has a psalm, has a teaching, has a tongue, has a revelation, has an interpretation. Let all things be done for edification.
How does that kind of service benefit America?

If all prophesy, an unbeliever is convinced and convicted, secrets revealed, falls and worships—encounter with Jesus. That spiritual awakening benefits community higher than anything else; tax exemption matters because it’s Jesus’s church.
How does that kind of service benefit America?

He didn’t say to bring that. 1 Corinthians 14:24: if all prophesy—speak and sing by the inspiration of the Spirit—and an unbeliever, unlearned, comes into the service, he is convinced by all of these things, he is convicted by all of these things—the songs, the prophecies, everything that’s going on. The secrets of his heart are revealed to him, and falling down on his face without being told to he will worship God and report God is truly in the midst of that church. Why? Because this unbeliever or unlearned person had an encounter with Him and God spoke to him what needed to be changed in his life. And that benefits America and a community higher than anything can—a spiritual awakening, a spiritual encounter with the person of Jesus Christ because God’s people come to bring something to contribute. New Testament church tax exempt benefits. All right, there’s an argument whether the church should be tax exempt or not. And the church is going to be a church whether we get tax exemption or not. But why is it important that our founding fathers and up to this present time gave a tax exemption to the church? Well, first of all it’s Jesus’s church
How does that kind of service benefit America?

1 Corinthians 14:24-25: But if all prophesy, and an unbeliever or an uninformed person comes in, he is convinced by all, he is convicted by all. And thus the secrets of his heart are revealed; and so, falling down on his face, he will worship God and report that God is truly among you.
Why tax exemption and the First Amendment?

Acts 5:39: if of God you cannot overthrow it lest you fight God—regulating by tax fights God. Separation was to keep government out of the church, not Christians out of government. Truth saves costs and gives eternal life; helping the poor is on the side.
Why tax exemption and the First Amendment?

and He can’t be restrained by tax or immoral laws. Acts 5:39: if it be of God, if anything be of God, you cannot overthrow it lest you be found fighting against God. And it’s God’s church, and if you try to regulate the church by taxation or tax benefits you’re going to be fighting against God directly Himself. And the separation of church and state was instituted by our government—the First Amendment—to keep government out of the affairs of the church. It wasn’t to keep Christians out of the affairs of government. It teaches Bible truths. A New Testament tax-exempt church—a real New Testament—there’s a lot of not-real New Testament churches—and truths protect people from preventable deaths, physical harm, mental harm, prevent emotional harm, thus saving families and government billions of dollars in medical, legal costs, police costs, criminal and immorality of all kinds of costs every year, every year. So besides that we give people eternal life, which is to know Jesus and God, and on the side we do help the poor.
Why tax exemption and the First Amendment?
Acts 5:39: but if it is of God, you cannot overthrow it—lest you even be found to fight against God.”
What does 501(c)(3) emphasize about a church?
He stresses people congregated to give aid to the community as the key federal accent.
May a 501(c)(3) church lobby or campaign?
He says absolutely no political lobbying or campaign involvement under their rules.
What percent of Americans does he say are the church?
He says 78% of the population, silenced by 501(c)(3) controls.
When does he say science says life begins?
At conception—yet he says women’s rights are put over the baby’s rights.
Is the church a physical building?
No. God does not dwell in temples made with hands; people are God’s building and living stones.
Did Jesus dismiss helping the poor?
No—He said you always have the poor and can help them whenever you want, but prioritized anointing Him then.
Who could be on the widow list in 1 Timothy 5?
Over 60, faithful to her husband, known for good deeds—not just handing out aid.
When may tongues be used in church?
He says if there’s no interpretation you can’t do it in church because there’s no understanding.
What happens if an unbeliever enters a prophesying service?
Convinced and convicted, heart secrets revealed, falls and worships, reporting God is truly among them.
What was separation of church and state for, in his view?
To keep government out of the church’s affairs—not to keep Christians out of government’s affairs.

items.t: How Do Some Civil Leaders Get into Office? — August 30, 2020
items.d: Pastor David G. Kincer defends America’s founders and calls abortion and same-sex marriage unrighteous decrees. He teaches that the Most High rules in the kingdom of men, setting up and removing kings and even…
p: Pastor David G. Kincer defends America’s founders and calls abortion and same-sex marriage unrighteous decrees. He teaches that the Most High rules in the kingdom of men, setting up and removing kings and even using evil rulers to correct His people. He reads Matthew 24 as fulfilled in Jerusalem’s fall and points to the coming great restoration.
No. After 244 years of liberty, it is wrong to call the 56 signers godless madmen.

They’re going to be at the national mall in washington dc on September 26. Next month. And if they’re going to be joining together prayer repentance a lot of groups are involved billy graham evangelistic association. Calvary chapel church a lot of big. Groups and churches are gathering together for this and so we want to promote it and be a part of this event so to spread the word about it you can go to your face you can go to this website it’s called the return.org. For the return.org easy. And you go down. To the video it says about the return. And you click on this little link here and you click on share. And it’ll give you options to share on. Facebook this doesn’t give me the options but on my phone you can click on facebook and you can post to your facebook account directly from the menu okay it’s pretty easy so you can share on your facebook with uh and everybody will hear about it all your friends may not be your friends anymore. But you can share online about this event. And uh. Right now we’re not sure on what our involvement is going to be we most likely will be here on the 26th. Uh but I need to confirm that and we’re going to stream it from the church on the Saturday the 26th this event going on so that is the update. Thank you so uh mrs daigle if I missed anything please let me know. Proverbs 24:16: For a righteous man may fall seven times And rise again, But the wicked shall fall by calamity.

God does; the Most High rules over every government of men.

items.t: How Do We Know That We Know God?
items.d: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer teaches from John 17:1–4 that eternal life is knowing the only true God and Jesus Christ, that only God gives it, and that we receive it in proportion to a hearing ear.…
p: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer teaches from John 17:1–4 that eternal life is knowing the only true God and Jesus Christ, that only God gives it, and that we receive it in proportion to a hearing ear. He explains how to know that we know God: the Spirit within us, keeping His commandments, being born again, and growing in the word.
What does “the hour has come” mean in John 17:1-4?

He says John 17:1–4 is about knowing God and Jesus Christ, a very basic and powerful teaching of the Bible. He says God glorified Jesus through the virgin birth, His miracles, and mostly His death, burial and resurrection, and Jesus glorifies the Father “by reconciling people back to the father.”
What does “the hour has come” mean in John 17:1-4?

Now today we’re going to be talking about knowing God and Jesus Christ. This is a very very basic teaching of the Bible and very powerful. All right. Knowing— and Catholics and Protestants alike are ignoring this important doctrine. Okay. We open the book here and it’s John 17:1-4: “Father, the hour is come.” The time has come. Appointed time has come. A season has come. Okay. What time? What season? Okay. And then he explains what’s come. “Now glorify your Son, that your Son might also glorify You.” Now God glorified Jesus by him being born of a virgin, preaching the gospel, doing miracles, bringing many into the kingdom. But mostly his death, burial, and resurrection. That’s how God honored. Glorify means honored. He honored the son with the ability to give his life. No one could take it. He had to give up his life and then he took it back again. And then how does Jesus glorify the father? By reconciling people back to the father. You see, and the time is here. We’re in that season. Jesus died on the cross. He, he went into the grave, rose again, and for the forgiveness of sin for the cleansing of sin for the freedom of sin and that we might receive him and have him living in us.
What does “the hour has come” mean in John 17:1-4?

John 17:1-4: Jesus spoke these words, lifted up His eyes to heaven, and said: “Father, the hour has come. Glorify Your Son, that Your Son also may glorify You, as You have given Him authority over all flesh, that He should give eternal life to as many as You have given Him. And this is eternal life, that they may know You, the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom You have sent. I have glorified You on the earth. I have finished the work which You have given Me to do.

He says Jesus has authority over all flesh and gives eternal life to as many as the Father gave Him, so “nobody on earth can give you eternal life but God and Jesus Christ.” He says “The church is simply a messenger,” and he is a messenger who can’t give you anything.

That’s how God glorify Jesus. All right. Then Jesus in turn reconciles us back to God and gives honor to God. Number two, you’ve given him Jesus authority over all flesh. Okay? Jesus has been given authority over everybody and every nation and every language upon the earth. He is the one running the kingdoms. All right, that’s number two. The hour is here and it’s been here. This season’s been here before creation. Not just when Jesus came in the flesh, but he was given this before creation. He created everything. He has that kind of authority. Number three, that he give eternal life to as many as you’ve given him. Now, this is quite a statement. You see, he gives eternal life to as many as God has given him. So we see here that God and Jesus Christ are involved in the process of eternal life. Not your church, not your pastor, not some author, nobody on earth can give you eternal life but God and Jesus Christ. The church is simply a messenger. I am a messenger. I can’t give you anything. I know a lot of priests and the pope and everybody, they act like they have something to give. But nobody can give you anything in the Bible. God gives it. Think on that. We have the tendency because somebody has some speaking skills or charisma to think that they possess something and they can give it to us. They can’t. There is no one on earth that can give you eternal life. Muhammad cannot give you eternal life. Nor can the Muslim religion. Only Jesus Christ can give you eternal life. And it says so right here. Ain’t that right? Very powerful. And he gives it to as many as the father gives him. Wow. So both God and the father are involved in us possessing eternal life. Then number four he says this is eternal life.
John 17:2: as You have given Him authority over all flesh, that He should give eternal life to as many as You have given Him.
Do all religions lead to the same God? (John 17:3)

He says John 17:3 defines eternal life as knowing “the only true God,” and “There’s only one God,” not the same God in every religion. He says the Bible explains exactly who this God is, “when you deflect from anything that he is, you got the wrong God,” and that Christians seek eternal life, not enlightenment.
Do all religions lead to the same God? (John 17:3)

He gives a definition of eternal life that they may know you the only true God. The only true God. There’s only one God. And don’t give me this stuff that Buddha and Muslims and Hindus all lead to the same. No, the Bible explains exactly who this one God is. And when you deflect from anything that he is, you got the wrong God. Amen. See, we’re not looking for enlightenment. We’re looking for eternal life. The Buddhists are looking for some kind of enlightenment, an arena where they’re not reincarnated anymore. And the Muslims are looking for a harem in heaven, a— women. That is stupid. You got God in heaven and you want a woman. I mean, how secular, how fleshly can you get? Are you with me? See, that just nullifies their God. See, now let’s take a look at these four things. We already know that Jesus has already died on the cross, rose again. Okay, God has glorified him and he has glorified the father by obeying his word and reconciling people by his blood to God. We already know that, right? That’s just basic Bible. Now you have given him authority over all flesh. Let’s check and see if historically in the scriptures this is true that Jesus Christ has authority over all mankind.
Do all religions lead to the same God? (John 17:3)
John 17:3: And this is eternal life, that they may know You, the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom You have sent.
Does Jesus have authority over all flesh, and why must the Lord of the harvest be involved? (Matthew 28:18, Daniel 7:14, Matthew 9:38)

He cites Matthew 28:18, 1 Peter 3:22 and Daniel 7:14 to say Jesus has authority over the spirit world and the earth, and is “the leader and ruler of all of them.” He cites Matthew 9:38 and says the Lord of the harvest has to be involved, using a picture of grain ground and baked into bread. He says churches that skirt the Lord of the harvest just to fill their buildings are “wasting your time,” and “We are just messengers.”
Does Jesus have authority over all flesh, and why must the Lord of the harvest be involved? (Matthew 28:18, Daniel 7:14, Matthew 9:38)

Matthew 28:18: “All power is given unto me,” Jesus said, “in heaven and in earth.” In heaven is the spirit world. That’s where the angels are, the seraphims are, the demons are. Satan is. So he has authority over that whole spirit world and he has authority over the earth where humans are. Amen. And he has how much authority? All. 1 Peter 3:22: “Angels, authorities, and powers being made subject unto him.” Angels are in the spirit world. Authorities, Satan, and principalities and powers of darkness are in the spirit world. Governors and presidents and kings and so forth are in the earthly world, mayors and governors and so forth. And he is what? He is the leader and ruler of all of them. But Daniel says it the best. Daniel 7:14: “There was given unto him dominion, glory, and a kingdom, that all people, nations, and languages should—“ what? “Serve him.” He has authority over all flesh. Matthew 9:38: “Pray the Lord of the harvest to send out laborers into his harvest.” Jesus said, “The field is mankind.” The seed is the word of God, and the harvest is ripe, ready to be harvest. So, we need the Lord of the harvest to be involved in reaching people and harvesting them, don’t we? Yeah. It’s the Lord of the harvest that has the knowledge and the authority to plant the seed and make it grow and then cut it down and put it in the barn and then bring it out and thresh it so it to separate the stalk and the husk from the grain. And then he puts it to the grinder and has all those kernels of grain ground into one body, one [unclear], losing their identity. And he knows how to put yeast in it, his spirit, and impregnate that, and put it in his oven, his fiery trials, so that it bakes and makes bread for the master’s table. That’s the Lord of the harvest. And you try leading people into eternal life without going through the Lord of the harvest, you’re wasting your time. You get it? He does have this power. And too many churches and too many ministers are skirting the Lord of the harvest just trying to get the churches filled. Folks, that don’t work. The Lord of the harvest has got to be involved in this. He’s the one that can do the job. We are just messengers. Could that be true? And if we do our part and message right, he will do his part and save those that will believe. So we find that’s true. Now what authority does Jesus have to benefit mankind through his death, burial, and resurrection? See, what kind of authority does he have to benefit mankind? And he has authority over all flesh. It says in point number three that God gives people to Jesus to give them eternal life. And so I turned that around and I asked the question, how are you interested in how God’s going to do this? How does God give people to Jesus and then Jesus gives them eternal life?
Does Jesus have authority over all flesh, and why must the Lord of the harvest be involved? (Matthew 28:18, Daniel 7:14, Matthew 9:38)

Matthew 28:18: And Jesus came and spoke to them, saying, “All authority has been given to Me in heaven and on earth. 1 Peter 3:22: who has gone into heaven and is at the right hand of God, angels and authorities and powers having been made subject to Him. Daniel 7:14: Then to Him was given dominion and glory and a kingdom, That all peoples, nations, and languages should serve Him. His dominion is an everlasting dominion, Which shall not pass away, And His kingdom the one Which shall not be destroyed. Matthew 9:38: Therefore pray the Lord of the harvest to send out laborers into His harvest.”
What does it mean to “take heed what you hear”? (Mark 4:23-24)

He cites Mark 4:23 on having “a hearing ear,” and says take heed means to understand, consider, apply and then experience the result. He uses a can labeled “Organic pumpkin” that opens to something that looks like tomatoes, to show that we must open things up and find out what is really inside.
What does it mean to “take heed what you hear”? (Mark 4:23-24)

Have any interest in seeing the answer to that question? See, this is imperative for us. Mark 4:23: “If anyone has ears to hear, let him—“ what? “Hear.” So, we need what? A hearing ear. And then he explains what kind of hearing ear. He said to them, “Take heed what you hear.” Now that word take heed is a complex word meaning you got to understand, you got to consider it. You got to understand it, you got to apply it and then you experience the result of it. Okay? For instance, now I know you guys go to school and you’re really intelligent. What does it say on that can? Organic pumpkin. Organic pumpkin. All right. What does it say? Organic pumpkin. So, he was right. Right. Okay. So, what are we going to find when we open this can? Pumpkin. Organic pumpkin. But how are we going to know unless we what? Apply and find out what’s really in the can. Okay, here you go. You guys know how to use a can opener? There you go. Open that can up for me. Now, guys, is that pumpkin? No. No, it’s not. No, but the can says pumpkin. It looks like salsa. It looks like tomatoes. Huh? Yeah. Is it tomatoes? Maybe. Is that a tomato? No.
What does it mean to “take heed what you hear”? (Mark 4:23-24)

Mark 4:23: If anyone has ears to hear, let him hear.” Mark 4:24: Then He said to them, “Take heed what you hear. With the same measure you use, it will be measured to you; and to you who hear, more will be given.
Should we dig deeper into what preachers tell us?

He says too many do not dig deeper to find out if what preachers say is true, so “we don’t experience the truth.” He says “a lot of people think they’re good on the inside until their inside is open.” He says a church leader has no authority to change what the Bible says: “You cannot change the word of God.”
Should we dig deeper into what preachers tell us?

Yes. Huh? That looks like it. Yeah, looks like tomato. You see, too many of us do not dig deeper and find out if what preachers are telling us is the truth. We don’t apply, we don’t put time into it, and so we don’t experience the truth. See, a lot of people think they’re good on the inside until their inside is open. All right? So, we need to put time in to what we’re hearing. Could that be an amen, church? You can’t just believe the pope. The pope just said that homosexuals is an acceptable thing. You know, the Catholic Church has got to change things for— The pope has no authority to do that.
What does “with what measure you mete” mean? (Mark 4:24)

He says measure means a standard of measure, and uses a teaspoon, a cup and a hose to show that the more time we put into seeking God, the more water we have to clean the house. He says Jesus said, “Out of your innermost being, rivers of water would flow,” a continuous flow that can cleanse us, our house and “the whole nation.”
What does “with what measure you mete” mean? (Mark 4:24)

You cannot change the word of God. Amen. See, the can doesn’t have the right stuff in it. Now, “with what measure you mete”: measure means a standard of measure. See that’s like this cup here. This is the two cup— cup. This is a teaspoon. All right. What standard of measure you meet? Which means to give out— what measure you give out is going to be measured, [unclear] given back to you. So, we want to clean the barn. All right. So, we get a teaspoon. We get a teaspoon and we’re going to clean this barn. Doesn’t do anything, does it? Okay. We go back to God and say, “God, it didn’t work.” You know, he said, “Well, get a bigger measure.” Okay, so instead of putting two minutes a day into God, we put five. And so we get more water. And God says, “Now clean your house. Clean the house.” So we didn’t work. There’s not enough water to get the job done, is there? Okay, God, it didn’t work. What do I do now? Well, get a bigger measure. Okay. All right, God. I’m going to get a bigger measure. Here we go. And I want you to clean yourself. Hallelujah. Clean the house. It didn’t work. See, we put 15 minutes into the day of seeking God and we got more, but we don’t have enough to get the job done. So then God says, “Have you ever read in the scriptures out of your innermost being, rivers of water would flow out?” Okay, God, I got it. I get a hose that has an endless supply of water. Now, can I clean the church? Yes. Yes. You see, we’re looking for teaspoons in cups. David said, “My cup runneth over.” Elijah filled the barrels with water. But Jesus said, “Out of your innermost being, rivers of water would flow.” A continuous flow of water that can not only cleanse us and our house and those around us, but the whole nation.
What does “with what measure you mete” mean? (Mark 4:24)

Mark 4:24: Then He said to them, “Take heed what you hear. With the same measure you use, it will be measured to you; and to you who hear, more will be given. John 7:38: He who believes in Me, as the Scripture has said, out of his heart will flow rivers of living water.”
How does hearing lead to more being given? (Mark 4:24-25)

He says “To you who hear, more will be given,” and when we respond to what God gave, He gives us more, which is how “we grow in grace.” He says whoever has not a hearing ear, even what he has “will be taken from him,” including a little faith and a little grace because they are not growing.
How does hearing lead to more being given? (Mark 4:24-25)

It’s an endless supply. But then you got to put in more time to get that water. Are you there? You got to read the word and you got to understand the word. So this is how they give us eternal life. They become involved and they respond with the response that you respond back. To you who hear, more will be given. See, they that hear and then they take what God has given them. Though God gives back more than he gave them. And when they respond and give God back, he responds and gives us more. And that’s how we grow in grace and things. For whosoever has whosoever has what? Faith, grace, a big church, a little church. No. Whosoever has ears to hear, more will be given. You see, we have to hear, understand, apply, and then we experience the results of what God said. Whosoever has not has not what? A hearing ear. Even that which he has will be taken from him. That little bit of faith that he has will be taken away. That little bit of grace that he has will be taken away because they’re not growing in faith. They’re not growing in grace. Now, isn’t that pretty clear? And that’s how God gets involved in our life and gives us eternal life by your response. Do we really know him? This is eternal life. The fourth principle was the fourth thing that we’re in the season of that they may know you, the only true God and Jesus Christ whom you have sent. That’s a powerful emphasis. Powerful. I can know God and I can know Jesus Christ. I can really know. See, these guys knew what was in the can when they opened the can. They knew it wasn’t pumpkin. They knew it was tomato.
How does hearing lead to more being given? (Mark 4:24-25)

Mark 4:24-25: Then He said to them, “Take heed what you hear. With the same measure you use, it will be measured to you; and to you who hear, more will be given. For whoever has, to him more will be given; but whoever does not have, even what he has will be taken away from him.” Mark 4:25: For whoever has, to him more will be given; but whoever does not have, even what he has will be taken away from him.”
How can I get to know God? (1 John 4:13, Ezekiel 36:27)

He says God promised we can know Him, and cites 1 John 4:13, “we dwell in him and he in us, because he hath given us his Spirit.” He cites Ezekiel 36:27, God putting His Spirit within us to cause us to “walk in my statutes.” He says “It’s not me trying to mentally make up my mind to do this,” but God providing the empowerment and desire to please Him.
How can I get to know God? (1 John 4:13, Ezekiel 36:27)

One of them said salsa. And that was close cuz salsa is made of tomatoes. And you can make some good salsa with what’s in that can. See that? But they knew it wasn’t pumpkin. And see, us Christians, we have got to dig deep enough to know what these preachers and these books are saying. We got to get understanding and we apply it. And if it doesn’t work, we know they’re wrong. And if it does work, we know that’s right. Now, we’re going to ask the question, how would I get to know God and Jesus? Well, God promised I could know him. How can I know him? 1 John 4:13. Hereby— by this we know that we dwell in him and he in us, because he hath given us his Spirit. This spirit that raises up a standard against our enemy. We know Jesus lives in us. And we live in him by that spirit. See, that spirit is involved. And it’s promised in Ezekiel 36:27. Hundreds of years before God promised that he would put his spirit within us. I will put my spirit within you. And what that spirit will cause you to walk in my statutes. Cause you to keep my judgments, cause you to do them. See, it’s God coming to my life that gives me the desire to obey his word to do that what’s pleasing to him. It’s not me trying to mentally make up my mind to do this. It’s him providing the empowerment, the desire, the compelling to please him. And see, when I make a mistake, that compelling picks me up and moves me on. I don’t stay in my mistake. I don’t stay in my failure. Why? Cuz the Holy Spirit’s there causing me to get up and keep pursuing his word, his righteous judgment, his righteous moral truths. Hallelujah. So, it’s important that I know God and God is spirit. See, so when God says, “I will put my spirit,” he’s going to he’s what?
How can I get to know God? (1 John 4:13, Ezekiel 36:27)

1 John 4:13: By this we know that we abide in Him, and He in us, because He has given us of His Spirit. Ezekiel 36:27: I will put My Spirit within you and cause you to walk in My statutes, and you will keep My judgments and do them.
How can we know that we know Him? (1 John 2:3-4)

He cites 1 John 2:3–4, that we know we know Him if we keep His commandments, and says the Spirit within compels us to repent, ask forgiveness and tackle the sin again until it is broken. He says those who say “I know him” but do not keep His commandments are liars and “The truth is not in him.” He says a Christian who stumbles and gets back up is different from one who lives in habitual sin.
How can we know that we know Him? (1 John 2:3-4)

I’m going to put myself in you. 1 John 2:3-4. Here it is again: “Hereby— by this we know that we know him.” You see, we can know if we know God. We can know if we are participators of that promise to know God and Jesus Christ if we keep his commandments. Now Ezekiel just told us when God comes to us, he’s going to cause us to keep his commandments. It’s not going to be, you know, well, I just got to figure this out. I just got to grunt and do this on my own. No, no, no. There is a spirit within you. There is a force within you that keeps compelling you and driving you to keep his word. And so therefore, I know I know him. Why? Yes, I’ve messed up three times in this area and I’ve asked forgiveness three times and here I did it again. But that spirit what? Compels me to repent. Compels me to ask God to forgive me for compels me to ask God to cleanse me and free me from this. And I get back up and I tackle that sin again. And then one day, the spirit has given me authority over it. Set me free from it. That’s how I know I know God. He that says, “I know him,” and keeps not his commandments, is a what? Liar. You know, homosexuals that say they’re going to heaven, and they’re living in habitual sin, and prostitutes and incest people and pedophiles and all this, they say, “Well, you know, God loves me and all this.” Listen, God loving the world has nothing to do with where you’re going. If you don’t respond with a hearing ear, you’re going to be everything’s going to be taken from you, including eternal life. Isn’t that what we read? And look at this last part. The truth is not in him. The truth, you see it up there. Truth. The truth is not in him. John 16:13, when he, the Spirit of truth is come, he will guide you unto all truth. So what’s not in him? When truth is not in him, what’s not in him? The spirit. See, he doesn’t know God. The spirit’s not in him. And John 14:6, I am the way, the truth, and the life. Jesus is the truth. So, who is not in them? Jesus and the spirit’s not in them. And they know it because they live in habitual sin. They’re not Christians just stumbling and making mistakes and getting back up.
How can we know that we know Him? (1 John 2:3-4)

1 John 2:3-4: Now by this we know that we know Him, if we keep His commandments. He who says, “I know Him,” and does not keep His commandments, is a liar, and the truth is not in him. John 16:13: However, when He, the Spirit of truth, has come, He will guide you into all truth; for He will not speak on His own authority, but whatever He hears He will speak; and He will tell you things to come. John 14:6: Jesus said to him, “I am the way, the truth, and the life. No one comes to the Father except through Me.

He cites John 14:16–17, that the Father will send “another Comforter,” the Spirit of truth. He says the Holy Spirit is “a friend” who mends the brokenhearted, sets the captive free and encourages us when we think all is lost: “He comes as a comforter. He doesn’t come as a quitter.” He says the world cannot receive Him because it neither sees nor knows Him.

They habitually live in sin. Now, isn’t that clear? And we can know him. And this same chapter of John 14 tells us we know him. Okay, let’s go to verse 16 of John 14: “I will pray the Father, and he will send you another Comforter, that he may abide with you forever.” Now this Holy Spirit’s not only spirit of truth but he’s a comforter. He’s a friend. He’s there to mend up the brokenhearted, set the captive free. He’s there to encourage you when you think all is lost and there’s no hope. He comes as a comforter. He doesn’t come as a quitter. Might as well just quit. Give up. No, the Holy Spirit’s an encourager, an inspirer. “Even the Spirit of truth.” See, that’s what he’s talking about in John 14. The spirit of truth, the Holy Spirit. Whom the world cannot receive because it sees him not, neither knows him. And they know they don’t know him because they don’t keep his word. The comforter and the spirit of truth, the Holy Ghost, the Holy Spirit’s all the same thing. But you know him. Oh, for he dwells with you and shall be in you.

John 14:16: And I will pray the Father, and He will give you another Helper, that He may abide with you forever— John 14:17: the Spirit of truth, whom the world cannot receive, because it neither sees Him nor knows Him; but you know Him, for He dwells with you and will be in you.
What does “with you” and “in you” mean, and is God three gods? (John 14:17)

He asks who was with the apostles when Jesus said the Spirit is with you and will be in you, and says it was Jesus, who is truth, with the pouring out of the Spirit still to come. He says “Us Christians do not believe in three gods. We believe in one,” who identifies Himself as the Father, the Son, the Holy Spirit and the Word. He cites John 1:1 and John 7, rivers of life-giving water flowing from our innermost being from the Spirit, who had not come yet because Jesus had not been glorified.
What does “with you” and “in you” mean, and is God three gods? (John 14:17)

You know him. Hallelujah. Now, what does he mean when he says he’s talking to his apostles and he says this Holy Spirit is with you. The spirit of truth is with you, but it’s going to be in you. Now, let me answer this by asking you this question. Who was with the apostles at the time he said this? Jesus, who is truth. The Spirit is truth. You see, God says, “I’ll pour out my Spirit.” It’s God’s Spirit. You know, the Muslims say that Christianity has three gods because they use the word trinity to try to express, you know, God. But the Muslims lying. Us Christians do not believe in three gods. We believe in one. And he identifies himself as the father, the son, the Holy Spirit, and the word. He identifies himself. So when we speak, we speak his identity. He’s the father. He’s the son. He’s the Holy Spirit. And he’s the word. Jesus said, “My word is truth.” In John 1:1, it says, “The word became flesh and dwelt amongst us. The word was with God and the word was God.” So the word is God. Jesus is God. God is God. And the Holy Spirit is God. Make no mistake, we worship one God. Can I hear an amen? Amen. Now Jesus is with them. So what is he talking about shall be in you? Well, he had told them to go and tarry in Jerusalem until they be clothed with power from on high. He had told them that there was going to be a pouring out of the Holy Spirit. When he was glorified, you see it says in John 7, he that believeth on me out of his innermost being what? Rivers of life-giving water would flow. This spake he of the spirit which had not come yet because he had not been glorified. He hadn’t died on the cross and rose again. So there is a promise of Jesus coming back and empowering us, filling us with his spirit.
What does “with you” and “in you” mean, and is God three gods? (John 14:17)

John 1:1: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. Luke 24:49: Behold, I send the Promise of My Father upon you; but tarry in the city of Jerusalem until you are endued with power from on high.” John 7:38-39: He who believes in Me, as the Scripture has said, out of his heart will flow rivers of living water.” But this He spoke concerning the Spirit, whom those believing in Him would receive; for the Holy Spirit was not yet given, because Jesus was not yet glorified.
What is the difference between God’s presence with us and the baptism of the Holy Spirit?

He tells of a conversation with a Catholic priest he invited to speak, who said he had been filled with the Holy Ghost at a large spirit-filled Catholic convention. He says what the priest experienced was “his presence with us,” which anyone can have when they gather and acknowledge Christ, not the baptism of the Holy Spirit. He says “That doesn’t mean your doctrine’s right.”
What is the difference between God’s presence with us and the baptism of the Holy Spirit?

But we also have him with us. Amen. Do you guys get this? Let me give you an illustration of this. I mingle a lot with other denominations and so especially when I was younger and I invited Father Fred, a Catholic priest in the community to come in and speak at the church. And he spoke a good message of faith and you know and in that message he said he’d been filled with the Holy Ghost. All right. And so after the service, me and him are talking, and he lights up a cigarette. And then he uses profanity like a truck driver. Blankly blanket this and blankly blanket that. And I go, “Uh, Father Fred, how did you get the Holy Ghost?” I said, “Number one, the first name of the spirit is holy. Holy Ghost. He said, “Well, I went down to the Anaheim Convention Center where the spirit-filled Catholics gathered together.” And if you haven’t been there, it was it’s powerful. These Catholics that were filled with the spirit 1968, God just visited denominational churches and just poured out his spirit on that. He didn’t ask anybody’s permission. He just did it. And so these Catholics would get together and they’d have a a big convention. I mean, there’s 10 or 12,000 down there, man. We walk in there and they’re worshiping Jesus and all that. The power of his presence is there. But see, that’s the presence with us. And that’s what he said. I walked into that and man, the spirit of God was just came all over me and I just felt God’s presence. And I said, “Father Fred, that is not the baptism of the Holy Ghost. That is his presence with us. Everybody can have that. When the church gets together, Jesus said, “I will be in the midst.” Presbyterians, Baptists, Methodists, Cath— I don’t care who you are. If you gather together and you acknowledge Christ, his presence will come. That doesn’t mean your doctrine’s right. I said, “Father Fred, Jesus said that the spirit would pour out of us.” I said, ‘You haven’t got the baptism of the Holy Spirit. You just experienced the first time the presence of God. And there’s a big difference. Hallelujah. And that’s what Jesus is telling his apostles. Now, there is some spirit-filled churches that believe if you don’t have the baptism of the Holy Spirit with speaking in tongues, you’re not saved and you’re going to hell.
What is the difference between God’s presence with us and the baptism of the Holy Spirit?
Matthew 18:20: For where two or three are gathered together in My name, I am there in the midst of them.”
Do you have to speak in tongues to be saved?

He says some spirit-filled churches believe if you don’t speak in tongues you’re not saved, and tells of parents who told a daughter she was going to hell for that. He says “the Bible says not all speak in tongues,” and that in Acts 2 they spoke in languages while in Acts 4 they “spoke in their own language.” He says the parents stuck with their church doctrine over Scripture because they didn’t take time to find out.
Do you have to speak in tongues to be saved?

And I’ve had to deal with these people. I’ve had to deal with parents, good parents, that told their child, they had two children. One got filled with the Holy Ghost and spoke in tongues, the other one didn’t. And they told this other daughter that she was going to hell. And I knew that girl. She was a fine Christian girl. And I’m pretty sure Mr. Barnes knows who I’m talking about. And I had to— you know, I had to deal with this thing. I can’t have this girl going through life thinking she’s going to hell because she don’t speak in tongues when the Bible says not all speak in tongues. My God, church. It doesn’t take a genius to figure this out, does it? Amen. In Acts chapter 2, yes, they spoke in languages. In Acts 4, they didn’t. They spoke in their own language. They didn’t speak in other languages. Are you with me? And that couple, as tremendous a couple as they was, and the guy was a successful businessman and they were very educated and knowledgeable, they stuck with their church doctrine over scripture because they didn’t take time to find out and get the understanding. See, that’s what Paul meant when he— or Peter meant when he said, “Unstable and unlearned people, twist the scriptures and bring destruction.” But I finally got to the young lady. Hallelujah. And she’s the one that needed to hear.

What does it mean to be born again? (John 3:5, John 1:12)

Can’t just be head knowledge. Can’t just be, you know, getting your name on a church and joining some group. God has to be involved. Not just forgive us, but cleanse us, wash the sin away. He will set us free from sin. He will give them power that receive him to become sons of God. See, sons of God, when you know the interpretation of the sons of God in the Bible, the sons of God live right. They live holy. Even Christians that need areas of their life straighten out have to admit they’re wrong. That’s the formula. Hallelujah. Then after we get saved, if we seek him and we seek the word, we will grow in the word.

What is the conclusion? How do we know God?

What is the conclusion? How do we know God?

1 Peter 2:2: as newborn babes, desire the pure milk of the word, that you may grow thereby, 1 Peter 1:23: having been born again, not of corruptible seed but incorruptible, through the word of God which lives and abides forever,
He says “Glorify means honored.” He says God honored the Son with the ability to give His life, and no one could take it.
What authority does he say Jesus was given before creation?

He says Jesus has authority over everybody and every nation and every language on the earth: “He is the one running the kingdoms.” He says this was given to Him before creation, and He created everything.
Can anyone on earth give you eternal life?
He says no: “There is no one on earth that can give you eternal life.” He says “Only Jesus Christ can give you eternal life.”
What is the difference between enlightenment and eternal life?
He says “we’re not looking for enlightenment. We’re looking for eternal life.” He says eternal life is defined as knowing the only true God.
What does he say the Lord of the harvest can do?

He says the Lord of the harvest has the knowledge and authority to plant the seed and make it grow, cut it down, thresh it and bake it for the master’s table. He says “He’s the one that can do the job. We are just messengers.”
What was the can illustration about?

He opens a can labeled “Organic pumpkin” that looks like tomatoes, and says “too many of us do not dig deeper and find out if what preachers are telling us is the truth.” He says we need to put time into what we hear.
Who does he say gets more from God?
He says it is not faith, grace, a big church or a little church: “Whosoever has ears to hear, more will be given.”
Is obeying God just my own effort?
He says no: “It’s him providing the empowerment, the desire, the compelling to please him.” He says when he makes a mistake, that compelling picks him up and “I don’t stay in my mistake.”
What does he say happens when a Christian keeps messing up in an area?
He says the Spirit “compels me to repent” and ask God to cleanse and free him, and he gets back up and tackles the sin again. He says one day “the spirit has given me authority over it.”
Are the Comforter and the Spirit of truth the same?
He says “The comforter and the spirit of truth, the Holy Ghost, the Holy Spirit’s all the same thing.”
Does he say Christians believe in three gods?
He says no: “Us Christians do not believe in three gods. We believe in one.” He says “Make no mistake, we worship one God.”
How does he say we grow after we are saved?

He says we “desire the sincere milk of the word that you may grow,” and you’ve got to have the word and the Spirit. He says “unless you go to church and get in Bible studies and you’re not going to grow.”

items.t: How Does a Just God Give a Second Chance? — July 18, 2021
items.d: Pastor David G. Kincer asks how a just God gives a second chance. Because there was no law before Moses, Christ preached to the spirits in prison from Noah’s day; he suggests a just God may give a second…
p: Pastor David G. Kincer asks how a just God gives a second chance. Because there was no law before Moses, Christ preached to the spirits in prison from Noah’s day; he suggests a just God may give a second chance to those who never understood, but urges taking it now. He criticizes faith-only teaching and lawless conservatives, calls free-salvation teaching socialism in the church, and closes with “neither do I condemn thee.”

Per Ephesians 5:27, He will present to Himself a glorious church without spot.

items.d: All Scripture is inspired and essential to the Christian walk. The world’s wisdom cannot answer Jesus, and twisting Scripture leads to destruction. We are saved by grace for good works, will appear before…
p: All Scripture is inspired and essential to the Christian walk. The world’s wisdom cannot answer Jesus, and twisting Scripture leads to destruction. We are saved by grace for good works, will appear before Christ’s judgment seat, and must love God and people—practicing righteousness.
All Scripture is given by inspiration of God—essential from the beginning of the Christian walk to the end.

items.t: How People with Faith in God Responded to a Miracle — June 6, 2021
items.d: Pastor David G. Kincer walks through John 9 and how people who believed in God responded when Jesus opened the eyes of a man born blind. Nobody had faith for the healing; the man believed after Jesus spoke to…
p: Pastor David G. Kincer walks through John 9 and how people who believed in God responded when Jesus opened the eyes of a man born blind. Nobody had faith for the healing; the man believed after Jesus spoke to him, testified about what he experienced, and was cast out. He says faith is overemphasized, tells how he was saved at an altar in Norwalk, California, and calls the church to invite Jesus through praise, assembling, prayer and the word.
Were Paul and Silas praying for deliverance in prison?
No. They were just seeking God, singing hymns and praising their master; we are to seek Jesus no matter what we go through.
