He says some in the Corinthian church “had it all figured out through human knowledge just like today,” so Paul tackles that first, and notes that “knowledge puffs up. It makes us proud.”
How does Paul deal with human thinking about spiritual problems?

He says Paul “knows his Bible,” and “he’s going to neutralize this human thinking factor in trying to find solutions to spiritual problems,” citing what the Bible already says about not being wise in your own eyes.
What does he say godliness is?
He says godliness is pleasing God, not pleasing your friend or your spouse. He says “living to please God is the final measuring stick of anything you believe.”
Does he say there is more than one way to God?
No. He says “there is no other gods” and “there isn’t any other way to God but God’s way.”
Does what you eat make you more spiritual?
He says food “has nothing to do with spirituality,” including diet and healthy eating, and that if you honor your parents and obey God’s word, he says the Bible promises long life and health.
What does Romans 14 say about eating?

He reads that one believes he may eat all things while another who is weak eats herbs, and that the one who eats should not despise the one who does not, and “let not him which eats not judge him that eats.”
What is a stumbling block in 1 Corinthians 8?

He says Paul is appealing not to their mental understanding but to their conscience, “that what you do can hurt other people,” and that your liberty can become a stumbling block to those who are weak.
Why does Paul call some believers weak?
He asks, “why do you think he’s calling them weak?” and answers that it is to make them “feel more important. We love it. We like to be the one that’s better. But wait till he gets done with it.”
What does he say most Christians do when they read the Bible?
He says “they read passages in the Bible and they come up with human thinking instead of the mind of the spirit.”
What does he conclude about people being offended?
He says he finally decided “I’m just going to do what I know is right. And if they get offended, that’s their problem. And that was a big freedom.”
Does he say Christians should never judge?

He says Paul tells them to judge what he is saying: “Here he is telling us to judge what he’s saying.” He contrasts that with “Judge not, let you be not judged,” and says the fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom.

items.d: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer continues 1 Corinthians 10, teaching that the cup of the Lord and the cup of devils cannot be shared and that churches cannot be built on human opinions. He gives Paul’s…
p: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer continues 1 Corinthians 10, teaching that the cup of the Lord and the cup of devils cannot be shared and that churches cannot be built on human opinions. He gives Paul’s practical advice about meat sold in the market and offered to idols, then turns to Acts 15:29, greed as idolatry, and the works of the flesh. He closes by arguing from James 2 and Revelation 2 that believers should not say “my faith” but follow the faith of Jesus.
What does it mean to sacrifice to devils and create your own religion? (Leviticus 17:7)

He says it is “Old Testament stuff”: they sacrificed “to devils, not to God, to gods whom they knew not.” He says “they created their own religion. And when you create your own religion, you’re going the way of Satan,” and he cites Leviticus 17:7, “They shall no more offer their sacrifices unto” devils.
What does it mean to sacrifice to devils and create your own religion? (Leviticus 17:7)

Well, what do you mean, to sacrifice to the devils? Well, it’s Old Testament stuff, basic. People know this that read their Bible. They sacrificed to devils, not to God, to gods whom they knew not. To knew God, they created their own religion. And when you create your own religion, you’re going the way of Satan. See, he loves for you to alter the one true God and the Bible that tells us how to get there. He’s just quoting Old Testament Scripture, Leviticus 17:7: “They shall no more offer their sacrifices unto” what? Devils. To idols, their own.
What does it mean to sacrifice to devils and create your own religion? (Leviticus 17:7)
Leviticus 17:7: They shall no more offer their sacrifices to demons, after whom they have played the harlot. This shall be a statute forever for them throughout their generations.” ’
Can you drink the cup of the Lord and the cup of devils? (1 Corinthians 10:21-22)

He says Paul’s point is “they’re not compatible.” Using your human understanding that an idol is nothing to “violate the direct commandments of God and provoke God to jealousy” is, he says, saying “we are God”: “You don’t come out and say it, you just do it with your beliefs, from your human thinking.”
Can you drink the cup of the Lord and the cup of devils? (1 Corinthians 10:21-22)

Religion isn’t that good. Hallelujah. Verse 21, still in 1 Corinthians chapter 10:21: “You can’t drink the cup of the Lord and the cup of devils, nor be partakers of the Lord’s table and of the table of devils.” They’re not compatible. “Do we provoke the Lord to jealousy? Are we stronger than He?” Because you got some human understanding that an idol is nothing and the meat sacrificed to the idol is nothing, do you use that understanding to violate the direct commandments of God and provoke God to jealousy? Are you stronger than God? Have you become a God? And when we do our own religious ways, come up with our own way of serving God--
Can you drink the cup of the Lord and the cup of devils? (1 Corinthians 10:21-22)

1 Corinthians 10:21-22: You cannot drink the cup of the Lord and the cup of demons; you cannot partake of the Lord’s table and of the table of demons. Or do we provoke the Lord to jealousy? Are we stronger than He?
What does “all things are lawful for me, but not all things are profitable” mean? (1 Corinthians 10:23)

He says you can do something “because of your human understanding of it,” but it is unprofitable because you start “taking on the nature, as we read earlier, of the religion that you’re embracing.” He asks how going into a pagan temple builds up the church, and says “that’s what we’re doing in America: we’re making our own religions, we’re coming up with our own way, and we just throw Jesus into it.”
What does “all things are lawful for me, but not all things are profitable” mean? (1 Corinthians 10:23)

We are saying we are God. You don’t come out and say it, you just do it with your beliefs, from your human thinking. Do you get it? He approached the human thinking way of justifying doing something against Scripture, and then he comes in with the spiritual allegory, the spiritual illustration, very powerful. “All things are lawful for me.” Yeah, you can eat the food, yeah, you can do it because of your human understanding of it, “but all things are not profitable.” What’s the profit in you doing it? There’s no profit there at all. In fact, you keep doing it, it’s going to be unprofitable, because you’re going to start what? Taking on the nature, as we read earlier, of the religion that you’re embracing. You’re going to take on the nature. You’re going to have eyes that see not, ears that hear not, a mouth that can’t speak-- Anymore. Isn’t that right? “All things are lawful for me, but all things” what? “Edify not.” It doesn’t build up. How? What does me, my liberty going into a pagan temple, how does that build me up, and how does that build the church up, when I’m directly violating the Ten Commandments and other commandments? How does that edify the church? It just what? Doesn’t. Isn’t this argument good? And folks, that’s what we’re doing in America: we’re making our own religions, we’re coming up with our own way, and we just throw Jesus into it, and it’s not profitable and it’s not edifying. Can I hear an--
What does “all things are lawful for me, but not all things are profitable” mean? (1 Corinthians 10:23)
1 Corinthians 10:23: All things are lawful for me, but not all things are helpful; all things are lawful for me, but not all things edify.
Can you build a healthy church on human opinions or denominations?

He says “you can’t build a healthy church and violate God’s Word,” and “it must be Jesus, His truth, His words, and the apostles’ doctrine.” He says “being a Baptist has nothing to do with anything. Being a Catholic has nothing to do with anything,” and that Paul gives a practical solution next “because Christians get weird.”
Can you build a healthy church on human opinions or denominations?

Amen. Conclusion of this approach, the spiritual approach, the spiritual illustration: do not partake of idols nor food sacrificed to idols. His conclusion was the same in both approaches. I like this guy, Paul. You can’t build a healthy church and violate God’s Word. You can’t build a healthy church, you’ve been using human understanding. You must have the mind of the Spirit. You cannot build a healthy church using your own opinions and your own beliefs. It must be Jesus, His truth, His words, and the apostles’ doctrine, who got their doctrine straight from Jesus. So Calvin, Wesley, and all the rest down through, or Roberts, Billy Graham, have nothing to do with anything. I must build my Christianity on Jesus Christ, His words, His truths. Amen. Being a Baptist has nothing to do with anything. Being a Catholic has nothing to do with anything. Verse 25 of chapter 10, 1 Corinthians 10:25: now here’s the practical solution. And why is he bringing out the practical? Because Christians get weird. You know, we read in the Bible, uh, to be modest. Well, then we decide, well, I can’t wear short-sleeve shirts, I can’t wear shorts, I can’t wear jewelry, or, and the Bible says don’t, women, don’t decorate yourself with your hair, don’t fix your hair up, and, and, and outward adorning of makeup and jewelry and all this stuff. So we don’t wear jew-- it doesn’t say jewelry there, but then we don’t wear jewelry, and we look like death warmed over, and we want to get a handsome man.
What extremes do Christians fall into?

He says “we go to extremes,” and recalls growing up in Pentecost churches where people wrote “spirit writing” that “made no sense.” Of people who say they have a word from God for you, he asks, “why do I need to keep getting words of God from people when I have the Bible, which the Bible says is a more sure word of prophecy?”
What extremes do Christians fall into?

And see, we go to extremes. You know, Pentecostalism, I grew up in Pentecost churches, and they had spirit writing, “Holy Ghost, come home,” and they’d write something and it made no sense, and all kinds of goony stuff. Today it’s a prophecy: “I got a prophecy, I got a word from God for you.” Well, why do I need to keep getting words of God from people when I have the Bible, which the Bible says is a more sure word of prophecy? I mean, what’s the problem here? Is it so you can--we--you can feed your ego by feeling like you know you’re in touch with God and I’m not? And I can go on and on. The Catholics and their holy water and their images, come on.
What extremes do Christians fall into?
2 Peter 1:19: And so we have the prophetic word confirmed, which you do well to heed as a light that shines in a dark place, until the day dawns and the morning star rises in your hearts;
Should Christians ask questions about food sold in the market or served at a feast? (1 Corinthians 10:25-27)

He says “don’t get weird in this stuff whatsoever.” About meat sold in the market, “ask no questions for conscience’ sake. Just buy the meat, because you already know it means nothing,” and at an unbeliever’s feast eat what is set before you, since over-investigating makes “a miserable life for ourselves.”
Should Christians ask questions about food sold in the market or served at a feast? (1 Corinthians 10:25-27)

Church, we got to approach God His way, and so we can’t get extreme. And so he’s going to give a practical thing: don’t get weird in this stuff whatsoever. “Sold in the marketplace,” the meat market, “ask no questions for conscience’ sake.” Just buy the meat, because you already know it means nothing. You know, don’t be one of these weird Christians: “Is it got the stamp? Is it culture? Is it got the Christian approval on it?” Don’t get--don’t investigate, just buy the stuff and go eat it. Doesn’t that make sense? But oh no, us-than-thou people, us witch hunters, we got to--we got to dissect and [unclear] everything, we don’t want any, and we--we create a miserable life for ourselves. “Ask no questions for the conscience’ sake. If any believer bid you to a feast, and you go, whatsoever is set before you”--any unbeliever, now they’re going to an unbeliever’s house, they’re throwing a festival, and it’s probably around their idol, because that’s what they did--“just what is set before you, eat, asking no questions for conscience’ sake.”
Should Christians ask questions about food sold in the market or served at a feast? (1 Corinthians 10:25-27)

1 Corinthians 10:25: Eat whatever is sold in the meat market, asking no questions for conscience’ sake; 1 Corinthians 10:27: If any of those who do not believe invites you to dinner, and you desire to go, eat whatever is set before you, asking no question for conscience’ sake.
When should you not eat meat that was offered to idols? (1 Corinthians 10:28-29)

He says if someone tells you it was offered in sacrifice to idols, “don’t eat it, for whose conscience’ sake? His, the one who told you,” so you don’t “offend the conscience of the other one, even the idolater.” He then says that in his youth things like pool were called sin, and “now we’re going to the other thing: everything’s okay, now there is no restraints.”
When should you not eat meat that was offered to idols? (1 Corinthians 10:28-29)

“Whose conscience? If any say it’s offered in sacrifice to idols, don’t eat it, for whose conscience’ sake?” His, the one who told you. See, now the cat’s out of the bag, you know, to obey the Scriptures. So you go, you know, “I’ll--I’ll just eat the potatoes and beans today.” Why? Because you don’t want to offend the conscience of the other one, even the idolater who knows you shouldn’t be eating meat sacrificed to his god. That’s why he brought it up. Then you can say, “Well, I didn’t know. I--I won’t have any of that, thank you. Just give me the mashed potatoes and the gravy and the beans, and everything will be fine.” Are you there? Is this good or what? Oh, this is--see, back in my day you couldn’t even have a deck of cards in your house. Back in my day, my teenage, you could not play billiards, pool. That was sin. Why? Because all the pool tables were in the bars or a pool hall where all the hoods and everybody hung out. So instead of saying the atmosphere was wrong, we--they just said playing pool, “that’s the devil’s game, man, that’s a sin.” And how many, you know, there’s nothing wrong with playing pool. How many, you know, I got a pool table in my garage. See, we got extreme, but now we’re going to the other thing: everything’s okay, now there is no restraints.
When should you not eat meat that was offered to idols? (1 Corinthians 10:28-29)

1 Corinthians 10:28-29: But if anyone says to you, “This was offered to idols,” do not eat it for the sake of the one who told you, and for conscience’ sake; for “the earth is the LORD’s, and all its fullness.” “Conscience,” I say, not your own, but that of the other. For why is my liberty judged by another man’s conscience?
What did the Jerusalem church decide about meat offered to idols, blood and things strangled? (Acts 15:29)

He says the apostles, elders and members “unanimously made it clear” in Acts 15:29 to “abstain from meats offered to idols,” and “100% unanimously voted yes.” On blood and things strangled, he says it relates to Christ’s blood sacrifice: “we only eat of His blood in the communion table,” because “the shedding of blood was imperative for the forgiveness of sins in the Bible from the beginning.”
What did the Jerusalem church decide about meat offered to idols, blood and things strangled? (Acts 15:29)

But isn’t this good? Isn’t this practical? You know, the Bible says in Ecclesiastes, “do not be extreme in anything.” Okay, and so we need to watch out with being extreme. We need to be practical. Now, the apostles, the elders, and the members of the church in Jerusalem unanimously made it clear--unanimously means they were not divided, which was the first topic that he talked about for four chapters, went to division--this church is in unity, and they make it very clear, Acts 15:29: “Abstain, abstain from meats offered to idols.” Is that clear? The apostles, the elders of the church, and the members, 100% unanimously voted yes, this is what we’re to follow. And these people, with their human thinking, were violating what they had already come up with. Can I hear an amen? Are you there? Through their human thinking. And he says, “from blood and things strangled.” Now, why do you think they said, don’t partake of blood and don’t eat of meat strangled? Because it’s related to Christ’s blood sacrifice for us. The blood had to be shed. You know, you can drink blood and you won’t die from it. You know, blood is a food, and unless it has germs and bacteria and disease in it, you’re not going to catch anything. Okay, a lot of nations and cultures eat blood, blood of cows and so forth. They will cut the vein in the neck of a cow-- Let the blood come out, just shoots out, fill up their cup, then they put pressure on the wound, and in just a few seconds the blood stops flowing. They drink their blood. See, it’s a food, but we don’t do it because of what Christ shed His blood, and so we only eat of His blood in the communion table, and we only partake of the thing that was shedding blood, not strangled, because the shedding of blood was imperative for the forgiveness of sins in the Bible from the beginning. Are you with me? It had nothing to do with being bad. Yes, the shedding of blood in Genesis--
What did the Jerusalem church decide about meat offered to idols, blood and things strangled? (Acts 15:29)
Acts 15:29: that you abstain from things offered to idols, from blood, from things strangled, and from sexual immorality. If you keep yourselves from these, you will do well. Farewell.
What does he say about Catholic idols and believers who still keep rituals? (Acts 21:20)

He says that “according to Paul, they’re wrong,” but “before you condemn them to hell” he points to Acts 21:20, where thousands of Jews who believed were still “doing the shadow laws that Christ fulfilled.” He says “people can actually be a believer in Christ and be doing things in an erroneous way and still be a believer,” and “you better start looking at yourself and at the Bible.”
What does he say about Catholic idols and believers who still keep rituals? (Acts 21:20)

Three, God sacrificed the first animal. Okay. And “from fornication”: sexual immorality. What was the second topic? Sexual immorality. Just thought I’d pass that on. Now, what about the Catholic idols? Well, obviously, according to Paul, they’re wrong. According to the Scriptures, they’re wrong. Can I hear an amen? They’re using human knowledge to clear their conscience of having something and having people partake in something that they should not be doing. Now, whether you like it or not, and whether your family’s Catholic or not, I’m sorry, when you’re wrong, you’re just what? Wrong. But using Paul’s wisdom, before you condemn them to hell, let’s take a little further look. Acts 21:20: Paul had come down to Jerusalem to, uh, sacrifice at the temple and preach the gospel down there in Jerusalem, and the apostles come to him and the leaders, and they say, “You see, Paul, how many thousands of Jews there are which believe.” See, there were thousands of Jews that came to the temple for the same feast of Israel, and this guy, these people, say, the leaders say, there are thousands of Jews which what? Believe. Are they believers? Are they believers? Yeah, it plainly says what they’re-- Believers, “but they are all zealous of the law.” They’re still offering animal sacrifices, they’re still burning incense, they’re still wearing certain clothes, they’re still doing the shadow laws that Christ fulfilled and have nothing to do now with anything in the shadow. We are now participators of the truth of those laws. Hello, church. I see, I had to work through this, because in the circles I was in, the Catholics were the [unclear] on the hill. In Revelation. They were the beast. You know, they were the church of, you know, man, man, you know, you’re a Catholic, boom, you’re dead, you’re gone, you’re, you’re hopeless. And it took God opening my understanding to things, that people can actually be a believer in Christ and be doing things in an erroneous way and still be a believer, because they haven’t learned or come to the place yet where they can let go of the rituals and just embrace the truth. Now, folks, that is good stuff. So before you condemn them, you better start looking at yourself and at the Bible. Okay. Now, what about Protestant idols? Oh, Protestants don’t have idols. Oh, they don’t? You didn’t know Protestants had idols?
What does he say about Catholic idols and believers who still keep rituals? (Acts 21:20)
Acts 21:20: And when they heard it, they glorified the Lord. And they said to him, “You see, brother, how many myriads of Jews there are who have believed, and they are all zealous for the law;
Are there Protestant idols, and is greed idolatry? (Colossians 3:5)

He says America is not into images: “they worship things that they should not worship.” Reading Colossians 3:5, he says greed is idolatry, and he criticizes the prosperity message, saying he watched ministers “talk senior citizens into giving their whole Social Security check.” But being rich does not make a person greedy: “the Bible doesn’t back up that at all.”
Are there Protestant idols, and is greed idolatry? (Colossians 3:5)

Well, they wouldn’t have an image. No Protestant church would have an image. I told you at the beginning that America wasn’t into images, they’re into things. They worship things that they should not worship. Well, show me a Protestant idol. Okay, glad you asked. First Colossians, that shouldn’t be First Colossians, I put that one in there to--never mind. Colossians 3:5: “Mortify, put to death, therefore, your members which are upon the earth”: sexual immorality, that’s one of the topics he talked about, “impurity, lust, evil desires.” That was the source of division. “I want it my way, I want it my way, and if you don’t go my way, I can’t go anywhere with you.” Division, and “greed, which is” what? “Idolatry.” Oh, greed is idolatry. Ew. Kenyon, Oral Roberts, A. A. Allen, T. L. Osborn, Kenneth Hagin, Jimmy Swaggart, Jim Bakker, Robert Tilton, Benny Hinn, Kenneth Copeland, Creflo Dollar, Eddie Long, Joyce Meyer, Paula White are just the few in the Protestant-- Arena that promote prosperity is what God wants for everyone. The prosperity message is promoted by all of these big men, and who? It’s a Ponzi scheme. You give to Kenneth Copeland, God will bless you; you give the dollar, God will bless you. The Ponzi scheme is: the ones on the top get what? The money, they get the benefit, and the ones down here get nothing. And I watched this as a young Christian in the church world. I watched these ministers talk senior citizens into giving their whole Social Security check, and I knew these senior citizens, I knew they just barely survived and barely lived. I even went up to them and I says, “You know, that old lady over there sitting beside me dropped in her whole paycheck, her whole Social Security. You know, you--aren’t you going to give that back?” “No way, man.” They had their Rolls-Royce Silver Shadow sitting out there, they had $500 suits. “Nothing is too good for the man of God.” I had to work through this stuff. See, you’re lucky, I’m telling you the truth. You don’t have to figure this stuff out. Greed is what? Idolatry. Now, does it mean because a person is rich that they’re greedy? No, the Bible doesn’t back up that at all. If a person goes to college, learns a good job skill, and they make good money of being a lawyer or doctor or whatever, that’s just the good old capitalistic system, and the system that the Bible--
Are there Protestant idols, and is greed idolatry? (Colossians 3:5)
Colossians 3:5: Therefore put to death your members which are on the earth: fornication, uncleanness, passion, evil desire, and covetousness, which is idolatry.
What are “individual idols,” and what are the works of the flesh? (Galatians 5:19-21)

He says individual idols, neither Protestant nor Catholic, are “wrong” according to Paul. In Galatians 5:19 “the works of the flesh are evident. They’re very clear, they’re very plain,” and he says the list, including idolatry, division and quarreling, belongs to “the topic of division that Paul covered”; “you’re carnal, you’re babies when you do this.”
What are “individual idols,” and what are the works of the flesh? (Galatians 5:19-21)

Promotes. And the sad thing is, these ministers just keep finding new suckers to support them, because they promise some miracles and they promise them, you know, “God’s going to, it’s going to be amazing, people just come, come along and give you money that you wouldn’t even know about,” and it doesn’t happen. Are you there? Now, the Catholic church, I can’t find any of this taught in the Catholic church. It’s Protestant. Hallelujah. Okay, what about individual idols? Individual idols, not Protestant, not Catholic. Well, according to Paul, they’re wrong, although they use human knowledge to clear their conscience. Galatians 5:19: “The works of the flesh are evident.” They’re very clear, they’re very plain. Okay, the bottom line: the works of the flesh will not inherit what? The kingdom of God. So what are the works of the flesh? Well, “adultery, fornication,” what Paul-- Addressed in his seminar on church growth, “uncleanness, envy, lewdness, idolatry,” what Paul is addressing now. Idolatry is a what? Work of the flesh. So if idolatry is in there, then any work of the flesh is what? Idolatry. “Spiritual adultery, sorcery, witchcraft, hatred”: you don’t like a certain race, you don’t like women because they’re women, or men because they’re men, or rich because they’re rich. “Hatred, wrath, contention, selfish ambitions, and dissensions”: quarreling, selfish ambition--do you want it your way?--and division are all in the topic of division that Paul covered. Are you there? It’s a work of what? The flesh. In fact, that’s what Paul said, it’s a work of the flesh. You’re carnal, you’re babies when you do this. “Jealousies, heresies, murders, drunkenness”--
What are “individual idols,” and what are the works of the flesh? (Galatians 5:19-21)

Galatians 5:19-21: Now the works of the flesh are evident, which are: adultery, fornication, uncleanness, lewdness, idolatry, sorcery, hatred, contentions, jealousies, outbursts of wrath, selfish ambitions, dissensions, heresies, envy, murders, drunkenness, revelries, and the like; of which I tell you beforehand, just as I also told you in time past, that those who practice such things will not inherit the kingdom of God.
Does the church adopt what culture pressures it to accept, and how do I examine myself?

He says “in every generation the church warms up to it in America and accepts it, and everybody’s okay, when it’s really idolatry.” Turning to the listener, he asks about drunkenness, hatred, jealousy, adultery and horoscopes and says “before we start straightening everybody else out, we need to” straighten ourselves out.
Does the church adopt what culture pressures it to accept, and how do I examine myself?

Intoxication. A big thing now is Christians getting drunk. We can get tattoos, no problem, our body is a, uh, what do they call the artist [unclear]? Yeah, and so I’m putting “Jesus saves” on my arm, hallelujah. Man, when the Bible prohibits it. And every what the public puts pressure on us to do, in every generation the church warms up to it in America and accepts it, and everybody’s okay, when it’s really idolatry. “Partying, and those who practice such things will not inherit the kingdom of God.” So what about you? You go, “Well, these preachers are horrible, doing that, that’s just wrong.” Okay, are you getting-- Intoxicated? Do you hate someone? Look down on them? Are you jealous of someone? Are you committing adultery? Premarital sex that Oprah says is okay? Okay. See, are you in the witchcraft? Do you read the horoscope every day? See, you see, that’s an idol, and you’re wrong. Before we start straightening everybody else out, we need to what? Straighten ourselves out. Now, let’s get down to this statement of my faith. Say the words, “my faith.” My faith, say it with substance, my faith. This is what Santorum--
Does the church adopt what culture pressures it to accept, and how do I examine myself?

Galatians 5:21: envy, murders, drunkenness, revelries, and the like; of which I tell you beforehand, just as I also told you in time past, that those who practice such things will not inherit the kingdom of God.
Is it biblical to say “my faith”? (James 2:18)

He says candidates in debates say “my faith” like “we can have a choice to believe what we want to,” but “my faith” is “only mentioned twice in the Bible,” and “we don’t have a right to say my faith.” In James he says “what I do is going to show you what I’m persuaded in,” and believing in one God makes you “as good as the demons.”
Is it biblical to say “my faith”? (James 2:18)

[Unclear], Romney all say, and Ron, all say in their debates: “my faith.” They say it like we can have a choice to believe what we want to. Romney says “my faith,” and what he means is he’s a Mormon, and, you know, they’re the only church going to heaven. He’s not going to say that, but that’s what they say. And they can have sacred marriage. And see, “my faith,” and then, you know, [unclear] comes along and he just got saved, he got, you know, probably got saved so he could get elected by the Christians. That’s the way politicians do. I--I don’t know that’s the case, but, you know, it could be. You know, and he’s got the Catholic faith, and then you got [unclear], “my faith.” They’re all saying “my faith.” Well, where does the Bible say “my faith”? It’s only mentioned twice in the Bible. Are you getting my drift? See, when I say “my faith,” what I’m saying is what I believe, and my opinions, they’re okay. Mr. Barnes’s faith can be different than mine, and so, and we got to accept everybody’s faith. That isn’t what the Bible says. Are you there? We don’t have a right to say “my faith,” and when you say “my faith,” you’re wrong. First place it’s used, James chapter 2:18: “Some say, you have faith, and I have works. Show me your faith without your works, and I will show you what”--my faith--how? By my works. See, what I do is going to show you what I’m persuaded in. How I live my life is going to show you what I really believe and I trust. “You believe there is one God. Wow, you’re as good as the demons.” They believe there’s one God, and they tremble, because they know that God is going to put them in the lake of fire forever. Wow, you’re equal to the demons. You’re really doing good, man. Whoopee. Are you there? “Oh foolish man, faith without” what? Works “is dead.” Don’t say “my faith.” I will know your faith by how you act, how you speak, what you speak, what you do. That’s the first place that’s used.
Is it biblical to say “my faith”? (James 2:18)

James 2:18: But someone will say, “You have faith, and I have works.” Show me your faith without your works, and I will show you my faith by my works. James 2:19-20: You believe that there is one God. You do well. Even the demons believe—and tremble! But do you want to know, O foolish man, that faith without works is dead?
Whose faith is “My faith” in Revelation 2, and why use the name of Jesus?

He says in Revelation 2 Jesus says “You have not denied My faith,” and asks “whose faith? Who’s speaking there? Jesus Christ.” Jesus “was persuaded that He was God, that He was the Son of God, that He was the Savior of the world, that no man could get eternal life but through Him.” He says to use the name of Jesus because “God” is “a general word that can fit into anywhere.”
Whose faith is “My faith” in Revelation 2, and why use the name of Jesus?

Second place, before you condemn them to hell, my little thing: in Revelation 2:12, to the church of Pergamos, “I know your works.” Faith without works is dead. “You have not denied My faith.” Whose faith? Who’s speaking there? Jesus Christ. Only used two times. The first one is, my faith must be accompanied with works that Jesus said for me to do, or it’s dead. Here Jesus plainly says it is “My faith” that you should-- Have. What was Jesus persuaded in? Jesus was persuaded that He was God, that He was the Son of God, that He was the Savior of the world, that no man could get eternal life but through Him. Jesus was persuaded in the Bible faith, God’s faith. He was persuaded that He would do nothing without the will of the Father. Are you there, church? That’s the faith of Jesus Christ. Did Jesus sin? No. He said, “Yeah, well, He’s God.” Yes, but we should be pursuing the goal, shouldn’t we? Hallelujah. Even to martyrdom they would keep the faith of Christ, even if it cost them their life. If they were in a bad marriage, they wouldn’t give in to the bad spouse; they would keep the faith of Christ even if that spouse left them. If they had a rebellious son or daughter that wanted to do something else, they would keep the faith of Christ no matter what that child-- Did. So the real statement should not be “my faith,” but “the Bible.” If we believe the Bible, it says, yes, we should say, “Yes, I’m a Christian and I follow Jesus and His Word.” Why is it important to use the name of Jesus? Because today “God” is a general word that can fit into anywhere, but they hate Jesus. Even though He’s God, they don’t want Jesus, because of what Jesus stood for. They want the freedom to go to heaven and have eternal life without a lifestyle that represents Jesus Christ.
Whose faith is “My faith” in Revelation 2, and why use the name of Jesus?

Revelation 2:12-13: “And to the angel of the church in Pergamos write, ‘These things says He who has the sharp two-edged sword: “I know your works, and where you dwell, where Satan’s throne is. And you hold fast to My name, and did not deny My faith even in the days in which Antipas was My faithful martyr, who was killed among you, where Satan dwells.
Can faith alone save a person, and what is “faith in your faith”? (James 2:14)

He reads James 2:14 and says “in America faith is all you need.” He says “you don’t have the right faith” when you have faith in your faith, in a church or in a minister, and “the Bible never says to have faith in your faith.” We are to have the faith Jesus had, and “I may not be there yet, but I’m working on it.”
Can faith alone save a person, and what is “faith in your faith”? (James 2:14)

Amen. “What does it profit,” James 2:14, “if someone says he has faith but does not have works?” What’s the profit? He says, you believe that you can go into the idol’s temple because idols are nothing, but what’s the profit? See, your works destroy your life. You get his argument. “Can faith save him?” And Paul is asking this question, and why? Because in America faith is all you need. The Baptist faith is all you need, you can live any way you want, but if you believe in Jesus, you’re going to heaven. That’s the truth. In many Spirit-filled circles, if you believe in Christ, boy, and especially you [unclear] and speaking tongues, man, you are, you are in. Everything is focused on faith. The Catholics, if you believe in the Catholic church, you’re saved. The Mormons, if you believe in the Mormon church, you’re saved. And Paul, or James, is saying, can that faith save him? Can faith without works save anyone? That’s what James is saying. Am I talking to the right people? And these preachers in Protestant arenas that preach prosperity back it up with faith. Faith and prosperity is their message. And when you have faith in your faith, or faith in a church, or faith in a minister-- You don’t have the right faith. Now, I think this is liberating stuff. You’re looking at me like, “Man, this is deep.” Do you know how many people I know that have faith in their faith, and the Bible never says to have faith in your faith? We’re to have the faith that Jesus had, faith in God, faith in God’s Word, and be living and believing what He says. I may not be there yet, but I’m working on it. See, there’s a difference. One says, “I don’t see nothing wrong with this,” the other one says, “You know, I’m working on this. I’m working on--I haven’t got through this one yet, but I’m working on it, and God promised me that I will get through it, and I’ll get to another arena, and there’ll be another one.”
Can faith alone save a person, and what is “faith in your faith”? (James 2:14)
James 2:14: What does it profit, my brethren, if someone says he has faith but does not have works? Can faith save him?
Is atheism a kind of faith?

He says those who hold beliefs such as atheism “have faith in what they believe.” He says the Supreme Court declared atheism a religion “because they have a belief system. They believe there’s no God, and they have no evidence there is--that there isn’t one. That is faith, that is belief.”
Is atheism a kind of faith?

Amen. Atheists, evolutionists, humanists, homosexuals, the freethinkers, pro-choice, the liberals, Democrats, the Socialist Party, all have faith in what they believe. It’s totally faith. The evolutionists have no evidence; it’s totally faith. The socialists have evidence that socialism has not worked, and they still believe socialism will work. That’s a fact, and it’s never-- Worked. Pro-choice women could care the least about the baby; they just don’t want any strings attached to their loose lifestyle, and if they get pregnant they want to get rid of it so they can keep living loosely. That’s their faith. See, it doesn’t edify, it doesn’t profit anybody else. And all of these are 501(c)(3), just like our religious exemption. They say they’re nonprofit corporations, they’re religions, they’re a belief system. The Supreme Court declared atheism a religion because they have a belief system. They believe there’s no God, and they have no evidence there is--that there isn’t one. That is faith, that is belief.
What does it mean to ask “are we stronger than He”?
He says it asks whether you use human understanding to “violate the direct commandments of God and provoke God to jealousy.” He asks, “Are you stronger than God? Have you become a God?”
Does Christian liberty mean anything goes?

He says “all things are lawful for me, but all things” do not edify. He asks how his liberty in going into a pagan temple builds him up or the church “when I’m directly violating the Ten Commandments and other commandments.”
What does he say a healthy church must be built on?

He says you cannot build a healthy church “using your own opinions and your own beliefs. It must be Jesus, His truth, His words, and the apostles’ doctrine, who got their doctrine straight from Jesus.”
Why does he point to the Bible when people say they have a word from God?
He asks, “why do I need to keep getting words of God from people when I have the Bible, which the Bible says is a more sure word of prophecy?”
Does he say playing pool is a sin?

No. He says “there’s nothing wrong with playing pool,” and that he has a pool table in his garage. He says in his youth it was called sin because the tables were in bars, “so instead of saying the atmosphere was wrong,” people called the game itself sin.
What does he say about being extreme?
He says “the Bible says in Ecclesiastes, ‘do not be extreme in anything.’” He says “we need to watch out with being extreme. We need to be practical.”
Why did the apostles say to abstain from blood and things strangled?
He says it is “because it’s related to Christ’s blood sacrifice for us. The blood had to be shed.”
Does he say a person in a church with rituals cannot be a believer?

No. He says it took God opening his understanding that “people can actually be a believer in Christ and be doing things in an erroneous way and still be a believer because they haven’t learned or come to the place yet where they can let go of the rituals and just embrace the truth.”
Does he say rich people are greedy?
No. He asks, “does it mean because a person is rich that they’re greedy? No, the Bible doesn’t back up that at all.”
Is hatred listed among the works of the flesh?

He reads it in the list and says hatred is when “you don’t like a certain race,” or women because they are women, or men because they are men, or rich because they are rich. He says it is a work of the flesh.
What does he say about reading the horoscope?
He asks, “do you read the horoscope every day?” and says “that’s an idol.” He says “before we start straightening everybody else out,” we need to straighten ourselves out.
How many times is “my faith” used in the Bible?
He says it is “only mentioned twice in the Bible”: the first place is James, where a person says “show me your faith without your works,” and the second is Jesus speaking to the church of Pergamos.
What does he say Jesus was persuaded of?

He says Jesus “was persuaded that He was God, that He was the Son of God, that He was the Savior of the world, that no man could get eternal life but through Him,” and that He “would do nothing without the will of the Father.”
Why does he say it matters to use the name of Jesus?
He says “God” is “a general word that can fit into anywhere, but they hate Jesus,” and they want “the freedom to go to heaven and have eternal life without a lifestyle that represents Jesus Christ.”

items.d: A Vine Cluster Church message on idols in the Old Testament, the New Testament and today. God commanded no other gods; Elijah faced Baal’s prophets and fire fell. Paul was called Hermes at Lystra, then stoned…
p: A Vine Cluster Church message on idols in the Old Testament, the New Testament and today. God commanded no other gods; Elijah faced Baal’s prophets and fire fell. Paul was called Hermes at Lystra, then stoned, and told Athens that God commands all people to repent. Today we idolize scientists, athletes and ourselves, yet technology can’t solve the moral problems families face.

1 Corinthians 6:9–10 lists idolaters among those who shall not inherit the kingdom. Paul, the chief of sinners, repented and turned; Jesus nails sin to the cross, buries it and gives power to live right.

We’re going to talk about idols this morning and how it applies to us last week we mentioned this scripture says the unrighteous shall not inherit the kingdom of God and he lists who he’s talking about in first Corinthians 6 verse 9 says neither fornicators nor idolaters adulterers. Effeminate sodomites thieves covetous drunkards revilers extortioners shall inherit the kingdom of God that’s important to remember because like we talked about last week you’ve got to make it when you make a commitment to Jesus Christ there is a transformation like Paul Paul’s testimony was that he turned from being the chiefest sinner he was the chief sinner he was the worst in our history of the world Paul was the worst and God turned him around God turned that man around and he repented Paul repented from his sin and he didn’t do those things again and that is the testimony of Jesus Christ that he can take your sin nail it to the cross I. Like that if you [unclear] nail it to the cross kill it bury it like what he did he died and he was buried and then he can come out of that grave with power give you power to live for Jesus Christ give you power to do what is right give you power to be a better father a better husband a better person. That’s what Jesus does and that transformation is that what we need to continue heading toward too. So we’re going to talk about idolatry this morning we’re going to look at idols in the Old Testament the New Testament and idols today. As you know a lot you know you don’t a lot of people don’t have you know the idol of gold in their house that they bow to or uh well.

1 Corinthians 6:9-10: Do you not know that the unrighteous will not inherit the kingdom of God? Do not be deceived. Neither fornicators, nor idolaters, nor adulterers, nor homosexuals, nor sodomites, nor thieves, nor covetous, nor drunkards, nor revilers, nor extortioners will inherit the kingdom of God.
What does God command about idols?

Exodus 20:3–5: you shall have no other gods before me; you shall not make any graven image nor bow down to them or serve them. God had just delivered Israel from Egypt, yet they made a golden calf and later served idols for generations.
What does God command about idols?

Depends. Exodus 20 verse 3 it starts God is laying out the law talking to Moses and the people of Israel when they came out of Egypt he just delivered them from Egypt that had them enslaved and in bondage and he starts giving them laws he says one of his laws is you shall have no other gods before me I just paid a big price getting you out of Egypt I I brought you out I delivered you you guys were praying to me and I came through so this is what I want you to do I want you to serve me. You shall have no other gods before me you shall not make unto me any graven image or any likeness of anything that is heaven above an earth beneath or the water under the earth and thou shalt not bow thyself to them or serve them and there’s our first offense in Israel they had a golden calf I mean this is before he got even said don’t serve other gods you know God brought them out and then they make a calf in an image of an image of gold and they started.
What does God command about idols?

Exodus 20:3-5: “You shall have no other gods before Me. “You shall not make for yourself a carved image—any likeness of anything that is in heaven above, or that is in the earth beneath, or that is in the water under the earth; you shall not bow down to them nor serve them. For I, the LORD your God, am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children to the third and fourth generations of those who hate Me,
What does Psalm 135 say about idols?

items.d: Preached as the coronavirus spread, this message compares the body’s immune system to a spiritual one. Some, like Asa, turned to physicians alone; Hezekiah and David turned to God. Lies spread like a virus…
p: Preached as the coronavirus spread, this message compares the body’s immune system to a spiritual one. Some, like Asa, turned to physicians alone; Hezekiah and David turned to God. Lies spread like a virus, but believers have authority over the enemy and must put on the armor of God, walk in the Spirit, and return to God in prayer and fasting.
What is the spiritual immune system?
Like our physical immune system fights viruses and bacteria, a spiritual immune system fights off the kingdom of darkness.

And this morning we’re going to talk about the immune system and the more this morning I want to the immune system like our physical immune system fights off and defends us from viruses and bacteria and also we have a spiritual immune system that fights off the kingdom of darkness and also has ways to attack viruses and bacteria that come into the body and this morning I want to look at this example and see how it relates to the spirit. But first I think God has a question for us this morning who will we turn to and have a few examples here that I’d like to go over first lady mary todd lincoln was Abraham lincoln’s wife when she when he was president and during their time there in 1862 she became inconsolable when her son died her son willie and instead.

In second Chronicles chapter 16 verse 12 we have the story of Asa he became diseased in his feet and his infirmity was severe says in the scriptures yet in his disease he did not seek the Lord but the physicians so here we have a case where someone only saw the natural solutions and did not seek God.

items.d: Christ holds the seven stars in His right hand. Those in God’s hand do His will and seek His glory, like Joseph. Don’t live under darkness’s hand or attack God’s people; no one can snatch us from His hand…

p: Opening a present truth series on Bible economics, Pastor David G. Kincer teaches that God commands six days of work and a day of rest, and promised supernatural protection to those who kept His feasts. He applies Deuteronomy 15:6 to national debt and to who rules a nation, insists that Christians work, and explains how he keeps the feast days as shadows fulfilled in Christ.

He says Bible economics includes work, leisure, recreation, property, money, saving, debt, medical necessities, retirement, banking, investments, insurance, foreign relations and military expense. He says “you better know about economics if you’re going to survive in this world,” and starts with work and rest.

Continuing and present truth we are going to be talking about Bible economics, including work, leisure, recreation, property, money, store or saving, debt, medical necessities, retirement, disability, banking, investments, insurance, foreign relations and military expense and whatever else comes under economics. He reads “six days shall you labor and do all your work,” and says the work here is income: “it is making money.” He says since Jesus said you can lead your ox to water or pull your donkey out of a pit on the Sabbath, the rest day is from earning income, not from every activity.

p: In the second part of Intro to Bible Economics, Pastor David G. Kincer describes the wise worker from Proverbs and Ecclesiastes: honest, diligent, educated, skilled and keeping up with technology. He teaches that two are better than one in marriage and work, that Paul commanded “if anyone will not work, neither shall he eat,” and that a believer who will not provide for his family is worse than an unbeliever.
What is a wise worker, according to Proverbs? (Proverbs 13:11; 14:23)

He says a wise worker does not gain dishonest wealth; the employee should give an honest day’s work and the employer an honest day’s pay. He says if employers paid employees as they would like to be paid “we’d have this thing cured and that’s Christian character,” and in all labor there is profit, but idle chatter leads only to poverty.

items.d: Following “Is Love a Lie?”, this message answers: God is love. He provided Himself as the Lamb, was wounded for our sins, and died for us while we were sinners. His love is for all who repent; He transforms us…
p: Following “Is Love a Lie?”, this message answers: God is love. He provided Himself as the Lamb, was wounded for our sins, and died for us while we were sinners. His love is for all who repent; He transforms us and delivers the godly, as with Noah and Lot.

items.d: God’s presence brings joy, but is it enough? Saul and Samson had His Spirit upon them yet didn’t obey. Joseph listened and was exalted. Elijah heard the still small voice. Jesus told Peter to feed His sheep.…

items.t: Is Jesus Christ the Same Today Concerning the Nations as Yesterday? — October 31, 2021
items.d: Pastor Kincer asks whether Jesus Christ is the same toward nations as yesterday. From Babel and Nimrod through Cyrus and Daniel 2, God has always ruled in the kingdoms of men, using nations to correct nations.…
p: Pastor Kincer asks whether Jesus Christ is the same toward nations as yesterday. From Babel and Nimrod through Cyrus and Daniel 2, God has always ruled in the kingdoms of men, using nations to correct nations. A nation’s long-term success depends on righteousness, and a remnant still pursues it.

items.t: It is Time for Judgment — November 1, 2020
items.d: Pastor David G. Kincer teaches that judgment begins at the house of God. Like Laish, the USA church dwells carelessly, quiet and secure, silent on injustice and the lost while culture shifted. Salvation…
p: Pastor David G. Kincer teaches that judgment begins at the house of God. Like Laish, the USA church dwells carelessly, quiet and secure, silent on injustice and the lost while culture shifted. Salvation requires repentance, and God calls His people to execute judgment and righteousness — not by might, but by His Spirit.
At the house of God; Judges 18 shows God has a time to deal with nations.

items.d: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer defines a miracle as something only God can do and gives two purposes for miracles in Scripture: to get people’s attention and to meet needs. He explains why some refuse…
p: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer defines a miracle as something only God can do and gives two purposes for miracles in Scripture: to get people’s attention and to meet needs. He explains why some refuse to believe even after seeing one, shows from John the Baptist that miracles are not required to believe, and calls repentance and the new birth the greatest miracle. He then teaches the story of the woman caught in adultery in John 8, and closes with a trust demonstration on faith and a call to believe for miracles in marriage and in salvation.
What is a miracle, and how does he describe the parting of the Red Sea? (Exodus 14:21-22)

He defines a miracle as “something beyond mankind’s ability to do. Human beings can’t do it, only God can do it.” He says it is not “the miracle of science. That’s not a miracle if mankind can do it.” He argues that “an army will not drown in one foot of water,” and that “God miraculously made the bottom of that sea dry.”
What is a miracle, and how does he describe the parting of the Red Sea? (Exodus 14:21-22)

A miracle is something beyond mankind’s ability to do. Human beings can’t do it, only God can do it. It’s called a miracle. We’re not talking about the miracle of science. That’s not a miracle if mankind can do it. That’s not a miracle. A miracle is something only God can do. And just for starters, these scientists say that the day the Israelites crossed over, it was at a place where there was one foot of water. Anybody with any brains between their ears knows that an army will not drown in one foot of water. God parted the Red Sea. The sides of the water congealed, they coagulated like buttermilk, only thicker, and they stabilized, and Israel went across on dry land. It didn’t take any time. God miraculously made the bottom of that sea dry. It takes days for a lake to become dry after the water’s gone. And then God destroyed the Egyptian army in that sea, because He miraculously, supernaturally, beyond mankind’s capability, parted those waters. Hallelujah. Same with creation. Scientists can say all they want, but when God spoke and said, “Let there be light,” there was instant light.
What is a miracle, and how does he describe the parting of the Red Sea? (Exodus 14:21-22)

Exodus 14:21-22: Then Moses stretched out his hand over the sea; and the LORD caused the sea to go back by a strong east wind all that night, and made the sea into dry land, and the waters were divided. So the children of Israel went into the midst of the sea on the dry ground, and the waters were a wall to them on their right hand and on their left.
Why does he say creation was instant, and what are two purposes of miracles? (Genesis 1:3; John 2:23; John 6:2)

He says when God said “Let there be light,” there was “instant light. Not a million years, not two million years, it was instant.” He says “He is a miraculous God,” and “miracles are part of His forte.” He gives two purposes: John 2:23, “when people see something done that human beings are incapable of doing, it gets their attention. If their heart is not hard, they will believe,” and John 6:2, “He wants to meet their need.” He says if a person is blind and “doctors can do nothing for him,” then “Jesus comes along and opens those eyes, that is a miracle.”
Why does he say creation was instant, and what are two purposes of miracles? (Genesis 1:3; John 2:23; John 6:2)

Not a million years, not two million years, it was instant, because God, when He speaks, bang, it happens. When He said, “Let the dry land appear,” bam. When He said, “Let the plants bring forth,” bam. It wasn’t even a day, He just did it one day and waited the next day to do something else. See, He is a miraculous God, and that’s the God of the Bible, and that’s the God that we Christians claim to know, and He is a miraculous God, and we forget that miracles are part of His forte. So us Catholics, us Protestants, Jews, and Muslims need to buck up to the Bible and let God be God. The purpose of miracles, John 2:23: “Many believed in His name, Jesus, when they saw the miracles which He did.” When people see something done that human beings are incapable of doing, it gets their attention. If their heart is not hard, they will believe. The second reason is He wants to meet their need. John 6:2: “A great multitude followed Jesus because they saw His miracles which He did on them that were diseased.” You see, they followed because they were doing miracles, they believed because they were doing miracles, and when He healed these diseases, He met a need. Leprosy could not be cured back in those days. In fact, it can’t even be cured today. You say, but Jesus, who is God, can do what humans cannot do. If a person is really blind, doctors can do nothing for him. Jesus comes along and opens those eyes, that is a miracle. That is the power of deity.
Why does he say creation was instant, and what are two purposes of miracles? (Genesis 1:3; John 2:23; John 6:2)

Genesis 1:3: Then God said, “Let there be light”; and there was light. John 2:23: Now when He was in Jerusalem at the Passover, during the feast, many believed in His name when they saw the signs which He did. John 6:2: Then a great multitude followed Him, because they saw His signs which He performed on those who were diseased.

Yeah, powerful.
What does “No man, Lord” show, and what does he say Jesus meant in John 8:11-12?

John 8:11: She said, “No one, Lord.” And Jesus said to her, “Neither do I condemn you; go and sin no more.” John 8:12: Then Jesus spoke to them again, saying, “I am the light of the world. He who follows Me shall not walk in darkness, but have the light of life.”
What does he say should be preached to sinners, and what was the trust demonstration about? (Hebrews 11:1)

He says “this is the kind of message that you preach to sinners,” not “church doctrine to sinners”: “They need to hear sinner sermons, are you with me? They need to hear sinner songs.” He then leads a volunteer through a trust exercise, saying “Faith is the substance, you see, it’s the reality of things hoped for, the evidence, the proof of things not seen,” and asks, “Do you believe I wouldn’t hurt you?” before asking her to fall backwards off the platform.
What does he say should be preached to sinners, and what was the trust demonstration about? (Hebrews 11:1)

Powerful, man. This is the kind of message that you preach to sinners. You don’t go out there like we tried a few years ago and preach church doctrine to sinners. They need to hear sinner sermons, are you with me? They need to hear sinner songs, and you don’t wait to go out there, you bring sinner songs in the church, and you put something in there for sinners in your messages. Face the congregation. Yes. Do you believe that I’m an honest man? Yes. Do you believe that I wouldn’t do anything to hurt you? Yes. Do you believe in the Lord Jesus? Yes. And His protection power? Okay, walk to my voice. Faith is the substance, you see, it’s the reality of things hoped for, the evidence, the proof of things not seen. All right, here, let me have your hand. You trust me not to let you bump into anything? Yes, yes, yes, yes. Okay, you got heels on? Yes. Now you’re walking like it. Now see, nothing happened, huh? No. You found me when you were blind and you couldn’t see me. Yes, you followed me through this path and you didn’t run into anything, and you couldn’t see if there were obstacles there, right? Yes. Hallelujah. Now, you ready to prove that you really believe? Sir, faith is the substance, the reality of things hoped for, it is the evidence and proof of things not seen. Okay, now, because nothing happened there, do you have the belief and faith to do this next thing I’m going to ask you to do, and nothing will happen? Mhm. See, nothing happened back there, right? Mhm. Okay, and just turn around like this. Okay, and inch yourself backwards. No, with your feet, inch yourself backward. Yes. Okay, right there. Now take one foot and take a step back and see what’s there. Oh, oh. Now put that foot back. No, no, no, stand there. Yeah, right there. Now, do you believe I wouldn’t hurt you? Yes, yes. All right, then I want to ask you, I’m going to let you go, I’m going to ask you just to fall backwards, straight backwards, off that platform. Really? Yes. I’m right here. See, we say we believe, but believe is a reality.
What does he say should be preached to sinners, and what was the trust demonstration about? (Hebrews 11:1)
Hebrews 11:1: Now faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen.
What does he say believing is, and is the Bible a book of faith? (Romans 10:17)

He says “believe is a reality. It’s not a fictitious thing, it’s not a fake thing, it’s a real thing.” He says faith is being convinced, and “He comes by His gospel, He comes by His Spirit.” He says “The Bible never says it is a book of faith,” that scientists and atheists say it to eliminate the Bible, but “the Bible says it’s a book of truth, and faith comes by hearing truth.” He says “we believe until we can’t see, and then, ‘Hold on here, I’m not going to take that step,’” and “this is where the American church is.”
What does he say believing is, and is the Bible a book of faith? (Romans 10:17)

It’s not a fictitious thing, it’s not a fake thing, it’s a real thing, of things hoped for. Do we hope to go to heaven? Do we hope Christ to empower us to live for Him here on earth, provide for our natural needs? Okay, the evidence, the proof. You see, because Christ can come with His gospel and convict me and convince me, which is faith. Faith is being convinced. He comes by His gospel, He comes by His Spirit, and He convinces Dave Kincer that He will save him from his sin, that He will give him eternal life. See, and scientists say that the Bible can’t be used because it’s a book of faith. The Bible never says it is a book of faith. That’s what scientists and atheists do to try to eliminate the Bible. The Bible says it’s a book of truth, and faith comes by hearing truth. Hallelujah. And how many of us are just like this young lady? We believe until we can’t see, and then, “Hold on here, I’m not going to take that step.” And this is where the American church is. And I keep saying the American church, because from my encounter in Third World countries, Africa, South America, Asia, which I’m going to be going to again this week, God is moving there. Things are happening. People are getting born again, prostitutes are changing their life, drug addicts are changing their life. I mean, things are happening, millions are coming to Christ in these nations every year, and in America we’re getting more and more religious.
What does he say believing is, and is the Bible a book of faith? (Romans 10:17)
Romans 10:17: So then faith comes by hearing, and hearing by the word of God.
What miracles does he say we should believe for, including salvation and marriage? (Romans 8:38-39; Ephesians 5:25)

He says that in Third World countries “millions are coming to Christ in these nations every year,” while “in America we’re getting more and more religious.” He lists miracles to believe in, including salvation, being “baptized in the Holy Ghost with power,” wisdom, knowledge, “understanding open up to understand the Scriptures,” and “marrying and staying married is a miracle.” He says “America’s marriages are falling apart like the world’s.” He concludes that “a miracle is something beyond human’s ability,” and “the reason some people won’t believe is because they don’t want their life to be exposed.”
What miracles does he say we should believe for, including salvation and marriage? (Romans 8:38-39; Ephesians 5:25)

And so we need to get back to believing in miracles: the miracle of salvation, the miracle of being baptized in the Holy Ghost with power, the miracle of having wisdom, the miracle of having knowledge, the miracle of having my understanding open up to understand the Scriptures, the miracle to love my wife as Christ loved the church, the miracle of a wife loving her husband and being loyal to him. That’s a miracle. Marrying and staying married is a miracle. Overcome the obstacles in marriage, fighting through the problems, hanging in there, and that’s what the Holy Ghost will do, and that’s what the Word will do. We need to see that, but we’re not seeing it in America. America’s marriages are falling apart like the world’s. Is the greatest miracle the power of the Word to convince you that you not only have eternal life when you die, but that you are an overcomer in this life? Amen. That the love of God is so great that nothing can separate you from His love. Nothing, nothing can draw you back into sin. That’s the kind of faith and that’s the kind of belief that the Bible speaks of. Just remember, a miracle is something beyond human’s ability. Jesus heals the body, the soul, and the spirit, so people will believe and so people’s needs will be met. Some won’t believe after seeing miracles, and some people believe without seeing miracles, and the reason some people won’t believe is because they don’t want their life to be exposed.
What miracles does he say we should believe for, including salvation and marriage? (Romans 8:38-39; Ephesians 5:25)

Ephesians 5:25: Husbands, love your wives, just as Christ also loved the church and gave Himself for her, Romans 8:38-39: For I am persuaded that neither death nor life, nor angels nor principalities nor powers, nor things present nor things to come, nor height nor depth, nor any other created thing, shall be able to separate us from the love of God which is in Christ Jesus our Lord.
How does he define a miracle?
He says, “A miracle is something beyond mankind’s ability to do. Human beings can’t do it, only God can do it.”
How fast does he say creation happened, and what is the first purpose of miracles he gives?

He says, “when God spoke and said, ‘Let there be light,’ there was instant light.” His first purpose is that “when people see something done that human beings are incapable of doing, it gets their attention.”
What second purpose of miracles does he give?
He says, “The second reason is He wants to meet their need,” and “when He healed these diseases, He met a need.”
Does he say miracles were only for New Testament times?
No. He says, “God is a God of miracles, and it wasn’t just for the New Testament time,” and “He did miracles then, He did miracles now, He did miracles in between.”
What does he say the leaders said about the miracle in Acts 4:16?
He reads that “a notable miracle has been done by them is manifest to all them that dwell in Jerusalem, and we cannot deny it,” and says “this is the Jewish leaders talking.”
How many great awakenings does he say America has had?
He says, “There’s been four great awakenings in America, there will be another.”
What does he say “the condemnation” in John 3:19 includes?
He says, “Condemnation is not only the judgment of what you did right and wrong, but it includes the punishment.”
What does he say is the whole purpose of Jesus coming to earth?
He asks, “What’s the whole purpose of Jesus coming to earth?” and answers, “To expose sin.”
Does he say John the Baptist did miracles?
No. He says, “John the Baptist did no miracles,” yet “was the greatest prophet,” “no physical miracle.”
What does he call the greatest miracle?
He says, “That is still the greatest miracle that God does,” and describes it as “when someone really gets born again, when someone really gets saved.”
Does he say to bring people to a church or to Jesus?
He says, “we got to bring people to Jesus, folks, not to a church group, to Jesus,” and “when I go witnessing, I don’t even talk about a church, I talk about the cross, I talk about Jesus.”
What does he think Jesus wrote on the ground?
He says the Bible “doesn’t tell us” what Jesus wrote, but “probably what Jesus wrote was Leviticus 20:10.”
What does he say Jesus told the woman in John 8:11?
He reads, “Neither do I condemn thee,” and says, “I won’t condemn you, and I have the right to condemn you. Isn’t that beautiful?”
Does he say the Bible is a book of faith?
No. He says, “The Bible never says it is a book of faith,” but “the Bible says it’s a book of truth, and faith comes by hearing truth.”
What does he say about marriage and miracles?
He says, “Marrying and staying married is a miracle. Overcome the obstacles in marriage, fighting through the problems, hanging in there, and that’s what the Holy Ghost will do.”

items.t: It's Time to Act Like Men
items.d: Pastor David G. Kincer uses Ezra as an example for the last-day church. God stirred Cyrus, raised leaders and people, restored the robbed vessels and united them as one man. Zerubbabel refused builders who…
p: Pastor David G. Kincer uses Ezra as an example for the last-day church. God stirred Cyrus, raised leaders and people, restored the robbed vessels and united them as one man. Zerubbabel refused builders who feared the Lord but served other gods. Despite legal opposition the house was finished through the prophets. Ezra fasted for adults, children and livelihood, and Revelation 21 shows the bride descending.

items.t: Jesus Christ’s Counterattack to Satan’s Secret Weapons 07/22/18
items.d: Pastor David G. Kincer finishes the parable of the sower: the good ground receives the word with an honest heart, obeys it, and bears fruit with patience. Then he gives Jesus Christ’s counterattack to Satan’s…
p: Pastor David G. Kincer finishes the parable of the sower: the good ground receives the word with an honest heart, obeys it, and bears fruit with patience. Then he gives Jesus Christ’s counterattack to Satan’s weapons: God restores and heals those on the path, the rock and among thorns, and restores the years the locusts have eaten.
What is the good ground in the parable of the sower?

The seed sown on good ground are they that, having heard the word, believe it and receive it with joy into an honest and good heart. They understand the full word, keep it, and bring forth fruit with patience.

items.t: Jesus Covers All, the New Covenant — August 4, 2024
items.d: The old covenant was a shadow, not the goal. In the new covenant God writes His laws on our hearts, is our God, lets all know Him, and remembers sins no more. Jesus is the guarantee of a better, final…
p: The old covenant was a shadow, not the goal. In the new covenant God writes His laws on our hearts, is our God, lets all know Him, and remembers sins no more. Jesus is the guarantee of a better, final covenant, and nothing may be added; any other gospel is accursed.

items.d: In “Jesus’ Goal,” Pastor David G. Kincer works through Isaiah 41 and 42, saying God challenges false religions, corrects his people yet never casts them away, and that Jesus’ goal is to bring justice to the…
p: In “Jesus’ Goal,” Pastor David G. Kincer works through Isaiah 41 and 42, saying God challenges false religions, corrects his people yet never casts them away, and that Jesus’ goal is to bring justice to the Gentiles so that they trust in him. He ties this to Matthew 12, the bruised reed and smoking flax, and the glory of grace and truth in 2 Corinthians 3:18.
Is Isaiah 41:2 about Cyrus of Persia or about Assyria?

He says commentaries read “one from the east” as Cyrus of Persia, but he believes it is Assyria because Isaiah has been talking about Assyria for several chapters. He says God named Assyria at the very beginning, in Genesis 2:14, when there were only Adam and Eve.
Is Isaiah 41:2 about Cyrus of Persia or about Assyria?

In Isaiah chapter 41, we’re going to be going through this chapter, and at the beginning he’s going to start out telling us about our enemies, God’s enemies, and their worthless religions and their worthless gods. Verse two of Isaiah 41, “Who raised up one from the east?” Now, I know your commentaries say this is Cyrus of Persia, but I’m going to tell you it’s Assyria, and I’m going to tell you why. He’s been talking about Assyria for several chapters, hasn’t he? Remember our past lessons, Assyria came, and then last week [unclear] they took all the cities of Judah and they surrounded Jerusalem, the king of Assyria, all right, and, uh, God came and slew their army. So Assyria is to the east, and. Uh, he says, who raised this nation up, who raised this king up, who gave nations unto him, who gave him the ability to conquer other nations, including Egypt, and made him rule over kings? Who has performed and done it, calling the generations from the beginning? Genesis 1, Genesis 2. “I, the Lord, am he.” Then he answers who did it. I raised up Assyria, I raised up the king of Assyria, and I said that Assyria was a nation and a people at the very beginning. Okay, which means he’s a supernatural God. Now, you go to Genesis 2:14, the third river is [unclear], it is one which goes toward the east of what? Assyria. Assyria, and he said the generations from the beginning. A generation can be the lifespan of one person, it can be a generation of a race, it can be a generation, a time period of a nation, and God at the very beginning named Assyria before it was even, there was only Adam and Eve, and yet he named Assyria at the very beginning. So I disagree with the commentaries. I do a lot of disagreeing, but I can give you biblical reasons why. And so God said it, and yes, at the beginning God talked about Assyria before it was even a nation, when it was just Adam and Eve. And then in verse 7, Isaiah, through the Holy Spirit, says the craftsman, the skillful worker, encouraged the goldsmith, the one that works with gold, and the goldsmith encouraged him who strikes the anvil, the one that works with iron, and the anvil worker encouraged the one who fastened it with pegs so that the, it would not totter, it wouldn’t tip over.
Is Isaiah 41:2 about Cyrus of Persia or about Assyria?

Isaiah 41:2: “Who raised up one from the east? Who in righteousness called him to His feet? Who gave the nations before him, And made him rule over kings? Who gave them as the dust to his sword, As driven stubble to his bow? Genesis 2:14: The name of the third river is Hiddekel; it is the one which goes toward the east of Assyria. The fourth river is the Euphrates.
Can idols and false religions tell the future?

He says God is challenging the religions of the world: if you really have a God, let your God tell us what is going to happen, as God named Assyria from the very beginning. He says an idol cannot do good or evil, and that candles and incense are no substitute for humbling ourselves in prayer and worship.

See, and what is he doing? He’s embarrassing them, because he’s showing them that it takes men to make an idol, and it takes something to hold it down so it won’t fall over, and if there is a real God, he don’t need any help and he don’t need to be fashioned by anybody. Okay, and that was the gods of Assyria, they worshiped idols. “Let them bring forth and show us what will happen.” So God is challenging the religions of the world. He said, if you really have a God, then let your God tell us what’s going to happen, because I, my God, Isaiah said, mentioned Assyria from the very beginning when it was just Adam and Eve. What do your God said that really happened? Amen. “Show the things that are to come,” verse 23, “that we may know that you are gods.” Predict something. Show us your God. He says, “Do good or do evil.” An idol can’t do good or it can’t do evil. It can’t part the Red Sea, it can’t bring rain on the harvest. These people that worshiped idols, and if, if the normal seasons brought the rain, then, you know, they said their idol did it, and their idol wasn’t doing anything, and if the rain didn’t come, then they thought their idol was mad at them, and so they did things to appease this idol that can’t do anything. It’s just logic. They have eyes, the Bible says, and they can’t see, they have ears and they can’t hear, they have a mouth, they can’t speak. So what good is an idol? And why the Catholic church uses them is beyond my biblical understanding. “Their [unclear] images,” verse 29, “are wind and confusion.” They are just confusion, because they can’t do anything. Listen, folks, lighting candles, burning incense, all these things that we substitute for the simplicity of humbling ourselves in prayer and worship and just living right, don’t do a thing. It doesn’t do anything to let it kindle. We feel like it does. You see, it doesn’t do anything. Prayer and talking to God, worshiping him are the principles he’s given us. Now remember, atheism, humanism are religions. The Supreme Court of the United States declared atheism as a religion, because a religion is principles that man use to worship, or, uh, teach and, and express a God. So atheists who don’t believe in a God, they have a lot of rules and a lot of teaching why there is no God, so they are religion. If there wasn’t a God, why would they even address the issue? p: In “Jesus’ Processing Plan, Part 2,” Pastor David G. Kincer says no one takes the honor of a calling to himself; God places people in the body as he sees fit, and the apostles were given authority and understanding by Jesus. He explains from his own experience why he moved away from personal prophecy to “a more excellent way,” love, and says all believers can worship, love and ask God for wisdom.

He says hanging around prophets or apostles does not make you one, and there is nothing wrong with being the best mother, dad or worker if that is what God has called you to.

items.d: Jesus taught it is best not to swear at all. Herod kept a wicked oath and was only sorry; Peter swore falsely, wept in remorse and was restored. As Numbers 30 foreshadows, Christ our Father and husband can…
p: Jesus taught it is best not to swear at all. Herod kept a wicked oath and was only sorry; Peter swore falsely, wept in remorse and was restored. As Numbers 30 foreshadows, Christ our Father and husband can overrule failed vows so we can start anew.

items.d: Session nine: Jesus’ “do not resist evil” is not about criminals, who must be punished, but about stopping fights before they start. Love enemies by doing good, blessing and praying; be merciful as the Father…
p: Session nine: Jesus’ “do not resist evil” is not about criminals, who must be punished, but about stopping fights before they start. Love enemies by doing good, blessing and praying; be merciful as the Father is—and still do justly and speak up.

items.t: Jesus Teaching on Divorce (Watch Till End)
items.d: A condensed edit of the June 26, 2022 message: Jesus stands firm against divorce, yet God permitted it for hard hearts and pardons; the abused may leave, and the divorced and widowed may remarry.
