p: The final message in the Job series shows how Job responded when God spoke from the whirlwind: he acknowledged God can do everything, admitted he spoke what he didn’t understand, heard God, and repented in dust and ashes. When Job prayed for his friends, God restored him double; we too must confess, hate evil, forgive and change our behavior.

That God brought them through chastening and it yielded fruits of righteousness.
Adultery with Bathsheba and the murder of Uriah.
What did David’s sin give occasion to?
For the enemies of the Lord to blaspheme.
What is said about the COVID shot in the bread prayer?
People identify with it to be made whole, but we identify wholeheartedly with the body of Christ.

items.d: Pastor David G. Kincer compares King David with King Jesus. David sinned but repented; Jesus died for all sin. Both were betrayed by close friends and opposed by leaders, yet God’s plan prevailed. God stopped…

items.d: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer asks why most Christians in America lack knowledge of the Scriptures. He walks through the bad fruit of the vineyard in Isaiah 5 and God’s way out of captivity in Isaiah…
p: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer asks why most Christians in America lack knowledge of the Scriptures. He walks through the bad fruit of the vineyard in Isaiah 5 and God’s way out of captivity in Isaiah 6: letting the old die, seeing Jesus, worshiping, confessing sin and answering “Here I am.” He ends with why Jesus spoke in parables and says understanding comes by coming to Jesus.
Why does he say most Christians in America lack knowledge of the Scriptures? (Isaiah 5)

He opens by saying “most Christians in America have no understanding of the scriptures at all,” and that if we know why, “we can, what, reverse it and get knowledge of the scriptures.” He says Isaiah 5 shows that we, the people of God, are his vineyard, “a parable, an allegory, a metaphor of the truth of God’s word,” and that this vineyard is producing bad fruit.
Why does he say most Christians in America lack knowledge of the Scriptures? (Isaiah 5)

It’s a negative title, because most Christians in America have no understanding of the scriptures at all, including many of you this morning. And if we know why we don’t have knowledge of the scriptures, then we can, what, reverse it and get knowledge of the scriptures. Hallelujah. And you just try to figure out right now the answer. Just say in your mind, “I think I got the answer to that,” and then see how it matches up at the end, when you get God’s answer. Is that a good one? Yeah, all right. Yeah, you know, you need to learn how to get involved in these things. All right, so we go to Isaiah chapter 5, and here God is going to talk about his vineyard, and he told us in Isaiah 5 that we, the people of God, are his vineyard. See, so the vineyard is a parable, an allegory, a metaphor of the truth of God’s word. So when you go to the vineyard in the Bible, you know he’s talking about what? The church, unless he specifically says it’s a wild vineyard, talking about sin. Okay, so here we are. This vineyard is producing bad fruit. So who is producing bad fruit? God’s people, believers. And Jesus said, “You know them by their fruit,” so fruit’s important. Your works are important, what you do and what you say is important.

Isaiah 5:7: For the vineyard of the LORD of hosts is the house of Israel, And the men of Judah are His pleasant plant. He looked for justice, but behold, oppression; For righteousness, but behold, a cry for help. Matthew 7:16: You will know them by their fruits. Do men gather grapes from thornbushes or figs from thistles?
What does he say about tyranny and social programs replacing justice and righteousness? (Isaiah 5:7)

He names the first bad fruit as replacing justice with oppression: “instead of justice we have oppression, we have tyranny,” with church leaders who “do nothing but manipulate the people,” when Jesus is the real shepherd. The second is replacing righteousness with welfare; he says “the church has not been given social programs,” and that turning people “to righteousness and to justice” is “their priority job.”

God has ordained that we assemble together to provoke one another to love and to good works and to exhort one another. We need to be reminded to live right. Isn’t that right? We don’t need to be told, “You’re okay the way you are.” No, the church is supposed to assemble together to build character and maintain character. I don’t care what group you’re in, there’s only one church anyway, and that’s the church of the Lord Jesus Christ. And that’s not the Latter-day Saints, that’s the church of the Lord Jesus Christ. You’re born into it, you’re birthed into it. I don’t care what the title is out on the door. Throw away the titles. And then what? The angel brought a coal from the fire, the altar of heaven, touched his lip, took away the guilt, cleansed his lip, and atoned for his sin. See, you repent until God births repentance, forgiveness in you. Till heaven touches you, you can’t get a baptismal certificate, or a church membership card, or whatever, I ain’t going to do anything, but you repent, you confess your wrong until heaven comes and touches you and cleanses you, and that’s what we call being born again. Are you there? Hallelujah. Now, so now we’re delivered from captivity. After being delivered from captivity, what’s next on God’s agenda? Hallelujah. “Whom shall I send to these people in captivity?” See, he is free now. He’s not going into captivity, he’s not in captivity, he’s free, and now God says, “Whom am I going to send to these people in captivity?” Does God always care for the people in captivity? Yes. Yes, church, he does. He’s always interested in them, but he has principles. Somebody’s got to go and talk to them. See, we can’t sit back and be non-involved Christians. We can’t be so worried about offending people that we are silenced by public opinion: keep your religion to yourself. Why is it that every subject’s okay to talk about but Jesus Christ? Because Jesus Christ brings conviction, and you either get mad or you get glad, one of the two. There’s no neutral reaction here. It’s always, they are mad because they don’t want to change their ways and they don’t want to hear you, or they’re glad because, “Hey, thank you for showing me the way.” The response of Isaiah, who is now cleansed, delivered, atoned for, says, “Here I am. I’m atoned for, I’m clean, I’m forgiven. Here I am, use me. I don’t know what to do, but here I am, use me.” Do you ever pray that prayer? Prayer in America, the, the prayers I hear, I hear this all the time: “God help me, God help me, God help me, God help me.” For 30 years people have been praying the same prayer. “God help me, God help me, God help me, help me to be a prayer, help me to be a worshiper.” Is God the hindrance here? No. We need to respond and say, “Here I am, use me. Make me a prayer, make me a worshiper, make me one that can speak the word of God with confidence.” But that requires responsibility to speak the word, you got to read the word. “Oh my gosh, I got to miss the soap operas, that’s a, that’s a big price. I’m going to miss my kid’s soccer game.” “Here I am.” What can you say? “Here I am, send me.” Let me hear it: “Here I am, send me.” Yes.
How does he say a person is cleansed and sent? (Isaiah 6:6-8)

Hebrews 10:24-25: And let us consider one another in order to stir up love and good works, not forsaking the assembling of ourselves together, as is the manner of some, but exhorting one another, and so much the more as you see the Day approaching. Isaiah 6:6-7: Then one of the seraphim flew to me, having in his hand a live coal which he had taken with the tongs from the altar. And he touched my mouth with it, and said: “Behold, this has touched your lips; Your iniquity is taken away, And your sin purged.” Isaiah 6:8: Also I heard the voice of the Lord, saying: “Whom shall I send, And who will go for Us?” Then I said, “Here am I! Send me.”
What message did God give Isaiah to preach, and for how long? (Isaiah 6:9-12)

He says God’s message was “be ever hearing” but “never understanding,” and that “it’s not your responsibility whether they listen or not, it’s your responsibility to speak the word of God.” When Isaiah asks how long, God says until the cities lie ruined, which he takes to mean the Babylonian captivity, “then he gives an exception.” He attributes this message to Ezekiel; see the editor note.
What message did God give Isaiah to preach, and for how long? (Isaiah 6:9-12)

Don’t be afraid to speak with fortitude, church. Guys, we sing some of our songs so wimpy. “I’m a child of the King” isn’t a wimpy song, that is a prophetic song. “I am his, royal blood flows.” Sing it like that. Could that be an amen? “Go and tell these people.” “Okay, here I am, use me.” You got to go and you got to do something. “But Lord, it’s embarrassing to tell people about God Almighty, and the public opinion is keep your religion to yourself.” That’s America. Isn’t that America? Oh yeah. And look at the message he’s going to give him now. I don’t know if you remember this or not, but Ezekiel was given a message to take to the people, and God said, “They’re not going to listen to you.” You want me to go preach to people that are not going to listen? Yeah, church, it’s not your responsibility whether they listen or not, it’s your responsibility to speak the word of God. Here’s the message: “Be ever hearing, but never understanding. Be ever seeing, but never perceiving.” Aren’t you just excited about this message? “I’m going to make your heart callous and your ears dull and close your eyes.” That’s the message I was given: the message, “[unclear] your heart, close your eyes, you can’t see, you can’t hear.” Oh man, can you just see the crowds coming to hear that one? Are you getting this? I would not want to go with this message. Give me the signs and wonders, man. “Otherwise you might see with your eyes and hear with your ears, understand with your heart, and turn and be healed.” Man, what kind of message is that? See, this is where you need revelation. Let me raise your hand right now and say, “Boy, this makes no sense right now.” The rest of you lying through your teeth. Wow. How many want to take this message to the [unclear]? Nobody. Yeah. What is he saying? And then Isaiah responds and said, “Well, how long am I to preach this message?” How long? I mean, I hope it’s just one day or five minutes. And God replies and said, “Until the cities lie ruined without inhabitant, houses deserted, fields ruined and ravaged, until the Lord has sent everyone far away.” Now you begin to understand that he’s going to take them into Babylonian captivity, and he’s going to give them a message where they can’t see and hear, unless something else is done. Are you there? “The land is utterly forsaken.” Then he gives an exception. Praise God for the exception. He always gives an exception.
What message did God give Isaiah to preach, and for how long? (Isaiah 6:9-12)

Isaiah 6:9-10: And He said, “Go, and tell this people: ‘Keep on hearing, but do not understand; Keep on seeing, but do not perceive.’ “Make the heart of this people dull, And their ears heavy, And shut their eyes; Lest they see with their eyes, And hear with their ears, And understand with their heart, And return and be healed.” Isaiah 6:11-12: Then I said, “Lord, how long?” And He answered: “Until the cities are laid waste and without inhabitant, The houses are without a man, The land is utterly desolate, The LORD has removed men far away, And the forsaken places are many in the midst of the land.
Who are the tenth, the holy seed that escape captivity? (Isaiah 6:13)

He says “though a tenth remain in the land,” and to be in that tenth you must die to the old, get in the new, become a worshiper and seek Jesus. He says “it’s righteousness that will protect you in any judgment or visitation of God,” that “repentance to do right, not faith in grace” escapes captivity, and that “the key is the word repent.” He says God “cuts us down to size, and then he starts growing us again.”
Who are the tenth, the holy seed that escape captivity? (Isaiah 6:13)

Church, everyone’s supposed to go far away, and everybody wants to take the word of God literally without balancing it out with the whole word of God. He’s going to give us an exception, all right. “Though a tenth remain in the land, it will be laid waste, but as trees leave stumps when cut down, so” how many is going to be left in the land? 10%. How many want to be part of the 10 [unclear]? Well, to be that part, you got to follow what we just taught, what Isaiah was revealed. You need to die to the old, get in the new, hallelujah, become a worshiper, look for Jesus, seek him. Now the tenth, the tenth, so the holy seed will be the stump in the land. I told you in the last message, it’s righteousness. It’s not being a Catholic, a Baptist, or Pentecostal or whatever, it’s righteousness that will protect you in any judgment or visitation of God. You don’t have to be a preacher, you don’t have to speak in tongues, you don’t have to prophesy, you don’t have to lead one soul to Christ. If you’re living righteous, God’s going to honor you, and by the way, if you are living righteous, he’s going to make you a fisher of men. The two go together. The holy seed. So repentance to do right, not faith in grace, that’s the one that’s going to escape the captivity. And when God judges America, and the road America’s on, on, I’m speaking this prophetically, by history and by the Bible, the road America’s on, God’s going to intervene. And I told you, Mexico can beat us militarily when God intervenes. Nobody and no army can protect you when God decides that a nation needs to be humbled. Are you there? Remember, Jeremiah said, “When the Lord has determined judgment upon a nation, upon a people, if they will turn and repent, he will turn from the judgment.” So we can, what? Change this road we’re on, and the key is the word repent. Say it: repent. People in America need to turn from their wrong and do right. 1 Corinthians 13. You know that us Pentecostals, because we speak in tongues and prophesy and get a word of knowledge sometimes, and, you know, we see, go, God healed the sick and all that. 1 Corinthians 13 is very clear, though: “Though I speak with the tongues of men and of angels and have not love, I’m nothing. Though I can prophesy and have faith to move mountains and do miracles and have not love, I’m nothing. Though I give my body to be burned, and though I bestow all my goods to feed the poor,” all these social programs that we’re into, drug rehabilitation, alcohol rehabilitation, prostitute rehabilitation, divorce rehab, all these social programs, “without love it profits me nothing.” And then he describes love very clear, in great detail. “Love is patient.” There went 50% of us. “Love is kind.” There went another 50% of the 50%. “Love doesn’t boast of itself.” We all went. We want people to brag on us, and if they don’t, we brag about ourselves. Are you there? See, the tree was a stump, and it grew into a tree. The stump, yes. God will cut us down, God will trim us, God will correct us, but any stump left will start growing into a tree again. Hallelujah. See, when the tree is wrong and the fruit’s wrong, God cuts it down. He doesn’t cut us out, he cuts us down to size, and then he starts growing us again. How many could use a regrowth? Yeah, yeah. Isn’t this powerful?
Who are the tenth, the holy seed that escape captivity? (Isaiah 6:13)

Isaiah 6:13: But yet a tenth will be in it, And will return and be for consuming, As a terebinth tree or as an oak, Whose stump remains when it is cut down. So the holy seed shall be its stump.” Jeremiah 18:7-8: The instant I speak concerning a nation and concerning a kingdom, to pluck up, to pull down, and to destroy it, if that nation against whom I have spoken turns from its evil, I will relent of the disaster that I thought to bring upon it. 1 Corinthians 13:1-5: Though I speak with the tongues of men and of angels, but have not love, I have become sounding brass or a clanging cymbal. And though I have the gift of prophecy, and understand all mysteries and all knowledge, and though I have all faith, so that I could remove mountains, but have not love, I am nothing. And though I bestow all my goods to feed the poor, and though I give my body to be burned, but have not love, it profits me nothing. Love suffers long and is kind; love does not envy; love does not parade itself, is not puffed up; does not behave rudely, does not seek its own, is not provoked, thinks no evil;
What does he say about end-time prophets and blood moons?

He says God “doesn’t need blood moons or anything to consummate the end time,” only “Jesus coming through that cloud.” He tells hearers “don’t believe that garbage,” calls it “salesmanship,” and says he told a Pentecostal in China that people following such prophets were following “false prophets.” These are his opinions about unnamed groups and have not been verified here.
What does he say about end-time prophets and blood moons?

See, I don’t care what God’s going to do, these Kansas City prophets and all these people with the blood moons and all this junk coming up, you know, scaring everybody to death. God doesn’t need blood moons or anything to consummate the end time. All he needs is Jesus coming through that cloud, and bam! Woo! Everybody is going to see. Are you there? And he’ll do it. He don’t need any planets lining up, he don’t need atomic bombs to renovate this earth, he’s going to do it on his own way and in his own time. So don’t believe that garbage, that’s just a, that’s just salesmanship. They make millions off of you guys, and when they’re wrong, they start all over again and make millions off the next bunch. Are you there? And in China, I told him, when one person told me, a Pentecostal, that they were following these prophets, I said, “Those are false prophets.” He goes, “They’re the nice people.” I don’t care if they’re nice people or not, they’re false prophets. I said, “You better be following James and John and Matthew and Luke.” Amen. Somebody’s got to say something.
Why did Jesus speak in parables? (Matthew 13:10-17)

He says the disciples asked why Jesus spoke in parables, and the answer is “it has been given you to know the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven, but to them it has not been given.” He says “whoever has, to him more will be given,” and that what the disciples had was “a response of heart”: they repented, believed and followed, so they got more.
Why did Jesus speak in parables? (Matthew 13:10-17)

Now, in conclusion, we’re going to give you the message that Isaiah was given. All right, and you can line up your interpretation that you gave at the beginning with the real answer. We find it in the New Testament. Okay, New Testament use of Isaiah chapter 6. “Why do you speak to them in” what? Say the word: parables. Remember, he speaks through shadow, laws, parables, metaphors, allegories, you know, uh, a historical report of Israel. He speaks to us through all these things. And so the disciples are saying, “Why do you speak to the people in parables? Why don’t you just say directly what you want to say?” Are you there? Are you with me so far? Yeah. Why did God use parables? Why did he just say what he wanted to say? “Because it has been given you to know the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven, but to them it has not been given.” Okay, he says, “You apostles, it’s been given to you to know the mysteries.” So are there secrets and mysteries hidden in the Bible? Yeah, the Bible says that, we taught you that before. Okay, why would God hide these things in the word? Why would he do that? Is that a good question? Why can’t I just open the book and, bang, I just get it? And, may, read Leviticus the first time and go, “Oh man, this is boring.” That was me. I couldn’t wait to get through it, it was torture going through Leviticus, just torture. Now when I go through Leviticus, bam! “For whoever has,” what’s the word? Has. What, what do these apostles have, these disciples have, that the other people didn’t have? You see, “whoever has, to him more will be given, and he will have” what? “Abundance. But whoever does not have,” what, don’t they have? “Even that which he has will be taken away from him.” So the one who has keeps having more, and the one who doesn’t have loses even that which he had. So he’s below zero. What did they have? First of all, Isaiah was sent to speak to the people in what? In what? In parables. Say it: parables. He was sent to speak to the people in parables. Why? Why would God do that, and not knowing that the parables they would not understand? Folks, what they had was a response of heart. When Jesus came to the apostles and said, “Follow me,” they just dropped everything and followed him. They responded. See, they didn’t have authority over sicknesses and demons at that time, they had a responsive heart. See, when Jesus preached “Repent and believe the gospel,” they responded, they repented, they believed. When he said “Follow me,” they just dropped everything and followed him. See, they had a response of heart, and every time Christ came with something new, they responded, so they got more. Are you there? And they that don’t have a responsive heart, you even lose the little bit you had. You might have knowledge of Christ, you might have knowledge of the Bible, you even lose that. Are you there? So why does God do this? Because parables have to be revealed by the Spirit, by Jesus himself, and unless you come to him, you can’t understand and be healed and be delivered, because only he and the Holy Ghost can open up the Bible to you.
Why did Jesus speak in parables? (Matthew 13:10-17)

Matthew 13:10-11: And the disciples came and said to Him, “Why do You speak to them in parables?” He answered and said to them, “Because it has been given to you to know the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven, but to them it has not been given. Matthew 13:12: For whoever has, to him more will be given, and he will have abundance; but whoever does not have, even what he has will be taken away from him.
How does he say we can understand the Bible? (John 6:44, Matthew 13:13-15)

He says “the word of God is beyond human intellect,” and that the answer is to come to Jesus, humble yourself and say “Lord, open my eyes, open my understanding.” He says “the Holy Ghost is what opens your eyes,” that American people lack knowledge of the scriptures “because they don’t humble themselves, come to Jesus,” and he urges listening to messages “on your knees.”
How does he say we can understand the Bible? (John 6:44, Matthew 13:13-15)

Didn’t Jesus say, “No man comes to me except the Father draw him, and no man comes to the Father but by me”? You can’t skirt, see, the revelation of God’s word, the drawing of his Spirit, by human intellect. And God knows that those that come to him, then they are candidates to be revealed the parables and healed and set free. Are you there? See, the word of God is beyond human intellect. If you keep it in the human intellect, you’re not going to understand that Bible. But when you come to Jesus and humble yourself and say, “God, open my understanding, open my eyes,” he will. I can remember when parables of the New Testament were opened to me. I can remember the day, bam, God came, because I didn’t understand those parables, things didn’t make sense to me, and bam, and once I understood the key parable, I understood them all, and then the New Testament just opened up tremendously, just like the Old Testament, in shadow, laws, and, and, uh, historical events of Israel, just revelation came. Are you there? See, why did he want Isaiah to talk in parables? Because the people must come to God to get the understanding, the knowledge, and that’s why American people don’t have knowledge of the scriptures, is because they don’t humble themselves, come to Jesus, come to God, let the Holy Spirit, let Jesus reveal the truth to them. You see it? Do you see it? Yes. See, that’s why you can’t get understanding just hearing me preach on Sunday morning. You need to get those messages and listen to them, like Mr. Barnes is trying to, been prodding you guys to do. You need to listen to them two or three times. You need to listen to them on your knees. You need to open that book on your knees, and you need to say, “Lord, open my eyes, open my understanding,” and he will. There’s no preacher has the authority and power to open your eyes and give you understanding. They are vehicles, they are vessels. The Holy Ghost is what opens your eyes. Amen. And see, if your heart’s not right, you’re not going to understand, and God’s going to discipline you. Are we here, church? Hallelujah. Now, did you get it? Well, at the beginning you had it all figured out. Yeah, yeah, yeah. Isaiah spoke to them in parables so those who were really genuine in God would understand and be healed and delivered, and those not, the religious people, didn’t get it. “Therefore I speak to them in parables, for they see not.” Now he’s quoting Isaiah: “and hearing they do not hear, seeing they do not see, nor do they understand.” And this is where the American church is. In them the prophecy of Isaiah’s fulfilled: “Hearing you will hear and shall not understand, seeing you will see and not perceive, for the hearts of these people have grown dull, their ears are hard of hearing, their eyes they have closed, lest they should see with their eyes, hear with their ears, understand with their hearts,” their mind, the heart is the mind, the intellect, “turn,” what’s another word for turn? Repent. “So that I should heal them.” And so God has all these mysteries and all these parables so that people have to come to him. And that’s the message Isaiah had. He had a message of parables, that if people weren’t genuine, they didn’t get the message, and people who were the tenth, they got the message, and they were saved from the captivity.
How does he say we can understand the Bible? (John 6:44, Matthew 13:13-15)

John 6:44: No one can come to Me unless the Father who sent Me draws him; and I will raise him up at the last day. Matthew 13:13-15: Therefore I speak to them in parables, because seeing they do not see, and hearing they do not hear, nor do they understand. And in them the prophecy of Isaiah is fulfilled, which says: ‘Hearing you will hear and shall not understand, And seeing you will see and not perceive; For the hearts of this people have grown dull. Their ears are hard of hearing, And their eyes they have closed, Lest they should see with their eyes and hear with their ears, Lest they should understand with their hearts and turn, So that I should heal them.’
What does he say the vineyard represents in the Bible?

He says Isaiah 5 shows “we, the people of God, are his vineyard,” and that when the Bible mentions the vineyard “he’s talking about what? The church,” unless it specifically says “a wild vineyard,” which is about sin.
What does he say it means that we know people by their fruit?
He says Jesus said “you know them by their fruit,” so “your works are important, what you do and what you say is important.”
Who does he say the real leader and shepherd is?
He says it is Jesus Christ, and that “all the rest of us are under-shepherds, we’re just delegated people” who need to “get off our high horse” and point people to him.
What does he say matters without righteousness?

He says “without righteousness you’re not beans,” and that “justice and righteousness are high principles in God’s word.” He says the church’s “priority job” is preaching the gospel and turning people to righteousness and justice.
What does he say “the year King Uzziah died” has to do with us?
He says “all things were written for our learning,” and that the king’s death shows “there has to be a death of the old thing before the bringing in of the new thing.”
What examples does he give of the old dying before the new?

He gives Saul and David (“David was a man after God’s own heart”), Moses and Joshua, and Jesus, who “had to die before the church was raised up.” He adds that “we got to die to ourself,” and quotes “if any man be in Christ” as being a new creation.
Does he say angels have wings?
He says no: “angels don’t have wings. Seraphim and cherubim have wings.” He says he has been trying to correct this for 40 years.
What does he say about praying in secret during corporate worship?
He says “worship isn’t the time to be secret, and corporate prayer is not a time to be in your closet. It’s an attitude.” He says “I’m not praying for people to hear, I’m praying to my God.”
How much time with God does he say we should give each day?
He asks people to give God “one hour a day,” and says “the word, prayer, and worship, the three work together,” with the Spirit giving “revelation of what you read.”
What does he say about making excuses for our failures?
He says “stop justifying your error. Just admit you’re wrong,” and that “the power of the blood of Christ is higher than the way you were raised.”
Does he say a person can be a “non-church person”?

He says “nobody can be a non-church person,” because God has ordained that we “assemble together to provoke one another to love and to good works.” He says “there’s only one church anyway, and that’s the church of the Lord Jesus Christ.”
Why does he say people avoid talking about Jesus?
He says every subject is okay to talk about but Jesus Christ “because Jesus Christ brings conviction and you either get mad or you get glad, one of the two.”
What does he say about the prayer “God help me”?
He says people have prayed “God help me” for 30 years, and asks “is God the hindrance here? No.” He says we need to respond, “Here I am, use me.”
What does he say 1 Corinthians 13 teaches about works without love?

Reading 1 Corinthians 13, he says that even tongues, prophecy, faith that moves mountains and giving to the poor are nothing “without love it profits me nothing.” He applies it to social programs and rehabilitation work.
What does he say about a tree that God cuts down to a stump?

He says “God will cut us down, God will trim us, God will correct us, but any stump left will start growing into a tree again.” He says God “doesn’t cut us out, he cuts us down to size, and then he starts growing us again.”

items.d: On his last day Belshazzar mocked God’s holy vessels; the queen remembered Daniel. The last-day church needs God’s wisdom, given liberally without fault-finding. People want miracles rather than wisdom, but…
p: On his last day Belshazzar mocked God’s holy vessels; the queen remembered Daniel. The last-day church needs God’s wisdom, given liberally without fault-finding. People want miracles rather than wisdom, but anyone can be reached.
Your last day on earth—Belshazzar; JFK was a great speaker, but could he go to hell?

Chapter five. The topic of this session is your last day on Earth. Your last day to live before standing before Jesus Christ and his judgment. We have a tremendous illustration here what’s going to take place at the last day judgment. And we’re going to see a man that has one day left to live. One day, less than one day. He’s got a few hours to live. And then he is going to stand before the judgment. Hebrews 9:27 says, “It’s appointed unto men once to die and after that the judgment.” I’m going to give you a couple of famous men that you know. All right. The Bible says, “Man looks [clears throat] on the outward.” Men will praise you for all your accomplishments. We have John F. Kennedy. He was a great speaker. He was a university graduate, a smart man, intelligent man. He was a war hero. He did a lot of good. He made some good speeches. “Don’t ask what your nation can do for you, but what you can do for your nation.” Powerful statement. He stood up to Russia when Russia was bringing missiles into Cuba. And they [clears throat] had them in firing order. They waited too late and the Russians actually had the missiles equipped to work. And they could have reached the major cities on the eastern coast of America. And Kennedy stood up against them, put a barricade around Cuba. And I remember, man, I was for my I didn’t care if he’s a Democrat. I didn’t care if he’s a Catholic. He was the first Catholic to be elected pres- This guy stood up for something that was right. And this boy, who was about 20 years old at the time was ready to join the military if these guys are going to mess around with us. And so he’s famous. We have another man, Martin Luther King, did a tremendous job of leading the civil rights movement to get rid of this separate but equal foolish Supreme Court decision that hung around for decades, uh like 80 years. 80 years of nonsense because the Supreme Court said it was constitutional. The Supreme Court, folks, isn’t always right. And your latest Supreme Court member is a homosexual. A female homosexual. They’re electing anybody to the Supreme Court. They’ve made many mistakes in days past. This guy led that civil rights movement, put his life on the line. He was another great speaker. I [clears have a dream. Throat]. And one of his famous statements is that man won’t be looked upon by what earth color of skin he has, but his character. Powerful statement. But both of these men flagrantly and continuously committed adultery, sexual immorality. Both of them. And I cannot find any John F. Kennedy lover that will a Catholic person that will say he could possibly go to hell because of look what he did. I cannot find one black person that will say it was possible for Martin Luther King to go to hell for his adultery. He died. Both of these men, those pictures were taken, they had about 1 minute to live. They had 60 seconds to live. Those pictures were taken 60 seconds and both of them were committing adultery. In fact, John F. Kennedy had a hookup in the city. Had a woman flown down for his use at the time of his assassination. Now, let me ask you this. Do you want to go into eternity facing Jesus Christ with that on your record? The church world thinks this thing is a joke. And they can’t possibly think, “How can Luther and and John F. Kennedy go to hell when look at what they did?” You’re not the judge. The Bible says, “Thou shalt not commit sexual immorality.” It’s one of the 10 Commandments. It is a hell sin. They both were married. They both had children. And they’re living that kind of permissive lives. And the American Christian on a high percentage are so ignorant of God’s word and so unlearned in their mind, they just can’t fathom that somebody like this could face Jesus and be sentenced to hell. Now, do we have your attention? Let’s look at this man. This man in chapter 5 has less than 1 day to live. He has a few hours. All right? Belshazzar, king of Babylon. Chapter 5, verse 1. He makes an alcoholic party. He throws a party with alcohol to get high and get drunk in. Okay? He calls in 1,000 of his leaders. If you know history and you read history, it wasn’t just leaders, the whole city was having a festival, a celebration, uh uh a holiday, and they were worshipping their gods and you know, getting drunk and doing what pagans do. He brought the gold and silver vessels from the house of God. Years before, Nebuchadnezzar brought the vessels from God’s house to Babylon.

p: In this short teaching Pastor David G. Kincer explains Jefferson’s “laws of nature and of nature’s God” from Bolingbroke and Blackstone as following God in his works and word—the Bible. He says America’s founding and the Declaration rest on Jesus Christ and Bible morals, and warns that lack of this knowledge destroys people.
What did Jefferson mean by “the laws of nature and of nature’s God”?

He asks what Jefferson meant and says research shows the phrase was used from the 1600s for over a hundred years by high officials and legal experts. From Lord Bolingbroke he shows “nature and nature’s God” equals following God in his works and in his word—the Bible and the Jesus of the Bible, divine law.

p: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer studies Isaiah 3 and 4 to explain why God removes designated leaders, saying unqualified leadership, role reversal in the home, and giving in to money, popularity and sexual temptation lead the church into error. He argues for Jesus as Lord over all leaders, discusses his views on conservative politics and fundamentalism, and says the word and Spirit must burn sin out of the church.
Why does God take away the designated leaders in Isaiah 3? (Isaiah 3:1, Isaiah 3:8)

He says Isaiah 3 shows God removing “all designated leaders, all approved leaders” from Jerusalem and Judea, which he says stand for the church in these latter days. He says it is because the church “has stumbled” and “has fallen,” since their words and doings are against the Lord, and when God’s people do that “God is going to intervene.”

In Isaiah chapter 3, we’re going to see a removal of all designated leaders, all approved leaders by God, all the ones that God determined would be leaders. God says he’s going to take them away, all designated leaders. In verse one of chapter 3, “The Lord takes away from Jerusalem and Judea.” Now, who’s Jerusalem? chur Church. Who’s Judea? Church. Church who Zion? Church. Yes. See, he uses the report of Jerusalem, the report of Judah, the report of Zion to teach us, in these latter days, the church. So he’s going to take away the support of the bread and water, that’s the economic part, and the support of, or leaning on, the mighty man, the man of war, the the judge, the prophet, the prudent, the ancient, the captain of 50, the honorable man, the counselor, the skilled worker and the eloquent speaker. Jesus Christ, the Lord himself, is going to take them away. Now, we’ve got to ask ourselves the question: why would he do that? And of course Isaiah 3 is going to tell us why. Why he’s going to take away the designated leadership okay in his people. Now, we’re not talking about the heathen, we’re talking about the church, God’s people. Isaiah 4:3: And it shall come to pass that he who is left in Zion and remains in Jerusalem will be called holy—everyone who is recorded among the living in Jerusalem. Isaiah 4:4: When the Lord has washed away the filth of the daughters of Zion, and purged the blood of Jerusalem from her midst, by the spirit of judgment and by the spirit of burning,
How do the word and the Holy Spirit burn sin out of us? (Jeremiah 31:33, Luke 24:32, Jeremiah 23:28)

He says the “spirit of judgment and the spirit of burning” (Isaiah 4:4) is God’s word and Spirit coming to us and burning things out of us, as he experienced, changing his thinking and desires “little by little.” He says he does not need psychology but a meeting with God, and that Scripture is a fire and a hammer, so we should read the Bible, since friends “they’ll agree you’re okay.”
How do the word and the Holy Spirit burn sin out of us? (Jeremiah 31:33, Luke 24:32, Jeremiah 23:28)

And so he will come and he will burn it out of you. And that’s what I experienced back there and at a [unclear] church, coming up every Sunday, letting God deal with something in my life. I didn’t know this word, but it was working. He would come to me and he would change my thinking, he would change my desires, little by little, step by step. He kept changing me by the word and the spirit coming to me. That’s the magical cure, the word and the Holy Spirit. Are you out there, church? That’s why prayer is important. That’s why alter calls are important. That’s why a real worship service in spirit and truth is important. It’s that time when God can burn. He’s either burning something out or he’s [unclear] burning something in. And that what he says in the new covenant: “I will inscribe my word in your minds and heart.” He’s either burning something in, the Ten Commandments was written by the finger of God, burnt right into the stone, or he’s burning something out. Wow. And so, see, I don’t need psychology, I don’t need human intellect, I need a meeting with God where he transforms my life supernaturally by the burning of his spirit and the burning of his word. And I experienced all that. I didn’t know all this stuff when I was experiencing. You don’t have to know it to experience it, but knowing it really expedites it, speeds up the experience, doesn’t it? I mean, I could have grew a lot faster if I had known what you people know. Luke 24:32: did not “Did not our heart burn within us while Jesus talked with us by the way, and while he open to us the scriptures?” Do the scriptures do that to you? Do they burn in you? Do they get opened? Or you just reading through your Bible, you’re not even reading it? Why do I push people to read their Bible? Because the Bible will burn things in you and burn things out of you. At my lowest time in my Christian walk, I never failed to read the Bible, and the scripture would bring me back to the middle of the road every time. You can’t trust your friends. They’ll agree you’re okay. I don’t need somebody telling me I’m okay when I’m not not okay. I need the Bible, who is impartial, just bucking me, telling me to buck up. How about you? Jeremiah 23:28: “The prophet who has my word, let him speak my word faithfully.” You know, if you ain’t got nothing to say, shut up. We got enough nonsense going around out there without yours. Everybody out there thinks they’re a preacher, and they’re babies and they’re children in God. “What is the chaff to the wheat?”
How do the word and the Holy Spirit burn sin out of us? (Jeremiah 31:33, Luke 24:32, Jeremiah 23:28)

Jeremiah 31:33: But this is the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel after those days, says the LORD: I will put My law in their minds, and write it on their hearts; and I will be their God, and they shall be My people. Luke 24:32: And they said to one another, “Did not our heart burn within us while He talked with us on the road, and while He opened the Scriptures to us?” Jeremiah 23:28: “The prophet who has a dream, let him tell a dream; And he who has My word, let him speak My word faithfully. What is the chaff to the wheat?” says the LORD.
What is God’s glory over His church, and how should we respond? (Jeremiah 23:29, Isaiah 4:5-6, Matthew 16:18, Romans 8:26)

He says Isaiah 4:5-6 promises “a cloud by day and a fire by night,” the glory of God as “the demonstration of his power” in the church, with gifts such as wisdom, knowledge, prophecy, tongues, healing and miracles, and a tabernacle for shade and shelter. He says we should get away from “the mighty man of God mentality,” pray “here I am, use me,” and let Christ burn in us and out of us, as he did in his own life.
What is God’s glory over His church, and how should we respond? (Jeremiah 23:29, Isaiah 4:5-6, Matthew 16:18, Romans 8:26)

Now we know that in most cases the chaff is the wicked people that is burned in that last day in the lake of fire. Okay, but also in the Bible the chaff is that worthless part of the wheat, that sinful, that old sinful nature of man, that old man, that chaff. And he says, “What is the chaff to the wheat? Is not my word like a fire that will burn that chaff out of you? Is not my word like a hammer?” If you’re hard and stubborn, that word will come along and keep chipping away until there is something beautiful formed in your life. Amen. How many could use a little hammering? Yeah, some of us are hard-headed. It takes the hammer. And uh, I needed both the fire and the hammer. I was hard-headed, and I needed things burned out of my life. Isn’t that beautiful? And see, Isaiah said all this thousands of years before our day, and this is what I like: tremendous promise. And I’m trying to get this church to rise up to this truth. Okay, after I get these things dealt with in my life, then the Lord, who’s going to do it? The Lord. Not Olstein, not Rick Warren, not Joy Meyers. The Lord is going to do this. All right, not Dave Kincer, by the way. “The Lord will create above every dwelling place of Mount Zion.” Okay, Mount Zion is the church. The dwelling places are the assemblies, the local churches like us. Every dwelling place in Zion, above her assemblies, “a cloud by day and a fire by night.” See, I told told you, and and he goes on to say, “for over all the glory there will be a covering.” I told you that the glory of God in the Bible was the demonstration of his power, where it was a cloud or a fire, parting the Red Sea, healing the sick, saving a soul. It was the glory. It was the demonstration of the power of his presence. And this is what Isaiah is saying, church. If you’ll let me burn in you you and burn things out of you, I will demonstrate myself in your midst. You will have a word of wisdom, a word of knowledge, a prophecy, a tongue, an interpretation, healing, miracles, discerning of spirits and faith. They will be active in your church, because that is the demonstration of my glory. Do the church need that? Yeah. Do Christians need the demonstration? Yes. Somebody’s got to push into this, folks. Now, we can talk about the things of God till we’re dead, but we need to enter into the things of God. God said he would do it. Like in prayer at the end, “Let there be a performance, Lord. You said Now put up.” Amen. See, do we really care about our nation, to seek God for his glory? Because his glory is going to turn this nation around, I guarantee you. You got to be really hard to reject Christ in that day, and a lot of the people on the fence, a lot of the lukewarm, are going to come over to the right side. Hallelujah. Then he goes on to say, “There will be a tabernacle for shade Allelujah in the daytime from the heat,” and there’s going to be a tabernacle for a refuge, a place of protection, a stronghold, and there’s going to be a tabernacle for a shelter from storms and the rain. The wise man built his house upon the rocks. When the storms came, the problems of life, the troubles of life came, he stood. Now folks, I don’t know about you, but it’s worth letting Christ burn out of me and burn in me to get these kind of results. And we got to get away from the mighty man of God mentality. God is building a church that the gates of hell should not prevail against. God is building a glorious church, church without spot or wrinkle, at think not some mighty man of God. And so when the church will press in, God will demonstrate, because when the church presses in, the streams the part they have flow out and makes a big river, and things get done. Are you with me? No, all of us won’t prophesy. The Bible says that all of us won’t speak in tongues, all of us won’t interpret, but there’ll be enough of us till we get the job done. Boy, I like that. There’s not enough of us now saying, “Here I am, Lord, use me.” That was what the Holy Ghost revealed to me this morning in prayer. They need to be praying, “Here I am, use me,” not telling me what I already know. They need to say, “Lord, use me. Here I am. There’s homes out there. Here I am, commission me, send me, equip me.” Are you there? You got to bring prayer down to your personal reaction. Anybody can pray about something, and anybody can wait for the pastor to do everything. That’s what we’ve been doing for decades in America, and it hasn’t worked, has it? But the real Christian will sayl, “Here I am, use me, use my prayers, use my worship, use my prayer, use my fasting through the week. Use me, Lord, if nothing else to ignite the one that can prophesy.” Amen. One of the young people came up to me this morning and said, “Were you speaking in tongues in prayer?” And I said, “Yes, I was.” I said it’s rare these days. I’ve only spoken in tongues about three times in the last year, and it used to be very steadily. And I was explaining to them how you can speak in tongues and you can interpret it and you can know what the Holy Spirit’s saying. See, the Bible says we don’t know how to pray as we ought, but the spirit does. See, and the Bible says pray in the spirit and sing in the spirit, isn’t that right? So we got to make that transition to the spirit. Hallelujah. I thought I was speaking low enough to were no one heard me, but they were nailing me, and they said they really help them. I said good, because in it’s real, it really ministers. When it’s not real, it’s just in the way. When we’re pantomiming, pretending to speak in tongues, it there’s nothing there. Amen. Church, so are we going to be this glorious church, this church at the gates of hell cannot prevail against? Let Christ burn in us and burn out of us. How many, you raise your hands and “Lord, bring me the burning”? Yes. See that, and that makes it, that makes it for me as a young Christian, when the Holy Spirit revealed these things to me, it really got me relaxed. God’s going to work in me. I I I can’t just grip my teeth and make this happen. God’s going to do this, and that just brought a peace on my life, and he did, he slowly got me there. I had to learn to like myself when I wasn’t [unclear]. I wanted to run, because, you know, the Lord shows light on you and you see yourself and, oh God, what there’s no hope, I’m still doing that same stupid thing I was doing two weeks ago when I asked God to deliver me from it. But see, when you know that you have done what God said to do, repent, admit it, and let God work, then you’re at peace, because you know he’s going to keep his word and get the job done. Hallelujah. Then I could live with myself, I could accept myself, and God used me while he was working on me. I led a lot of people to Christ while he was leading me to Christ. Amen, church.
What is God’s glory over His church, and how should we respond? (Jeremiah 23:29, Isaiah 4:5-6, Matthew 16:18, Romans 8:26)

Jeremiah 23:29: “Is not My word like a fire?” says the LORD, “And like a hammer that breaks the rock in pieces? Isaiah 4:5: then the LORD will create above every dwelling place of Mount Zion, and above her assemblies, a cloud and smoke by day and the shining of a flaming fire by night. For over all the glory there will be a covering. Isaiah 4:6: And there will be a tabernacle for shade in the daytime from the heat, for a place of refuge, and for a shelter from storm and rain. Matthew 16:18: And I also say to you that you are Peter, and on this rock I will build My church, and the gates of Hades shall not prevail against it. Romans 8:26: Likewise the Spirit also helps in our weaknesses. For we do not know what we should pray for as we ought, but the Spirit Himself makes intercession for us with groanings which cannot be uttered.
What does he say Jerusalem, Judea and Zion stand for?
He says that Jerusalem, Judea and Zion are used “to teach us in these latter days the church,” so Isaiah 3 is about the church and not the heathen.
What does he say causes the church to stumble?
He says one source, the one Isaiah deals with, is “unqualified leadership,” and that it “may be okay for the crowd” to approve of things that are against God but “it doesn’t matter if they approve.”
What is the difference between “babies” and “children” in Christ?
He says babies know the Lord and are saved by the blood but have problems with sin, and children are learning and obeying but have not conquered Satan or become strong in the scriptures yet.
What does he say about home Bible studies?
He says when he investigated them “it’s just a bunch of babies and children Christians trying to teach babies and Christian children.”
Who does he say should lead the home?

He says children should not lead the home, parents should, “and specifically the father,” who has directly from God the responsibility to provide food, clothing, shelter and medical care for his wife.
Does he say women can be leaders?

He says “in the Bible, women can be rulers, but they are a small percent,” and that God chooses few women; he says it is wrong both to be against women leaders and to think just being a woman qualifies you.
What does he say a church leader must not do?
He says a church leader cannot give people what they want, because “you’re only allowed to preach what the Bible says to preach,” even if people do not like it.
Does he say leadership depends on race, gender or age?
He says no: it is “not the color of your skin… not whether you’re male or female… young or old… a college degree,” but “what you’ve experienced… the wisdom from above.”
What does he say about politics and the Bible?
He says it is “a big lie that the American church has believed” that the Bible cannot be used for civil matters, since government, family and economics are all Bible topics and his word “is spirit.”
What is the difference between praying “about” and praying “with compassion”?
He says praying about something is different from “praying with compassion because you care,” and singing “about the Holy Spirit” is different from singing “by the Holy Spirit.”
What does he say about “once saved always saved”?
He says it is “just wrong” and that it “taken repentance, turning from sin, right out,” and likewise says that the idea that water baptism is only symbolic is “the most ridiculous lie.”
What does he say it means to make Jesus Lord?
He says “when you do what he says, that makes him your Lord,” and that when you only say “Jesus is my Lord and Savior” without doing it, “he’s not your Lord.”
What does he say a wife should do if her husband asks her to violate the Bible?
He says “your Lord Jesus is your number one leader,” and when a husband asks you to violate the lordship of Jesus, “you’re supposed to do what’s right.”
What does he say about raising his hands when he was first saved?
He says he was “bashful and timid” and raising his hands “was a killer” because he thought everybody was watching, but he had the message to “repent and do what’s right.”
What does he say about speaking in tongues and being real?
He says he speaks in tongues only about three times a year now, that tongues and interpretation can show what the Holy Spirit is saying, and that when it is not real, “it’s just in the way.”

items.t: Learning and Following What the Bible Says
items.d: In this message a speaker at Vine Cluster Church says a worn-out Bible belongs to someone who reads it, and uses the raising of Lazarus in John 11 to show that Jesus has something else in mind when things look…
p: In this message a speaker at Vine Cluster Church says a worn-out Bible belongs to someone who reads it, and uses the raising of Lazarus in John 11 to show that Jesus has something else in mind when things look hopeless. He then calls hearers to put Jesus’ words into practice, using the wise man on the rock, Israel’s disobedience, the cost of discipleship and James 1:22.
What does it mean that a Bible that’s falling apart belongs to someone who isn’t?

He says he saw a plaque quoting an old Baptist preacher, and that it “really hit home” because people who have followed God a long time have Bibles that look like “it’s been through the war.” He says a customer’s worn, marked-up Bible shows that people who read it “a lot” know “it is a storehouse of treasure.”
What does it mean that a Bible that’s falling apart belongs to someone who isn’t?

Last weekend we took the weekend off and I went to uh we were up in Big Bear looking around and hanging out up there for a few hours. And we went into the store and I saw this. Plaque and it had a little sign a little sign and it said a Bible that’s falling apart usually belongs to someone who [unclear]. And that really, that really hit home with me and I realized later who said it it was Charles Spurgeon an old Baptist preacher from the 19th century from England but if you think about that for a minute that really does hit home because you see sometimes you go to these churches and you see these people that have been following God for a long time they’ll whip that Bible out and it’ll look like it’s been through the war pages will be falling apart it’ll the binding will be all broken down in fact I remember seeing someone the other day that where I work a customer came in and they’re Christians and they gave me this little paperback Bible that someone had given them and we get to talking about Jesus every now and then here and there and uh the guy pulled out his Bible and it was just almost destroyed the pages were all worn and he had it marked all over the place he had notes here notes there and his wife said I bought him a new one but he always comes back to this old one and I said well I know why is because
Why read the Bible, and why learn from other people’s mistakes?

He says the Bible is “a storehouse of treasure” and that if you apply it to your life “in general they work because it’s good advice.” He says “it’s easier to learn from what someone else has failed than it is to learn the hard way,” though “some of us are stubborn.”
Why read the Bible, and why learn from other people’s mistakes?

he has it all marked up you know how long it would take to mark up that new. One but the reason why the person isn’t falling apart is because everybody that has read their Bible and read it a lot knows that it is a storehouse of treasure is that can I get an amen on that it is a storehouse of treasure even even if you just read you and I know everybody’s heard this even if you just read Proverbs a proverb a day you can read one a month on the. Average and my favorite proverb is. This be quick to listen and slow to speak now I don’t always have the ability to follow that but I will say that that is very good advice because sometimes you hear people talking and then they jump right in there before they’re finish talking and you interrupt them but wait a minute and you didn’t let them make their point. And if you just read those Proverbs and apply them to your life you’ll see that they in general they work because it’s good advice is it not and the Bible’s like that and what’s really interesting is we can learn from other people’s mistakes we can look and see what other people have did how they have fallen and and the areas that they failed in and we can learn from what they had failed to do and how many know that it’s easier to learn from what someone else has failed than it is to learn the hard way and have to go through it yourself isn’t it easier to realize that you can turn things around without having to do it the hard way but some of us are stubborn I was like that in my younger years I had to learn the hard way but I will say this when you do you never forget.
Why read the Bible, and why learn from other people’s mistakes?
James 1:19: So then, my beloved brethren, let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak, slow to wrath; Proverbs 15:1: A soft answer turns away wrath, But a harsh word stirs up anger.
Why did Jesus wait two days after hearing Lazarus was sick, and why was he “glad” he wasn’t there?

He says the sisters sent word with “a sense of urgency” and “an enormous amount of faith,” but Jesus “stayed where he was two more days.” He says Jesus told the disciples “for your sake I’m glad I wasn’t there… so you may believe,” meaning “he’s got something else in mind.”
Why did Jesus wait two days after hearing Lazarus was sick, and why was he “glad” he wasn’t there?

Why did Jesus wait two days after hearing Lazarus was sick, and why was he “glad” he wasn’t there?

John 11:1-6: Now a certain man was sick, Lazarus of Bethany, the town of Mary and her sister Martha. It was that Mary who anointed the Lord with fragrant oil and wiped His feet with her hair, whose brother Lazarus was sick. Therefore the sisters sent to Him, saying, “Lord, behold, he whom You love is sick.” When Jesus heard that, He said, “This sickness is not unto death, but for the glory of God, that the Son of God may be glorified through it.” Now Jesus loved Martha and her sister and Lazarus. So, when He heard that he was sick, He stayed two more days in the place where He was. John 11:7-15: Then after this He said to the disciples, “Let us go to Judea again.” The disciples said to Him, “Rabbi, lately the Jews sought to stone You, and are You going there again?” Jesus answered, “Are there not twelve hours in the day? If anyone walks in the day, he does not stumble, because he sees the light of this world. But if one walks in the night, he stumbles, because the light is not in him.” These things He said, and after that He said to them, “Our friend Lazarus sleeps, but I go that I may wake him up.” Then His disciples said, “Lord, if he sleeps he will get well.” However, Jesus spoke of his death, but they thought that He was speaking about taking rest in sleep. Then Jesus said to them plainly, “Lazarus is dead. And I am glad for your sakes that I was not there, that you may believe. Nevertheless let us go to him.”
What did Jesus say to Martha and Mary: “I am the resurrection and the life”?

He says Lazarus had been in the tomb four days, and that Martha believed “in the resurrection her brother would” rise again. He says Jesus then said “I am the resurrection and the life,” and when Mary and the others wept, “Jesus wept.”
What did Jesus say to Martha and Mary: “I am the resurrection and the life”?

What did Jesus say to Martha and Mary: “I am the resurrection and the life”?

John 11:17-27: So when Jesus came, He found that he had already been in the tomb four days. Now Bethany was near Jerusalem, about two miles away. And many of the Jews had joined the women around Martha and Mary, to comfort them concerning their brother. Then Martha, as soon as she heard that Jesus was coming, went and met Him, but Mary was sitting in the house. Now Martha said to Jesus, “Lord, if You had been here, my brother would not have died. But even now I know that whatever You ask of God, God will give You.” Jesus said to her, “Your brother will rise again.” Martha said to Him, “I know that he will rise again in the resurrection at the last day.” Jesus said to her, “I am the resurrection and the life. He who believes in Me, though he may die, he shall live. And whoever lives and believes in Me shall never die. Do you believe this?” She said to Him, “Yes, Lord, I believe that You are the Christ, the Son of God, who is to come into the world.” John 11:28-37: And when she had said these things, she went her way and secretly called Mary her sister, saying, “The Teacher has come and is calling for you.” As soon as she heard that, she arose quickly and came to Him. Now Jesus had not yet come into the town, but was in the place where Martha met Him. Then the Jews who were with her in the house, and comforting her, when they saw that Mary rose up quickly and went out, followed her, saying, “She is going to the tomb to weep there.” Then, when Mary came where Jesus was, and saw Him, she fell down at His feet, saying to Him, “Lord, if You had been here, my brother would not have died.” Therefore, when Jesus saw her weeping, and the Jews who came with her weeping, He groaned in the spirit and was troubled. And He said, “Where have you laid him?” They said to Him, “Lord, come and see.” Jesus wept. Then the Jews said, “See how He loved him!” And some of them said, “Could not this Man, who opened the eyes of the blind, also have kept this man from dying?”
Why did Jesus raise Lazarus after four days, and what does it teach about situations that seem hopeless?

He says by delaying, “he had something else in mind,” and when Lazarus came out of the tomb their faith “grew enormously.” He says “death isn’t the end it’s the beginning” for those who follow Jesus, and that “time and time again when you think there’s no other way he provides one.”

Sin was not imputed without law, Christ died to bring us to God, and the same water that destroyed the wicked saved the righteous.

items.d: In this message, Pastor David G. Kincer teaches that Leviathan in Isaiah 27 and Job 41 pictures Satan, “king over all the children of pride,” and that Jesus destroyed his power over believers. He then teaches…
p: In this message, Pastor David G. Kincer teaches that Leviathan in Isaiah 27 and Job 41 pictures Satan, “king over all the children of pride,” and that Jesus destroyed his power over believers. He then teaches on Lucifer in Isaiah 14, the stars of God, angels and the destroyer, and the believer’s authority, ending with the saints taking the kingdom and Jesus as the Lion of the tribe of Judah.
What is Leviathan, and can anyone overcome him? (Isaiah 27:1, Job 41:1–10)

He says Leviathan is a serpent: in Isaiah 27:1 the Lord “will punish Leviathan the fleeing serpent,” “the twisted serpent.” Turning to Job 41, he says “any hope of overcoming Leviathan is false” and “man cannot defeat this snake.” He says God hides mysteries by switching between the natural and the spiritual, and “only the Holy Ghost can reveal them to you.”
What is Leviathan, and can anyone overcome him? (Isaiah 27:1, Job 41:1–10)

We’re going to ask ourselves, what is Leviathan? Okay, and we, of course, will go to the Bible to find out what Leviathan is. Uh, they made a movie about it, and this has nothing to do with that movie. Isaiah 27, verse 1: “In that day,” now remember that “day” is mentioned over and over and over and over in Isaiah, speaking of the future events of God. “In that day the Lord,” the Lord is Jesus Christ, “with his severe sword, great and strong, will punish Leviathan the fleeing serpent.” So Leviathan is a serpent. Okay. “Leviathan the twisted serpent.” Again, Leviathan is a serpent, “and he will slay the reptile that is in the sea.” So we got a bunch of snakes being talked about here, and, uh, we find that Leviathan is a serpent, okay, a snake. Then we’re going to go to Job 41, where God himself, talking to Job, gives us great details about Leviathan, thorough details. Job 41: “Any hope of overcoming Leviathan is false.” That’s a false hope. Man cannot defeat this snake. “One shall be overwhelmed at the very sight of him.” He’s just going to be terrorized just by looking at this snake. “No one’s so fierce that he would dare stir up Leviathan.” No human being got enough courage, enough military strength, the warrior, to overcome and stir up Leviathan. And then God switches. Now remember, Isaiah would be talking about a nation or an Israel, and then he would switch to the future. Okay, and this is how God hid his mysteries in the Bible, and only the Holy Ghost can reveal them to you. You can’t go to college and get this stuff, it’s not an intellectual thing, it is a spiritual thing. All right.
What is Leviathan, and can anyone overcome him? (Isaiah 27:1, Job 41:1–10)

Isaiah 27:1: In that day the LORD with His severe sword, great and strong, Will punish Leviathan the fleeing serpent, Leviathan that twisted serpent; And He will slay the reptile that is in the sea. Job 41:1-10: “Can you draw out Leviathan with a hook, Or snare his tongue with a line which you lower? Can you put a reed through his nose, Or pierce his jaw with a hook? Will he make many supplications to you? Will he speak softly to you? Will he make a covenant with you? Will you take him as a servant forever? Will you play with him as with a bird, Or will you leash him for your maidens? Will your companions make a banquet of him? Will they apportion him among the merchants? Can you fill his skin with harpoons, Or his head with fishing spears? Lay your hand on him; Remember the battle— Never do it again! Indeed, any hope of overcoming him is false; Shall one not be overwhelmed at the sight of him? No one is so fierce that he would dare stir him up. Who then is able to stand against Me?
Why does God use Leviathan to ask who can stand against him? (Job 41:10–29)

He says God uses this “overwhelming snake” to ask “who then is able to stand against me?”, because Job “was righteous until he blamed God for his problems.” He describes Leviathan’s fire, breath and scales and the failure of swords, spears and arrows, saying “nothing can touch this guy.”
Why does God use Leviathan to ask who can stand against him? (Job 41:10–29)

So God uses this overwhelming snake to turn it around and say, “Who then is able to stand against me?” Because that’s what Job had done. He had blamed God. Job was righteous until he blamed God for his problems. He accused God. And so, “Who then is able to stand against me?” If you can’t, you guys can’t conquer this snake, then who has the guts to stand up against me? Amen. So it’s, it’s a good illustration, and remember, Jesus said, “I speak to you of earthly things so you can understand heavenly things.” All right, now he goes on, verse 19: “Out of Leviathan’s mouth go burning lights, sparks of fire shoot out, smoke goes out of his nose as from a boiling pot and a burning bush.” It rushes. The Bible says that he caused the depths of the sea to boil when he opened his mouth with fire. His breath kindles coals, a flame goes out of his mouth. Verse 26: “Though the sword reaches him, it cannot avail.” Can’t pierce this snake. “Nor does a spear, a dart, a javelin,” and back in verse 7, even, I passed over it because I wanted to stay on the topic back there, the harpoon, the javelin, the dart, the spear cannot pierce his skin. His scales are so tight and so hard, nothing can touch this guy. “He regards iron as straw.” You know, you throw a war axe at him and it just breaks like a straw. “Bronze is rotten wood.” The arrow cannot make him flee. So he has used up the weapons of a man. A man’s weapons cannot hurt this reptile, this serpent. “Slingstones become like stubble to him.” They sling them at him and they just break like a clod of dirt. “Darts are regarded as straw.” They throw a spear at him, just like throwing a piece of straw. That’s how vicious this animal was, this snake.
Why does God use Leviathan to ask who can stand against him? (Job 41:10–29)

Job 41:10: No one is so fierce that he would dare stir him up. Who then is able to stand against Me? Job 41:19-21: Out of his mouth go burning lights; Sparks of fire shoot out. Smoke goes out of his nostrils, As from a boiling pot and burning rushes. His breath kindles coals, And a flame goes out of his mouth. Job 41:26-29: Though the sword reaches him, it cannot avail; Nor does spear, dart, or javelin. He regards iron as straw, And bronze as rotten wood. The arrow cannot make him flee; Slingstones become like stubble to him. Darts are regarded as straw; He laughs at the threat of javelins.
Is Leviathan a real creature, and who is king over the children of pride? (Job 41:33–34)

He says Leviathan, talked about “five times in the Old Testament,” is “the natural snake that can breathe out fire,” and tells hearers not to believe “versions of the Bible that say it’s a crocodile.” He says the “switch” comes at the end of Job 41, where this snake is “king over all the children of pride,” illustrating that “nobody can stand against him.”
Is Leviathan a real creature, and who is king over the children of pride? (Job 41:33–34)

That Isaiah said God would destroy in that day. What day, and what would God do? Destroy him. Okay. “He laughs at the threat of javelins.” Now, you got to remember, all water animals survived the flood. You say, “Well, we know dinosaurs got wiped out back there.” Well, any monster in the sea would be fine. So get away from that. God does know what he’s talking about, all right. Now, natural scientists don’t believe that, but God is literally talking about, and Leviathan’s talked about five times in the Old Testament, five times, and God is using the natural snake that can breathe out fire, nothing can oppose him, to illustrate. And don’t believe these, these, um, versions of the Bible that say it’s a crocodile or something. Just accept it the way God said it, okay? And that’s the way he’s saying it, and it’s important that you do, because the spiritual truth lines up with this, all right. Verse 33: “On earth there is nothing like him, which is made without fear.” This snake fears nothing. “He beholds every high thing,” and here comes the switch from the natural snake. “He is king over all the children of pride.” He is king over all. Now here’s the switch. Now he’s switching. This snake cannot be king over humans at all, can it? They can’t rule them, can’t have any effect on them. And so he’s using this terrible creature to illustrate how people cannot stand before God, and like it was said this morning, nothing is impossible with God. He will save, he will deliver, he will, nothing can stop him. Okay, he is a Savior, he is a Deliverer, he is a Healer, and nobody has authority to stand against God, the Lord Jesus Christ. Is that an amen? Yeah. So he’s using this bad snake to illustrate how powerful Jesus Christ is, okay, that nobody can stand against him. And then he’s using this snake to illustrate that there is a king over, in the spirit world, over all the children of pride. Now, the word “pride” there in the Hebrew has a two-fold meaning. It is a pride of lion cubs, a family of lions.
Is Leviathan a real creature, and who is king over the children of pride? (Job 41:33–34)
Job 41:33: On earth there is nothing like him, Which is made without fear. Job 41:34: He beholds every high thing; He is king over all the children of pride.”
What does pride have to do with Satan as a lion? (1 Peter 5:8, Proverbs 16:18)

He says pride has a “two-fold meaning,” “a pride of lion cubs” and being proud, and that Satan is a “lion king” who “has a pride,” children and offspring. He cites 1 Peter 5:8, “your adversary the Devil is as a roaring lion,” and says “understanding Leviathan helps us understand Satan” and that “people are so proud they won’t bow their need to God.”
What does pride have to do with Satan as a lion? (1 Peter 5:8, Proverbs 16:18)

And it also is being proud. You see, people are so proud, they won’t admit their sins and God forgive them and deliver them, they won’t admit it. People are so proud they won’t bow their need to God. I mean, what do they think they’re going to do in heaven? The angels and the elders are all kneeling, and a number that can’t be numbered are kneeling, and you’re going to stand there and say, “Huh, no”? Now it’s pride. Pride comes before a fall. Yes. And so he is over this king that he’s talking about, and illustrating by the snake, is over, he is ruling over the children of pride, being proud, and the offspring of the lion. This next side says Satan is a lion. King, he is a lion king, he has a pride, he has children and offspring, and he is a king of a certain area. It says in 1 Peter 5:8 that we’re to be sober and vigilant, because “your adversary the Devil is as a roaring lion, walking about seeking whom he may devour,” may destroy. Okay. The New Testament is the revelation, the amplification that opens up the truths of God in the Old Testament, and the Old Testament expands those truths because they were there before, but the New Testament opens up the door so we can expand these truths. You got it? So understanding Leviathan helps us understand Satan, all right. He is a lion king over the proud, the pride. John 12:31: “Now shall the prince of this world be cast out.” Who is he talking about? Satan. So he is a king, he is a ruler, okay, and he’s a ruler over this world.
What does pride have to do with Satan as a lion? (1 Peter 5:8, Proverbs 16:18)

Proverbs 16:18: Pride goes before destruction, And a haughty spirit before a fall. 1 Peter 5:8: Be sober, be vigilant; because your adversary the devil walks about like a roaring lion, seeking whom he may devour.
Who are Satan’s children? (John 12:31, Ephesians 2:2, Matthew 13:38, Psalm 10:4, John 3:19–20)

Citing John 12:31, Ephesians 2:2 and Matthew 13:38, he says Satan is “a ruler over this world” with children, and “we know them because they disobey the word of God.” He says those who “reject Christ and reject the word” are “our biggest opposition,” that they do not admit their wrong, and that people who accept “a Jesus that does not reveal their sins” have “the wrong Jesus.”

Now, Satan has children of pride, a lion’s cubs, he has a family, he has children. Ephesians 2:2: “The prince and power of the air, the spirit that now works in the children of disobedience.” So Satan is a king of the air, this earth, and he has children, and we know them because they disobey the word of God. Okay, they’re under the control of Satan, they follow Satan’s rules. Got it? All right, Matthew 13:38: “The tares are the children of the wicked one. He says the word “day” is mentioned “over and over and over and over in Isaiah, speaking of the future events of God.”
Who does he say can reveal the mysteries hidden in the Bible?
He says God hid his mysteries by switching between the natural and the spiritual, and “only the Holy Ghost can reveal them to you.”
What does he say about Leviathan and the flood?
He says “all water animals survived the flood,” so “any monster in the sea would be fine.” This is his explanation and is not verified here.
What does he say about pride?
He says Satan “has a pride,” and that “pride comes before a fall.” He says people are so proud they “won’t bow their need to God.”
Why does he say atheists do not want to believe in God?
He says atheists do not want to believe because “they want to sin.” This is his statement about a group, not a verified claim.
What does he say about people who blame Satan?
He says that when people say “Satan’s followed me and Satan did this to me,” they “don’t understand the power of Christ in your life.”

Does he say a Christian can be demon-possessed?
He says “Christians can’t be demon-possessed” because “Jesus lives in us.”
What difference does he draw between Jesus as Savior and as Lord?
He says “there’s a difference between Jesus the Savior and Jesus the Lord,” and that a slave of Jesus says “Yes, Master.”
What does he say the name Lucifer means?
He says Lucifer means “the shining one.”
Where does he say sin begins?
He says sin “doesn’t begin down here,” and that “the heart’s the head, the mind.”
Who does he say created Satan?
He says “God did,” and that God “cannot do evil.” He says hell and the lake of fire were made for “Satan and his angels and those who follow him.”
What does he say angels do?
He says angels “come to minister to you” and “have a message for you,” and that they are “ministering spirits.”
What does he say Satan has authority to do?
He says Satan has authority to test and tempt mankind, but that obedient believers “have authority over Satan and his fallen angels.”
What does he urge believers to do about Satan?
He urges “a prayer life,” “a word life” and “a fasting life,” and says it “won’t hurt you to fast once a week.”
