Okay. Jesus’s first coming, as we know, was not to condemn the world. In John 3:17, but that the world through him might be saved. His first coming was not to judge the world. He come to warn the world there’s a judgment coming and, “My blood will forgive you your sins, clean you your sins, and you can correct all your wrongs. Your slate can be clean and you can be reconciled back to God.” That was his message. “He that believes on him is not condemned. He that believes not is condemned already, because he hasn’t believed on the name of the only begotten Son of God. And this is the condemnation: that light has come into the world, and men loved what? Darkness rather than light, because their deeds were what? Evil. For everyone that does evil hates the light.” Who’s the light? Jesus and his word. “Neither comes to the light.” Who’s the light? Jesus and his word. “Lest his deeds should what? Be exposed.”
Why did Jesus come the first time, and what is the condemnation? (John 3:17-20)

John 3:17-20: For God did not send His Son into the world to condemn the world, but that the world through Him might be saved. “He who believes in Him is not condemned; but he who does not believe is condemned already, because he has not believed in the name of the only begotten Son of God. And this is the condemnation, that the light has come into the world, and men loved darkness rather than light, because their deeds were evil. For everyone practicing evil hates the light and does not come to the light, lest his deeds should be exposed.
Why do people reject the message, and when will the word judge us? (John 12:48, Acts 17:31)

He says people who reject the message blame the preacher or the church, but the truth is “they want to sin and they don’t want anybody telling them they can’t.” He says the same word will judge us in the last day, that God has “an appointed day,” and that no one should rely on predicted dates.
Why do people reject the message, and when will the word judge us? (John 12:48, Acts 17:31)

You know, people that reject the message, they blame the preacher, they blame the church, they put the blame on everything. And the truth is, they want to sin and they don’t want anybody telling them they can’t. So they reject Christ because what? Christ is going to convict them of their sin so he can save them. And that’s why he came the first time. He didn’t come to back up that Old Testament law. But the second coming, John 12:48: “The word that I’ve have spoken to you, the same shall judge you” what? “In the last day.” Acts 17:31: he was a there was “He has appointed a day on which he will” what? Judge the world. It’s not an in-minute thing. There is an appointed day. This is going to happen. And when that day comes, it’s going to happen. And you can put out teaser dates and you can predict dates all you want, but the thing of it is, God has a design, a plan, and he has a day when he’s coming, and he’s going to judge the world. And you die before that, you’re still accountable. That’s your judgment day. And you’re going to be resurrected to this one.
Why do people reject the message, and when will the word judge us? (John 12:48, Acts 17:31)

John 12:48: He who rejects Me, and does not receive My words, has that which judges him—the word that I have spoken will judge him in the last day. Acts 17:31: because He has appointed a day on which He will judge the world in righteousness by the Man whom He has ordained. He has given assurance of this to all by raising Him from the dead.”
Will believers appear before Christ, and is God partial? (2 Corinthians 5:10)

He says “we will all appear before the judgment seat of Christ,” and that being a believer does not exempt you because Judas also believed, preached and cast out demons. He says many Christians think God would be partial to those who believe, and says that is “a lie.”
Will believers appear before Christ, and is God partial? (2 Corinthians 5:10)

Second Corinthians 5:10: “We will all appear before the judgment seat of Christ.” How many of us? “But I’m a believer of Christ.” So what what? Judas was a believer of Christ too, you know. Have I got you thinking? Yeah, he believed in Christ. Is he in the lake of fire? Yes, he’s in the lake of fire. We don’t know our Bible. Did Judas preach the gospel? Yes. Did he cast out demons? Yes. Did he heal the sick? I mean, God healed the sick through him. Yeah. Are you there, church? You see, this thing is the power. This is the message of the gospel of Christ. This judgment is strong and it’s powerful and it moves us forward. We’re going to all appear. And and see, a lot of Christians don’t think they’re going to appear before Christ. They think God is partial because we believe in him. “Believed in you, Lord. I’m committing sexual immorality and doing everything this guy over here did, but he didn’t believe in you.” And and and so God says, “Well, he didn’t believe in me, I’m going to I’m going to mess him up. But you, you believe, all right.” Is God partial, folks? We’re lying to the people, and the people love to believe a lie.
Will believers appear before Christ, and is God partial? (2 Corinthians 5:10)
2 Corinthians 5:10: For we must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ, that each one may receive the things done in the body, according to what he has done, whether good or bad.
What does it mean to be judged by works? (Revelation 20:13, 2 Corinthians 5:10)

He says they were judged each one according to their works, and that believing in Christ does not help a family if you abuse them, and does not help a sinner if you tell them they don’t have to turn. He says living for Christ helps our neighbors and families, and that grace and faith are not all there is to it.
What does it mean to be judged by works? (Revelation 20:13, 2 Corinthians 5:10)

“Anyway, that he may receive the things done when in this body according to what he has done, whether it be good or bad.” All right. “The sea gave up the dead who were in it. Death and Hades delivered up the dead who were in them. They were judged each one according to his” what? What’s the word? Works. See, it doesn’t do my wife and children any good I believe in Christ, and then I’m going out on my wife and I’m beating my kids to death because they do things that irritate me. And that doesn’t help them any. And I believe in Christ, and I tell the sinner, “You know, you just believe in Christ, you don’t have to turn from that.” Doesn’t help that sinner any or his home any. You see, us living for Christ is what helps our neighbor. That’s what helps our family. And now that’s a good place for a good amen. You may not agree with me, but that’s the key. And they got us thinking that this grace and faith is all there is to it. No, you can be a tremendous blessing in your home by following the word of God, and you can go to heaven.
What does it mean to be judged by works? (Revelation 20:13, 2 Corinthians 5:10)
Revelation 20:13: The sea gave up the dead who were in it, and Death and Hades delivered up the dead who were in them. And they were judged, each one according to his works.
Does Jesus come only once, and what is the new heaven and new earth? (Matthew 16:27, Revelation 21:1)

He says the Bible nowhere says Jesus comes “once, twice, and the third time”; He comes one time, judges the world, resurrects the people, and then comes eternity. He says everything now will be “renovated by fire” and replaced by “a much better” heaven and earth, not surfing or fishing.
Does Jesus come only once, and what is the new heaven and new earth? (Matthew 16:27, Revelation 21:1)

Matthew 16:20: “For the Son of Man shall come in the glory of his Father with his angels, and then he will reward every man according to his” what? Works. See, nowhere in the Bible does he say he’s coming once, twice, and the third time. It says he’s coming one time, and he’s going to judge the world, and he’s going to resurrect the people, and they’re going to stand before God, and then eternity. Revelations 21:1: “I saw a new heaven and a new earth, for the first heaven and the first earth [unclear] passed away. Also there was no more sea.” I love these young Christians when they say, “Boy, I can’t wait to catch that wave in heaven,” you know, surfing, or “Boy, just imagine the fishing in heaven.” and And I look at, I, you’re not getting this. Everything that you see here is going to be renovated by fire. It’s going to be burned up: buildings, everything’s gone, water gone, moon, stars, sun, everything’s gone, and a much better comes to replace it.
Does Jesus come only once, and what is the new heaven and new earth? (Matthew 16:27, Revelation 21:1)

Matthew 16:27: For the Son of Man will come in the glory of His Father with His angels, and then He will reward each according to his works. Revelation 21:1: Now I saw a new heaven and a new earth, for the first heaven and the first earth had passed away. Also there was no more sea.
What will eternity be like? (Revelation 21:4-5, 2 Peter 3)

He says God “will wipe every tear from their eyes,” there will be no more death, sorrow, crying or pain, because the former things have passed away, and God says “I make what? All things new.” He says the heavens will pass away with a great noise and a fervent heat, and that the new earth is “much better than what we know.”
What will eternity be like? (Revelation 21:4-5, 2 Peter 3)

Hallelujah. So get rid of those fairy tales. God has something much better than what we know. Now, “God will wipe every tear from their eyes. There will be no more death,” why? Cuz death is is conquered. Now, “no sorrow, no crying. There will be no more pain, for the former things have” what? Passed away. And remember, “with a fervent heat the heavens passed away with a great noise, the earth was burned up and everything in it.” And they want us down here on earth. Ain’t nothing to be down here for until he recreates the new earth. Hallelujah. I’m just throwing out some things to help you get through this nonsense out there. Then “he who sat on the throne said, ‘Behold, I make what? All things new.’” Wow. Fresh. Now I don’t know about you, but that sounds pretty good to me.
What will eternity be like? (Revelation 21:4-5, 2 Peter 3)

Revelation 21:4: And God will wipe away every tear from their eyes; there shall be no more death, nor sorrow, nor crying. There shall be no more pain, for the former things have passed away.” 2 Peter 3:10: But the day of the Lord will come as a thief in the night, in which the heavens will pass away with a great noise, and the elements will melt with fervent heat; both the earth and the works that are in it will be burned up. Revelation 21:5: Then He who sat on the throne said, “Behold, I make all things new.” And He said to me, “Write, for these words are true and faithful.”
Will everyone get the same reward in heaven?

He says there “are levels,” so what you do now depends on your reward; you will get eternal life, but people who do not pursue or grow in God will not get the same reward as those who do. He says the idea that everyone is treated equal is “the Disneyland gospel,” and that there are things to be rewarded up there.
Will everyone get the same reward in heaven?

Is it worth living for Christ for 70 to 80 years on this earth to inherit an eternity like that? And we we already talked about Christ, you know, we get to love him and know him up there, and he’s the focus of everything, plus we get all the new heaven and a new earth to live in. There are levels, uh, so it’s important what you do now. Depends on your reward. These people think they all get the same reward. See, that’s just like these lazy people. They don’t want to work and they think they should be able to be fed and everything and drive cars just like the workers. And the Christians are like that, you know. We don’t pursue God, we don’t grow in God, yet we want the same reward that those who applied God, and it’s not there in the Bible. Now, you will get eternal life, don’t get me wrong, but remember there’s a new heaven and new earth, things are going on there’s a order up there, and I don’t know about you, but you want to be as high as you can when you get there. Amen. You say, “Man, that sounds weird.” Yeah, I know, because we love the fair tale, the Disneyland gospel. We don’t want any responsibility or accountability to do anything, and we want everything handed to us, and it’s not that way. You will be judged according to your works. You see, Blake gets a very good paycheck because he has a good marketing uh skill to market, and see, you guys, want some of you want the same paycheck without putting the effort in, and it ain’t going to happen. Picking on Blake today. And all of you believe this fantasy from TV and radio that, “Oh man, your faith and gra, everybody’s treated equal, everybody get.” No, you didn’t do beans for Christ, you’re barely going to get in, and thank God you got in. But there’s things to be rewarded up there, and you want those rewards. Is that a good amen? Hallelujah.
What is the message of the cross, and how should we respond? (Proverbs 20:11)

He says Jesus wants to keep us from “that lake of fire, that second death,” by choosing Him for forgiveness and starting to “start walking on the right road,” and going back to the cross when we fall. He says the message is “a total package”: forgiveness and cleansing plus a commitment to obey His word, with growth over time until we shine “by your good works, giving glory to God.”
What is the message of the cross, and how should we respond? (Proverbs 20:11)

Young people, stop what you’re doing. Here, I love young people. They look at each other to see if this is cool or not. Young people, the Bible says, “Even a child is known by its ways, whether it is bad or whether it’s good.” And so we’ve got to choose to live the right way, and this is what the message is all about. Jesus wants to keep you from that lake of fire, that second death, and so he’s coming to tell you. You’re not looking at me. That’s it, sweetie, that beautiful face. I’d love to see those eyes. Do you understand when you do that you distract those around you? Yeah, they look to see what you’re doing. Adults do that. And see, a serious thing, our eternal life is on the line here, and we got to get enough respect to listen and soak it in and make a decision. And this is what I’m getting to. Jesus is telling us to choose him for forgiveness for wrong and to start walking on the right road and start living for him. And if you fall, you go back to him, back to that cross, asked him to forgive and get back up on that road and keep walking. And you can reject it today. You can want to please your friends around you. You want to be the cool crowd. You can believe the lie. Adults can believe the lie that’s preached on radio and TV. I told you over the weekend that if Jesus Christ preached the message that preachers are preaching today, he would never have been crucified, because they are not warning you to turn from evil and do right and serve the living God. That’s why they killed him. They didn’t want to change, and religious people didn’t want to change. And so young people and adults this morning, this is the message of the cross. Are you going to choose not only the forgiveness of Christ and the cleansing of sin that he offers, but a commitment to obey his word and live for him? It’s a total package. And let him slowly, you know, doesn’t have to be too slow now, but a lot of this doesn’t happen overnight. So when I’m telling you, some of you drag your feet way too long, but let him building. You keep getting back up. Keep letting him deal with it until that thing is gone. You just keep working on these things to finally you shine like a light in this world by your good works, giving glory to God.
What is the message of the cross, and how should we respond? (Proverbs 20:11)
Proverbs 20:11: Even a child is known by his deeds, Whether what he does is pure and right.
Who does he say goes to the lake of fire?

He says cowards who do not stand up for Jesus, the unbelieving, the sexually immoral, sorcerers, idolaters and liars, if they do it “flagrantly and consistently,” will have their part in the lake that burns with fire and brimstone, which is the second death.
What does he mean by “the cowardly” in Revelation 21:8?

He says it does not mean being afraid to drive on the freeway; it means not having “the courage of your faith” to stand up for what’s right and instead giving into the crowd, especially for teenagers who are peer pressured.
How does he say we grow spiritually?
He says “get with people that are up there above you,” because “we get influenced by who we’re around and the quality of life that they have.”
What does he say about work and laziness?

He says “no working, no eating” was the first law, and quotes the Proverb that a man’s stomach will drive him to work. He says letting people be lazy and still feeding them, or letting children stay at home to age 40, does not build self-esteem.
What does he say about eating blood?

He says the command not to eat meat with the life blood was a “shadow law” of the blood of Christ, with no punishment attached. He says you can actually eat blood “if you don’t overdo it,” and it is used in many nations, like other parts of the animal.
What does he say about marriage?

He says marriage is “a public declaration” before God and people that you will be faithful, love that person, treat them right and raise your kids right. He says many people are “just shacking up,” but “Christians get married.”
Whose fault does he say it is when evil happens?

He says it is not God’s fault but ours, because God gave human beings the responsibility to “take care of the criminal” and judge. He says he gets tired of people blaming God and “his perfect word when it is our fault.”
What does he say about immigrants and the law?

He says “we’re to allow immigrants into our nation, but they should come in the legal way,” because it is not fair to those who came legally. He says government leaders who do not back up the law are “wimps.”
Who does he say is supposed to punish criminals?

He says civil leaders, not the church, are supposed to deal with criminals and carry out punishment by death, and says “they’re not doing it.” He says the church’s greatest punishment is excommunication.
Why did Jesus not judge the world at His first coming?
He says Jesus came to warn that a judgment is coming and to offer forgiveness and a clean slate through His blood, and that those who do not believe “condemned already.”
What does he say about Judas?

He says Judas “believed in Christ,” preached, cast out demons and healed the sick through God’s power, yet “he’s in the lake of fire,” to show that believing alone does not exempt anyone from judgment.
What does he say about grace and faith being all there is to it?
He says “they got us thinking that this grace and faith is all there is to it,” and that following the word of God is what makes you a blessing to your home and takes you to heaven.
What does he say about surfing and fishing in heaven?
He says everything here “is going to be renovated by fire” and replaced by something “much better than what we know,” so people should get rid of those “fairy tales.”
Why does he say living for Christ is worth it?
He asks if it is “worth living for Christ for 70 to 80 years on this earth to inherit an eternity like that,” where we get to love and know Him and have a new heaven and new earth.
What does he say about preachers today?
He says if Jesus preached the message that preachers are preaching today “he would never have been crucified,” because they do not warn people to turn from evil.

items.t: The Epistles to the Churches Encouraged Morality
items.d: Pastor David G. Kincer surveys the epistles’ call to morality: Romans on creation and same-sex sin, baptism killing the old nature, love fulfilling the law; Corinthian church discipline; Galatians’ true gospel…
p: Pastor David G. Kincer surveys the epistles’ call to morality: Romans on creation and same-sex sin, baptism killing the old nature, love fulfilling the law; Corinthian church discipline; Galatians’ true gospel versus moral compromise; Ephesians/Colossians on fathers; and 1 Timothy on the law for the lawless including kidnappers.
Do the New Testament epistles encourage morality?
He says the epistles to the churches encourage morality—the just live by faith in morals and in the Just One, Jesus. Creation is defended because denying the Creator was already a problem.
Do the New Testament epistles encourage morality?

We’re going to look at the epistles today. And we’re going to find that they encourage. Morality. That the writers of these epistles and there are 17 churches that they’re writing to plus there’s more than 17 but I got 17 listed here Rome current galatia ephesus philippi colossa. Thessalonika and so forth asia all right we’re going to take a look at some of the statements in these epistles and see what the early church. Stood for and we’re going to find that they address the signs of moral decline in the roman empire. In Romans 1:16 the just shall live by faith. What comes before living by faith. Just. They are morals. They believe in morals they’re moral people. And live by faith means if you know your english language they live by faith in what. Morals. What is just what is right. We’ve been told for decades that just shall live by faith focusing on faith the focus is not on faith the focus is on being just. Are you there. When I was a boy I was told this but the emphasis was faith or if I just believe it isn’t believing the just you decide to be moral you decide to live right you decide to live honest and you do that by your persuasion in being just. Hallelujah and faith in the just one who is the just one Jesus yes. Number two. Creation he talks about creation back there why because creation was a problem back then some say the world always existed some say the world you know was created by some other method and so forth and and uh they said the earth was flat and they said that the when the Bible says it was a sphere and they say that the earth was held up by atlas. Hallelujah. When the Bible says it was hung on nothing. And so they addressed. These theories back there because they’re not new in our generation. People are always coming up with theories to. Distract people from the moral standards of the Bible.
Do the New Testament epistles encourage morality?

Romans 1:17: For in it the righteousness of God is revealed from faith to faith; as it is written, “The just shall live by faith.” Romans 1:20: For since the creation of the world His invisible attributes are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made, even His eternal power and Godhead, so that they are without excuse,
What does Romans 1 say about same-sex relationships?
Romans 1:26–32 hits same-sex relationships as against nature; those who practice such things are deserving of death—eternal death, not killing backbiters. He speaks out against it plainly.
What does Romans 1 say about same-sex relationships?

The Bible says God created it and you can tell there was a creator by looking at creation. So he hid it. Next in verses 26-32. He hits same-sex. Relationships why because the roman. Caesars and the roman government was into homosexuality let alone the nation. So he hits homosexuality woman with woman man with men. Along with a list of other things. You see. Backbiters haters of God violent proud boasters inventors of evil thing disobedient to parents and on and on and on. See he hits it why he’s addressing the moral decline of the roman empire.
What does Romans 1 say about same-sex relationships?

Romans 1:26-32: For this reason God gave them up to vile passions. For even their women exchanged the natural use for what is against nature. Likewise also the men, leaving the natural use of the woman, burned in their lust for one another, men with men committing what is shameful, and receiving in themselves the penalty of their error which was due. And even as they did not like to retain God in their knowledge, God gave them over to a debased mind, to do those things which are not fitting; being filled with all unrighteousness, sexual immorality, wickedness, covetousness, maliciousness; full of envy, murder, strife, deceit, evil-mindedness; they are whisperers, backbiters, haters of God, violent, proud, boasters, inventors of evil things, disobedient to parents, undiscerning, untrustworthy, unloving, unforgiving, unmerciful; who, knowing the righteous judgment of God, that those who practice such things are deserving of death, not only do the same but also approve of those who practice them.
How does water baptism relate to the old immoral nature?
Romans 6: being born again is a new creature; old things passed away. Water baptism is God’s work to kill the old immoral nature for believers who follow Christ.
How does water baptism relate to the old immoral nature?

He’s speaking out against it. And he goes on to say. They are deserving of death now is he talking about killing backbiters. Okay what death is he talking about. The spiritual death the second death in the lake of fire these people are going to be judged and burned in the lake of fire therefore don’t approve of them speak out on standards so you can save them from the eternal death the second death in the lake of fire isn’t that just common sense yeah. Romans 6:6. People say that water baptism is a sacrament of the church. That’s like saying being born again is the sacrament of the church. Being born again is a spiritual experience a new creature. The old things passed away. And in water baptism this is what. Was written to the church in Rome our old man is crucified with Jesus that old man of sin that evil behavior that immoral person. In water baptism that the body of sin might be destroyed that henceforth we should not serve sin reckon yourself therefore to be dead to sin you see water baptism is another step to get you connected with moral standards of the Bible. Hallelujah. And you relate to Christ when he went into the grave we go under the water we’re dead we come up when Christ rose he was a eternal being no blood he couldn’t die again that body Christ the spirit never died he could never die but the body died.
How does water baptism relate to the old immoral nature?

Romans 6:3-6: Or do you not know that as many of us as were baptized into Christ Jesus were baptized into His death? Therefore we were buried with Him through baptism into death, that just as Christ was raised from the dead by the glory of the Father, even so we also should walk in newness of life. For if we have been united together in the likeness of His death, certainly we also shall be in the likeness of His resurrection, knowing this, that our old man was crucified with Him, that the body of sin might be done away with, that we should no longer be slaves of sin.
How does love fulfill the law in Romans 13–14?

Romans 13: government punishes evildoers. Love does no harm to a neighbor—love is the fulfillment of the law. Shadow food laws (pork) differ from moral priority; Romans 16:17 mark those who cause divisions contrary to the doctrine.
How does love fulfill the law in Romans 13–14?

So water baptism is very important. For believers who follow Christ. It’s a work of God to kill your old immoral nature. Romans 13 government punishes evil doers and praises good doers see they don’t close the door of the church. Of morals. And right behavior they don’t do that. They punish evildoers and they honor good doers what is he doing addressing the moral decline in the roman empire. We are to pay taxes to them and we got people today that don’t want to pay taxes but the Bible says to pay taxes to your government but it should be a fair tax. And it should be by the representation of the people. And then he says this tremendous statement in the same context. Love does no harm to a neighbor therefore love is the fulfillment of the law. You see love doesn’t harm anyone. See love doesn’t brag about itself love is patient love is kind. Love. Doesn’t uh bring up. Old issues of harm done to it love never quits it never quits on morals. And so we find. Everything that was taught in the Old Testament taught by Jesus and taught the apostles now being addressed in the churches in Romans 14 he hits what you food you eat and holidays why because there’s always people want to bring spiritual things down to natural. Yeah okay Bible says don’t eat pork so but don’t eat pork the Bible says that was a shadow law. You can eat pork all day and it won’t do anything to your spiritual man Jesus said it’s not what you eat that defiles the man it’s what comes out of your mouth. It’s not what goes into your mouth and so see these aren’t new things today we got people telling us we can’t eat this and can’t eat that and so forth and then the holidays oh my gosh if you don’t have a Christmas tree at Christmas and and and you know just just go all out you’re just a stick in the mud I’ve heard it over and over and over. And Paul simply said hey if they want to keep a holiday then keep it if they don’t want to keep a holiday they don’t have to keep it why why do we want to fight and quarrel over nonsense. Morals is the high priority of the Bible. Could that be an amen. Yeah. Then in chapter 16 verse 17 he plainly says mark those. Who cause divisions and offenses offenses is causing you to roam from Christ and truth morals. Contrary to the doctrine you have learned what’s the doctrine they taught morality. Righteousness. Truth honesty. You see avoid these people don’t don’t get around these people except to try to preach the gospel to them you young ones need and I’ve said this over and over for 40 years you need to be around mature Christians. Whose life will bring you up to a higher level and not hang around your peers. Who are going to approve of your low level of christianity. He says they serve their own appetite their own lust their own desires not Jesus they do what they want to do because they feel like doing it they can drink they can smoke they can chew and they can run with people that do it don’t bother you know everything’s okay I’m I’m under the blood you know hallelujah I’m saved by grace through faith and not of works hallelujah I can do what I want. And they deceive by their speech the simple. You see. How do they offend. Because by their talk they convince people to. Deviate from morality and when they do they’re deviating from Christ.
How does love fulfill the law in Romans 13–14?

Romans 13:3-4: For rulers are not a terror to good works, but to evil. Do you want to be unafraid of the authority? Do what is good, and you will have praise from the same. For he is God’s minister to you for good. But if you do evil, be afraid; for he does not bear the sword in vain; for he is God’s minister, an avenger to execute wrath on him who practices evil. Romans 13:10: Love does no harm to a neighbor; therefore love is the fulfillment of the law. Romans 16:17: Now I urge you, brethren, note those who cause divisions and offenses, contrary to the doctrine which you learned, and avoid them.
How did Paul address Corinth’s church immorality?

1 Corinthians 5:11: don’t keep company with a so-called brother who is sexually immoral, covetous, idolater, reviler, drunkard or extortioner. 1 Corinthians 6: the unrighteous will not inherit—they need to hear they are wrong. 2 Corinthians 2:6: punishment by the majority can be sufficient; judgment is by behavior, not denomination.
How did Paul address Corinth’s church immorality?

p: In this fourth session on present truth, Pastor David G. Kincer reviews eleven present truths about the last days and then examines the falling away. He describes how the medieval church fell away from the simplicity of Christ, the good news and godly living, and asks hearers to see how many of the same things are happening in Catholic and Protestant churches in America and Europe today, saying the remnant who keep God’s commandments are the hope.
What are the first present truths about the last days?

He recaps that we are in the last days, which started in 33 AD and run until the day of the Lord: the days of salvation and the outpouring of God’s Spirit in Acts 2:16, more than one outpouring, and all who call on the Lord shall be saved. Present truth number two is that Jesus the Messiah, God, has come in the flesh.
What are the first present truths about the last days?

Thank you for joining us in our fourth session of present truths out of second Peter 1:12. We are to be established in present truth. Ecclesiastes, you remember, says God has a purpose under heaven and he does it in certain seasons and certain times. And 1 Chronicles 12 tells us that the children of Issachar had understanding of the times to know what Israel ought to do. Today we’re going to be looking at the falling away. First of all of review so that this gets in your cranial structure. The first present truth that we talked about were is that we’re in the last days which started in 33 AD till the day of the Lord when he comes. That’s also the days of salvation and the days of the pouring out of God’s spirit in Acts 2:16. This is that which is spoken by the prophet Joel. Then in the last days I will pour out my spirit. Last days plural. There’ll be signs in heaven and in earth before the day singular one season of the Lord. I will pour out my spirit in those days. What days? The last day. So there’s more than one pouring out. And all who call on the Lord shall be saved. So the first present truth is we’re living in the last days. We don’t know how long they are. And these days are the days of salvation and the outpouring of the Holy Spirit. Present truth number two that we have taught Jesus the Messiah, the Christ, the prophet, the king and God has come in the flesh. 1 AD we’ll call it.
What are the first present truths about the last days?

And on My menservants and on My maidservants I will pour out My Spirit in those days; And they shall prophesy. I will show wonders in heaven above And signs in the earth beneath: Blood and fire and vapor of smoke. The sun shall be turned into darkness, And the moon into blood, Before the coming of the great and awesome day of the LORD. And it shall come to pass That whoever calls on the name of the LORD Shall be saved.’

He says there are many false prophets and antichrists until Jesus returns, and false prophets are known mainly by saying sin is okay. He says Jesus’ followers are hated and persecuted till the end for three biblical reasons: preaching the kingdom of God and repentance, living godly, and simply believing in Jesus.

We’re living in that season. Present truth number three. There are many false prophets and antichrist from 1 AD till Jesus returns. And we know that today some of our antichrists are Jews who don’t accept Christ coming in the flesh. Muslims who distort he didn’t die on the cross. Atheists, religionists, liberals, humanist, and communists are a few of the antichrists in the world today that we live in. False prophets, we know them mainly by them saying sin is okay. It’s okay that you sin for any reason, faith, grace, whatever. Present truth number four. Jesus followers are hated and persecuted till the end. Okay, they were persecuted back there when Christ was here after Christ and the apostles. They’ve been persecuted all through and they’ll be persecuted till Jesus returns. The three biblical reasons for persecution is for preaching the kingdom of God and repentance. The second one is living godly. So you threaten their lifestyle. And the third one is simply believing in Jesus. If you are persecuted for doing wrong, the Bible says there’s no profit in it. There’s no reward in it. But the Bible acceptance of persecution is one of these three things. Okay? And mainly if you go out talking about repentance, people aren’t going to like it.

He will come. So the reason he didn’t come any minute and he didn’t come today and he didn’t come yesterday is all things haven’t been restored.

Acts 3:19-21: Repent therefore and be converted, that your sins may be blotted out, so that times of refreshing may come from the presence of the Lord, and that He may send Jesus Christ, who was preached to you before, whom heaven must receive until the times of restoration of all things, which God has spoken by the mouth of all His holy prophets since the world began.

He says present truth number eight is that Israel became a nation again in 1948, and number nine is that no one knows the times and seasons: Jesus said it is not for you to know, and in Mark 13:32 “no one knows the day or the hour.” So when people trouble you about the second coming, wars and tsunamis, do not be troubled.

And the man said, the words are closed up and sealed to the time of the end. Many shall be purified, made white, that’s that salvation season, and tested. But the wicked will do wickedly, and none of the wicked will understand, but the wise will understand. The children of Issachar had understanding of the time. Present truth number eight. Israel became a nation again in 1948 after 2600 years of not being a nation. Present truth number nine. No one knows the times and the seasons. Is a present truth. We showed you that in Daniel. We shown it here in Acts. Will you at this time restore the restore the kingdom to Israel? Jesus said, “It’s not for you to know the times of the seasons which the father has put in his own authority.” Mark 13:32, “No one knows the day or the hour.” So when these people are troubling you with the second coming of the Lord and all these things and wars and and uh tsunamis and whatever, don’t be troubled.

Acts 1:6-7: Therefore, when they had come together, they asked Him, saying, “Lord, will You at this time restore the kingdom to Israel?” And He said to them, “It is not for you to know times or seasons which the Father has put in His own authority. Mark 13:32: “But of that day and hour no one knows, not even the angels in heaven, nor the Son, but only the Father.
Has the gospel been preached to all nations as a witness?

He says present truth number ten is that the gospel as a witness to all nations has not been fulfilled, because if it had, Jesus would have come. He says all nations were not known until the 1500s, so those predicting the second coming before then did not understand God’s seasons.

No one knows. We will know when it’s activated. When God activates it, we’ll start getting it. Present truth number 10, the gospel as a witness. Can’t leave that statement out. Preached to all nations has not been fulfilled yet because if it had Jesus would have come. That means all things would have been restored. And so the gospel as a witness has not been preached to all nations yet. And we didn’t even know all nations until the 1500s when the other continents were discovered. And people prophesying the second coming of Christ before that didn’t understand the seasons and the times that God has ordained to happen before he comes.

Matthew 24:14: And this gospel of the kingdom will be preached in all the world as a witness to all the nations, and then the end will come.
Are wars and earthquakes signs of the end?

He says present truth number eleven is wars, earthquakes, famines and plagues, but from Luke 21:11 and Mark 13:7 “the end is not yet.” He says they are not a sign of the second coming, and asks hearers to think, as he describes the medieval church, about how many of these things are happening in America and Europe since 1960.

items.ser: Why Jesus Is Important to All Mankind
tg: Why Jesus Is Important to All Mankind
p: Pastor David G. Kincer follows the Father’s business after Jesus was filled with the Spirit: led into the desert, tested by the devil, and returned in power. Testings work patience and show where we are. The early church prayed in unity, spoke with great power, rejoiced in persecution and grew as the word transformed people.

p: Continuing his present truth series, Pastor David G. Kincer reviews the marks of the last days and adds citizens as the fifth necessary but risky group, showing from Jotham, Pilate and Felix that corrupt citizens can bring judgment and manipulate government. He traces God correcting corrupt people from the flood to Sodom, Canaan and the golden calf, and answers critics that God is a King, Judge and Father doing His job.
What have we learned about the last days? (Acts 2:16-17; 1 John 4:1)

He reviews that we are living in the last days: days of salvation, of the outpouring of the Holy Spirit, and of Jesus the Messiah having come in the flesh. He says it is also a time of many false prophets, false teachers and “many antichrist not one many.”
What have we learned about the last days? (Acts 2:16-17; 1 John 4:1)

We’re going to continue with present truth and. We’re going to take a little remember e. Remembrance of what we’ve learned. We have learned that we are living in the last days Acts 2:16 Daniel 12 we have learned that the last days are days of salvation people can get saved from sin and it is times of the outpouring of the Holy Spirit Acts 2 it is the time when Jesus the messiah the Christ the prophet the king and God that was promised to come has come in the flesh it is also a time of many false prophets false teachers and many antichrist not one many 1 John 4:1 Matthew 24.

items.t: The Gift of the Holy Spirit
items.d: Pastor David G. Kincer teaches that the gift of the Holy Spirit has the same requirements as salvation and is promised to all flesh in these last days. He walks through the Spirit’s expressions in Acts—wind…
p: Pastor David G. Kincer teaches that the gift of the Holy Spirit has the same requirements as salvation and is promised to all flesh in these last days. He walks through the Spirit’s expressions in Acts—wind, fire, tongues, boldness, signs, guidance into truth—and concludes that the most powerful proof is being changed into a good person and staying that way, with love as the more excellent way.

items.d: In this session on present truths Pastor David G. Kincer teaches that the gospel of the kingdom and of repentance and remission of sins will be preached to all nations as a witness, confirmed by signs and…
p: In this session on present truths Pastor David G. Kincer teaches that the gospel of the kingdom and of repentance and remission of sins will be preached to all nations as a witness, confirmed by signs and wonders. He walks through the signs that follow believers, the signs of an apostle and the results in Acts, and says a last-days visitation greater than the early church is coming, with the ministries of apostle and prophet restored.
What message will usher in the end time? (Matthew 24:14; Luke 24:47)

He says the gospel of the kingdom shall be preached to all nations “as a witness,” and Jesus said repentance and remission of sins should be preached in His name to all nations. He says that message, not prosperity, the second coming, positive thinking, personal prophecy or poverty, is what will usher in the end time.

p: Pastor David G. Kincer teaches from Titus 2 that the grace of God that brings salvation has appeared to all men in Jesus, full of grace and truth. Grace is manifold, given to serve one another. items.d: Pastor David G. Kincer preaches Ezekiel 36: God puts His Spirit in His people for His name’s sake, so the heathen will know He is the Lord when His people keep His word. The Spirit gives believers words before…
p: Pastor David G. Kincer preaches Ezekiel 36: God puts His Spirit in His people for His name’s sake, so the heathen will know He is the Lord when His people keep His word. The Spirit gives believers words before rulers, as with Elihu, the apostles and Paul before Felix and Agrippa: repent and turn to God.

I do not do this for your sakes but for My holy name’s sake, which you profaned among the heathen.

The Bible when we read it is so powerful. We’re gonna go to a prophet in the Old Testament and see a tremendous promise God made to his people. I do not this for your sakes God says I’m going to do something but I’m not going to do it for your sake o Israel my people I’m not doing it for my peoples sake. For my own name’s sake it’s what I’m gonna do it for I’m gonna do this for my name.

Ezekiel 36:22: “Therefore say to the house of Israel, ‘Thus says the Lord GOD: “I do not do this for your sake, O house of Israel, but for My holy name’s sake, which you have profaned among the nations wherever you went.

So the heathen will know that He is the Lord; God cares about those who don’t believe as much as about His people.

items.d: Pastor David G. Kincer shows that the unchanging God’s Holy Spirit worked in the Old Testament as in the New: he spoke through the prophets, filled the tabernacle builders, gave David the temple pattern…
p: Pastor David G. Kincer shows that the unchanging God’s Holy Spirit worked in the Old Testament as in the New: he spoke through the prophets, filled the tabernacle builders, gave David the temple pattern, cleanses by judgment and burning, and fills with power. Now poured on all flesh, he gives tongues as a sign to unbelievers, calls and sends ministers, and moves in God’s seasons—so the church must learn to hear him and recognize the times.

items.t: The Holy Spirit Speaks to All Mankind 10/15/2017
items.d: Pastor David G. Kincer teaches that the Holy Spirit speaks to all mankind—backsliders, the faithful and the world—through the conscience, with or without preaching. From 1 Timothy 4, John 7 and John 16 he…
p: Pastor David G. Kincer teaches that the Holy Spirit speaks to all mankind—backsliders, the faithful and the world—through the conscience, with or without preaching. From 1 Timothy 4, John 7 and John 16 he covers the seared conscience, the outpouring on all flesh, conviction of sin, righteousness and judgment, and guidance into all truth, then argues from John 3:18–21 and Romans 2 that people are condemned for evil deeds against conscience, and calls the church to get the message out.

He speaks to all mankind, so we must hear him. We need him to show up, speak and manifest his power—the third part of the Godhead.

items.t: The Kingdom of God and Those Outside It
items.d: From Mark 4:11 Pastor David G. Kincer explains that knowledge of the mystery of the kingdom is given, hidden in parables from those who close their eyes. He lays out the steps into the kingdom, who will not…
p: From Mark 4:11 Pastor David G. Kincer explains that knowledge of the mystery of the kingdom is given, hidden in parables from those who close their eyes. He lays out the steps into the kingdom, who will not inherit it, who the “dogs” and sleeping watchmen are, what the kingdom is—righteousness, peace and joy in power—and how believers should live wisely before those outside.
What is “given” to those who know the mystery of the kingdom?

From Mark 4:11 and its parallels (Matthew 13, Acts 28, Isaiah 6) he says knowledge of the mystery of the kingdom of God is given—not acquired or paid for. A mystery is something hidden you must search for, and the kingdom is the dominion ruled by God; those without that knowledge are outside the kingdom.

p: In this message a guest speaker at Vine Cluster Church continues his study of Esther in chapters 8–10 as a parable of the new covenant. He teaches that the new covenant has authority over the old, that the ceremonial “shadow laws” point to Jesus while the moral law stays, and that Jesus gives his church power. p: In this message a guest speaker at Vine Cluster Church reads Esther 3–7 as a parable of the new covenant. He says Haman pictures the proud scribes and Pharisees and Mordecai pictures Jesus, who would not bow to them. He then follows Esther going before the king, her two banquets, and Haman’s end, and closes by urging believers to surrender old ways.
What is the parable of Haman and Mordecai in Esther 3, and was Mordecai the king’s employee?

He says parables are “a short allegorical story designed to illustrate or teach truth,” and that the Old Testament stories “not just historical events they are examples and illustrations.” He says he had assumed Mordecai worked for the king, but “mordecai wasn’t necessarily employed by the king,” while Haman was “promoted above all the princes.”

We’ve got to remember that we do not want to be like these people we don’t want to get into a state in our christianity where we become like the scribes and the Pharisees we become and he says it very plainly hypocrites. Haman as you learn in this story is an example of the scribes and Pharisees now in actuality. When Jesus came who died who died. Tell me Jesus Christ died. But in this story in the story of Esther here Haman died. So we got to understand what’s what’s the deal here you you see when Jesus died. The old covenant the old way stopped. The burnt offerings stopped. The ceremonies stopped. Amen. The old covenant the old way stopped. See when Jesus died on the cross the veil was rent in two that the the all those laws about the son of Aaron and all only certain people could go into the temple that all stopped. When Jesus died everyone now can come in everyone now has an opportunity everyone now that has a desire to please the king can come in.
