Revelation 11:15: Then the seventh angel sounded: And there were loud voices in heaven, saying, “The kingdoms of this world have become the kingdoms of our Lord and of His Christ, and He shall reign forever and ever!” Matthew 28:18: And Jesus came and spoke to them, saying, “All authority has been given to Me in heaven and on earth.
Is the third woe really a “woe” for the saints? (Revelation 11:17-18)

He says the nations being angry, the dead being judged and the saints being rewarded are “all happening at the same time.” He says “the third woe… doesn’t sound like much of a woe to me when you’re on the right side,” and that resurrection and judgment are described together in the passage.
Is the third woe really a “woe” for the saints? (Revelation 11:17-18)

He says, “You have taken Your great power and reign.” “The nations were angry, for Your wrath has come, and the time of the dead that are judged, and the rewards for the saints.” Look at this. Everything is happening at the same time. Watch this, just read it. The nations are what? Do they, a lot of the people, nations means people, are a lot of people mad at Jesus? They don’t like you saying that name. Is our government mad at Jesus? They don’t want the name said. Yeah. “Your wrath has come.” Okay, these plagues, these things that God does to get people’s attention and get them to repent, as we learn. “And the time of the dead being judged.” Oh, how does the dead get judged? They got to be what? Resurrected. See, this is all happening at the same time. “And the saints are rewarded.” Ooh, that don’t sound like a big woe to me. The third woe has come. Doesn’t sound like much of a woe to me when you’re on the right side, does it? Rewards, I can handle rewards. Are you with me? Hallelujah. But boy, they got it all complicated. And, you know, saints are resurrected, then later the dead in sin are resurrected, and all this stuff, but right here it says what? It’s all happening at the same time.
Is the third woe really a “woe” for the saints? (Revelation 11:17-18)

Revelation 11:17-18: saying: “We give You thanks, O Lord God Almighty, The One who is and who was and who is to come, Because You have taken Your great power and reigned. The nations were angry, and Your wrath has come, And the time of the dead, that they should be judged, And that You should reward Your servants the prophets and the saints, And those who fear Your name, small and great, And should destroy those who destroy the earth.”
What does he say is the problem with the prophecy charts?
He says each chart has several periods of three and a half years that “adds up to about 14 years, not seven,” and that the two witnesses are “a real problem with this chart.”
What does he say about a temple being rebuilt?

He says “the natural temple was destroyed in 70 AD,” so “he’s not talking about measuring that temple, is he? No.” He says people want a rebuilt temple “because they’re trying to reduce this down to a natural temple.”
Does God live in buildings made by people?
He says no: “God does not dwell in temples made with hands.” He says the real temple is the church and the Jewish temple “pointed to the church, the real temple of God.”
Why does he ask where Mount Sinai is?

He says Galatians says Hagar is Mount Sinai “in Arabia,” and asks Bible scholars, “could it be that the maps are wrong and Mount Sinai is actually in another place that the maps haven’t told us?” He says he is “just throwing that out.”
What does he mean by “the new Jerusalem”?
He says “we are come to… the new Jerusalem, the church,” and “He’s after you. He’s interested in you.”
What is a temple, according to him?
He says “a temple is an abiding place, a home is a place of residence, abiding place. He wants to take up residence in your life.”
Can a Christian defile the temple of God?
He says yes, in the sense that “us human beings are not to defile the temple,” since “you are the temple of God and the Spirit of God dwells in you.”
How long do the two witnesses prophesy?

He says “for three and a half years,” with fire coming out of their mouths, and they “tormented the people on earth.” He says to the young people that God is going to manifest Himself and “you’re going to be glad you chose Christ when that happens.”
Why does he say the two witnesses are not Moses and Elijah?
He says “no man of God has ever gone through the earth spitting fire out and destroying those who oppose them,” and “it’s definitely not Moses and Elijah.”
Does the Bible say the beast is the antichrist?
He says “nowhere in the Bible, church, does it say the beast is the antichrist.” He adds, “Nowhere does it say the beast and the antichrist are the same person.”
How can everyone on earth see the two witnesses?
He says it is the same as everyone seeing Jesus when He comes: “does God need a satellite TV to do that? No, He just opens your eyes to see.”
Why were 7,000 people killed in the earthquake?
He says it “doesn’t make sense” for “millions of people in the city” unless you know of “7,000 in Israel that did not bow their knee.”
When does he say the sacrifices ceased?
He says “it’s when Jesus died on the cross. Right. When He died, there was no more sacrifices.” and when He said “It is finished,” that is “when the sacrifices were finished.”
What sacrifice does he say is left for believers?
He says “the sacrifice of praise, the fruit of our lips, giving thanks unto His name,” which “most Christians will not do” because of the way they were raised.
He says yes: “Is He the King of kings and Lord of lords of the nations now? Yeah.” He cites “All power is given to Me in heaven and in earth.”

items.d: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer teaches from Revelation 12 that the manchild is Jesus, the dragon is Satan the accuser, and the brethren overcome him by the blood of the Lamb and the word of their…
p: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer teaches from Revelation 12 that the manchild is Jesus, the dragon is Satan the accuser, and the brethren overcome him by the blood of the Lamb and the word of their testimony. He says the remnant lives on earth and is called to rule over sin now.
Who is the woman and the manchild in Revelation 12?

He describes the woman clothed with the sun, the manchild, and the dragon who persecutes her. He asks, “is the woman Israel?” and “Is it the church? Is it Mary?” He says of the manchild, “We know that Jesus is the manchild. There’s no question about it.”
Who is the woman and the manchild in Revelation 12?

Let’s go to Revelations 12. It talks about a woman with the moon under her feet, clothed with the sun, and delivering a manchild. Okay? She’s going to birth a manchild. And the dragon comes to keep the woman from birthing the manchild. And then the dragon comes to persecute the woman who birthed the manchild and her seed. Okay, let’s watch this. Now, is the woman Israel? You know, she’s got 12 stars in her crown, as we can see there. She’s got a crown up there. There’s 12 tribes. Actually, there’s 13. Is it the church? Is it Mary? We know Mary birthed what? Jesus Christ. We know that. We know that Jesus is the manchild. There’s no question about it. There ain’t no confusion here. But who’s this woman? Who is this woman? Is it Israel? Is it Mary? “The woman fled into the wilderness, prepared by God, that they would feed her 1,260 days,” or three and a half years. Here we are, another three and a half years. “And when the dragon saw he was cast to the earth, he persecuted the woman who gave birth to the male child.”
Who is the woman and the manchild in Revelation 12?

Revelation 12:1-6: Now a great sign appeared in heaven: a woman clothed with the sun, with the moon under her feet, and on her head a garland of twelve stars. Then being with child, she cried out in labor and in pain to give birth. And another sign appeared in heaven: behold, a great, fiery red dragon having seven heads and ten horns, and seven diadems on his heads. His tail drew a third of the stars of heaven and threw them to the earth. And the dragon stood before the woman who was ready to give birth, to devour her Child as soon as it was born. She bore a male Child who was to rule all nations with a rod of iron. And her Child was caught up to God and His throne. Then the woman fled into the wilderness, where she has a place prepared by God, that they should feed her there one thousand two hundred and sixty days.
Can the woman be Mary or Israel?

He says there is “no record that she was persecuted by Satan, and obviously no flood,” and that Israel was persecuted yet “did not eliminate that nation.” He notes that “many of them, by the way, have accepted Christ.”
Can the woman be Mary or Israel?

“But the woman was given two wings like a great eagle to fly into the wilderness, where she is nourished for three and a half years. The serpent spit out water out of his mouth like a flood, trying to drown the woman and carry her away by a flood. But the earth opened up and helped the woman and swallowed up the flood.” Now, we know Mary birthed Jesus. We know that she fled into Egypt. We don’t know how many years, but she did go into Egypt. We have no record that she was persecuted by Satan, and obviously no flood. Israel is made up of 12 tribes, and one person out of Israel, Mary, birthed Jesus.
Can the woman be Mary or Israel?

Revelation 12:14-16: But the woman was given two wings of a great eagle, that she might fly into the wilderness to her place, where she is nourished for a time and times and half a time, from the presence of the serpent. So the serpent spewed water out of his mouth like a flood after the woman, that he might cause her to be carried away by the flood. But the earth helped the woman, and the earth opened its mouth and swallowed up the flood which the dragon had spewed out of his mouth.
Is the woman the church, and what is God’s goal for her? (Galatians 4:19, Colossians 1:27, Ephesians 4:13)

He reads “My little children, in whom I travail and birth again until Christ be formed in you,” and says God’s goal is “the fullness of the stature of… Jesus Christ,” not the preacher, the TV evangelist or the great book writer. He says, “God has a goal, a destiny, to birth Himself in you till you are like Him.”
Is the woman the church, and what is God’s goal for her? (Galatians 4:19, Colossians 1:27, Ephesians 4:13)

And Satan has persecuted Israel since Christ was here, and even before. Okay? Satan’s persecution of Israel did not eliminate that nation. They’re still with us today in spite of the persecution. And many of them, by the way, have accepted Christ. The church. Galatians 4:19. Are you ready for this? “My little children, in whom I travail and birth again until Christ be formed in you.” Oh, oh, Christ be formed in you. Ah, Colossians 1:27: “God would make known what is the riches of His glory of this mystery among the nations,” among the unbelievers, “which is Christ in you, the hope of glory.” Ephesians 4:13: “Till we all come into the unity of the faith, the knowledge of the Son of Man, unto a perfect man, unto the measure and the stature of the fullness of Christ.” Wow. Not only is He being formed in His church, but it tells us what the goal is: the fullness of the stature of the preacher? No. The TV evangelist? No. The great book writer? No. Of Jesus Christ.
Is the woman the church, and what is God’s goal for her? (Galatians 4:19, Colossians 1:27, Ephesians 4:13)

Galatians 4:19: My little children, for whom I labor in birth again until Christ is formed in you, Colossians 1:27: To them God willed to make known what are the riches of the glory of this mystery among the Gentiles: which is Christ in you, the hope of glory. Ephesians 4:13: till we all come to the unity of the faith and of the knowledge of the Son of God, to a perfect man, to the measure of the stature of the fullness of Christ;
Has the church been persecuted since Jesus ascended?

He says “Satan has persecuted the church since Jesus ascended,” and gives figures from the Voice of the Martyrs and the International Bulletin of Missionary Research. He gives examples from different centuries and countries and asks, “That sounds big to me. How about you?”
Has the church been persecuted since Jesus ascended?

God has a goal, a destiny, to birth Himself in you till you are like Him. Wow. We know these things. Are you there? Satan has persecuted the church since Jesus ascended. More than 43 million Christians have been killed for their faith since the crucifixion of Jesus Christ. These statistics are from the 2004 Voice of the Martyrs and the International Bulletin of Missionary Research. Six to 12 million Christians were killed the first 250 years after Christ. And we’re looking for some great persecution up the road as the only one, as the big deal, as the big tribulation. That sounds big to me. How about you? That’s big time. The Catholic Church persecuted and killed many Protestant believers in Europe for leaving the Catholic Church. According to many resources, Hitler killed 3 million Christians and persecuted millions more during the Second World War. Leading up to it and during it, the Muslims have killed people in our day. October 2005, three teenagers were beheaded because they were going to a private Christian school in Indonesia. Three 12-year-old Indonesian Christian schoolgirls were beheaded by the Muslims. Again, in October 2010, a 14-year-old boy working in a factory was beheaded because he would not denounce Jesus Christ. Orphanage workers were beheaded in August of 2010, just last year. In 2008, they sliced off the head of a 25-year-old man in Kenya for converting to Christianity. China killed 30,000 Christians in 1900. In 1912, 40 had their eyes put out and they were beheaded because they wouldn’t denounce Christ. Thousands have died when the communists took over in China.
Is the great tribulation still in the future?

He recounts that believers behind the Iron Curtain told missionaries, “You told us we wouldn’t go through the tribulation. What do you think we’ve been in, man?” He gives more present-day figures, and says “this tribulation thing, it isn’t something we’ve got to wait for. It’s in the world right now.”
Is the great tribulation still in the future?

An estimated 250,000 Christians died in China from the 1950 takeover, that era, until the present. How many know that’s serious tribulation? In fact, when the Iron Curtain opened back up and we were allowed to go back in, the first thing the believers there told the missionaries that came is, “You told us that we would not go through the tribulation.” That was the first words out of their mouth: “You told us we wouldn’t go through the tribulation. What do you think we’ve been in, man?” Are you there? Is this making sense to you? Or am I confusing you? There’s a lot of persecution been going on, folks, for a long time. 270 Christian martyrs happen every 24 hours for the last 10 years. That’s over a million Christians that have died for Christ since 2001. That’s big-time stuff. There have been more than 26 [unclear] documented cases of martyrdom from 1900 to the year 2000. More than 200 million Christians in over 60 nations face persecution each day. 150,000 are martyred each year, and about one and a half million over a 10-year period. Christians today are the most persecuted group in the world. Persecution is on the rise because of communism and the expansion of Islamic and Hindu extremism. Literally hundreds of thousands of people today are being killed and brutalized, sold as slaves, tortured, imprisoned, threatened, discriminated against, and arrested solely because they are Christians. That’s some serious persecution, folks. That’s some serious tribulation times. Am I right? And you don’t have to be a Christian. You can be persecuted just because of your nationality or your race. Remember the blacks in the United States were persecuted for a long time. When I was a boy, they had to take shoeshine jobs and sweeping the floors, and they were terribly mistreated. I’ve seen it with my own eyes. And over in Africa right now, the whites are being persecuted by the blacks. Their property is taken, they’re killed. The blacks, which rose up and said, “The whites are mistreating us,” once they got in power, they reversed it. And whites in Africa are being tormented, tortured, and killed, and their property taken away. Why? Because they’re white. So this tribulation thing, it isn’t something we’ve got to wait for. It’s in the world right now. Could that be an amen? Yes. Religions have persecuted religions. Atheists have persecuted believers and killed them.
Who is the male child who rules with a rod of iron? (2 Timothy 3:12, Revelation 2:26, Acts 1:9, Psalm 2:9)

He says “all that live godly in Christ shall suffer” persecution, and that the male child is Jesus: “That part’s a no-brainer.” He reads Revelation 2:26 and says “we can overcome to what we rule… He will cause us to rule.”
Who is the male child who rules with a rod of iron? (2 Timothy 3:12, Revelation 2:26, Acts 1:9, Psalm 2:9)

Now, you’re going to tell these people that the great tribulation hasn’t come yet? Think about it. Are you with me? It’s something that’s been around for 2,000 years. The Bible says in 2 Timothy 3:12 that “all that live godly in Christ shall suffer” what? Persecution. You know, it’s not about being a believer. They don’t care if you believe in Christ. They just don’t want you living for Him. Now, the male child. You want to find out who the male child is? This is an easy one. Jesus. “She bore a male child who was to rule all nations with a rod of iron.” “And her child was caught up to God and His throne.” Okay. Revelations 2:26: “He that overcomes and keeps My works until the end, to him will I give power over the nations, and he will rule them with a rod of iron. As the vessels of a potter shall they be broken to shivers, even as I received from My Father.” So who’s the person that rules with a rod of iron? Jesus. And we can what? Do the same. We can overcome to what we rule. See, we don’t have to sin like the nations sin. We don’t have to give in to things like the nations give into. He will cause us to rule. Amen. Because that’s what He is. He’s an overcomer. Acts 1:9. “While they watched, Jesus was taken up, and a cloud received Him out of their sight.” And the angel said in verse 11, “This same Jesus, who was taken up from you into heaven, will so come in like manner as you saw Him go into heaven.” So who’s the one that’s the manchild that’s born and ascended back to the Father? Jesus Christ. That part’s a no-brainer. That’s an easy one. Psalms tells us that Jesus would rule the nations with a rod of iron. Psalms 2:9. Okay. Now, who’s this dragon? This persecutor. He hates our guts. Well, this same chapter tells us it’s Satan. “Another sign appeared in heaven: a fiery red dragon having seven heads and 10 horns and seven diadems on his head.
Who is the male child who rules with a rod of iron? (2 Timothy 3:12, Revelation 2:26, Acts 1:9, Psalm 2:9)

2 Timothy 3:12: Yes, and all who desire to live godly in Christ Jesus will suffer persecution. Revelation 2:26: And he who overcomes, and keeps My works until the end, to him I will give power over the nations— Acts 1:9: Now when He had spoken these things, while they watched, He was taken up, and a cloud received Him out of their sight. Psalm 2:9: You shall break them with a rod of iron; You shall dash them to pieces like a potter’s vessel.’ ”
Who is the dragon in Revelation 12? (Revelation 12:3-9)
He reads that the dragon is “that old serpent called the Devil and Satan,” and asks, “what’s Satan’s job? To deceive the whole world.” He says Satan is on the earth, “He’s here, folks.”
Who is the dragon in Revelation 12? (Revelation 12:3-9)

“His tail threw a third of the stars from heaven to the earth. And the dragon stood before the woman who was ready to give birth, to devour her child as soon as it was born.” And Satan was thrown out of heaven. “And Michael and his angels fought with the dragon, and his angels, and they were cast down. That old serpent called the Devil and Satan,” verse 9, “who deceives the whole world. He was cast to the earth, and his angels were cast out with him.” So wait, what’s Satan’s job? To deceive the whole world. Okay? And where is he at? On earth. He’s here, folks. He’s the one that tested Jesus in the garden. Remember, I mean, in the wilderness, remember?
Who is the dragon in Revelation 12? (Revelation 12:3-9)

Revelation 12:3-9: And another sign appeared in heaven: behold, a great, fiery red dragon having seven heads and ten horns, and seven diadems on his heads. His tail drew a third of the stars of heaven and threw them to the earth. And the dragon stood before the woman who was ready to give birth, to devour her Child as soon as it was born. She bore a male Child who was to rule all nations with a rod of iron. And her Child was caught up to God and His throne. Then the woman fled into the wilderness, where she has a place prepared by God, that they should feed her there one thousand two hundred and sixty days. And war broke out in heaven: Michael and his angels fought with the dragon; and the dragon and his angels fought, but they did not prevail, nor was a place found for them in heaven any longer. So the great dragon was cast out, that serpent of old, called the Devil and Satan, who deceives the whole world; he was cast to the earth, and his angels were cast out with him.
What does it mean that Satan is “the accuser of our brethren”? (Revelation 12:10, Luke 10:17-18)

He says Satan accuses you in your mind, “See, you’re no good. You’re a failure,” and “Christ isn’t finished with your life yet.” He ties Revelation 12 to the 70 who returned and Jesus saying, “I saw Satan as lightning fall from heaven.”
What does it mean that Satan is “the accuser of our brethren”? (Revelation 12:10, Luke 10:17-18)

He’s here. He’s already been thrown down. He’s been here for a long time. Ain’t that right? Don’t we know that? We know that. “Then I heard a voice saying in heaven, ‘Now salvation, strength, and the kingdom of our God and the power of Christ have come. For the accuser of our brethren, who accused them before our God day and night, has been cast down.’” So he’s called the serpent, Satan, the Devil, and the what? Accuser. And yes, he’ll come and accuse you. You make a mistake, he’s going to be right there talking in your mind, your subconscious, saying, “See, you’re no good. You’re a failure. Just quit pretending.” What’s he doing? He’s accusing you. That’s his job. That’s what he does. He lies. He accuses. He tries to deceive you. But see, Christ has a goal for you. Christ isn’t finished with your life yet. And he don’t want Christ finishing with your life yet. He don’t want you becoming an overcomer. He don’t want you overcoming sin and living rightly in this world and being a blessing to yourself and to your family. And so he is out to deceive you. Hallelujah. Now, in Luke 10:1, 17, it says the 70 returned after being sent out with Christ, and they said, “Lord, even the devils are subject to us through Your name.” And Jesus said, “I saw Satan as lightning fall from heaven.” Okay. These 70 went out, preached the gospel, people got saved, demons were cast out, and Jesus likened it to what?
What does it mean that Satan is “the accuser of our brethren”? (Revelation 12:10, Luke 10:17-18)

Revelation 12:10: Then I heard a loud voice saying in heaven, “Now salvation, and strength, and the kingdom of our God, and the power of His Christ have come, for the accuser of our brethren, who accused them before our God day and night, has been cast down. Luke 10:17-18: Then the seventy returned with joy, saying, “Lord, even the demons are subject to us in Your name.” And He said to them, “I saw Satan fall like lightning from heaven.
Have Satan and his angels already been cast down? (Jude 6, Job 1:9)

He says “this is a past tense thing” and “Has Satan and his angels already been cast down? Yeah.” He says “It isn’t some special time up the road. He’s working on us now,” and brings in Satan before the Lord in Job.
Have Satan and his angels already been cast down? (Jude 6, Job 1:9)

Satan falling. Hallelujah. So these things have been done and can be done. “If God spared not the angels that sinned, and cast them down to hell and delivered them into chains of darkness to be reserved unto judgment.” Have the angels that sinned already been cast down? Where are they reserved? In darkness till the judgment. See, this is a past tense thing. Jude 6: “The angels which kept not their first estate.” There’s only one chapter in Jude. Jude 1:6. “But left their own habitation, He has reserved in everlasting chains under darkness until the judgment of the great day.” Amen. So, has Satan and his angels already been cast down? Yeah. Is Satan trying to deceive us? Yeah. It isn’t some special time up the road. He’s working on us now. Job 1:9: Satan presented himself before the Lord after going to and fro upon the earth. So, was Satan going to and fro upon the earth in the Old Testament? Yes. To seek whom he may devour? To see who he could get to deceive and turn from God. And he accused Job before God. See, the accuser of our brethren, what does he do? Well, you know, “If Job wouldn’t serve You if You let some problems come in his life, You’ve got a hedge around him and he doesn’t have any problems. You let some problems come, You take his health, You take his kids, You take his wealth, and he’ll curse you to his face.”
Have Satan and his angels already been cast down? (Jude 6, Job 1:9)

2 Peter 2:4: For if God did not spare the angels who sinned, but cast them down to hell and delivered them into chains of darkness, to be reserved for judgment; Jude 6: And the angels who did not keep their proper domain, but left their own abode, He has reserved in everlasting chains under darkness for the judgment of the great day; Job 1:9: So Satan answered the LORD and said, “Does Job fear God for nothing?
Will God raise up a church like Job?
He says “in these last days, God’s going to raise up a church like Job.” He says, “We serve Him because He deserves to be served.”
Will God raise up a church like Job?

And so God said, “Okay, go do your thing, Satan. You don’t know My servant Job.” And I’ll tell you, in these last days, God’s going to raise up a church like Job. We don’t serve God because He blesses us, because He gives us money and finances and health. We serve Him because He deserves to be served. We serve Him because He’s true. He’s righteous. He’s wisdom. He’s knowledge. He’s understanding. He’s everything. Amen. We know Him. We love Him. And so, Satan’s been doing this for quite a while now. Who are the brethren in Revelations 12? And who are the remnant? All right.
Who are the brethren who overcame Satan, and where are they? (Revelation 12:10-11, Matthew 12:48-50)

He says that if the brethren overcame Satan, they are “still where? On earth. They haven’t been raptured anywhere.” He cites Jesus saying those who do the Father’s will are His brethren, mother and brother.
Who are the brethren who overcame Satan, and where are they? (Revelation 12:10-11, Matthew 12:48-50)

Now, look at this. This is powerful. Very powerful. The big bad beast hadn’t even come along yet. We’ll deal with him next week. “The accuser of our brethren, who accused them before our God day and night, has been cast down.” Now, who are the brethren? The next verse, chapter 12, verse 11: “They overcome him,” which is who? Satan. Satan. They overcame. Where are they still? Where’s the saints? If they’re overcoming Satan, where are they? They’re still where? On earth. They haven’t been raptured anywhere. How are you going to get credit for overcoming Satan and up in heaven where Jesus is and God and all the angels? The credit is you overcoming where? Right here on earth. And these brethren, and the Bible throughout the New Testament, Jesus said to His disciples, “They that do the will of My Father are My brethren and My mother.” Are you aware of that? Matthew 12:48: “Who is My mother and who are My brothers?” And He stretched forth His hand toward His disciples and said, “These are My mother and My brother. For whosoever does the will of My Father, the same as My brother and My mother.” Remember that word I asked you to say earlier, “mother.” Say it again. Mother.
Who are the brethren who overcame Satan, and where are they? (Revelation 12:10-11, Matthew 12:48-50)

Revelation 12:10-11: Then I heard a loud voice saying in heaven, “Now salvation, and strength, and the kingdom of our God, and the power of His Christ have come, for the accuser of our brethren, who accused them before our God day and night, has been cast down. And they overcame him by the blood of the Lamb and by the word of their testimony, and they did not love their lives to the death. Matthew 12:48-50: But He answered and said to the one who told Him, “Who is My mother and who are My brothers?” And He stretched out His hand toward His disciples and said, “Here are My mother and My brothers! For whoever does the will of My Father in heaven is My brother and sister and mother.”
How do the brethren overcome Satan? (Revelation 12:11)
He says “We overcome Satan by the what? Blood of the Lamb,” and “There’s power in that blood to forgive and cleanse sin.” He adds, “You need to open your mouth. The word of their testimony.”
How do the brethren overcome Satan? (Revelation 12:11)

A mother produces something. See, in her womb is formed something, and she gives birth to something, and the church is to give birth to Jesus Christ and His righteousness. Are you with me now? Look how powerful you are. How many understand you’re the brethren? Yeah. I mean, the apostles when they wrote “brethren,” didn’t they use that word? We are the saints. We are the brethren. The brethren overcame Satan by the blood of the Lamb. And this is why I got upset last week at these two ministers. They put human counseling above the power of the blood. We overcome Satan by the what? Blood of the Lamb. There’s power in that blood to forgive and cleanse sin. “Man, by the word of their testimony.” That’s why you need to speak. You need to praise Him. You need to open your mouth. The word of their testimony. I’m a believer in Jesus. I’m a Jesus boy. See, you’ve got to speak the word. Can I hear an amen? “And they love not their life even unto death.” They put Jesus first. They overcame who? Look at that. Ain’t that cool? Now, the Bible says He will bruise Satan under your feet in [unclear]. Shortly. What are you waiting on? What’s the word? Shortly. This don’t take a lot of time. Why, man? He’s powerful. His blood’s powerful.

He says “That’s why you need to speak. You need to praise Him. You need to open your mouth. The word of their testimony.”

Why does he say we should not wish to be taken out?
He says “these people got us thinking we’ve got to get raptured out of here to get any peace of mind,” and “He wants you to have an effect on this mess.”
What does he mean by “rule in this life”?
He says “Say it. Rule in this life,” and “I am a believer. I am a brethren. I am a remnant. I am His church.”

Jesus said the man born blind suffered neither for his sin nor his parents’, but to reveal God’s works. Islanders assumed Paul was guilty when bitten. items.d: Pastor David G. Kincer teaches that signs are written so belief can grow. Jesus was born to an engaged virgin and had a stepfather, step-siblings and a single-parent home, so He identifies with broken families…
p: Pastor David G. Kincer teaches that signs are written so belief can grow. Jesus was born to an engaged virgin and had a stepfather, step-siblings and a single-parent home, so He identifies with broken families and troubled pasts. Whatever your past, He can change you. The service closes with communion and prayer for healing.

items.t: The Simplicity That is in Christ
items.d: From 2 Corinthians 11:3 Pastor David G. Kincer teaches that Christ is simple and that his church grows morally even in corrupt nations. Walking through Rome, the mistreatment of Jews, Israel’s 1948 survival…
p: From 2 Corinthians 11:3 Pastor David G. Kincer teaches that Christ is simple and that his church grows morally even in corrupt nations. Walking through Rome, the mistreatment of Jews, Israel’s 1948 survival and America’s flaws, he says people are still drawn to what is good, and from Ecclesiastes, Deuteronomy, Genesis 1 and Isaiah 9 shows that wisdom excels folly and believers reflect Jesus, the great light.
Is Jesus complicated, and will Christians have trouble?

From 2 Corinthians 11:3 he teaches the simplicity that is in Christ: Jesus and the Bible are simple, plain and basic, and people who don’t know him complicate him. From John 16:33, in him you may have peace—it takes a commitment—but in the world you will have trouble.

What defiles a person, according to him?
He says it is things within that defile us, not what we eat or wear: “it’s what comes out those words and those actions that’s what defiles us.”
Why did the religious leaders worry that all would believe on Him?
He says they wanted people to believe in their group and their doctrine, but “We’re supposed to be believing and trusting in and following Jesus Christ.”
How many books does he say the Bible mentions in heaven?
He says the Bible tells us about eight books, including the book of life, the book of works and the book of remembrance.
Was part of Daniel’s sealed book fulfilled in 70 AD?
He says the destruction of Jerusalem in 70 AD fulfilled Daniel, so at least part of Daniel’s sealed book was opened.
Who does he say is antichrist?
He says the apostle John said there are many antichrists: those who oppose Christ and say He did not come in the flesh.
What does he say about guns and murder?
He says “it’s not the gun that kills people,” and if you change the heart of a person you have control.
Why does he say end-time teachers make things look bad?
He says “They want it to look bad because people like bad news”; trouble gets our attention.
Can Satan act without God’s permission?
He says Satan “can do beans without God giving permission,” and Satan is ready and willing any time God will let him.
How does he say Christians renounce Christ today?
He says that by saying sexual immorality is acceptable or that it is okay for Christians to divorce, “we just renounced the Bible”; we deny Him by our actions.
Is there a seven-year tribulation in the Bible?
He says “Nowhere in the Bible does it say there’s seven years of tribulation”; they have to manufacture it out of Daniel.
What does the seal of the Holy Spirit guarantee?
He says it is a guarantee that He will finish the good work He has begun in us; as long as he serves and seeks Him, He will get him to the goal.
He says no; the list of tribes even leaves out Dan and Ephraim, and “there’s an innumerable group of people up there in heaven.”

He says it is about the power and revelation of Jesus Christ, “it’s not about the beast and the troubles in the seven years of tribulation it’s about the conquering Jesus.”

items.d: Others called Jesus the son of Joseph; He called Himself the Son of God. Isaiah foretold a virgin birth and Matthew shows its fulfillment. God gave the Son the nations, so everything we need is found by coming…
p: Others called Jesus the son of Joseph; He called Himself the Son of God. Isaiah foretold a virgin birth and Matthew shows its fulfillment. God gave the Son the nations, so everything we need is found by coming to Him.
