How does God show patience with people? (the flood, Lot, Judas)

Shouldn’t we, your wife, your husband, in the home, especially in this Christmas season? The home just gets attacked, trying to live up to some kind of cultural thing of buying all kinds of presents and living up to some kind of cultural ideal of Christmas. The pressure comes on, and, ah, how many know husbands and wives should give each other time to change? Yes, through forgiveness. See, through forgiveness you can do that. Now, let me remind you that at the flood God gave the people 100 years, with Noah preaching righteousness, to change. Okay, only three people got converted during that flood, if you count Noah’s children and his wife, seven people got converted, but I’m assuming that his kids were raised and they were believers, but if they weren’t, then you got seven people converted. That’s all. 100 years for seven people. God gave them space, and then He brought the punishment. Okay. Lot, Sodom. Lot went down to Sodom, and so for several years while Lot lived in Sodom, the Bible says that he was living righteously. He was an example to those people, and they knew, but they didn’t listen to Lot. And they didn’t listen to Lot when he went and said they’re going to destroy the city. His sons-in-law laughed, and his daughters laughed at him and said, “You’ve got to be joking.” But when the angels came, they only have a few hours. And so the point is, we don’t know if we got several years, a lifetime, or a few hours, so we need to what? Buck up, just listen. Then you got, of course, Israel: 1,000 years God promised if they disobeyed Him they would go into captivity. It took a thousand years to fulfill that, or just under. And then Judas, who was the thief that Jesus Christ picked to be on His staff, His ministry staff. Judas did miracles, Judas cast out demons, Judas preached the gospel, and people repented and came to Christ, and Christ gave him three and a half years to repent, and he didn’t. He was a thief. He never changed, and then he got the punishment. He killed himself.
How can I forgive when it hurts so much, and can I forgive myself? (Ephesians 4:32)

He says people can’t forgive “because they let themselves be hurt,” and “when you get emotionally involved… truth goes out the door… and your emotions start running your life.” He says we need to forgive ourselves and give ourselves space to change, and cites Ephesians 4:32, “Be kind one to another.”
How can I forgive when it hurts so much, and can I forgive myself? (Ephesians 4:32)

And a lot of people kill themselves because they can’t handle their bad choices. They come to a place where they just kill themselves. Okay, you got that? We need to give people space. You need to give yourself space. You know, if you’re not a perfect Christian yet, start working on it and give yourself some space, but don’t take a lifetime. You know, if you want to attain something, you’ve got to get in and get involved with it. Amen. But we need to forgive ourself. A lot of people cannot forgive themselves, and we need to give ourselves space to change and grow into that divine nature. Now, how can I forgive when it hurts so much? One of the biggest sources I find in dealing with people why they can’t forgive is because they let themselves be hurt. They get hurt, they get emotionally affected, and when you get emotionally involved, bombed, truth goes out the door, the Scriptures go out the door, and your emotions start running your life. Now, that was a good statement. You see, and so we justify our accusations and our hatred and our verbal attacks and our physical attacks on the person that hurt us because we’re hurt. Hallelujah. So here’s Paul, our fourth candidate, and his approach to forgiveness. Our fourth baptism of the Holy Ghost [unclear]. Ephesians 4:32: “Be kind one to another.” Wow, even when they hurt me.
How can I forgive when it hurts so much, and can I forgive myself? (Ephesians 4:32)
Ephesians 4:32: And be kind to one another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another, even as God in Christ forgave you.
Is forgiving others a higher sign than tongues? (Ephesians 4:32, Colossians 3:13)

He says forgiveness “is much higher than tongues or no tongues, much higher than miracles or no miracles,” and that we are to forgive as “God in Christ forgave you,” not by our level but His. He says we need the Holy Ghost’s empowerment, and that Jesus died for us before we asked, so “why are you waiting for the person to change before you forgive them?”
Is forgiving others a higher sign than tongues? (Ephesians 4:32, Colossians 3:13)

Didn’t Jesus say turn the other cheek, go the extra mile? Didn’t He say if you only forgive those that forgive you and treat those that treat you right, you’re no better than the publicans, because that’s what they do, and God wants us to be above that? He empowers us to be above that. “Kind, tenderhearted,” compassion, in a [unclear] care about their condition. Yes, they hurt us, but we go beyond the hurt, and we want to help them because we care about their condition that brought them to hurt us. Wow, that was good. Are you guys getting this? And this is what the Holy Ghost does for you. This is much higher than tongues or no tongues, much higher than miracles or no miracles. This has an effect in your home, your daily life, and it’s very powerful: forgiving one another. And then he tells us what level of forgiveness we are to forgive one another, and that level is, “as God in Christ forgave you,” as Christ forgave you. I want you to forgive what? Not my level of forgiveness, His level of forgiveness. Now, I am glad Jesus forgave me, and I am glad He gave me space to correct my errors as a young Christian while I was growing. I’m glad of that, and I’m glad He revealed it to me, so I didn’t excommunicate myself from Christianity while I was growing and changing from fault to fault. But we’re to forgive on the standard and level that Christ forgave us. In other words, if you want Christ to forgive you of anything, then you’ve got to give that forgiveness to those that hurt you. Wow. Now, how many, right quick, would say that’s going to take some empowerment by the Holy Ghost? I look in the mirror, and this guy is not going to do that. “You smack me, I’m going to smack you back. But you attack me verbally, I’m going to put you up verbally back.” So we need what? The empowerment of the Holy Ghost to do this, and that is what He promised. He promised a baptism of power to be witnesses unto Him. Colossians 3:13: “Bearing with and forgiving one another.” Bearing with, putting up with. And you know, you’ve got to put up with some offenses, you’ve got to put up with some errors, you’ve got to put up with some mistakes in your marriage, and with the right attitude of being tenderhearted and compassionate. Give that person time. Yes. You say, “You know what, you did hurt me,” but you don’t carry the hurt. You forgive. And for them to find forgiveness, they’ve got to confess and admit it. For you to find forgiveness, you’ve got to confess your hurt. You don’t like this person because of what they did to you, but you forgive them, even if they don’t ask you to forgive them. You forgive them. Jesus died before we asked Him to forgive us, isn’t that right? True. Isn’t that right? So why are you waiting for the person to change before you forgive them? Christ forgave us while we were still, the Bible says, in Romans— Galatians, “dead in our sins,” dead in trespasses and sins. “While we were yet sinners, Christ died for us.” He forgave us, He did what was necessary to help us in our situation. Isn’t that good? Amen.
Is forgiving others a higher sign than tongues? (Ephesians 4:32, Colossians 3:13)

Matthew 5:46-47: For if you love those who love you, what reward have you? Do not even the tax collectors do the same? And if you greet your brethren only, what do you do more than others? Do not even the tax collectors do so? Ephesians 4:32: And be kind to one another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another, even as God in Christ forgave you. Acts 1:8: But you shall receive power when the Holy Spirit has come upon you; and you shall be witnesses to Me in Jerusalem, and in all Judea and Samaria, and to the end of the earth.” Colossians 3:13: bearing with one another, and forgiving one another, if anyone has a complaint against another; even as Christ forgave you, so you also must do. Romans 5:8: But God demonstrates His own love toward us, in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.
What does Matthew 6:12-15 say, and how does he say it answers “once saved, always saved”?

He says in the Lord’s Prayer Jesus says, “if you don’t forgive men their sins, your Father will not forgive your sins.” He says “when a believer stops forgiving, God won’t forgive him,” and calls this “a direct statement against ‘once saved, always saved.’”
What does Matthew 6:12-15 say, and how does he say it answers “once saved, always saved”?

And the baptism of the Holy Ghost does this. “If anyone has a complaint against another, even as Christ forgave you, so you also must forgive them.” Now, that is powerful, folks. Now, I tell you, if you want a sign of the baptism of the Holy Ghost, here’s a good one. Could that be an amen? Now, Matthew 6:12: “Forgive us our debts,” right in the Lord’s Prayer, “as we forgive our debtors.” Then He goes on to say in verse 15, “If you don’t forgive men their sins, your Father will not forgive your sins.” Now, that’s a powerful statement. We want God to forgive us, we say the Lord’s Prayer, but we don’t go down below and see what Christ said about that. If Dave Kincer doesn’t forgive people that hurt him, that do him wrong, then God is not going to forgive Dave Kincer of the things he’s doing wrong that hurt other people. And God, and here is your clarity on once saved always saved. One of the clarities: when a believer stops forgiving, God won’t forgive him. You see, you can’t just come up with statements: “When saved, I’ll be saved, hallelujah, nothing can pluck us out of the Father’s hand, hallelujah, hallelujah, hallelujah, I can live any way I want. Hallelujah.” No. Here is a direct statement against “once saved, always saved.” Do you see it? See, he once was forgiven, he once was saved, but if he don’t forgive, God won’t forgive him. Now he’s not saved. Hallelujah. Yeah, see, you need answers out there, and there’s other answers for this “once saved, always saved.” This is just another one.
What does Matthew 6:12-15 say, and how does he say it answers “once saved, always saved”?

Matthew 6:12-15: And forgive us our debts, As we forgive our debtors. And do not lead us into temptation, But deliver us from the evil one. For Yours is the kingdom and the power and the glory forever. Amen. “For if you forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you. But if you do not forgive men their trespasses, neither will your Father forgive your trespasses.
How many times should I forgive, and what is the parable of the unforgiving servant? (Matthew 18:21-35)

He says Jesus answered Peter’s “seven times” with “seven times seventy.” In the parable a king forgave a servant a huge debt, but the servant demanded a small one from another servant, so the king called him “wicked,” and he says paying all that is due “is eternal in the lake of fire.” He says “we should treat people like Christ has treated us.”
How many times should I forgive, and what is the parable of the unforgiving servant? (Matthew 18:21-35)

Okay, Matthew 18:21: “How often shall my brother sin against me?” Now, we showed you the seven times in a day here. Jesus said, of course this guy’s thinking, “You know, seven times. You know, how often should I forgive him? Till seven times?” So he repeats what Christ said before, and Christ, knowing his sneaky little heart, says, “No, seven times seventy.” Wow, that’s a lot of forgiveness. Amen. See, forgiveness keeps me in a right attitude. Forgiveness, by responding right, keeps me from a bad attitude. I don’t want to see that person hurt, I want them to change, so I respond different. Instead of attacking them back, I try to show them a way out of hurting people. Are you there? Now, we’re not talking about murderers, and, you know, come on. Now here we go, this is the real kicker. In Matthew 18, Jesus gives them a parable of the kingdom of heaven. He likens the kingdom of heaven unto a certain king which took account of his servants, and one owed him $10,000, and, uh, he called the servant in to pay his debt, and the servant pleaded with him and says, “You know, give me a little more time, give me some space, and I’ll pay it back.” And the Lord was so moved with compassion for his servant that he says, “I tell you what, I’ll just forgive the debt. There’s no guilt, no punishment, you don’t have to pay it back. It’s done. Go and live.” The servant went out and immediately finds someone that owes him $10. I’m converting that over to up-to-date money in case you, uh, are wondering what’s going on. So this guy owes him 10 bucks, and he, the one who was forgiven by the king, demanded that this guy pay him his 10 bucks, and the guy said, “I don’t have the money, give me some space and I’ll get you the money.” The guy said, “No way, I want my $10,” and he took him and had him arrested and put in jail and all that, and paid the price for his debt to him. And then through the grapevine word got back to the king that that guy you forgave held a guy accountable for 10 bucks when you forgave him of 10,000. So the king brought that servant back in. Are we servants of God? Yeah. I want you to understand who He’s talking to. He’s talking to you. He brought him back into the king, the king brought him back in and says, “Hey, I forgave you a horrible debt, a deep debt, and then you go out and you hold someone accountable for offending you on a little thing.” Doesn’t a lot of us get offended over something really little? Yeah. He says, “Now, you wicked servant.” Is this a good servant? No. He says, “You wicked servant, you didn’t forgive. I forgave you all that debt because you asked it of me. Should not you also have had compassion on your fellow servant as I had pity on you? Should not have you treated the other people like I treated you?” How many know that’s a good statement? We should treat people like Christ has treated us, not like people are treating us. Amen. “His lord was angry.” God got angry, Jesus got mad, and “delivered him to the tormentors till he should pay all that was due unto him.” Folks, paying all that’s due is eternal in the lake of fire. We don’t want that, so we need to what? Forgive. How many could use a little more forgiveness in your life? The rest of you, lying. You’re just flat-out lying. “So likewise,” now listen, He clarifies who He’s talking to, “so likewise shall my heavenly Father do also unto you,” the people He’s preaching to, “if you from your heart,” genuinely, with compassion and tenderheartedness, bearing up with one another, “if you from your heart do not all forgive, everyone his brother, their trespasses.” Wow.
How many times should I forgive, and what is the parable of the unforgiving servant? (Matthew 18:21-35)

Matthew 18:21-35: Then Peter came to Him and said, “Lord, how often shall my brother sin against me, and I forgive him? Up to seven times?” Jesus said to him, “I do not say to you, up to seven times, but up to seventy times seven. Therefore the kingdom of heaven is like a certain king who wanted to settle accounts with his servants. And when he had begun to settle accounts, one was brought to him who owed him ten thousand talents. But as he was not able to pay, his master commanded that he be sold, with his wife and children and all that he had, and that payment be made. The servant therefore fell down before him, saying, ‘Master, have patience with me, and I will pay you all.’ Then the master of that servant was moved with compassion, released him, and forgave him the debt. “But that servant went out and found one of his fellow servants who owed him a hundred denarii; and he laid hands on him and took him by the throat, saying, ‘Pay me what you owe!’ So his fellow servant fell down at his feet and begged him, saying, ‘Have patience with me, and I will pay you all.’ And he would not, but went and threw him into prison till he should pay the debt. So when his fellow servants saw what had been done, they were very grieved, and came and told their master all that had been done. Then his master, after he had called him, said to him, ‘You wicked servant! I forgave you all that debt because you begged me. Should you not also have had compassion on your fellow servant, just as I had pity on you?’ And his master was angry, and delivered him to the torturers until he should pay all that was due to him. “So My heavenly Father also will do to you if each of you, from his heart, does not forgive his brother his trespasses.”
How should we treat people we disagree with, and is tongues the only sign of the baptism of the Holy Ghost?

He says our responsibility is to “forgive them, give them space,” and share with them, and that he preached in Catholic and Baptist churches “with other truths.” He says tongues is not the only sign: “the real signs are the character, the divine nature of God,” and many people avoid the Holy Ghost because of big arguments.
How should we treat people we disagree with, and is tongues the only sign of the baptism of the Holy Ghost?

So, I don’t like the Catholics, and the holy water, and their idols and all that. What is my responsibility in this thing? Forgive them, give them space, and share with them. And how can I share with them if I have nothing to do with them? You see, I hate these Pentecostals that roll around on the floor and shake and quake and slaying out the p— and all these guys on TV. All okay, they are making some mistakes, but what is our responsibility? Give them space and address the issue, and how you going to do that if you won’t have anything to do with these Pentecostals and charismatics? So we had four witnesses in the Bible. I gave you my witness of the baptism of the Holy Ghost. Tongues was a small part of that baptism. That baptism of love, that baptism to respond right, that part of the Holy Ghost was the thing that really got my attention, the part that drove me to the Bible to learn it and not just depend on people from the pulpit teaching me. That part of the Holy Ghost to love people, to stay in unity, even with Catholics. I preached in Catholic churches, I preached in Baptist churches, I had no offenses even though I disagreed with them. And I wouldn’t go in there with my disagreements. I would go in there with other truths and get, let get them to know me. Are you with me? I have had a chance to witness to the number one guy of the American Baptist Association and the Southern Baptist Association in one meeting in California, because they saw in me something different than other Pentecostals and Spirit-filled people had, and that’s what they told me. “We’ve never met a Spirit person like you.” And my response was, “Well, you haven’t met any of them because you won’t have anything to do with them. I came to you, I got involved with you.” But I had the chance, from the Scriptures, they showed me their argument, and I had a chance, from the Scriptures, to show them their argument wasn’t Scriptural. Hallelujah. One of those Baptist leaders was in the Assembly of God church, sought for the baptism of the Holy Ghost, he told me, didn’t get to speak in tongues, so he just felt it was a bunch of nonsense, and he left and went into the fundamental church. And I told him that’s one of the mistakes Pentecostals and charismatics make. They say the tongues is the only sign of the baptism of the Holy Ghost, and it is not. The Bible doesn’t say it’s the only sign, and it’s not the only sign. And the real signs are the character, the divine nature of God. Can you honestly say amen to that? And all of us can have it. It’s poured out on all flesh, but you get it when you get it, and if you don’t have it, you’ve got to admit you don’t have it to get it. Now, how many would like the promise of God to have the baptism of the Holy Ghost that brings you into the divine nature? Let me see your hand. Yeah, you see, a lot of people are so scared of the Holy Ghost now because of big arguments, they won’t seek the very thing that can revolutionize their life, their marriage, their church.
How should we treat people we disagree with, and is tongues the only sign of the baptism of the Holy Ghost?

Does he use “baptism of the Holy Spirit” and “filled with the Holy Spirit” for the same thing?
He says yes: the baptism of the Holy Ghost “is the baptism of the Holy Spirit, which is being filled with the Holy Spirit. They’re all synonymous terms.”

He says no: he says it isn’t saying “if I drink and I don’t get intoxicated, I’m fine,” and that wine “will distort your judgment, alcohol will, and so you can’t use that to justify drinking at all.”
Did Jesus speak in tongues when He was filled with the Holy Ghost?
He says no: “He didn’t speak in tongues… He didn’t pass out in the water, He didn’t get slain in the Spirit.” He says Jesus “went immediately into the wilderness to be tested.”
What does he say the Bible says about alcohol?
He says John the Baptist “shall drink neither wine nor strong drink,” and that “the Bible does not approve of intoxication of any kind,” because “God isn’t for anything that destroys you.”
Does the Bible record Stephen or Paul speaking in tongues when they were filled?

He says for Stephen “there’s no record that he spoke in tongues when he got the Holy Ghost. There’s no record that he didn’t.” For Paul he says “there is no indication,” though “he speaks in tongues more than y’all” later.
What is forgiveness, according to his piece-of-paper illustration?

He says you throw the mistake away like a wadded-up piece of paper, take it to the dump “and you never get it back again. Forgiveness is forgiving and forgetting. Pardoning, you know, no condemnation, no guilt.”
Who does he say is our example?
He says “the Bible plainly says Jesus Christ is our example. We’re to model after Him and Him only,” and quotes Paul, “follow me as I follow Christ.”
Can a pastor, priest or evangelist free you from sin?
He says no: “the pope can’t free you from sin, the priest can’t free you, I can’t free you from sin, the evangelist can’t free you from sin. We are all voices trying to bring you to Christ.”
Does he say he may hate people he thinks are wrong?
He says no: “I have a right to confront wrong, but I don’t have a right to hate Catholics and look down on Catholics and not fellowship with Catholics.” He says, “I have a right to address wrong.”
He says yes: “these people say unconditional love, unconditional love… The Bible has a condition on things, and here the condition is, you forgive and God will forgive you.”
What does he mean by “perception hurt”?
He says some people weren’t really hurt by the other person: “that person that was hurt perceived they did or said something that the people didn’t really do or say.”
Why does he say some people cannot forgive?

He says “they let themselves be hurt. They get hurt, they get emotionally affected, and when you get emotionally involved… truth goes out the door, the Scriptures go out the door, and your emotions start running your life.”
Should you wait for the person to change before you forgive?

He says no: “you forgive them, even if they don’t ask you to forgive them… Jesus died before we asked Him to forgive us.” He says “why are you waiting for the person to change before you forgive them?”
What is the parable of the unforgiving servant?

He says a king forgave a servant a $10,000 debt, but that servant demanded $10 from another and had him jailed. The king called him “wicked” and, he says, “delivered him to the tormentors till he should pay all that was due.”
Is tongues the only sign of the baptism of the Holy Ghost?
He says no: “They say the tongues is the only sign… and it is not. The Bible doesn’t say it’s the only sign.” He says “the real signs are the character, the divine nature of God.”

items.d: In “Three Revelations Part 1,” Pastor David G. Kincer introduces the book of Revelation through its opening verse, saying it gives three revelations: the revelation of Jesus Christ, the revelation of the…
p: In “Three Revelations Part 1,” Pastor David G. Kincer introduces the book of Revelation through its opening verse, saying it gives three revelations: the revelation of Jesus Christ, the revelation of the righteous judgment of God, and the revelation of the church. He teaches that Revelation is written to all of God’s servants, uses Romans 2 and Revelation 20 to show judgment by works and the Book of Life, and begins the revelation of the church as the body of Christ from Romans 16 and Ephesians 3 and 5.
Why does he say we should listen to John, who wrote Revelation on Patmos?

He says John was banished to the isle of Patmos after being tarred and feathered for preaching the gospel, and that on the island, in that affliction, he received the book of Revelation. He says that when somebody pays a price like that, “we need to listen to them.”
Why does he say we should listen to John, who wrote Revelation on Patmos?

This John got this on the isle of Patmos. He was banished by the local authorities to the isle of Patmos after he had been tarred and feathered and somehow survived for preaching the gospel. I mean, if you really want to go out and preach the gospel, people aren’t going to like you. It is not like the church in America today where we flatter people. And this is what you’re going to find in the book of Revelations, these guys that really went out and preached the gospel, they were [unclear], they were in prison, they were beaten, I mean they were subject to abuse all the time. Today, not so, because we’re really not preaching the gospel. We’re preaching a very flattering message that doesn’t challenge anyone, doesn’t shake up anyone. Most, now not all the church, but the majority of the church, and the majority of the church is on TV and radio, because you want numbers and you want money, you have to water down the message. You don’t want to hurt anybody’s feelings. But John wasn’t like that. He preached the gospel, he was tarred and feathered, and they banished him, and on that island, in that kind of affliction, he got this book of Revelation. And so when somebody pays a price like that, we need to listen to them. Could that be an
What are the three revelations in the book of Revelation?

He says the book is the revelation of Jesus Christ, not of the beast or Satan, and that there are three revelations: of Jesus Christ, of the eternal judgment, and of the church. He says that if you read the Bible without looking for Jesus, “you’re going to miss the whole point of the Bible.”
What are the three revelations in the book of Revelation?

amen? Revelations 1:1, it starts out by saying “the revelation of Jesus Christ.” Not the beast, not the revelation of Satan, not the revelation of the [unclear] sitting on the seven mountains. Are you hearing me? It’s the revelation of who? Jesus Christ. This book is going to tell us about Jesus Christ. Revelation means to disclose, to reveal things, even things that have not been seen before. Okay, and so we’re going to have the revelation, the revealing, the disclosure of Jesus Christ. And we find that there’s three revelations in the New Testament. That’s the revelation of Jesus, the Lion, the Lamb, the Captain of the host, the Head of the church. I mean, He’s the big guy, He’s the chief honcho in the Bible, and when you read the Bible, if you’re not looking for Jesus, you’re going to miss the whole point of the Bible. Secondly, it’s the revelation of the judgment. The Bible tells us there’s a revelation of the eternal judgment, and you don’t hear this message much anymore, that you’re going to be held accountable for what you say and do, and God is going to sentence you by what you say and do. You don’t hear this much anymore. When I was a kid you heard it all the time. They scared the hell out of you. I mean, man, you wanted Jesus and you wanted to get to heaven. But then we got into the love thing, everybody’s okay. And then the revelation of the church. I meet very few American Christians that even understand the basic revelation of the church. They think it’s a building with people in it. And I’d submit to you today, you don’t know it.
What are the three revelations in the book of Revelation?
Revelation 1:1: The Revelation of Jesus Christ, which God gave Him to show His servants—things which must shortly take place. And He sent and signified it by His angel to His servant John,
Is the church just a building with people in it?

He says no: the Bible calls the church the body of Christ, each member with a particular function, and that it is also a flock, an army, and a house, a temple of God. He says that seeing what the church really is “should revolutionize” how you use your time and approach God.
Is the church just a building with people in it?

Because if you did, it would change your life. It would change the way you do things. When we get through with the book of Revelation and you see what the church really is, it should revolutionize the way you schedule your time and you approach your God. It will make all the difference in the world, because the church isn’t some building with people in it. The Bible refers to it as the body of Christ. You see all those heads? See, we are the body of Christ and each one a member in particular, with a particular function. We have a function. Your little finger has a function. The smallest in God’s church has a function, a purpose and an objective. We are a flock, we follow the Shepherd, we need His protection, but we’re also an army, and we’re also a house, a temple of God. But we will get into that later, and this is what the Bible speaks of, these three revelations.
What are the three points in Revelation 1:1, and how do we get understanding?

He says Revelation 1:1 gives the revelation of Jesus Christ from God, things shown to “his servants,” which is all believers and not only the seven churches in Asia, and things that must shortly come to pass. He says we must pray for understanding of the scriptures because the Spirit is the only one who can open them to us.
What are the three points in Revelation 1:1, and how do we get understanding?

Now Revelations 1:1 has three points in it. Number one, the revelation of Jesus Christ, as we talked about, which God gave to Him. Who gave this to Him? God. All right. It’s not like Muhammad, it’s not like Joseph Smith. Those are imitators, as we’ll show you a little later. And you got to be [unclear]. You got to know truth if you want to be free and you want others to be free. It’s the truth that sets you free. Free from what? Your traditions, your unbelief, your [unclear] doctrines, your doctrines of men. It sets you free from these things. Amen. And sin. Now number two, “to show unto His servants things.” Okay, He’s going to show us things, and it’s not just to the seven churches in Asia. To show unto His servants, all of us who accepted Christ. Christ is the King and we are His servants, and so He wants to show everybody, not just the seven churches of Asia. This is directed to everyone, isn’t that true? And He’s going to show us things. How many want your eyes open to the things He wants to show? Yeah. You got to pray. One of your main prayers is not only wisdom, but you need to pray that God gives you understanding of the scriptures, because the Spirit is the only one that can open the scriptures up to you. That’s what the Bible says, they are spiritually discerned. The Spirit has to do it. See, we can use our human intellect, but it is the Spirit that really bursts the truth in us.
What are the three points in Revelation 1:1, and how do we get understanding?

Revelation 1:1: The Revelation of Jesus Christ, which God gave Him to show His servants—things which must shortly take place. And He sent and signified it by His angel to His servant John, John 8:32: And you shall know the truth, and the truth shall make you free.” 1 Corinthians 2:14: But the natural man does not receive the things of the Spirit of God, for they are foolishness to him; nor can he know them, because they are spiritually discerned.
Do we need a special prophet or teacher to explain Revelation to us?

He says no, because it says it was written to God’s servants, all of us. He says we do need preachers and teachers, but “they’re not the ones to follow,” and our faith should be in Jesus Christ and His truth, not in any man or man’s teaching.
Do we need a special prophet or teacher to explain Revelation to us?

Amen. And number three, read this last one with me: “which must shortly come to pass.” Read it again: “which must shortly come to pass.” Now I submit to you, it’s 2,000 years. Shortly? It doesn’t sound very shortly, does it? Hallelujah. These words, Revelations 22, now we’re at the last chapter of the book, all right: “These words are faithful.” You can count on them. The words of Revelation, they are truth. They’re just like all the other books in the Bible. “The Lord God of the holy prophets sent His angel to show His servants.” There we are again, to show who? His servants, all of us. Do we need some special prophet opening the book of Revelation to us? No. Why? Because He wrote it for all of us. You see, only in America do we have this mentality, we need the gurus, we need Osteen, we need Joyce Meyer, we need somebody. Why? ’Cause that’s what they tell us, they preach we need them. But here it says this is to who? All of us. Is God partial? We just taught on it. Do you have every right to every inheritance just like anybody else? Absolutely. Do we need preachers and teachers? Yes, we do, but they’re not the ones to follow, and they’re not the ones to worship. They should be leading us to the One, and our faith should not be in any man or any man’s teaching. Our faith should be in the Jesus Christ and His truth.
Do we need a special prophet or teacher to explain Revelation to us?
Revelation 22:6: Then he said to me, “These words are faithful and true.” And the Lord God of the holy prophets sent His angel to show His servants the things which must shortly take place.
What does he say about “shortly come to pass” and end-time prophecy teachers?

He says the book plainly says these things must shortly come to pass, and that end-time prophets twist and stretch scriptures to make it fit our last days. He warns that what you believe determines your behavior, and says there are people making up their own doctrine today.
What does he say about “shortly come to pass” and end-time prophecy teachers?

Amen. The things which must what? Shortly come to pass. He emphasizes it again. And what do all these end-time prophets do with Revelation? They twist and stretch all kinds of scriptures to get it to fit into our last days. Am I right? I am right. And it says plainly, these things must what? Shortly come to pass. Wow, you youngins got that? He says you need to take heed. Jesus told him, take heed, beware of the doctrine of the scribes and the Pharisees. Why? What you believe is what will determine your behavior. And the Pharisees had made up their own doctrine, and the Sadducees had made up their own doctrine, and have, you know, there’s people today making up their own doctrine, and people will try to please a church group in their doctrines of faith rather than please Christ and His book of faith. Could that be true? Now you young people understand this now. This is good stuff. This is deep stuff. This is not for the weak-hearted.

Revelation 1:1: The Revelation of Jesus Christ, which God gave Him to show His servants—things which must shortly take place. And He sent and signified it by His angel to His servant John,
How does he say we should study the book of Revelation?

He uses an illustration of being shipwrecked on an island with only the book of Revelation, and says to use other true scriptures to confirm it. He compares it to a book about aerodynamics that mentions turbulence: the book is about how airplanes fly, and Revelation is about the revelation of Jesus Christ, not the other things it mentions.

This stuff is meat. It will get into your innards and work powerful in your life. So these three things: revelation of Jesus, He’s going to show His servants things, and it’s going to be brought about what? Shortly. Shortly. Okay, let’s look at the revelation of the righteous judgment of God in Romans chapter 2. Now we’re going to use the book of Revelations as the book. We’re going to pretend that we’re on an island, we got shipwrecked, and we’re on an island, and we were just a dumb sinner before that, and then this book comes floating in on shore, somehow it got in the ocean and it washed up on shore, and we got one book and it’s the book of Revelation. Now is the book about storms and turbulence, or is it still about aerodynamics? Aerodynamics. Okay, this book is about the revelation of Jesus Christ, and if He talks about other things, the book isn’t about those other things. It’s about what? The revelation of Jesus

Christ. And so the New Testament gives us three revelations: the revelation of Jesus Christ, the revelation of the judgment to come. deeds. You say, did Judas believe in Jesus? You’re looking at me like you’re afraid to answer. Absolutely, he did. Did Judas preach the gospel? Yes. Did Judas heal the sick? Yes. church. Just getting them here isn’t it. It’s getting the darkness broken off of their light. It’s getting the Jesus into them. items.ser: To Cover or Not to Cover · Part 1
tg: To Cover or Not to Cover
p: In “To Cover or Not to Cover Part 1,” Pastor David G. Kincer begins a study of praying and prophesying with the head covered or uncovered in 1 Corinthians 11. Before the topic itself, he stresses following Christ rather than other people or man-made traditions, then lays out the chain of command in 1 Corinthians 11:3. He then starts working through the verses about men and women praying and prophesying, and the series continues in Part 2.
Should Christians pray and prophesy with their head covered or uncovered?

He says Paul takes up this question in 1 Corinthians 11, and that our problem is we have problems with things “and we start making doctrine out of the problems.” He sets up the question with pictures of women of Bible times and of churches that say women must wear a veil to pray, and says Paul will address it today.
Should Christians pray and prophesy with their head covered or uncovered?

Now today he’s going to hit the topic of praying and prophesying with a head covering or uncovered. You know, do we pray and prophesy with our head covered or uncovered? Now some of you have a problem with that already. “What’s that idiot doing? That’s a woman thing.” That’s our problem: we have problems with things, and we start making doctrine out of the problems. And so he’s going to hit this issue. Now you’ll see on your screen, up in the upper left-hand corner, a woman of that day, a typical woman during Christ time, during the New Testament times, with a covering on her head, okay? On the lower right-hand corner you’re going to see a Jewish woman with a veil or covering on her head, and she’s got long hair and it covers all of her hair all the way down to the end. And then in the lower left-hand corner you’re going to see a couple of Christians in church praying with a veil over their head, because their church says women got to have a veil over your head to pray. Okay, now Paul’s going to hit this thing today. Don’t I look handsome up here with this scarf on me?
Who should Christians follow: Jesus or church leaders?

He says Paul begins by saying to follow him as he follows Christ, so we are not to follow other religious leaders, famous preachers or any church movement, but Jesus Christ. He says Jesus only taught and lived by the Word of God, always did the will of the Father, and that a preacher should preach the Scriptures, not their opinion or some church doctrine.
Who should Christians follow: Jesus or church leaders?

Okay, now Paul opens with this statement. He says, “Be you followers, imitators of me, even as I also am of Christ.” Now it’s important that he introduces this subject this way, because when he comes to the conclusion you’re going to need this introductory subject. Okay, he says be followers of me as I follow Christ. In other words, we almost follow who? Christ. And people who follow Christ. Yes. My covering is slipping. I need [unclear]. Now let’s don’t get carried away. In other words, we’re not to follow Muhammad, we’re not to follow Joseph Smith, we’re not to follow the Pope, we’re not to follow Billy Graham, we’re not to follow Oral Roberts or Joel Osteen or Rick Warren, or the emergent church or the seeker-friendly church or the Pentecostal church or the Baptist church or whatever. We are to follow who? Jesus Christ. And he’s hitting a very important issue before he gets into this subject. We get our eyes off Christ and we get our eyes on other things, and we have problems. Could that be an amen? And said, “I only do what I see Christ do. I only do what Jesus teach. You follow me as I follow Him, and if I don’t follow Jesus, don’t follow me,” is what he’s saying. Now Jesus did no sin. Wow, that sure beats all these other guys I listed. Jesus only taught and lived by the Word of God. He taught the Scriptures; He didn’t teach other books. Remember, there were books there. Homer was there, Greek and Roman mythology books were there, Aristotle was there, Socrates was there, the Jewish book of traditions was there. He never taught any of that. He taught what? The Scriptures. He said follow me as I follow Christ. How many, you know, a preacher should be preaching the Scriptures, not their opinion or some church doctrine. See, he’s setting this thing up for a real good answer. Jesus always followed and did the will of the Father, always. You see, Jesus went to the synagogue every Saturday. I’ll [unclear]. This is how these women do that. There we go. Now I won’t fall off. Aren’t I cute? See, Jesus did the will of the Father. He went to the synagogue. He worked till He was 30 years old and went into the ministry. He actually worked; He was a carpenter. He actually held a job, just like the Bible tells us to. Jesus laid down His life and He picked it up again and lived again. Jesus said, “No greater love hath any man than he lays down his life for his friend.” Jesus said, “You are my friends if you do what I ask you to do.”
Who should Christians follow: Jesus or church leaders?

1 Corinthians 11:1: Imitate me, just as I also imitate Christ. John 15:13-14: Greater love has no one than this, than to lay down one’s life for his friends. You are My friends if you do whatever I command you.
How did Jesus’ apostles live, and why does Paul praise the Corinthians?

He says there is no record of the apostles Jesus taught directly, except Judas, misusing church money, committing sexual immorality, idolatry, complaining or dividing, and that they kept serving God until they died. He says we need to follow people who follow Jesus, and that Paul honors the Corinthians for keeping his teachings even though they were “crude,” because when he corrected them, they changed.
How did Jesus’ apostles live, and why does Paul praise the Corinthians?

And we’re to lay down our life for our friend. Jesus, isn’t that right? See, follow Jesus. Forget these other people; follow Jesus. Jesus taught directly 14 apostles. He encountered them and sent them to teach His Word. And there is no record of any of these apostles that He directly taught, except Judas who was picked for that, there’s no record of these guys misusing church money, these guys committing sexual immorality, whether it was incest, homosexuality, adultery or fornication. No record; they didn’t do it. There’s no record of them using extortion because of the position in the church, getting people to do things for them and give them things. They kept preaching and serving God all the days of their life till their hearts stopped or they were killed. They martyred and died, isn’t that right? They never needed a sabbatical to get their head together. These guys were powerful. That’s the kind of people Jesus makes. How many, you know, we need to be following Jesus, and we need to be following people that are following Jesus. And so this is very important. Now Paul then goes in to honor them for changing wrong beliefs and wrong behavior when he taught them proper Bible tradition, Bible rules, Bible truths. And he says, “I praise you, brethren, that you remember me in all things and keep the ordinances,” the traditions, the customs, the rules, the teachings, “as I delivered them to you.” And as crude as this church was, with their division, their sexual immorality, their idolatry, their faith in men instead of the power of God, and not seeking the high prize of God, and the complaining when Paul would come and correct them and teach them, they would change, and he honored them for it. I mean, that’s a powerful thing. I mean, we should have that kind of heart. You know, we might have some errors, but goodness, when we hear truth, let’s change. See, he’s setting this up good for this interesting topic.

He quotes “Lord, You have covered my head in the day of battle” and says that covering points to having the Lord Jesus Christ and His authority covering us.

items.ser: To Cover or Not to Cover · Part 2
tg: To Cover or Not to Cover
p: In “To Cover or Not to Cover Part 2,” Pastor David G. Kincer finishes his study of 1 Corinthians 11, saying Paul answers male ego arguments with the truth that man and woman were both made in God’s image and are one in Christ. He argues that “power on her head because of the angels” means real authority, not a symbol, and that Paul’s phrase about nature and long hair is about origin and a woman’s hair being given to her as a covering. He ends with Paul’s final answer, that the churches of God have no such custom.
Were both men and women made in the image of God?

He says Genesis 1:26-28 shows both were made in the image of God and given dominion, and that Paul knows this but is “concentrating on these male egos.” God said “let us,” not “I will,” so the Godhead is plural, and “mankind” means the human race, not male. He adds that the woman was given the same blessing, “but Paul left that part out.”
Were both men and women made in the image of God?

Genesis 1:26, we got to make it clear that both were made in the image of God. See, Paul knows this, but he didn’t bring out the fact that the woman was made in the image of God also. See, Paul knows this, but he didn’t bring it out. Why? He is concentrating on these male egos that he is going to bury here in a couple of verses. “Let us make man in our image.” There’s the plural: “let us.” God didn’t say “I will,” He said “let us.” The Godhead is plural. Do you understand that? Jesus was back there at the beginning. “Let us make man,” mankind; it’s not man, male; it’s mankind. A lot of words for man in the Bible is mankind, the human race. It’s not male at all. “Let us make the human race in our” what? “Image.” There’s the plural again: “our” is plural. “After our likeness, and let them have dominion.” So God created man. Verse 27, “in His own image, male and female created He” what? “Them.” And both of them what? Were made in the image of God, the likeness of God, and had dominion; they had rulership. Yes. Jeez. Now more ego, self-important arguments: “for the man is not of the woman, but the woman of the man; neither was the man created for the woman, but the woman was created for the man.” Man, he’s really got him going. Genesis 1:28, “God blessed” what? Plural: man and woman. And God said to what? “Them,” plural, man and woman, Adam and Eve: “Be fruitful, multiply, replenish the earth, subdue it, and have dominion and authority over every living thing.” We got to understand that the woman was given the same blessing, but Paul left that part out. Why? He’s feeding these guys. They’re really feeling good right now. Yeah, man. “Get that babushka on your head. Woman, keep quiet in the church. Woman.”
Were both men and women made in the image of God?

Genesis 1:26-28: Then God said, “Let Us make man in Our image, according to Our likeness; let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, over the birds of the air, and over the cattle, over all the earth and over every creeping thing that creeps on the earth.” So God created man in His own image; in the image of God He created him; male and female He created them. Then God blessed them, and God said to them, “Be fruitful and multiply; fill the earth and subdue it; have dominion over the fish of the sea, over the birds of the air, and over every living thing that moves on the earth.” 1 Corinthians 11:8-9: For man is not from woman, but woman from man. Nor was man created for the woman, but woman for the man.
What does “power on her head because of the angels” mean in 1 Corinthians 11:10?

He says nowhere in the Bible does it say a woman has to have power over her head because of the angels, and that several translations say “power” is the sign of the husband’s authority, which he calls “a big mistake.” He says the word means real supernatural power, as in Matthew 28:18 and Luke 10:19, and that angels are spirit beings who do not need a covering, while Satan acts like an angel of light.
What does “power on her head because of the angels” mean in 1 Corinthians 11:10?

Now verse 10, “For this cause ought the woman to have power on her head because of the angels.” Now, folks, nowhere in the Bible does it say a woman’s got to have power over her head because of the angels, and you got to watch your translations here. Here’s a good example: the New King James, the NIV, New International Version, the Living Bible, the Amplified Bible, the American Standard Bible all say “power” is the sign of the husband’s authority, and that’s a big mistake. If you’re going to deal with angels, you don’t want a sign, you don’t want a symbol, you want power. Are you there? And see, we read our Bible and we just accept; we don’t dig. King James has it right, the Darby Bible has it right. The word “power” there is the same word that the Bible uses all through, showing that there’s supernatural power, there is authority. Okay, in Matthew 9:6, “the Son of Man has power on earth to forgive sins.” Now do you want Him to have a symbol of that, or you want Him to have the power? The power. All right, Matthew 10:1, Jesus gave His twelve disciples power over unclean spirits, and to heal all manner of sicknesses, and to preach. Did He give them a symbol of power? You know, here’s a dove, here, go preach, you; a symbol of a dove, or symbol of a fish, or whatever we symbolize? No, He gave them power. He gave authority. Matthew 28:18, “All power is given unto Me in heaven and earth.” Does He have a symbol of power? Does He have power? Is He the authority over all the earth? You see, He is. And listen to this, Luke 10:19, “I give you power to tread upon serpents and scorpions,” talking to us, “and over all the power of the enemy, and nothing shall by any means hurt you.” Now do you want a symbol of power or do you want the power? Yeah. The Devil don’t care if you got a symbol. He doesn’t care if you wear a cross; it doesn’t bother him a bit. What he cares is who the strong man of your house is. Jesus Christ is living in you, and he can’t do anything without Jesus’s permission. That’s power. And so he’s really got these guys right where he wants them, right? Now, angels. What angels? We know there are angels of God, messengers that minister to us, isn’t that right? Hebrews 1, yes. Okay, that, you know, if the angel comes to a woman to minister to her and she doesn’t have a babushka on her head, “Yeah, oh, I can’t come. You know, oh, I can’t talk to you, you don’t have a covering.” I mean, what kind of wimpy angel is he? See, when the angel came to Rebecca and showed her about the two boys that she had, and didn’t reveal it to Isaac, it doesn’t say anything about, “Well, she’s got a covering on her head, so I can talk to her,” or “If she doesn’t have a covering, I can’t talk to her.” Come on. Angels could care the least; they’re spirit beings. Are you with me? Okay, but Satan is as an angel of light. Whoa, that changes everything, doesn’t it? He acts like an angel of light, and he’s not.
What does “power on her head because of the angels” mean in 1 Corinthians 11:10?

1 Corinthians 11:10: For this reason the woman ought to have a symbol of authority on her head, because of the angels. Matthew 9:6: But that you may know that the Son of Man has power on earth to forgive sins”—then He said to the paralytic, “Arise, take up your bed, and go to your house.” Matthew 10:1: And when He had called His twelve disciples to Him, He gave them power over unclean spirits, to cast them out, and to heal all kinds of sickness and all kinds of disease. Matthew 28:18: And Jesus came and spoke to them, saying, “All authority has been given to Me in heaven and on earth. Luke 10:19: Behold, I give you the authority to trample on serpents and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy, and nothing shall by any means hurt you. Hebrews 1:14: Are they not all ministering spirits sent forth to minister for those who will inherit salvation? 2 Corinthians 11:14: And no wonder! For Satan himself transforms himself into an angel of light.
Do husbands and pastors need real authority or a symbol of authority?

He says a husband needs real authority and power, not a symbol of it, and that real leadership is not pushing and kicking people around: like a cord, if you lead, it follows. He says husbands should follow Christ and their wife will have no problem following, and a pastor should lead the church and not “beat them up every Sunday.”
Do husbands and pastors need real authority or a symbol of authority?

Does she need authority or a symbol of authority when Satan comes to tempt and seduce and test her? She needs authority, and she needs a husband with authority. She don’t need no husband with a symbol of authority. “I’m a delegated authority; I’m a big deal, bud.” We need some action in this home. Amen. That husband needs authority; he needs power. Okay, I want to get this cord over there. I can push, kick, push, and nothing is happening. And this is what a lot of people think leadership is: just beat people up, push them, kick them around, get moving. But if I just lead this cord, it follows me. No effort, no nothing. I get it where it belongs, we both get there, and the key, husbands, is to be a leader. Do what Paul said: follow Christ, and your wife will have no problem following you. You try to push your ways on her and force your ways on her, and especially when they’re your traditions, she’s got no choice but to follow Christ. Now that was good. Amen. Same with a pastor of a church. If you want your church to get to the high mark of the calling of God, lead them into it. Don’t beat them up every Sunday; lead them there. That way they can reject you for leading, but they can’t reject you for bullying and pushing and being lord over you. That’s a good place for an amen. I told you this Paul’s good.
How do we stand against Satan and his angels, with a symbol or real authority?

He says another word for angels is messenger, and that when demons come around you need the real authority of Christ, not a symbol, with both husband and wife under the power of Christ. He says if people reject you they are rejecting the one who sent you, and that the bigger problem than demons is people who follow Satan with their own traditions and doctrines, which you need authority to withstand.
How do we stand against Satan and his angels, with a symbol or real authority?

Now Satan has angels, Satan and his angels. Another word for angels is messenger. Okay, when these little demons come around trying to mess with you and all that, do you need a symbol of authority or do you need real authority? You need the real thing. Husband, we need to get with it in the home. We need to get under that power of Christ, and a woman needs to be under the power of Christ, and as a team nothing’s going to mess with that home. Hallelujah. And we both lead these kids in the ways that are right. Now John the Baptist was called a messenger. John’s disciples were called messengers. Jesus sent His disciples to a Samaritan village to announce He was coming there, and it says they were messengers, and when they got there and said, “Jesus has come,” they said, “We don’t want Him,” and so they rejected the messengers because they rejected the One who sent the messengers. And if people reject you, it’s not you they’re rejecting; they’re rejecting the One that sent you with the message. Now Satan has children, the children of the wicked one, and Matthew 13, the parable of the sower. So demons aren’t really your big problem once you get Christ; it’s these people that follow Satan, and they come up with their own traditions, their own doctrines, their own way of doing things, and you need authority to withstand them. You need authority to reject their message. Ain’t that right? And a scarf isn’t going to do nothing. You know, I got a scarf on me, man, Hitler ain’t going to bother me, I got a scarf.
How do we stand against Satan and his angels, with a symbol or real authority?

Luke 9:52-53: and sent messengers before His face. And as they went, they entered a village of the Samaritans, to prepare for Him. But they did not receive Him, because His face was set for the journey to Jerusalem. Matthew 13:38: The field is the world, the good seeds are the sons of the kingdom, but the tares are the sons of the wicked one.
What does “neither is the man without the woman” mean in 1 Corinthians 11:11-12?

He says Paul concludes his ego arguments by showing they prove nothing: in the Lord neither is the man without the woman nor the woman without the man, and all things come from God. He says that “when we come to Christ, this nonsense is gone,” and that men did not get here unless a woman brought them into the world, so get your ego back “down to earth.”
What does “neither is the man without the woman” mean in 1 Corinthians 11:11-12?

Now Paul concludes these ego arguments. He’s going to conclude that these things prove nothing. I told you he set them up to pop their balloon, and he’s going to prove it by pointing to them that all things come forth from God. “Nevertheless,” but however, “neither is the man without the woman, and the woman without the man, in the Lord.” Say “in the Lord.” In the Lord. See, when we come to Christ, this nonsense is gone. “For as the woman is of the man, even so is the man also by the woman.” Men, you didn’t get here unless some woman brought you into this world, so let’s just get your ego back down to earth. Ain’t that right? Ain’t Paul good? Yeah. All of a sudden, bam, man, they went from up here to right below the rug real quick.
What does “neither is the man without the woman” mean in 1 Corinthians 11:11-12?

1 Corinthians 11:11-12: Nevertheless, neither is man independent of woman, nor woman independent of man, in the Lord. For as woman came from man, even so man also comes through woman; but all things are from God.
What does it mean to be baptized into Christ and “put on Christ”?

He says everything comes from God, and that in water baptism the sinful nature is put to death and the new creature comes out of the water. It is “not a symbol, an outward sign of an inward work,” he says, but an inward work that God does, as we identify with the death, burial and resurrection of Christ.
What does it mean to be baptized into Christ and “put on Christ”?

“But all things are of,” come forth from who? God. Everything comes from God: the prayer, the prophecy, the traditions, the customs, the rules, the laws, the image, the likeness, the glory, the dominion, the authority, all come from who? God. Now I know you guys knew all this stuff. I’m just boring you with warmed-over meals here, but look here, it’s backed up also in the Scriptures. Galatians 3:27, “As many of you have been baptized into Christ have” what? “Put on Christ.” In water baptism you kill the sinful nature. Water baptism is not a symbol, an outward sign of an inward work; it is an inward work God does. Things in water baptism that you need to know: the old nature of man, of sin, is put to death, and the new creature, the man of righteousness, Christ, we put on Him, comes out of that water. Amen. Water baptism is important. We identify with the death, burial and resurrection of Christ.
What does it mean to be baptized into Christ and “put on Christ”?
Galatians 3:27: For as many of you as were baptized into Christ have put on Christ.
Are men and women equal in Christ?

He says that in Christ there is neither Jew nor Greek, slave nor free, “male nor female,” and that God does not see those differences. He says we are all one in Christ Jesus, heirs of the promise, and that Acts 2 says sons and daughters, male and female, will prophesy.
Are men and women equal in Christ?

“There is neither Jew nor Greek.” Greek is a non-Jew, a heathen, unbeliever. “There is no bond or free”: slave. They had slaves there in Corinth, and masters over them. He says you in God, He don’t look at a slave when they come in; He don’t look at a Gentile, a non-Jew. You know, an African comes in or an Asian comes in, God don’t see that, because in Christ these things just don’t happen. “Neither is there” what? “Male nor female.” Wow, he’s plain English there. Amen. “For you are all” what? “One in Christ Jesus. And if you be Christ’s, you’re Abraham’s seed and heirs according to the promise.” Heirs of the image, heirs of the likeness, heirs of prophecy. It says in Acts 2 that “upon your sons and daughters I will pour out My Spirit,” and the son and the daughter, the male and the female, shall what? Prophesy. That’s why that utterance was good today. We should come to the house of God with something to give, not just get. See, you’re contributors. We are heirs. We have authority, we are under authority, we inherited it all, and together we can do great things in the earth. Amen.
Are men and women equal in Christ?

Galatians 3:28-29: There is neither Jew nor Greek, there is neither slave nor free, there is neither male nor female; for you are all one in Christ Jesus. And if you are Christ’s, then you are Abraham’s seed, and heirs according to the promise. Acts 2:17-18: ‘And it shall come to pass in the last days, says God, That I will pour out of My Spirit on all flesh; Your sons and your daughters shall prophesy, Your young men shall see visions, Your old men shall dream dreams. And on My menservants and on My maidservants I will pour out My Spirit in those days; And they shall prophesy.
Can women be leaders and pastors in the church? What about Deborah?

He says women have been mistreated by people twisting Scriptures to say they cannot speak in church, have a leadership position or be a pastor, and says God is “no respecter of persons.” He says a prophet is higher than a pastor, and points to Deborah as a real leader whom the men followed, with Barak saying he would not go unless she went.
Can women be leaders and pastors in the church? What about Deborah?

Now Acts 10:34 said God is “no respecter of persons.” And this message is getting long, but I got to get this out. Women have experienced mistreatment from people taking Scriptures and twisting them for a long time and misinterpreting them. Long hair, you know, you can’t cut your hair, you got to have long hair; you can’t have styled hair; you can’t have jewelry; you can’t wear pants because men wear pants; you can’t speak in church services; you can’t have a leadership position; you can’t be a pastor. And look, a prophet is higher than a pastor, I don’t know if you know that, and she can prophesy. See, the reason men like that is they don’t want a woman to tell them what to do. Well, don’t that show you you got a heart problem? If the woman is a real leader, Deborah was a real leader, the men did what she said. When Barak was told to go out and defeat the army, he said, “I ain’t going anywhere unless you go, lady.” So here’s Deborah right on the front lines. Man, go get them, boys. Yeah, yeah, whip them, man, beat these guys down. She was on the front lines of that battle. Are you there? Hallelujah. And yes, it’s used a lot less, but it’s still used, and let me tell you, if God depended on men to get everything done in the kingdom, we wouldn’t even be where we’re at today, because men are just big talkers and not doers. That’s the truth. They like to sit there. “Oh yeah, hallelujah, let’s go witnessing.” “No, I’m going to watch football.” You know, “Let’s learn an instrument and let’s prophesy unto the Lord.” “No, no, I’m going to learn how to eat pretzels while I’m watching football.” But boy, when you ask the man anything, he knows it all. Hallelujah. Aren’t you glad you came to church today? They don’t read the Bible, they don’t pray, they don’t learn anything, they can’t even pay attention in Bible studies, you just ask them anything and they know it all.
Can women be leaders and pastors in the church? What about Deborah?

Acts 10:34: Then Peter opened his mouth and said: “In truth I perceive that God shows no partiality. Judges 4:8: And Barak said to her, “If you will go with me, then I will go; but if you will not go with me, I will not go!”
Have women been ministers and leaders throughout church history?

He says history is filled with women ministers: the Methodist movement, the Quakers and the Baptists had women leaders until about the turn of the twentieth century, when someone twisted Paul’s Scriptures. He says the Pentecostals and the Salvation Army kept women in leadership, and describes how limited women’s rights were in the early part of the nation.
Have women been ministers and leaders throughout church history?

Now women in our nation, early part of our nation, could not own property. If they had kids when they divorced, they didn’t get the kids. It was unheard of; you couldn’t do it. You’re a woman, you don’t know how to raise kids. They couldn’t hold political office, they couldn’t vote, they couldn’t be a leader in the workforce, they couldn’t be a leader anywhere. They couldn’t be educated above eighth grade, because they’re just there to take care of the home. And that’s, I mean, that’s true in our nation. Yeah, and yet history is filled with women ministers. John Wesley’s movement, the Methodist movement, had many women preachers and leaders. The Quakers and the Baptists had women leaders till the turn of the twentieth century, when somebody came in, twisted Paul’s Scriptures, and said women got to shut up, and the Baptists and the Quakers accepted it. But the Pentecostals came along at that time, and the Salvation Army, and the Pentecostals had a black leader at Azusa; blacks could not rule over whites back then, do you know that? But when God’s into something, there is neither Jew nor Gentile, Pentecost or Protestant or whatever, black or white; they were just touching God, and everybody wanted God, and women helped him lead the church on Azusa Street.
Why is the woman called “the glory of the man”?

He says “the woman is the glory and the splendor of the man,” the brightness of the man, and that we like our women with their hair fixed up. He goes back to Adam, who named all the animals and could not find a helpmate, and says that when God made the woman from the rib and brought her to Adam, Adam lit up.
Why is the woman called “the glory of the man”?

And in the Pentecostal churches women had a part, most of them anyway. The holiness movement came along. The head of the Salvation, Booth, he got convinced that women should not be preachers. The head of the Salvation Army started the Salvation Army, and then he met this woman called Catherine. And man, you know, remember back there, the woman is the glory and the splendor of the man, the brightness of the man, and we like our women with hair and fixed-up hair. Huh. Yeah. Now you go back to Adam and Eve. Adam, the Bible says, he named all the animals, and yet he couldn’t find a helpmate for him. We’re going to talk about the glory and the splendor of the man. And then God took a rib out, made a woman, woke Adam up, and brought the woman to Adam. Naked. I mean, wow. Can you just see, man, he lit up. I mean, those lions and tigers did nothing, the fishing did nothing. Man, when this, what? And she’s new, she’s naked. Then God brought her. [unclear] And this is where Adam got the first idea of a fig leaf. Man.
Why is the woman called “the glory of the man”?

Genesis 2:19-22: Out of the ground the LORD God formed every beast of the field and every bird of the air, and brought them to Adam to see what he would call them. And whatever Adam called each living creature, that was its name. So Adam gave names to all cattle, to the birds of the air, and to every beast of the field. But for Adam there was not found a helper comparable to him. And the LORD God caused a deep sleep to fall on Adam, and he slept; and He took one of his ribs, and closed up the flesh in its place. Then the rib which the LORD God had taken from man He made into a woman, and He brought her to the man.
Did the Salvation Army’s Booth change his mind about women preachers?

He says Booth had been convinced that women should not be preachers, then married Catherine, a woman preacher who kept on preaching, and when he went to hear her he came back converted. He says the proof was there because people got saved and the Word worked: “what matters is God moved and He used the woman.”
Did the Salvation Army’s Booth change his mind about women preachers?

Yeah, man, he had things in him he didn’t know was there yet. And then God’s given them this big long sermon like I’m giving you today: “Replenish the earth, you know, subdue it, have dominion, I’m making you my likeness in your image, I want you to replenish the earth.” And man, you can just see Adam: “I wish he’d hurry up and shut up. I’ll get [unclear] busy with replenishing this here if he leaves.” And she’s over there [unclear] this guy’s turned on, man, and she’s over there, takes a flower and puts it in her hair. Man, he’s all worked up, and she’s worked up because he’s worked up. Now she’s saying, “When’s this guy going to get done telling us all this? We got to get busy fulfilling replenish and fill the earth.” So when Booth married, guess who he married? Catherine. And guess what? She was a woman preacher. He don’t believe in women preachers. They got a big clash at the beginning, and these two get married. Did she stop preaching because her husband didn’t believe in women preachers anymore? No way. She just kept on doing what she was doing before they got married. And so one day Booth said, “I’m going to go down, check this thing out,” so he goes down to listen to his wife preach, and he came back converted. You see, the evidence was there, the proof was there. People got saved, people got touched, the Word worked. It didn’t matter if it was a woman or what; what matters is God moved and He used the woman. So the proof is there. And so Booth threw his women [unclear] preach doctrine right out the door with one visit, and it was his own wife. See, you can’t argue with the evidence, and if they haven’t got anything to say, then shut up. “We can’t have women speaking,” because women want to speak, they got to have something to say, ain’t that right? “I’m a woman, I’m tired of being beat down all these years, I want to preach.” “You ain’t got anything to say.” “I know, but I’m a woman, I got to make up for all these years of getting persecuted.” Yeah, now you’re going to persecute us, we got to sit there and listen to you say nothing. Anyway, Lutheran, Calvin came up with this “women can’t preach” stuff, and a lot of people fell for it.
Did the Salvation Army’s Booth change his mind about women preachers?

Genesis 1:28: Then God blessed them, and God said to them, “Be fruitful and multiply; fill the earth and subdue it; have dominion over the fish of the sea, over the birds of the air, and over every living thing that moves on the earth.”
What does “nature itself teach you” about long hair mean in 1 Corinthians 11:14?

He says Paul is always using the word “judge” and telling us to make judgments, and here asks whether it is proper for a woman to pray uncovered. When he tried “nature” as the animal kingdom, the lion did not work, so he says the word means origin, the birthing: men and women are born with certain things about them, and the long hair in the verse is a decorated lock or ornament, not just length.
What does “nature itself teach you” about long hair mean in 1 Corinthians 11:14?

Now Paul gives the answer to the question. Okay, judging yourselves: is it proper that a woman, a wife, pray unto God covered or uncovered? Okay, now here it is again. Paul’s always using this word “judge,” and yet out there in the world they’re saying, “Judge not, let [unclear] be not [unclear].” They take one Scripture of the Bible they don’t even believe in, yet they take the one Scripture when we try to tell them, “You got to change your way,” and, you know, “You judge not, lest you be [unclear], man. Don’t be judging anybody.” And Paul’s always telling us to make judgments, isn’t he? And he’s telling you now, you judge, you make a decision: is it proper that a woman pray and prophesy uncovered, unveiled? “Doesn’t nature itself teach you if a man have long hair it’s a shame to him?” Now when I was a young Christian, you know, I read the books and all that, and the first thing I read about this verse is nature teaches you, the animal kingdom teaches you. And I thought, “Wow, yeah, that’s great, men can’t have long hair because of the animal kingdom.” And the first animal I went to was the lion. And the lioness had no hair, and the lion had all kinds of hair, long hair. I go, “That didn’t work.” I didn’t go any further; I just, it didn’t work. But when I began to look at this word, it doesn’t mean that kind of nature, it means origin, the birthing. You see, us men are birthed with certain things about us, and the women are birthed with certain things about them, and this long hair does not mean long hair as just long hair. All right, he repeats it, and it’s only used two times in the Bible, this word “long hair” here, two times. But if the woman have long hair, you see, it is a glory, a splendor to her. Now here’s the difference: the long hair there is a tassel, a lock, a decorated lock, an ornamental. Women do things with their hair that us men don’t have it in us to do. Are you there?
What does “nature itself teach you” about long hair mean in 1 Corinthians 11:14?

1 Corinthians 11:13-14: Judge among yourselves. Is it proper for a woman to pray to God with her head uncovered? Does not even nature itself teach you that if a man has long hair, it is a dishonor to him? Matthew 7:1: “Judge not, that you be not judged. 1 Corinthians 11:15: But if a woman has long hair, it is a glory to her; for her hair is given to her for a covering.
Is a woman’s hair her covering?

He says hair is given to her for a covering, so “she don’t need a babushka,” a scarf or a veil. He says it is her splendor and her brightness, and it is about what women do with their hair and why they do it, not its length, and he says Paul gave the Corinthians a bunch of nonsense to bring the truth to them.
Is a woman’s hair her covering?

I mean, when I married Rebecca, she was a gorgeous woman, and she had this hairstyle. Man, I tell you, if she’d have been baldheaded, I’d have went right on by. Why? Because he’s showing us it’s, we’re born, women were born to make their hair attractive and, you know, to decorate it and do things with it. Men weren’t born for that, and it’s got nothing to do with the length; it’s got to do with why they do it. See, no man goes around doing things to their hair. It’s in their right mind that women do, and if they did, they still wouldn’t look good, and I’ll show you that in a minute. And here he answers their question: “her hair is given to her for a” what? “Covering.” She don’t need a babushka, she doesn’t need a scarf, she doesn’t need a veil. Her hair was given to her by God. That’s her splendor, that’s her brightness, and men like her for it. Hallelujah. Now when the hippies were here, they used this to beat the hippies up, and you can’t do that. It’s got to do with what women do with their hair and the look they have. I mean, when Rebecca walked down the street, man, she turned all heads with that hair and that face of hers, and every, wow. Wow. You shave her head and they would know about it, they’d be looking all right. Amen. Now isn’t Paul good? I mean, he gave them a bunch of nonsense to bring the truth to them, and they fell for it, just like you have been falling for it all these years reading these Scriptures. Here is a Jewish couple back in Christ’s day; they both have a covering on their head. All right, here is a Greek couple. Okay, you see the little decoration she’s got, these little curly things hanging down, and this braid going across the front and all that. That’s what women do. They think up these ways to, yeah, get their men all excited, in love with it, and we love it. Okay, here’s an Asian couple. Now check that guy. I mean, what’s that thing on his head? Good Lord. But look at his wife, man, she’s got long hair, and it’s all, I mean, oh wow. Here’s the Egyptians during that time. Look at her hair, it’s real long. His hair is long. See, her hair is long, and it’s got little tassels, little decorations at the end. And here’s some more long hair, and a guy has longer long hair too, but not as long, and, you know, not styled. Are you there? And here’s the real agents of civilization. We got Steven Tyler there. He’s got long hair and puts a little gray streak in it or something like that, and none of us men would ever want to kiss him. But look at that lady by him. They both have long hair, but wow, [unclear]. See, that’s what Paul’s talking about. The woman’s hair was given to her by God, not only to excite that man, but that’s what God did to women, made them special in that area, and he says their hair is their covering, they don’t need anything. And then he’s really going to lay them out. You ready for this? I mean, he’s going to lay them out good. He’s got them that their natural hair is their covering.
Is a woman’s hair her covering?
1 Corinthians 11:15: But if a woman has long hair, it is a glory to her; for her hair is given to her for a covering.
Is the blood of Jesus our covering?

He says Hebrews 10:19 says nothing about a covering for the head: “the blood of Jesus is our covering.” We go in by His blood and by the body that took the pain, and it does not matter if we have long hair, short hair, or coats and ties, but whether we accept the blood, His sacrifice and His authority.
Is the blood of Jesus our covering?

Hebrews 10:19. Before he lays them out, I want to confirm what Paul said. “Therefore, brethren, have boldness to enter the Holiest” where God is, by the what? Blood. Anything about a covering? No. The blood of Jesus is our covering.
