Okay, “by a new and living way which He has consecrated,” He has set apart for us, “through the veil, that is, His flesh.” See, He took the beating, He took the nails in His hand, He took the spear in His side, He took the crown of thorns. He is our covering. We go in by His blood, we go in by that body that took the pain and all that; we go in that way. “Let us draw near, and having a High Priest over the house of God.” He is the High Priest, He is the Shepherd. Amen, He is the authority. “Let us draw near with a true heart in full assurance of faith,” having our, number one, going back to number one, “hearts sprinkled”, they sprinkled things in the Old Testament with the blood, “from an evil conscience, and our bodies washed with pure water.” That’s water baptism and the washing of the water of the Word. And we can go in. It doesn’t matter if we got long hair, short hair, coats and ties; that ain’t got anything to do with it. It’s do we accept the blood, do we accept His sacrifice of His body, do we accept His authority, and we can go in, and we can touch God, and we can be used of God.
Is the blood of Jesus our covering?

Hebrews 10:19-22: Therefore, brethren, having boldness to enter the Holiest by the blood of Jesus, by a new and living way which He consecrated for us, through the veil, that is, His flesh, and having a High Priest over the house of God, let us draw near with a true heart in full assurance of faith, having our hearts sprinkled from an evil conscience and our bodies washed with pure water.
Does the Bible command women to wear a head covering (1 Corinthians 11:16)?

He calls the covering question “a silly issue,” and says Paul’s final answer is that we have “no such custom,” and neither do the churches of God, including Corinth, Jerusalem and Antioch. He ends: “There is no commandment that women have to do anything but pray and prophesy.”
Does the Bible command women to wear a head covering (1 Corinthians 11:16)?

And this covering thing was a silly issue. And then here’s his final answer, after saying the woman’s hair is her covering. This is his final answer. He says, “If any of you seem to be contentious,” quarrel, “some question in this, we have” what? “No such custom,” tradition, rule, “neither the churches of God,” not only the Corinthian church but the church in Jerusalem, the church at Antioch, and all the other churches. There is no commandment that women have to do anything but pray and prophesy.
Does the Bible command women to wear a head covering (1 Corinthians 11:16)?
1 Corinthians 11:16: But if anyone seems to be contentious, we have no such custom, nor do the churches of God.
Why does he say “let us make man” shows the Godhead is plural?
He says God did not say “I will,” He said “let us,” so the Godhead is plural, and Jesus was there at the beginning. He adds that “mankind” is the human race, not male.
What does he say about “the woman was created for the man”?
He calls these “ego, self-important arguments” that Paul is using to feed the men, and says Paul left out that the woman was given the same blessing and dominion.
Which Bible translations does he say get “power on her head” wrong?

He says the New King James, the NIV, the Living Bible, the Amplified Bible and the American Standard Bible all say power is the sign of the husband’s authority, and that King James and the Darby Bible have it right.
Did Jesus give His disciples a symbol of power or real power?
He says Jesus gave His twelve disciples power over unclean spirits, to heal and to preach, not a symbol like a dove or a fish. “No, He gave them power.”
Does the Devil care if you wear a cross?
He says the Devil doesn’t care if you wear a cross; “what he cares is who the strong man of your house is,” and whether Jesus Christ is living in you.
Would an angel refuse to speak to a woman without a covering?
He says no: “what kind of wimpy angel is he?” When the angel came to Rebecca, he says, the Bible says nothing about her having a covering, and angels are spirit beings who “could care the least.”
What does he say is a bigger problem than demons?

He says once you have Christ, demons “aren’t really your big problem”; it is people who follow Satan and come up with their own traditions, doctrines and way of doing things. You need authority to withstand them and reject their message.
What happens to these arguments when we come to Christ?
He says “when we come to Christ, this nonsense is gone,” because in the Lord neither is the man without the woman nor the woman without the man.
Where does he say everything comes from?
From God: the prayer, the prophecy, the traditions, the customs, the rules, the laws, the image, the likeness, the glory, the dominion and the authority all come from God.
Who was Deborah, and why does he mention her?
He says Deborah was a real leader whom the men followed; when Barak was told to go out and defeat the army, he said he would not go unless she went, and she was “on the front lines of that battle.”
What does he say about men and the work of the kingdom?

He says if God depended on men to get everything done in the kingdom, “we wouldn’t even be where we’re at today,” because men are big talkers and not doers, and he jokes about men who would rather watch football than go witnessing.
What does he say about women in the early part of the nation?

He says they could not own property, did not get the kids when they divorced, could not hold political office or vote, and could not be educated above eighth grade, and that this twisting of Paul’s Scriptures carried into the church.
Why does he say Paul keeps using the word “judge”?

He says Paul is always telling us to make judgments, and yet people in the world say “judge not,” taking one Scripture of the Bible they don’t even believe in when we try to tell them they have to change.
Is a woman’s hair covering about how long it is?
He says no: “it’s got nothing to do with the length; it’s got to do with why they do it.” Women are born to make their hair attractive and decorate it, which men were not.
Did people use this passage against long-haired men?
He says that when the hippies were around, people used this passage to beat them up, “and you can’t do that,” because it is about what women do with their hair and the look they have.

items.d: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer teaches that it is as important to stay saved as to get saved, and gives the Bible’s procedure for renewed lives to stay renewed. Using 1 Corinthians 6, Hebrews 6:12 and…
p: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer teaches that it is as important to stay saved as to get saved, and gives the Bible’s procedure for renewed lives to stay renewed. Using 1 Corinthians 6, Hebrews 6:12 and Hebrews 12:1-2, he says to stop being lazy, be around people who possess the promises, lay aside every hindrance, run with patience, and look to Jesus. Along the way he compares Jesus to government and speaks on politics, culture and history.
What is the Bible’s procedure for renewed lives to stay renewed?

He says “the Bible has a procedure for renewed, ruined lives to stay renewed,” because “it’s not just as important to get saved as it is to stay saved.” He gives the subtitle as how to avoid spiritual and moral crashes, backslidings, and giving up on Jesus.
What is the Bible’s procedure for renewed lives to stay renewed?

The Bible has a procedure for renewed, ruined lives to stay renewed. I mean, I know it’s not just as important to get saved as it is to stay saved. Yes. Or a subtitle: how to avoid spiritual and moral crashes, backslidings, and giving up on Jesus. Recently, the United States and the whole world for that matter’s economy was ruined and needed to be renewed, restored to its former condition. Uh, it’s questionable by the same politicians that brought the economy down to begin with, but we are working on it. The brightest minds right now are trying to solve the problem to avoid another crash, another downslide, and complete economic depression.
Why does he compare a renewed life to the economy and to government?

He says the economy “was ruined and needed to be renewed,” and that government leaders “have brought us into economic crises before and take credit for getting us out.” He says Jesus, “on the other hand,” has a procedure to keep restored lives restored, and “Jesus is not partial like our governments to the wealthy or the famous.” This part also carries his claims about stimulus money, politicians’ pay and wealth, and assassinations, which the transcript shows and this site has not checked.
Why does he compare a renewed life to the economy and to government?

You’ll notice that the stimulus money, which is really new printed money, they just made it. They just created it out of nothing. It went to the wealthy banks, to the stock market, mainly benefiting wealthy Americans and increasing welfare dependency of middle to low class Americans. Americans need jobs, not welfare, and millions of jobs have been sent overseas to other nations. In a slow process, Americans and American Christians, with Jesus, the Bible, and the Constitution, are being neglected and even rejected for a global government, a global economy, and a global set of values that all people can identify with. Now, I’m not the only one concerned for the future of our children in America. Many Americans, especially Christians, should have noticed that Americans’ wealth has been and is being passed to other nations, leaving us gradually less wealthy. Do you understand what I’ve said so far? We know from history our government leaders have brought us into economic crises before and take credit for getting us out, and then we go back in again, and no one wants to take credit for going back in, but they all like to take credit for coming back out. Of course, the wealthy never really experienced these economic crises, just the other classes of society do. When you’ve got all those millions of dollars, a depression never affects you. It seems that government officials can commit crimes that we citizens get punished for, but they are immune to and even protected. There have been 30 assassinations that have killed politicians, well, in modern times, and 11 of them who survived, uh, including modern-day presidents: Ford, Nixon, Kennedy, Reagan, Kennedy’s brother, Truman, Roosevelt, McKinley. And then others not in the political arena necessarily, like Martin Luther King and George Wallace, who was running for president, and several Congress members. So it is putting your life on the line when you take political office, and we have a high respect for that, but we question the immediate wealth when elected to office. Palin and Obama, for example, uh, immediately turned into multimillionaires. Uh, our Congress is paid $174,000 per year, plus all the perks: money from their campaign funds, travel expenses, furnishings for their offices and such, staff to do their work, paid staff, image money, just millions of dollars just to make themselves look good to the public. They have a great pension plan, a health plan, and they have all these tax exemptions that we don’t have. Now, Jesus, on the other hand, not only can restore and renew spiritually ruined lives, but He has a procedure to maintain those restored lives so they stay restored and renewed, not up and down. How many would like to meet a Jesus like that? Yeah. The Bible says in Ezekiel that the stairway always leads upward, not up [unclear] in that temple of God. Jesus is not partial like our governments to the wealthy or the famous. His procedure can restore and maintain both the poor and the wealthy, the wicked and the not so wicked. Even those of us who are good need renewed and restored, or we think we are good. The Bible says all have sinned and come short of the glory of God.
Why does he compare a renewed life to the economy and to government?
Romans 3:23: for all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God,
What were the first three steps he reviews from last time?

He says “Jesus, of course, is our substitute,” the second step is “You have a part in this. You have to respond,” and the third is that Jesus gets involved “to motivate and encourage and inspire us and deliver us through the indwelling and power of the Holy Spirit.”
What were the first three steps he reviews from last time?

So last time we talked, we talked about God’s plan for renewal and restoration, and Jesus, of course, is our substitute. He takes our place for our punishment, our pain, our, our curse. He is our mediator, He is our warrior, and we need a substitute to take our place, ‘cause we can’t do it on our own. How come you raise your hand and say, “That’s right, we can’t do it on our own”? And so Jesus Christ, the Christian religion is the only one that offers a substitute and an involvement in your life. After hearing the word of Christ, the second step that motivates us to deliver ourselves through Him. Remember, the Bible says, “Deliver yourself, O Zion.” You have a part in this. You have to respond. You have to get involved. Uh, and then of course the third step was Jesus got involved in our lives to motivate and encourage and inspire us and deliver us through the indwelling and power of the Holy Spirit.
What were the first three steps he reviews from last time?
Zechariah 2:7: “Up, Zion! Escape, you who dwell with the daughter of Babylon.”
What proof does he give that the gospel changes lives? (1 Corinthians 6:9-11)

He reads 1 Corinthians 6:9 and its list of sins, then stresses “Such were some of you. They aren’t now,” and “That’s the power of Jesus Christ and His gospel, a change for a lifetime.” He says believers were “washed, sanctified, that means made holy, justified, made right in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ.” He also tells of the Salvation Army song “Onward Christian Soldiers” and says it “tells how powerful the church is supposed to be and is.”
What proof does he give that the gospel changes lives? (1 Corinthians 6:9-11)

So, uh, a quick review. We’ve got to remember the Bible gives us proof that there’s power in Jesus Christ and His gospel. It says in 1 Corinthians 6:9, “Don’t be deceived: sexual immorality, idolaters, adultery.” He lists here all the different areas of sexual immorality, boy: homosexuals, uh, men using boys for homosexual acts, sodomy as the homosexual act, thieves, covetous, drunkards, verbal abuse, nor extortioners shall inherit the kingdom of God. And here’s that magic word, read it with me: “Such were some of you.” They aren’t now. They were adulterers, they were fornicators, they were homosexuals, they were thieves, they were extortioners, they were drunkards, but they’re not now. That’s the power of Jesus Christ and His gospel, a change for a lifetime. Amen. And the Bible gives us proof of this, and it says we were washed, sanctified, that means made holy, justified, made right in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ and by the Spirit of our God. God gets involved by His Spirit and works a miraculous thing in our life. Now, folks, that’s a great hope. Amen. That song that they sung about “Onward Christian Soldiers,” that’s the theme song of the Salvation Army, and Colonel [unclear] would go down into the scums, and back in those days drunkenness was just rampant before the women came along and protested alcohol and all that. And the Salvation Army would be singing this song, and they’d go down into the streets and they’d get a wagon, and they would just load these drunks up, put them in the wagon, take them back to the Salvation Army headquarters, and sober them up and clean up their life. Amen. You see, “Onward Christians,” so very powerful song that was. It tells how powerful the church is supposed to be and is.
What proof does he give that the gospel changes lives? (1 Corinthians 6:9-11)

1 Corinthians 6:9-11: Do you not know that the unrighteous will not inherit the kingdom of God? Do not be deceived. Neither fornicators, nor idolaters, nor adulterers, nor homosexuals, nor sodomites, nor thieves, nor covetous, nor drunkards, nor revilers, nor extortioners will inherit the kingdom of God. And such were some of you. But you were washed, but you were sanctified, but you were justified in the name of the Lord Jesus and by the Spirit of our God.
How does he answer someone who says he is too strict? (1 Peter 4:3-4)

Reading 1 Peter 4:3, he says those who still live that way “think it strange that you do not run with them in the same flood of indulgence.” When told he was “too strict,” he says he answered, “I never tell anybody what to do. I just tell them what the word says, and I give them the solution.” He says “the Holy Spirit’s job is to renew you and restore you. My job is to preach the gospel to you. Your job is to respond to it.”
How does he answer someone who says he is too strict? (1 Peter 4:3-4)

Now here in 1 Peter 4:3, “doing the will of the Gentiles.” We used to do the will of the Gentiles when we walked in lewdness, lust, drunkenness, revelries, drinking parties, abominable idolatries. In regards to these, they think it strange that you do not run with them in the same flood of indulgence. You see, “Of such were some of you,” but you don’t do that now. And those that still do it just can’t figure you out. But you got born again, you got changed by the power of Christ and by the power of His word. And see, someone told me recently that, “I don’t come to Mountainside anymore because you’re too strict.” I said, “I never tell anybody what to do. I just tell them what the word says, and I give them the solution.” How do you know what you need to be restored from if the Bible doesn’t tell you what you’re doing is wrong? Could that be an amen? Amen. I don’t go around looking over anybody’s shoulder. I don’t go to your house to see if you’re walking the line or not. That’s the Holy Ghost’s job. See, the Holy Spirit’s job is to renew you and restore you. My job is to preach the gospel to you. Your job is to respond to it. Now, that was good preaching. See, we can’t, we don’t want ministers flattering us, we want them to preach the gospel. Didn’t Jesus tell the apostles, “Teaching all things whatsoever I commanded you”? That’s all they were allowed to teach, no opinions. Amen. And so we got to hear the bad news before we hear the good news, so we know there’s good news to get us out of the bad. Now, this is the power of the gospel in Jesus Christ. There’s proof that we can be saved and stay saved and be healthy, strong Christians in this world.
How does he answer someone who says he is too strict? (1 Peter 4:3-4)

1 Peter 4:3-4: For we have spent enough of our past lifetime in doing the will of the Gentiles—when we walked in lewdness, lusts, drunkenness, revelries, drinking parties, and abominable idolatries. In regard to these, they think it strange that you do not run with them in the same flood of dissipation, speaking evil of you. Matthew 28:20: teaching them to observe all things that I have commanded you; and lo, I am with you always, even to the end of the age.” Amen.
What is the first step of the procedure? (Hebrews 6:12)

Reading Hebrews 6:12, he says the first step is “don’t be lazy,” but to follow and imitate “those who through faith and patience inherit the promises.” He says “in America this thing ‘not of works’ has just destroyed so many Christians that they think they don’t have to do anything,” and that “you have to follow, you have to pursue, you have to pray, you have to read your Bible.”
What is the first step of the procedure? (Hebrews 6:12)

Now, what is the procedure? Hebrews 6:12, “Do not become sluggish,” lazy, “but follow,” imitate. It includes imitating, follow, uh, you know, uh, run behind or whatever, but to imitate what you’re running behind, what you’re pursuing, what you’re chasing after, “those who through faith and patience inherit the promises.” Don’t be lazy. Lazy people don’t work, do they? And in America this thing “not of works” has just destroyed so many Christians that they think they don’t have to do anything. And you do have to do something. You have to follow, you have to pursue, you have to pray, you have to read your Bible. Isn’t that right? Isn’t that work? I don’t know about you, but it’s work. I have to set aside a time and I got to put some effort into it. So He says don’t be lazy, and that’s the problem in the church in America right now. We are Christian lazy people because we’ve overemphasized certain areas of the Bible that we feel we’re okay and we don’t have to do anything. Could that be true?
What is the first step of the procedure? (Hebrews 6:12)
Hebrews 6:12: that you do not become sluggish, but imitate those who through faith and patience inherit the promises.
Why does he say to get around people who possess the promises?

He says to “get around some people that are possessing the word of God,” people “pursuing Christ themselves and actually possessing the promises,” rather than only those who “follow our opinion” and “feel sorry for us.” He says “when you are around people better than you, you get better,” and that where you go to church matters: “If you go to a church where everybody’s okay the way they are, you’re not going to move up the mountain.”
Why does he say to get around people who possess the promises?

Okay, so the first step: don’t be lazy, but follow, imitate those who through faith and patience inherit the promises. Get around some people that are possessing the word of God. Now, we’re going to show you what the promises are. We have a tendency to run with people that follow our opinion, believe what we believe, sympathize with us, feel sorry for us, but we need to be around people that are pursuing Christ themselves and actually possessing the promises. You see, when you are around people better than you, you get better. When you are around all the time people worse, you get worse. That’s the principle. And so the first step is we got to quit being lazy, and we got to make, some of you need to just bug the [unclear] just to death. Go over and knock on the door and invite yourself to dinner. Be around people that possess things. That’s right. I mean, don’t give them any rest. Martha just wear her out. Now, the [unclear] is, yes, get free dinners and get free influence. Hallelujah. You notice I didn’t put the [unclear] in. There I am. Serious. You see, I didn’t know the Bible said that, but I found being around, when I was a young Christian, people that possess things rubbed off on me and encouraged me and ignited me. When I was around my peers, it was a worthless thing. Mostly we were just a bunch of critics. I went around peers, but when you’re around other people, you get ignited to move upward. Could that be an amen? Hallelujah. And you know, where you go to church makes all the difference in the world. If you’re going to a church where they don’t possess any of the promises, you’re not going to be inspired to possess anything. If you go to a church where everybody’s okay the way they are, you’re not going to move up the mountain. And so where you decide to go to church is very important. Who you decide to run around with and be close with is very important if you want to grow in God and maintain that restoration and renewal that God started in your life. Is that clear? Hallelujah. Now, “He who walks with wise men will be wise, but the companion of fools will be destroyed.” So we see here that what I’m around is going to affect my life, whether it’s bad or whether it’s good. You notice we’re not told to follow those that can speak well, those that can sing well, those that can play musical instruments well. Neither are we told to follow those that are financially successful and career success, like an athlete or an actor or a politician or somebody successful. In poverty, that I, I, I’ve ran into this, that poverty is spiritual, and the more poor you are, the more successful you are, and they use the Bible to come up with that nonsense.
Why does he say to get around people who possess the promises?
Proverbs 13:20: He who walks with wise men will be wise, But the companion of fools will be destroyed.
Why does he say we should not look only for people who share our past?

He says Jesus “didn’t have to be a prostitute to relate to prostitutes,” and “the word of God does the relating.” He says “you need to get into the Jesus group and identify with Him,” and that he has seen “more destruction” from people who think they can relate because of what they have been through, ending in psychology with “no power of the gospel and no power of the Spirit at all.”
Why does he say we should not look only for people who share our past?

And you know, we’re also not to run with people in our restoration, uh, “Well, I was once a drug addict, so I got to help the drug addicts.” “Well, I was once a prostitute, so boy, I’m going to start a ministry to help the prostitutes. I can relate.” “Well, I, you know, I was a thief, so I’m going to, you know, identify with the thieves.” I saw a bunch of women that came out of pornography in a church over here in, uh, uh, Buena Park, I believe, and they all were going to one church. And, you know, folks, Jesus didn’t have to be a prostitute to relate to prostitutes. He didn’t have to be a drunkard to relate to drunkards. The word of God does the relating. Can I hear an amen? You know, I don’t have to be a poor person to relate to poor, and I don’t have to be a rich person to relate to the rich. It’s the word of God. And so we, you know, we want to get in these recovery groups where people identify with us. Listen, you need to get into the Jesus group and identify with Him, because when you run with the best, you will become the best, and Jesus is the best. I’ve actually seen more destruction from these people thinking that because they’ve been through something someone else has been through, they can relate to them, and it winds up nothing but a bunch of psychology and no power of the gospel and no power of the Spirit at all. Could that be true? Hallelujah.
What does he say about the media, a global government, and the economy?

He says it is hard to find “wholesome, morality-building news in the media, the entertainment world, and even the sports arena.” He describes a “pursuit for global government, global economy, global morals” and says groups he names have “a hidden conspiracy” for “a new world order,” which he sees “as an open expression of change that they want in the world.” He says TV promotes “incest, homosexuality, smoking, drinking,” and he says “we want to be a nation that stands alone under God in whom we trust.” His figures on foreign aid, the dollar, jobs and the United Nations are his own and are not checked here.
What does he say about the media, a global government, and the economy?

It’s hard to find today wholesome, morality-building news in the media, the entertainment world, and even the sports arena. And meanwhile, while we’re reading all this kind of news, political leaders are slowly increasing our taxes, and, as I said before, this pursuit for global government, global economy, global morals, and a universal God, all religions lead to the same God, no Jesus, no Bible, religion, and no commitment to the Constitution. We’re actually leaving the Constitution of the United States. The Illuminati, the Bilderberg, the Trilateral Commission that a lot of people are promoting have a hidden conspiracy, and they do. They stand for a new world order, one world government, one world economy, and share the wealth and raise the taxes to do it. But I don’t see it as a conspiracy theory. I see it as an open expression of change that they want in the world. These are facts. The United States gives foreign aid of $50 billion a year. Fifty billion of our tax dollars goes to [unclear]. The dollar value has declined over 90% since 1913. A million jobs a year are shipped overseas. We know that from reading the newspaper. I trust you read. Okay. And then we wonder why our people are unemployed, and then they want to tell them to go to college and get a trade and all the rest. What if they don’t want to go to college? Why should we ship jobs overseas when our people don’t have jobs here? Amen. You know, what’s this frame of mind they’re getting us into, that we got to be, you know, the data nation, you know, the information nation? What’s wrong with manufacturing ball bearings for, uh, skateboards? Amen. And, you know, yes, it pays less money, but that’s their choice in life. Shouldn’t they have a freedom to make that choice? And a lot of people aren’t college material anyway. And see, and I’m telling you this stuff, I’m, I’m, I’m comparing Christ to our government because you need to be aware of both the natural and the spiritual and have a, a right mental understanding of it so you can live in it and be an asset to it. That was good. But our young people and most Americans are just into TV, and there’s nothing on TV that has anything moral. They got around, they got their earbuds in their ear and listen to music all the time. That is worthless. The shows on TV leave you with no morality. In fact, they promote incest, homosexuality, smoking, drinking, everything that’s destroying lives and destroying homes in America. When we turn on a TV, they enforce it. Isn’t that right? Yes. And our government’s doing these things. We know that they want to decrease arms. Uh, the United Nations costs $17 billion a year, and they are trying to be able to tax us as a nation from the United Nations and wanting to pass laws that govern the United States from the United Nations. Folks, we don’t want that. We want to be a nation that stands alone under God in whom we trust, and let God be the deciding factor of our future rather than the nations of the world. Can that be an amen?
What does he say Christians should do while living in this world?

He says “Christians cannot just get saved and wait for the rapture,” because “we got to live 70 to 80 years in this world, and we need an impact on it.” He lists his claims about government debt and bankruptcy, compares big government to “what the communists did,” and says “what we need is jobs and work, and if you don’t work, it’s your problem.”
What does he say Christians should do while living in this world?

Amen. Christians cannot just get saved and wait for the rapture. We got to live 70 to 80 years in this world, and we need an impact on it, and so we need to understand these things. The federal government is in debt $14 trillion. Yet if we go into debt and don’t pay our bills, we go to jail. State and city governments are going bankrupt, and it’s very close to a domino effect. California is bankrupt. They are borrowing money and living on other money because they can make decisions to straighten the finances of this state out, and we live in this state, and we’re more interested in the Super Bowl than we are in our California future, because the media and everything has got us thinking that way. They give us the impression that a bowl of rice or a bowl of beans daily in our home is worth the high taxes and big government rulership while they eat steak and wear the best clothes. And that’s exactly what the communists did. The communists promised the, I’ve read it, a bowl of rice in every home. Yeah, that was it, a bowl of rice, and you had to line up to get it for hours. I mean, no, that’s no way to live. What we need is jobs and work, and if you don’t work, it’s your problem. We don’t need government taking everybody’s money and giving everybody a [unclear]. Could that be true? But see, slowly our government is leaning that way.
What does he mean by “I have a conspiracy,” and which lies about people does he name?

He defines a conspiracy as “a hidden or open plan to reach a goal that changes present accepted established ways,” and says “I have a conspiracy to destroy these conspiracies.” He says the hidden part is a lie, giving as examples the lie that “blacks were not human” so they could be sold as property, and that women were “inferior and like children in their mind” so they could not vote or lead. He ties both to evolution (“Both of them came from evolution”). These historical claims are his own and are not checked here.
What does he mean by “I have a conspiracy,” and which lies about people does he name?

Now, I have a conspiracy, and it’s not secret either. And many of us have that conspiracy. A conspiracy is a hidden or open plan to reach a goal that changes present accepted established ways to institute their own ways, their own government, their own values, their own politics through force or of law or by arms. And I have a conspiracy to destroy these conspiracies. Now, let me show you the hidden part. Let me show you what the hidden part of a conspiracy is, and they can be open. Blacks back in the old days were sold as property, and to get people to believe that, they taught the lie that blacks were not human, so therefore they could be sold as property, and then people believed the lie. Are you out there? And that’s what they’re doing today. They’re not hiding this thing. What they’re doing is hiding the lie. Do you understand me, church? Women were inferior and like children in their mind. Therefore they can’t vote and they can’t lead in politics or in industry. And so for years women weren’t allowed freedom that everybody else in America had. And where did they get this stuff? Both of them came from evolution, and why blacks and women would even think about accepting evolution is beyond my cranial understanding. Darwin is the one that taught this stuff. That was the thinking back there, along with, the church is in our way because of its moral standards. We got to get rid of the church. We got to, you know, get rid of blacks, and we got to get rid of women, or not get rid of, uh, suppress them. Are you there? Those of you who know your history, can you raise your hand, say yes, that’s what happened? Yeah. Read Darwin. That’s what he said: women have the mind of a child. They didn’t evolve. Well, and yet women, a lot of women, I, we need to know this stuff. And see, the lie was there so then you could do what you wanted to to get your way.
What lies does he say are told today about the unborn and homosexuality?

He says the lie today is that “The embryo is not a baby, it’s just a mass of tissue, so it can be aborted,” and that “Homosexuals were born that way.” He says “Americans have believed the lie,” citing “over 50% now say that homosexuality is an acceptable lifestyle,” and that a communist leader said “If you keep repeating a lie, it becomes an accepted truth.” He says some “twist the Scriptures for whatever they want to do.” His statistics are not checked here.
What lies does he say are told today about the unborn and homosexuality?

All right, let’s move to modern day. The embryo is not a baby, it’s just a mass of tissue, so it can be aborted. What’s the lie? A mass of tissue, it’s not a baby, doesn’t have life yet. In fact, they’ll use Genesis where it says when God breathed into Adam the breath of life, then he became a living soul. Until the baby’s out of the womb and breathes air, it’s not a living person. They use the Scriptures for that. They twist the Scriptures for whatever they want to do. Are you guys aware of this stuff? You need to be aware of this stuff. Homosexuals were born that way, so it’s not a criminal act, then they should be allowed to be married. See, Americans have believed the lie. Over 50% now say that homosexuality is an acceptable lifestyle. Just 10 years ago it wasn’t even close to that, and 20 years ago it was almost zero. But you see, Lenin said this. He says, “If you keep repeating a lie, it becomes an accepted truth.” Lenin was the one that wrote the Marxist, Lenin, manifesto of communists. And what did Lenin and them do? They told Russia lies until Russia believed the lies, and they took Russia over. Are you out there? You see, and so we got to be aware of these lies.
What lies does he say are told today about the unborn and homosexuality?
Genesis 2:7: And the LORD God formed man of the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living being.
What does he say about following the crowd? (Exodus 23:2, 1 Corinthians 15:33)

He says Jesus is consistent, unlike government, and reads Exodus 23:2, “You shall not follow a crowd to do evil.” He reads of a woman who “eats, wipes her mouth, and says” she has done nothing wrong, and of 1 Corinthians 15:33, “Do not be misled: bad company corrupts good character.” He applies it to sinners who feel no guilt and to Christians who “hide behind faith and grace,” and says “we fail because the power of Christ and the power of His word is not being preached.”
What does he say about following the crowd? (Exodus 23:2, 1 Corinthians 15:33)

This thing is not done in secret, it’s openly. It’s the lie that’s the secret that they’re bringing as a truth. Are you there? Hallelujah. Aren’t you glad Jesus isn’t like our government? Hallelujah. Yes, He’s consistent. It’s obvious that government leaders are running with the [unclear] crowd. They’re not running with the wise. Whoa. “You shall not follow a crowd to do evil,” Exodus 23:2. “This is the way of an adulterous woman: she eats, wipes her mouth, and says, ‘I’ve done nothing wrong.’” [unclear] Corinthians 15:33, “Do not be misled: bad company corrupts good character.” And this is in America. This is where we’re at in America right now. He’s not talking just about an adulterous woman, he’s talking about sinners. See, they eat, no problem. They’re not worried about anything. They don’t feel guilty. They’re just going on through life. They wipe the crumbs off of their mouth: “I’ve done nothing wrong. I’m just like everybody else.” The thief, the homosexual, the sexually immoral. And in America many Christians hide behind faith and grace to wipe their mouth and say, “I’m okay.” Isn’t that correct? And we, then we, we fail to attain the promise of, “Such were some of you.” You see, we fail because the power of Christ and the power of His word is not being preached, and it’s that power that changes us from drunkards and prostitutes and homosexuals and thieves into something good.
What does he say about following the crowd? (Exodus 23:2, 1 Corinthians 15:33)

Exodus 23:2: You shall not follow a crowd to do evil; nor shall you testify in a dispute so as to turn aside after many to pervert justice. Proverbs 30:20: This is the way of an adulterous woman: She eats and wipes her mouth, And says, “I have done no wickedness.” 1 Corinthians 15:33: Do not be deceived: “Evil company corrupts good habits.”
What are the “cloud of witnesses” and the weights to lay aside? (Hebrews 12:1-2)

He says “a witness is one that has experienced something,” firsthand, and that we push them aside to be with people “that flatter us.” Second, “Let us lay aside every weight,” which he explains as hindrances and sin, and “Sin is the violation of God’s word.” He gives TV and a sports night as examples of hindrances, and says “There’s nothing in the Bible that says cigarette smoke will send you to hell,” but it is “killing you,” and secondhand smoke is a hindrance to a home. He defines patience as “calmly enduring mistreatment, troubles, problems, sorrows, and anguish without complaining and remaining steady.”
What are the “cloud of witnesses” and the weights to lay aside? (Hebrews 12:1-2)

Three more steps to success. All right, Hebrews 12:1 and 2. First, He’s repeating the first step I just gave you. “We are compassed, circled about with so great a cloud of witnesses.” A witness is one that has experienced something. They possess the information. They actually firsthand experience, wasn’t secondhand information, firsthand. So it goes back to those people, those heirs that possess the promises. See, they’re the witness. They’ve experienced the promises. They possessed it, and it says you’re circled about. When you’re circled about, everywhere you go there’s one of those witnesses. And so God is telling us, if you look, they’re all around you. But we push them aside to go and be with those that aren’t possessing, that agree with us, that flatter us. We love to be flattered. “You’re okay, I’m okay, everybody’s okay.” Secondly, “Let us lay aside every weight,” a hindrance. If you put a weight on your feet, it hinders you from running and jumping over the hurdles. We got to lay aside. Here is that effort again. What do we got to do? Lay aside the hindrances. That TV is keeping you from studying the Bible and praying, lay aside the hindrance. You know, Monday night football with the boys and a six-pack of beer is keeping you from loving your family and spending time with your kids, then lay aside the hindrance. You got to do it. Yes. See, you got to put forth an effort in this thing, and lay aside the sin. Sin is the violation of God’s word, “that so easily besets us,” or destroys us. You say, if alcohol is your problem, then let’s put an effort to lay it aside. If cigarettes are killing you and your kids are starting to smoke because you smoke, then lay aside the cigarettes. There’s nothing in the Bible that says cigarette smoke will send you to hell. It’s just, if you’re going to go to hell, you’re going to get there quicker. It’s killing you, and secondhand smoke. I just dealt with an acquaintance whose wife died from secondhand smoke. His smoke. And so, see, that’s a hindrance. That’s a hindrance to my home, that’s a hindrance to my children, so what do I do? I lay it aside. Yeah, I may have freedom to do it, but what should I do? Lay it aside. “Let us run,” participate. Run is to participate “with patience.” Patience is calmly enduring mistreatment, troubles, problems, sorrows, and anguish without complaining and remaining steady. You don’t quit, you don’t give up. That’s patience. How many could use a little patience? How many could use a whole lot of patience?
What are the “cloud of witnesses” and the weights to lay aside? (Hebrews 12:1-2)

Hebrews 12:1-2: Therefore we also, since we are surrounded by so great a cloud of witnesses, let us lay aside every weight, and the sin which so easily ensnares us, and let us run with endurance the race that is set before us, looking unto Jesus, the author and finisher of our faith, who for the joy that was set before Him endured the cross, despising the shame, and has sat down at the right hand of the throne of God.
Why does he say the Christian life is a race, and what does he say about church-hopping?

He says “the race is a competition” and “we’re in a race against good and evil.” He says “whether you like it or not. You’re in the race,” and that “Americans just go from church to church and group to group,” including a “bar church.” He says you have to “hang in there for right.”
Why does he say the Christian life is a race, and what does he say about church-hopping?

Yeah. See, we got to participate. Here is that again. We got to put forth the effort. I got to get in the race, man, and the race is a competition. When I get in a race with Mr. Barnes, I’m out to beat him. If I play ping pong, I’m out to win. Ain’t no ties. Here I want to be on top. But we’re in a race against good and evil. Good against evil, we’re in a competition, we’re in an opposition. They’re opposing us, and we got to run this race. We got to participate, whether you like it or not. You’re in the race, and you got to hang in there for right. And you know, Americans just go from church to church and group to group. They, and, uh, “Well, the church don’t even relate to me anymore, and I read all this stuff and hear all this stuff and whatever.” Yeah, and one guy’s got a church in a bar now where they pray and they read a scripture and then they drink, and, you know, it’s called the bar church because the churches don’t relate to me anymore.
What does “looking unto Jesus” mean, and where does the church come from? (Hebrews 12:2, Matthew 16:18)

He says “Looking means giving attention to,” and “That means my time, my actions, my mind.” He says Jesus said He will build His church, “the called out ones,” and “the gates of hell shall not prevail against them.” He says “only Jesus can finish the work He’s begun in you,” that other believers “can’t do beans for me other than be the example,” and “you got to give attention to Jesus Christ.”
What does “looking unto Jesus” mean, and where does the church come from? (Hebrews 12:2, Matthew 16:18)

Well, where do you find that in the Bible? Jesus said, “I will build my bar.” “I will build my home group.” “I will build my church,” the called out ones, “and the gates of hell shall not prevail against them.” Amen. And then the fourth one is “looking unto Jesus, the author and the finisher of our faith.” Looking means giving attention to. You’re focusing in on something. When I’m watching a football game, I’m focused in on it, so I have to set aside time to do that. I have to do the same thing with Jesus. I got to set aside time, and I got to focus on Jesus Christ. I got to focus on His word. I got to give attention to Him. And, folks, that’s higher than the heirs who possess the promises. And they’re great to have around, but if you don’t have any around, if you’re on [unclear] out in a remote post where there’s nobody around and you can’t fellowship with anyone, then you better know how to touch this man Jesus. He started your walk of Christ, He started your new life, He started your restoration, and He’s the one that can finish the restoration. Nobody else. Us who possess it can encourage you, we can be an example to you, but only Jesus can finish the work He’s begun in you. So I must take time to come to church. I must take time to read my Bible and get into Bible studies. I must take time to sing and praise Him and do what the Bible says to give attention to Him. Then people say, “Well, I don’t have time for my Bible, and I don’t have time for prayer.” You better make time if you’re going to maintain your walk with Christ. If you’re going to maintain a mature, strong Christian character, you got to give attention to Jesus Christ. I can’t say it any better than that. Is that what the Scripture says? It’s just not a star-eyed gaze, “Oh, Jesus is up in heaven.” No, I give attention to Him. That means my time, my actions, my mind. We are worshiping the pulpit and ministers when we should be focusing in on Jesus Christ. And thank God for the witnesses that possess, that encourage me that I can do it too, but they can’t do beans for me other than be the example and show me that it works. Jesus is the one that causes me to possess the promises.
What does “looking unto Jesus” mean, and where does the church come from? (Hebrews 12:2, Matthew 16:18)

Matthew 16:18: And I also say to you that you are Peter, and on this rock I will build My church, and the gates of Hades shall not prevail against it. Hebrews 12:2: looking unto Jesus, the author and finisher of our faith, who for the joy that was set before Him endured the cross, despising the shame, and has sat down at the right hand of the throne of God.
Why does he say staying saved matters?
He says “it’s not just as important to get saved as it is to stay saved,” and that the Bible has a procedure so renewed lives do not crash or give up on Jesus.
Does he say Jesus helps both the rich and the poor?
Yes. He says “His procedure can restore and maintain both the poor and the wealthy, the wicked and the not so wicked,” and that even those who think they are good need to be renewed.
What does he say Jesus does as our substitute?

He says “He takes our place for our punishment, our pain, our, our curse,” and that we need a substitute “’cause we can’t do it on our own.” He says “the Christian religion is the only one that offers a substitute and an involvement in your life.”
Does he say it is his job to watch over people’s lives?
No. He says “I don’t go around looking over anybody’s shoulder,” and “I don’t go to your house to see if you’re walking the line or not.” He says that is the Holy Spirit’s work.
What does he say about ministers who flatter?
He says “we don’t want ministers flattering us, we want them to preach the gospel,” and that “we got to hear the bad news before we hear the good news.”
What does he say is the problem in the church in America?
He says “we are Christian lazy people because we’ve overemphasized certain areas of the Bible that we feel we’re okay and we don’t have to do anything.”
What happens when you are around people who are worse than you?
He says “when you are around people better than you, you get better,” and “when you are around all the time people worse, you get worse.” He calls it a principle.
Who does he say we are not told to follow?

He says “we’re not told to follow those that can speak well, those that can sing well, those that can play musical instruments well,” nor people just because they are financially or career successful.
What does he say about TV and music?
He says “there’s nothing on TV that has anything moral,” and that young people with earbuds listening to music all the time is “worthless.” He says the shows leave you with no morality.
Does he say Christians should just wait for the rapture?
No. He says “Christians cannot just get saved and wait for the rapture,” and “we need an impact on it,” meaning on this world.
What does he say many Christians do with faith and grace?

He says “in America many Christians hide behind faith and grace,” and that “the power of Christ and the power of His word is not being preached,” the power that changes drunkards, prostitutes, homosexuals and thieves “into something good.”
He says “Sin is the violation of God’s word that so easily besets us.” He says we must put forth effort to lay aside whatever hinders us.
What if there are no other believers around?
He says if you are somewhere with nobody to fellowship with, “you better know how to touch this man Jesus,” because Jesus started your restoration “and He’s the one that can finish the restoration.”
Why does he say you must make time for the Bible and prayer?
He says “you better make time if you’re going to maintain your walk with Christ,” and “if you’re going to maintain a mature, strong Christian character, you got to give attention to Jesus Christ.”

p: In “Two Mothers of Revelation Part 1,” Pastor David G. Kincer preaches from Revelation on the two mothers it mentions. He says the woman of Revelation 12 is a spiritual mother, the church, whose children overcome Satan and are persecuted by him, then turns to the second woman of Revelation 17, whom he describes as people who use Christ’s name but do not follow him, serving God their own way. He teaches that Revelation is a spiritual illustration, not a list of natural kingdoms, and speaks about the beast, the seven mountains and spiritual fornication.
