And so many Christians give up because the word isn’t made plain to them and they think it’s impossible. No, everywhere you’re at, God sees it as perfection. Why? Because that’s exactly where you should be. Let me ask you this. Would Christ abuse or mistreat and be cruel to children? No. Would Christ abuse their spouse, mistreat them? No. So what’s the problem with this divorce and these family problems in the church world? What is the problem? The embryo hasn’t been developed right. They are following a religion, a philosophy, an idea, instead of Christ. Do you see that? Yeah, they blame everything else, but the real problem is they have got to respond to that word in their spiritual man, because Christ would not do that. They wouldn’t handle snakes and drink poison to show their faith. Christ wouldn’t do that. Christ would not say, “Well, you’re sick, you can’t go to the doctor, or you don’t have faith.” Would he? No. Jesus himself said, “They that are sick need a physician.” Yes, God can heal, but if he doesn’t, you better get to a doctor. Jesus himself said, if you’re sick you need a physician. So this is a lot in the Pentecostal areas. They just make us look stupid, these people with this nonsense. “Cut off your hand or pluck out your eye.” The Bible says, you know, better to pluck your hand off and pluck out your eye and let it, you cause you to sin. That is an allegory, idiot. Jesus never went around cutting off people’s hands. He didn’t go around plucking out people’s eyes, neither the apostles. You see, these are ignorant people that twist the Scriptures to their own destruction, which we already showed you, and you got to follow Christ. You got to realize that Christ would do certain things and wouldn’t do certain things, and when you’re doing things Christ wouldn’t do, that tells you you’re wrong. Amen.
Is every stage of growth “perfect,” and what would Christ not do? (Pentecostal practices, doctors)

Matthew 9:12: When Jesus heard that, He said to them, “Those who are well have no need of a physician, but those who are sick. Matthew 5:29-30: If your right eye causes you to sin, pluck it out and cast it from you; for it is more profitable for you that one of your members perish, than for your whole body to be cast into hell. And if your right hand causes you to sin, cut it off and cast it from you; for it is more profitable for you that one of your members perish, than for your whole body to be cast into hell. 2 Peter 3:16: as also in all his epistles, speaking in them of these things, in which are some things hard to understand, which untaught and unstable people twist to their own destruction, as they do also the rest of the Scriptures.
What does he say Jesus would and would not do about welfare, homosexuality, the poor and education?

He says Jesus “wouldn’t take the bribe of welfare,” that welfare “should be connected with work,” though he allows help for people who are “destitute.” He says Jesus does not approve of homosexuality, would not “remove himself from the affairs of the world,” and that family should care for family, then the church.
What does he say Jesus would and would not do about welfare, homosexuality, the poor and education?

Would Jesus work and provide for himself? Yeah. He wouldn’t take the bribe of welfare. Yes, welfare is a bribe. Welfare is a bribe to get you to lean towards a philosophy that is not necessarily healthy. Of the fifteen apostles that was chosen to be apostles, was there one of them on welfare? Were all of them successful career people, every one of them? Were? He never went to the widow in her mite. He never went to the beggar and said, “I’m going to make you an apostle.” In fact, the Bible says if you don’t provide for yourself in your own household, you’re worse than an unbeliever. And so welfare should be connected with work. If we’re going to give people money from the federal government, they’re going to take our taxes, then they should be out there picking strawberries, cleaning hotel rooms, doing something, so they have some self-respect. They’re working for the, now, this is an unpopular message, but church, somebody has got to get this and move forward in America. Are you with me? Now, is there a time where people need help? Absolutely. Come on. I showed you the people in the thirties, that Great Depression with the dust bowl and all that. I’m not going to fault the government for going in there and helping them. Those people were destitute. No, they couldn’t find jobs. They needed some help to get through the problem. Amen. We just need to keep this stuff in control. All right. Would Jesus approve of homosexuality? No. He doesn’t approve of adultery, fornication, pedophilia, he doesn’t approve of incest or anything, let alone homosexuality. Would Jesus remove himself from the affairs of the world, civil laws, justice, education, eternal life in the kingdom of God? Would he remove himself? No way. Why are American Christians removing themselves from the affairs of this nation? They need us involved with the right mentality. Can I hear an amen? See, we’re supposed to be in the image of his Son. Would Jesus ignore the poor? No. Did Jesus, is there any record in the Bible that Jesus gave to the poor? You’re looking at me, I got a question that stumped you. There is no Scripture. But he told us to help the poor. He didn’t make it a priority in his ministry, and the Bible says that a family’s supposed to take care of family. Does that sound fair? You bring kids into this world, you take care of them, right? If something happens in your home, the family comes and they do what’s necessary to correct the problem. Then the church said, if there’s people without a family, then the church will help you. Now we know that’s reasonable help. All right. Would he ignore wrongly educated curriculum, curriculum that’s teaching lies? No. But the church is. Why? Because the embryo is missing. There’s many embryos, and that one is missing.
What does he say Jesus would and would not do about welfare, homosexuality, the poor and education?
1 Timothy 5:8: But if anyone does not provide for his own, and especially for those of his household, he has denied the faith and is worse than an unbeliever.
What is the “growth test”: which of the four responses are you?

He gives four responses, one being an “unborn, ungrowing fetus,” another a “born-again, probably a baby Christian,” a third who “aborted the Scripture stage,” and a fourth who justifies their own opinions and has “a defective birth.” He says there is “nothing wrong with being a baby Christian at all.”
What is the “growth test”: which of the four responses are you?

Here’s a growth test. You ready for a growth test? See which one you are. Do you mock Scripture, put it off for a convenient time? Do you believe, [unclear] temptation, the cares of this life, have some fruit? You tremble at the word and you’re growing into a Christian. Do you hate, harm, abuse Jesus, the Bible and growing Christians? And do you justify your opinions of Jesus, the Bible, the church and morals through criticism of the Bible, morals and growing Christians? See, you justify your own opinions by putting the truth down and they that follow it. All right, one, two, three, four. If you are number one, you’re an unborn, ungrowing fetus. If you are number two, a green, you are a born-again, probably a baby Christian, and there’s nothing wrong with being a baby Christian at all. Number three, the purple one: if you do this one, you aborted the Scripture stage, even if you believe. You see, and the last one, if you justify your opinions, you have a defective birth. Okay, solution. You got some things now. You got some things in your life that hasn’t grown to fruitfulness yet. How many can raise your hand, say, “I got, I know”? Before you start putting these up, I got some things in my life. Okay, about twenty-five percent of us are honest. First Peter. What’s the solution? First Peter 1:23: “Being born again by the” what? Word of God. See, we’ve got to listen to that word. If we haven’t got wisdom, we need to listen to that word of wisdom. You see, if we haven’t repented, we need to listen to that word of repentance, belief and faith, water baptism, Holy Spirit baptism, baptism into the body as he sees fit, laying on of hands for impartation, healing, blessing, resurrection of the dead and eternal judgment.
What are the “seeds” to add to faith, and why give God one hour a day? (1 Peter 1:23; 2 Peter 1)

He says we are “being born again by the … word of God,” and all the seeds of the word are needed, including repentance, baptism and the Holy Spirit. He says these are “kindergarten doctrines” and we must add “virtue” and “knowledge,” and “we won’t give God one hour a day in the Bible and in prayer.”
What are the “seeds” to add to faith, and why give God one hour a day? (1 Peter 1:23; 2 Peter 1)

You see, all of these is a seed of the word, and you need all the seeds growing in your life to be a complete Christian. Are you with me? Let’s continue. Then we go over to Second Peter, and we find we add to our faith virtue, or good morals, justice. Should Christians stand for justice, for goodness, for right? Yes. That’s the “add to your faith virtue.” You say, we like to stay over here in the second coming, and oh, we argue and quarrel about water baptism and Holy Spirit baptism and baptism of the body. We haven’t even, we quarrel over those things, and those things the Bible says are kindergarten doctrines. They’re the first principles of God, they’re not deep stuff at all. Everybody thinks the second coming is deep. Yeah, you talk about the Holy Ghost, deep. No, the Bible says these are kindergarten, first grade doctrines, primary doctrines. You got to go on to the character doctrines: virtue, good morals. Knowledge, knowledge of the Scriptures. Jesus said, “You do err, not knowing the Scriptures nor the power of God.” You see, we need to know the Scriptures. “My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge.” And we won’t give God one hour a day in the Bible and in prayer to get knowledge. It just floors me. He asked for one hour. One hour, sixty minutes, and we got time to watch everything on TV, we got time to play sports, we got time to hang glide, we got time to surf, we got time to do all this. “Oh, I’m so busy.” You’re busy satisfying your own agenda. God asks for one hour of your day and you’re not giving it to him. That’s how you grow to be good, that’s how you grow in knowledge. You got to be in the word and pray the word. Forget this “now I lay me down to sleep” stuff. Pray the word. Self-control: we got to grow into controlling ourselves, and the reason we won’t give God one hour a day is we lack self-control. Patience. You see, now we’re climbing the ladder. I mean, these are big things. See, God has an organized structure. Self-control and patience are big fruits. Love your enemy. Love God, love the right believer. Jesus said, “A new commandment I give unto you, that you love one another.” I got to love myself, and I got to love my family, I got to love my wife, I got to love my kids, I can’t hurt them, and love is the goal. The high mark of the calling of God is to love God, love his word, love people, and do nothing to harm them. And we’re way down the ladder. Most of us are back here with these two, grace and faith. That’s as far as we go.
What are the “seeds” to add to faith, and why give God one hour a day? (1 Peter 1:23; 2 Peter 1)

1 Peter 1:23: having been born again, not of corruptible seed but incorruptible, through the word of God which lives and abides forever, 2 Peter 1:5-7: But also for this very reason, giving all diligence, add to your faith virtue, to virtue knowledge, to knowledge self-control, to self-control perseverance, to perseverance godliness, to godliness brotherly kindness, and to brotherly kindness love. Hebrews 6:1-2: Therefore, leaving the discussion of the elementary principles of Christ, let us go on to perfection, not laying again the foundation of repentance from dead works and of faith toward God, of the doctrine of baptisms, of laying on of hands, of resurrection of the dead, and of eternal judgment. Hosea 4:6: My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge. Because you have rejected knowledge, I also will reject you from being priest for Me; Because you have forgotten the law of your God, I also will forget your children.
What comes after knowledge: self-control, patience and love? (John 13:34; Romans 1:17; 2 Corinthians 1:10)

He says “self-control and patience are big fruits” and “love is the goal,” the “high mark of the calling of God.” He says righteousness is revealed “from faith to faith,” that being filled with the Holy Ghost did not end his problems, and that God is “in the midst of delivering us.”
What comes after knowledge: self-control, patience and love? (John 13:34; Romans 1:17; 2 Corinthians 1:10)

How many would raise your hand and say, “Lord, give me some more embryos”? If you don’t ask, you don’t get. Now, how many were raised? “Lord, I want more embryos. Yeah, I want them growing.” Listen now, how many will give him one hour a day to let that happen? Uh-huh. Now, now we’re getting somewhere. Romans 1:17. You got to understand this now. You young ones, pay attention here. This is really good, because Satan really likes to get on you young ones, because the Bible says flee youthful lust. There’s certain lust of the flesh that youth have because they’re growing into adulthood. All right, “the righteousness of God is revealed from faith to faith.” So what should my faith be doing? Bringing me into the righteous character of Christ, one seed at a time. Yes, I might not have self-control yet, but God said he’s going to reveal it as I respond to the previous doctrines. I will get that patience, I will get that self-control. Are you there? See, it’s a growing process. When I got saved in Pentecostal churches, man, they said if you got filled with the Holy Ghost, bang, your problems were over. I got filled with the Holy Ghost and bam, I had more problems. I didn’t even know I had problems before he came along and shined light on them. Man, and I had to work through these things. There was no [unclear] power [unclear], man, just got me through some of these trials and tribulations and growth things. I had to work the work of faith, I had to pursue knowledge, I had to pursue Christ to get through them. 2 Corinthians 1:10: “Who delivered us from so great a death, and does deliver us, in whom we trust that he will still deliver us.” That great death is what? The wages of sin. He delivers us. See, but he is in the midst of delivering us, and tomorrow he’ll be there to still deliver you. Why? Because you need to grow, and you’re violating God’s inheritance, God’s commandments, in certain areas, and so you need deliverance on the way up to that top fruit of love. I can’t make it more clear than that. And remember, every stage in God is perfect, but when you are a baby when you should be a child or a young adult in God, that’s the problem, as we will see as we pursue this. Are you with me? But we need to get the inner right. Okay, the word delivers us and sets us free from sin, sets us free to do right and obey truth.
What comes after knowledge: self-control, patience and love? (John 13:34; Romans 1:17; 2 Corinthians 1:10)

John 13:34: A new commandment I give to you, that you love one another; as I have loved you, that you also love one another. Romans 1:17: For in it the righteousness of God is revealed from faith to faith; as it is written, “The just shall live by faith.” 2 Corinthians 1:10: who delivered us from so great a death, and does deliver us; in whom we trust that He will still deliver us,
Are we the “glorious church” yet, and why must we get the word out? (Ezekiel 14:14)

He says Noah, Job and Daniel were saved by their own righteousness, and “I can’t be saved because my mom and dad were righteous.” He says the church is not yet the glorious church because “we can’t even fellowship with people outside of our corral,” that “who much is given, much is required,” and that the word must go out “printed word, audio word, video word, any word.”
Are we the “glorious church” yet, and why must we get the word out? (Ezekiel 14:14)

Noah, Job and Daniel are mentioned in God’s hall of fame in Ezekiel 14:14, and what was the only thing that would save them from wars, earthquakes, plagues? Their righteousness. You got it? You got it. I can’t be saved because my mom and dad were righteous. I can’t be saved because the pope is righteous. I can’t be saved because Billy Graham is righteous. I got to be, I will be saved because I have been birthed in Christ and I’m growing in him, and I’m at the stage where I’m at, and God sees it as perfect and saves me so I can go on to the next stage. See, growth is a stage, there, steps. End-time prophets look at Israel, they look at acts of God, they look at wickedness, instead of the glorious church overcoming the gates of hell. The Bible says in Revelation that he’s coming and his bride has what? Made herself ready. Ephesians says that he’s coming for a bride that is a glorious church without spot or wrinkle or any such thing. Are we there yet? No, we can’t even fellowship with people outside of our corral, our denomination, our beliefs. We’re not there. Are we destroying the gates of hell in America today as a corporate church? No way. The homosexuals, the atheists, everybody’s having free rein with us. You’re going to be sad that you were here this morning, because who much is given, much is required. Church, God has given this church a fantastic word, but if we don’t take it seriously and get it out to others and just live our life, grazing, kids, working a job, going through every day routine, we’re not going to help anybody. So I submit to you, we got to get the word out, and get them to hear the word and read the word. That word will set people free, that word will heal people, but we can’t keep putting it off. We can’t just stay at this place where, “Oh boy, we got a word, hallelujah, that was a good message.” No, we’ve got to get a hunger and desire and a compelling to get it out to others. Could that be an amen? Printed word, audio word, video word, any word, we need to get it out, because it’s the word that sets us free, and who much is given, much is required, and we need to get this word out. We need to challenge. I’m ready to get on radio and TV and challenge the leaders of our day, both political and church leaders. They are wimps when they deny the truth of the Bible just to have a big congregation and a lavish lifestyle. That is wrong. We need to preach truth no matter if it takes everything, every possession we got.
Are we the “glorious church” yet, and why must we get the word out? (Ezekiel 14:14)

Ezekiel 14:14: Even if these three men, Noah, Daniel, and Job, were in it, they would deliver only themselves by their righteousness,” says the Lord GOD. Revelation 19:7: Let us be glad and rejoice and give Him glory, for the marriage of the Lamb has come, and His wife has made herself ready.” Luke 12:48: But he who did not know, yet committed things deserving of stripes, shall be beaten with few. For everyone to whom much is given, from him much will be required; and to whom much has been committed, of him they will ask the more.
What does he mean by the “unborn fetus stage” of growth?
He says it is when the word is planted: “when you hear the word, that’s when God will come by his Spirit and try to plant that word in your inner man, in your spirit.”
Does he say baptism should be delayed?
No. He says “give me scripture for putting off baptism. There is none,” and that the jailer was baptized “the same night.”
What does he say about baptism being “an outward sign of an inward work”?
He says “that is not in the Bible,” and that “a lot of people have been robbed of a great experience in water baptism” because they treat it as a ritual: “there is something in it.”
What does he call the “shooting stars” in the parable of the sower?

He calls the rocky-ground hearers “shooting stars”: they “get saved and they put on these great things,” and “then poof, they’re gone, because there’s no root.” He also says “a lot of churches preach that Christians don’t go through testing.”
What does he say “good ground” looks like?
He says they have “an honest heart,” “they’re not hiding any sins,” “if they make a mistake, they admit it,” and “they keep the word.”
What does he say happens when he witnesses to atheists?
He says he tells them “I can prove there’s a God” if they “obey the principles of this book,” and that when they pray about their sins “they start shaking” and “don’t want it to be real.”
Why does he compare rejecting the word to abortion?
He says Felix “aborted the word” after he “shook and he trembled,” “just like people abort babies today. They don’t want them, they’re inconvenient, and they abort them.”
What does he say the word “Christian” means?

He says the suffix “ian” means “to come from, belong to, or to follow,” so “a Christian follows Christ, period,” not “a Protestant denomination.” He says “I can be a Pentecostal, I can be a Baptist, I can be a Methodist, I can be a Catholic and follow Christ.”
What does he say happened in 1968?
He says “God poured out the Holy Ghost upon all the denominations,” and the denominations “kicked them out,” though the Catholics said “go ahead, do your thing in the back room.”
What does he mean by a “religionist”?
He says “religionist is someone that puts their opinions above the Scripture,” and “when you put your opinions or your denomination’s opinions above Scripture, you are a religionist.”
Does he say being a baby Christian is a problem?

No. He says “if you’re a baby, you’re a baby, there’s nothing wrong with that,” and “God looks at you and says that person is perfect” because “they’re right where they’re supposed to be at this time.”
Does he say Christians should see a doctor?
Yes. He says “God can heal, but if he doesn’t, you better get to a doctor,” citing Jesus: “They that are sick need a physician.”
What does he say about welfare?
He says “welfare is a bribe,” that it “should be connected with work,” and that “somebody has got to get this,” while saying “is there a time where people need help? Absolutely.”
What does he say it means to be a “baby Christian”?
He says “if you are number two … you are a born-again, probably a baby Christian, and there’s nothing wrong with being a baby Christian at all.”
How much time does he say God asks for each day?
He says “God asks for one hour of your day,” “in the Bible and in prayer,” and that people have “time to watch everything on TV” but are “busy satisfying your own agenda.”

items.d: In this session on present truth, Pastor David G. Kincer recaps the seasons of the last days and then turns to recognizing hatred and persecution. From John 15 and Second Timothy 3:12 he says believers are…
p: In this session on present truth, Pastor David G. Kincer recaps the seasons of the last days and then turns to recognizing hatred and persecution. From John 15 and Second Timothy 3:12 he says believers are hated for following Jesus and living godly, shows that John the Baptist, Jesus and Stephen were killed for speaking morally, recounts early martyrs, the Inquisition and modern persecution, and urges American Christians to stand for Bible morality.
What does it mean to be established in present truth?

He says God accomplishes his purposes in times and seasons, the children of Issachar understood God’s times, and Second Peter 1:12 says to be established in present truth. He recaps that we are in the last days, the salvation season, plural days in which God poured out his Spirit in 1900, 1948 and 1968, and in a 2,000-year season of false prophets and antichrists.
What does it mean to be established in present truth?

Again I’d like to thank you for coming and join us in another session of present truths. Remember we have found that God has a purpose under heaven and he accomplishes that in a time and a season First Corinthians 12:38 tells us the children of Issachar had understanding of God’s times God’s seasons to know what Israel ought to do and so if we’re going to be established in present truth as II Peter 1:12 says we need to know what present truth is. Remember. We found that we are living in the last days we’re in the last day season. Which is the salvation season people can come to Christ and be saved from their sins in this season the last days is plural there’s more than one day one season one happening in these last days and we don’t know how long they are. And he says I’ll pour out my spirit in those days plural again before the day singular of the Lord comes. And so God did he poured out his Holy Spirit in 1900 1948 1968. The last days. We also found were in the false prophet and the antichrist season. Present truth the present truth is we are living and we have been living for 2,000 years in the false prophet season and the antichrist season from the time Jesus began to preach there was false prophets even before that when he began to preach they were antichrist they that opposed Christ or antichrist he didn’t come in the flesh wasn’t born of a virgin didn’t rise from the dead or whatever.
What does it mean to be established in present truth?

1 Chronicles 12:32: of the sons of Issachar who had understanding of the times, to know what Israel ought to do, their chiefs were two hundred; and all their brethren were at their command; 2 Peter 1:12: For this reason I will not be negligent to remind you always of these things, though you know and are established in the present truth.
What are the clues of false prophets, and where does persecution start?

He recaps that false prophets say sin is okay, are in it for the money and behave immorally. He says Jesus’ followers are hated, and it starts in their own family: the more you want to serve God the more people separate from you, and it can branch out to persecution and martyrdom by all nations until the end.
What are the clues of false prophets, and where does persecution start?

And we found false prophet clues were they say sin is okay they’re in it for the money. They behave immorally. And we found that there’s a future projection. When some of these false prophets will do signs and wonders but we haven’t seen that yet. We found we’re in the season. The time where Jesus followers are hated they’re mistreated. And it starts in their own family. The more you want to serve God and do what’s right the more people want to separate from you your friends change and then it can branch out to persecution and even martyrdom. But. We found that all nations were going to persecute the church until the end.
Has the falling away already happened?

He says Christ could not have come before the 1500s because all nations were not yet known. He says the great falling away already happened in the dark ages, from 476 A.D. to around 1500, and end-time prophets troubling people that Jesus is coming any minute are doing what the Bible says not to be shaken by.
Has the falling away already happened?

And all nations were not discovered until the 1500s so God couldn’t have come before the 1500s because we didn’t know there was other nations out there and people who prophesied his coming before that missed it because they didn’t understand understand the scripture that we don’t know. That’s put in the hands of God and these things have to be fulfilled. We found we’re in the season of falling away. Has already happened. And will it happen again that’s up to God but we know in history there was a great falling away of the church of Christianity. Uh we call them the dark ages from 476 A.D. to around 1500 a little bit before. There was a tremendous falling away the church was very corrupt and it says don’t be troubled. By spirit or by word don’t be shaken in your mind that the day of the Lord is at hand let no man deceive you and this is what end time prophets are doing they’re just troubling the minds and the hearts of God’s people thinking that any minute Jesus is going to come when the Bible says don’t be shaken by these people don’t be shaken by these people. We also found that the gospel. Will be preached to all nations as a witness. And so we and then shall the end come so we know because of this scripture.
Has the falling away already happened?

2 Thessalonians 2:2-3: not to be soon shaken in mind or troubled, either by spirit or by word or by letter, as if from us, as though the day of Christ had come. Let no one deceive you by any means; for that Day will not come unless the falling away comes first, and the man of sin is revealed, the son of perdition,
Has the gospel been preached to all nations, and is knowledge increasing?

From Matthew 24:14 he says the gospel has not been preached to all nations as a witness, because if it had, the end would come. He says we are in the season of increasing knowledge since the printing press, and the book of Daniel was sealed until the time of the end, when the wise shall understand, so wisdom will be restored.
Has the gospel been preached to all nations, and is knowledge increasing?

The gospel has not been preached to all nations. Because if it has, the end comes. And that’s in Matthew 24:14. North and South America had not even been. Discovered till the 1500s Australia and the islands of the seas and so people who predicted the second coming before this time didn’t know what they were talking about because God has to fulfill these scriptures. Jesus said everything every jot and every tittle of the word will be fulfilled. We also found. That there will be an increase in knowledge. And we. Found that we are living in that season of increase in knowledge and technology industrial revolution the printing press being invented in 1440 just started changing everything where they used to hand write 40 pages a day now they could print 3600 pages a day books became cheap knowledge began to increase. And we’ve got to remember that the book was sealed until the time of the end even Daniel did not understand what God was talking about in Daniel 11 and 12. And he said I I hear you but I don’t understand it and he says this book is sealed up until the time of the end many will be purified made white and tried people are going to be saved people are going to be following God the wicked will do wickedly and none of the wicked shall understand but the wise shall understand so there’s going to be a restoration of wisdom so I’m going to be one of the things restored. We also found that restoration and refreshing times have come from the presence of the Lord in Acts 3. And there’s more to come. Till the end.
Has the gospel been preached to all nations, and is knowledge increasing?

Matthew 24:14: And this gospel of the kingdom will be preached in all the world as a witness to all the nations, and then the end will come. Matthew 5:18: For assuredly, I say to you, till heaven and earth pass away, one jot or one tittle will by no means pass from the law till all is fulfilled. Daniel 12:8-10: Although I heard, I did not understand. Then I said, “My lord, what shall be the end of these things?” And he said, “Go your way, Daniel, for the words are closed up and sealed till the time of the end. Many shall be purified, made white, and refined, but the wicked shall do wickedly; and none of the wicked shall understand, but the wise shall understand.
Why hasn’t Jesus come yet, and are disasters signs of the end?

He says Jesus has to remain in the heavens until all things are restored, so there is more to be done, and if you are dry and dead, let Jesus refresh you and restore the wasted years. He says wars, quakes, famines and plagues have been present since Jesus preached, but Jesus said “the end is not yet.”

p: Pastor David G. Kincer explains Bible sin from Cain and Abel: God rejected Cain’s evil works, not merely his produce offering. He distinguishes shadow, spiritual, wise and civil laws, names rejecting Christ as the hell-sending spiritual law, shows sin hurts neighbors more than it “hurts” God, and closes with Joseph’s refusal and Job’s repentance that turns captivity.

Genesis 4: Cain’s produce offering vs Abel’s flock; God respected Abel and his offering, not Cain. Leviticus 5:7–11 shows flour from the ground can be a sin offering, so rejection was not because fruit of the ground was invalid. Shadow offerings never took away sin (Hebrews 10:4); they pointed to Jesus the Lamb. Isaiah 1: God wants people to stop evil and learn to do good.

items.d: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer teaches from Isaiah 43 that God’s people are victorious in afflictions because God created, formed, redeemed and called them by name, and will be with them in the waters…
p: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer teaches from Isaiah 43 that God’s people are victorious in afflictions because God created, formed, redeemed and called them by name, and will be with them in the waters and the fire. He ties the waters to baptism, teaches that grace says no to ungodliness, and warns that living for Christ brings conflict. He ends with the hindrances to victory (not calling on God, impatience, forgotten offerings) and the invitation to “state your case” to God.
Why are God’s people victorious in afflictions?

He goes to Isaiah 43:1–3 and says God “directly makes four statements himself that explain, totally explain, why Christians are victorious in afflictions.” He defines afflictions as “misery, pain,” and says they can come through sickness, poverty, persecution, acts of war, acts of God, or be self-inflicted.
Why are God’s people victorious in afflictions?

Isaiah 18. Why God’s people are victorious in afflictions. We’re going to go to Isaiah chapter 43, verses 1 through 3, and we’re going to see there that God makes four statements. He directly makes four statements himself that explain, totally explain, why Christians are victorious in afflictions. Afflictions is misery, pain. And in the Bible, afflictions can come through sickness, poverty, persecution, acts of war, acts of God, or self-inflicted. How many you know, a lot of us go through our own afflictions, we self-inflict them. And so, but God’s people are going to be victorious in these things. Verse 1.
Why are God’s people victorious in afflictions?

Isaiah 43:1-3: But now, thus says the LORD, who created you, O Jacob, And He who formed you, O Israel: “Fear not, for I have redeemed you; I have called you by your name; You are Mine. When you pass through the waters, I will be with you; And through the rivers, they shall not overflow you. When you walk through the fire, you shall not be burned, Nor shall the flame scorch you. For I am the LORD your God, The Holy One of Israel, your Savior; I gave Egypt for your ransom, Ethiopia and Seba in your place.
What does it mean that God created and formed you?

He says the first statement, “created and formed you,” is in the New Testament “being born again”: “God personally comes to us when we come to him, and he births us by the Spirit and by the word.” He says Jesus is forming us into “the likeness, the character of Jesus Christ,” and “therefore we can handle afflictions.”
What does it mean that God created and formed you?

Number one, “Thus saith the Lord who,” number one, “created and formed you.” I created you. In the New Testament we call it being born again. “Anyone in Christ,” if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creature, a new creation, “all things are passed away, all things are made new.” Why? Because God personally comes to us when we come to him, and he births us by the Spirit and by the word, and we become a new creature, and therefore we can be victorious in afflictions. In Galatians 4:19, “I labor in birth again till Christ is formed in you.” You see, Jesus is forming us, and the Bible says in Corinthians that we come into the same image of Christ. “By the Spirit of the Lord” we are changed, transformed, metamorphosed into the same image of Christ. See, he’s fashioning us into his image, not your pastors, not the great mighty man of God in the earth, but we are fashioned unto the likeness, the character of Jesus Christ. And so therefore we can handle afflictions when they come, pain and poverty, whatever, whatever faces us, we can handle it, be victorious, because he, number one, has created us, and he, number two, has fashioned us and formed us. Then he says the second reason is, “Fear not.” Don’t be afraid, “for I have redeemed you.” Now I remember when I first read the Bible through, and I came to Isaiah, I understood a little bit about chapter one, I didn’t understand beans till I got to Hezekiah

2 Corinthians 5:17: Therefore, if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation; old things have passed away; behold, all things have become new. That’s where you just thank God, “Thank you, Lord.” “I will enter his gates with thanksgiving in my heart.” You see, the way into the presence of God is thanksgiving. Hebrews, the last chapter, says, “By him therefore let us offer the sacrifice of praise,” that thank offering, that peace offering, and then explains what it is: “the fruit of our lips giving thanks unto God.” If you are a silent saint, you’re not a growing saint. You got to learn to lift up your lips. It’s a sacrifice, because you don’t want to do it. Man, it was humiliating when they said, you know, “Lift your hands and, and, you know, praise God.” Oh gosh, this guy died a thousand deaths. But I had to get to the place where I wanted God or I wanted myself. Then you have the sin offering and the trespass offering, the guilt offering. How many know your sins are forgiven? How many still get some guilt over sin? Yeah. See, God knew that, so he had a guilt offering. He comes and kills the guilt that you haven’t let go of from the sin offering. You still feel guilty. Hallelujah, isn’t that good? Yeah. “And honor me by sacrifices,” which is the peace offering, the fruit of our lips. Now, this is hindrances to victory over afflictions. We won’t humble ourself and call on God. We get impatient with God when we’re doing our own thing. And we forget the burnt offering, Jesus can cleanse us and forgive us, and the praise offering. You burden God with your sins, you’re accepting sin in your life. That’s a hindrance to victory over afflictions. But God comes and he said, this is powerful, church, this is so powerful: “State your case, state your cause, that you may be acquitted,” set free. He says, you know, you got sin in you, you’re impatient with me, you won’t call upon me, so just come and state your case.
How do impatience with God and forgotten offerings hinder victory?

Hebrews 13:15: Therefore by Him let us continually offer the sacrifice of praise to God, that is, the fruit of our lips, giving thanks to His name. Psalm 100:4: Enter into His gates with thanksgiving, And into His courts with praise. Be thankful to Him, and bless His name.
What does it mean to “state your case” to God?

He reads “state your case, state your cause, that you may be acquitted,” and says “You got a complaint, don’t go to body members.” He tells of throwing down his guitar after a year without feeling God’s presence and listing what he was doing for God, and a still small voice said “It’s about time. You’re doing this all on your own strength,” after which peace and power came.
What does it mean to “state your case” to God?

All right, Moses stated his case. People, and all these people are, he stated his case, so what did God do? He came and gave himself the over 70 elders that caused him nothing but trouble for 40 years. And that’s what elders do in the church today, they are nothing but trouble if they are not a real elder, a Bible elder. They are nothing but trouble. They don’t have no spiritual growth to stand for righteousness and stand for truth at all, they just got a title. And that’s a good amen. Moses, when God wanted to destroy the people for sinning, he went and stated his case and said, “God, kill me instead of the people.” And what did God do? He saved the people. State your case. You got a complaint, don’t go to body members. We learned last Sunday that when we start [unclear] complaining, we’re on our way back to Egypt. That was good last Sunday. That’s a sign you’re on your way back to the old life. Go to Jesus and state your case, complain to him. I remember as a young man, I’ve used this before, I’d been saved about three or four years, and I was, man, I was ministering at the prisons, at the juvenile halls, on the street corners, door-to-door, I was doing all these things. I had my guitar, my banjo, I put in tune, I was ministering, really soon, you know, hallelujah. But almost a year went by and I had not felt the presence of God, and this day I had to go minister, and I’m getting songs together, and I know there’s nothing in the songs, I know there’s nothing in my message, I know there’s nothing, because I know when there’s something. And so I get mad at God. I threw my guitar down, broken, this was a thousand-dollar guitar back then. I mean, I was, I was stating my case like an idiot, but I was stating my case. And I went through the list, “Man, I’m saving souls, and I’m administering here, and I’m doing this, and I’m in the church, and I’m teaching Sunday school, and I’m leading the youth service, and I’m doing all this, and you’re not doing nothing.” That was my case. And that still small voice came to me and says, “It’s about time.” I said, “I quit, I quit.” He says, “It’s about time. You’re doing this all on your own strength, all in your own head knowledge. You left me back there. You need to get back with me.” And just the tremendous peace and power, God come on me, began to weep. See why? Because I stated my case, I complained to him, and he come and set me free from my own initiated affliction. Are you there, Jeff? So don’t complain to people. If you’ve got a complaint, go to him. He can set you free. Powerful. We, we, we’re in sin, and he’s going to free us from those sins, we’re impatient, and he’s going to free us from that impatience. Hallelujah. “Remember me, who blots out your sin, remember me.
What does it mean to “state your case” to God?
Isaiah 43:26: Put Me in remembrance; Let us contend together; State your case, that you may be acquitted.
What does he say to remember about God when we face afflictions?

He says “forget your pastor, forget your elders, forget the pope, forget the rabbis, remember who? Jesus Christ,” who can blot out your sin. He says God “created and formed you,” called you by name “so you don’t have to be afraid,” “he is not out to destroy you,” and “He will finish the good work he began in you.”
What does he say to remember about God when we face afflictions?

Don’t forget me.” Church, forget your pastor, forget your elders, forget the pope, forget the rabbis, remember who? Jesus Christ. “I can blot out your sin, I can do it.” Hallelujah. You know, we go through 12-step programs, seven-step programs, this kind of program, that kind of program, and Jesus is up in heaven’s, and, “Folks, remember me. I’m the one that can acquit you, I’m the one that can set you free, and I will if you state your case honestly before me. I will deliver you.” Remember, he can heal sicknesses, the physical sicknesses, the mental sicknesses, the emotional affliction. He can improve your poverty level. You can have peace in the middle of battles. Remember, God created and formed you, God is involved in this, he come to you personally and called you by name, so you don’t have to be afraid. He’s not out to destroy you. I don’t care how bad of a Christian you are, he is not out to destroy you. Do not be afraid. He will finish the good work he began in you. Be patient with yourself, be patient with others. He’s with us, and if he’s with us, we’ll get through anything. And for our charity, “I will deal with those that trouble you.” We may look like we’re losing the battle in America today, but there is coming a day of reckoning, and we want to be ready as righteous Christians in that day of reckoning. Amen. He will trouble those who trouble us, and we’ve got to state our case before God.
What does he say to remember about God when we face afflictions?

Isaiah 43:25: “I, even I, am He who blots out your transgressions for My own sake; And I will not remember your sins. Philippians 1:6: being confident of this very thing, that He who has begun a good work in you will complete it until the day of Jesus Christ;
Why does he compare being redeemed to buying a car?
He says “when you purchase a car you take care of it because it’s an investment.” He concludes “God’s going to want to take care of us, he’s purchased us, we’re his property.”
What did he see in China about baptism?
He says “over there they waited six months to a year to baptize them. Folks, that is not Bible.” He says he asked a lot of questions about how quickly someone should be baptized.
Does he say John the Baptist and Jesus both said to repent and be baptized?
He asks, “Did John the Baptist say, ‘Repent and be baptized for the remission of sin’?” and says “Jesus, when he came along,” said the same, and “he added one thing to it,” to believe the gospel.
How does he say he came to Christ?
He says an old man in an Assembly God church led him to Christ, taking him “right through the Scriptures.” He says “that load of sin went off of me that I didn’t even know I had.”
What does he mean by “get your baptism doctrine right”?

He says “we pass on error to other people, we read error and we pass on error without really finding out and experiencing these powers in God.” He says the presence of God in water baptism “is a powerful thing.”
What does he say about people who just join a church and say a prayer?
He says “you just say a little mechanical sinner’s prayer, you got nothing,” and “That’s how we become a new creature” by being born again, whatever the denomination.
What does he say was wrong with what he was first taught about suffering?
He says “they were teaching me wrong back there, the faith camp,” who said “nothing bad is going to happen.” He points to the lives of Jesus and the twelve apostles, who were afflicted.
Does he say you must witness door-to-door to be in conflict with the world?
No. He says “all you have to do is go through the day, live in your life for Christ, and you’re going to be at war with the enemy.”
Was he timid about sharing Christ?
He says “you may be too timid, like me, to share Christ with anybody. I broke that within a year.”
Whom does he say not to mess with?
He says “if they’re pursuing Jesus and righteousness, don’t mess with them. They may not believe everything you believe, but those two things are the priority things.”
Does he say being righteous by the blood of Christ is enough?
He says someone may say “I’m righteous by the blood of Christ,” and answers “that doesn’t help your wife you’re beating up.” He says real birth from God means “you do not continue in sin.”
Where does he say self-control comes from?
He says “Self-control comes from grace, as well as the Holy Spirit, as well as the Bible,” and that “self-control is just controlling yourself.”
What does he say about living for God in the present age?
He says to live “so that they see the light in you and come and inquire of your God,” and that “he wants you to make a difference now.” He says that is “much better than him coming a second time.”
What does he say the guilt offering is for?
He says God knew some still feel guilt after forgiveness, “so he had a guilt offering. He comes and kills the guilt that you haven’t let go of from the sin offering.”
What does he list as the hindrances to victory over afflictions?
He says “We won’t humble ourself and call on God. We get impatient with God when we’re doing our own thing. And we forget the burnt offering.”

items.d: Babylon’s occultists and intellectuals faced four young Hebrews. When the wise men couldn’t tell Nebuchadnezzar’s dream, Daniel asked for time, prayed and praised God who changes times and seasons. Humble and…
p: Babylon’s occultists and intellectuals faced four young Hebrews. When the wise men couldn’t tell Nebuchadnezzar’s dream, Daniel asked for time, prayed and praised God who changes times and seasons. Humble and unconcerned with credit, he revealed the statue of kingdoms.
The occult and intellectuals versus four young Hebrews whose possessions and temple were taken.

It’s a war between the occult and intellectual versus four young Hebrew Jews. Now, you must remember that God’s people have lost their jobs. They’ve lost the war. They’ve been taken captive to a foreign land. Those that left behind are starving, have diseases. Things are not looking too good for the people of God. They’re heavily taxed. Their possessions have been taken away as a spoil by the Babylonian army. Their temple has been desecrated. It looks like God does not have any power, the God of the Jews, to perform his promise to his people. It looks like it does not pay to serve God. It looks as if it’s all over for the nation of Israel and the Jewish religion. But God said that he would correct his people for sinning and Israel went into captivity because most of them, the majority, were sinning, disobeying God, violating scripture. And God said he would confront the unbeliever for their sins, the very people he uses to correct his people, he will confront and correct them. Now, this is the season we are in in America. It looks as though the church in America is losing the war of righteousness. Jesus is being put down and desecrated all the time and comedian by comedians and atheists and actors and everybody else. The Bible is being undermined and laughed at. And if we can watch what God does in the midst of this condition in Daniel, we will know what God can do in the future of America. Hallelujah. So, here we are. We have this condition. Now, watch what God does. You see, now people are proclaiming that God’s not involved in the affairs of mankind. Just like they’re saying today in America. But suddenly, God starts turning things around. And he starts by giving King Nebuchadnezzar a troubled dream that he cannot even remember the dream. But he orders all the magicians, the astrologers, the sorcerers, and the Chaldeans. The Chaldeans were the noted for being the wisest in that generation. He says, “You guys, you tell me my dream.” And they said, “Well, you tell us the dream and we’ll tell you the interpretation.” He said, “Uh-uh, I don’t remember the dream, but I want to know.” And he says, “You guys are going to die because you’re lousy counselors.

Daniel 2:1-2: Now in the second year of Nebuchadnezzar’s reign, Nebuchadnezzar had dreams; and his spirit was so troubled that his sleep left him. Then the king gave the command to call the magicians, the astrologers, the sorcerers, and the Chaldeans to tell the king his dreams. So they came and stood before the king.
Could the wise men tell the dream?
