items.t: Was the U.S. Supreme Court Fully Right About Studying The Bible?
items.d: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer reviews the 1980 Supreme Court line (quoting 1963) that the Bible may be used in studying history, civilization, ethics and comparative religion, then asks what the Court…
items.ser: Clarity on Crucial Choices · Full sermon
p: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer reviews the 1980 Supreme Court line (quoting 1963) that the Bible may be used in studying history, civilization, ethics and comparative religion, then asks what the Court missed: Jesus, eternal life, last-day judgment, the spirit world and true happiness. He applies 2 Peter’s “add to your faith” to civil crime, defines just government’s purpose, and cites midwives, Daniel, the apostles and John the Baptist as models for standing against unjust laws including Roe v. Wade and same-sex marriage.
What did the 1980 Supreme Court say about studying the Bible?

He says the 1980 decision, quoting 1963—two witnesses—declared the Bible may constitutionally be used in appropriate study of history, civilization, ethics (Bible morality), comparative religions, or the like.
What did the 1980 Supreme Court say about studying the Bible?

Today we’re going to ask this question: was the United States Supreme Court fully right about the constitutional right to study the Bible? We’re going to remind you of the 1980 Supreme Court decision that quoted from a 1963 Supreme Court decision—so thus two witnesses confirming. And this is what the Supreme Court said: the Bible may constitutionally be used in an appropriate study of history, civilization, ethics—what we know as morality, Bible morality—comparative religions, or the like. The Supreme Court thusly said it is constitutionally legal.
How does he say the Bible covers history, civilization and ethics?

He says Scripture records over 4,000 years from creation to 100 A.D., civilizations from pre-flood through Rome and Canaan’s peoples, and Bible morality summing Exodus through the prophets; comparative religion contrasts one holy God with sects and idolatry.
How does he say the Bible covers history, civilization and ethics?

History in the Bible: it’s true from creation to 100 A.D., or over 4,000 years of history. Civilization: the pre-flood civilizations to Abraham and the Hebrews, to the Assyrians, the Syrians, the Persians, the Greeks, the Roman Empire, and all the other civilizations that came with it—all the Canaanites and all the “-ites” in Canaan land. We have a recorded history of civilization. Ethics: as we have shown you, Bible morality sums up all the law—Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers, Deuteronomy and the prophets. Comparing religion: the Bible’s one holy God versus a sect, a group out of that group, and the doctrines of men which create sect groups in groups, and then idolatry,
What did the Court miss about Jesus?
From Luke 24:44 he says the Law, Prophets and Psalms concern Jesus—Exodus through Malachi and the Psalms wrote about Him—so Jesus is the first thing the Court’s list missed.
What did the Court miss about Jesus?

devils, the worship of devils, witchcraft, and animism—which is a spirit is in the rocks and the trees and everything—and even the evolutionists say that humans are part of nature. Now, what did the Supreme Court miss? See, they gave us these things, but what did they miss and just told us to deal with it? Well, Jesus, number one. And Luke 24:44: all things must be fulfilled which are written in the law of Moses and the prophets and the Psalms concerning Me. So Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers, Deuteronomy, Isaiah, Jeremiah down to Malachi and all the prophets in between wrote about Jesus, and 150 Psalms wrote about Jesus.
What did the Court miss about Jesus?

Luke 24:44: Then He said to them, “These are the words which I spoke to you while I was still with you, that all things must be fulfilled which were written in the Law of Moses and the Prophets and the Psalms concerning Me.”
What about eternal life and last-day judgment?

From John 5:39 he says the Scriptures testify of Jesus, the door to eternal life. From Matthew 12:36 and Revelation 20:12 he says idle words and works are recorded for judgment—the Court overlooked that.
What about eternal life and last-day judgment?

Eternal life. John 5:39: search the Scriptures, the Bible; in them you think you have eternal life, and they testify of Me. The Scriptures tell us about life after death. And you won’t come to Me that you might have life. So not only is there eternal life, but the door to eternal life is Jesus Christ. The last-day judgment they overlooked. Matthew 12:36: every idle word men shall speak they will give an account in the day of judgment—and thus just idle words. But in Revelation 20:12, at the great white throne judgment, they were judged according to their works, their behavior, written in the books. God’s keeping a record of our speech and of our behavior.
What about eternal life and last-day judgment?

John 5:39: You search the Scriptures, for in them you think you have eternal life; and these are they which testify of Me. Matthew 12:36: But I say to you that for every idle word men may speak, they will give account of it in the day of judgment. Revelation 20:12: And I saw the dead, small and great, standing before God, and books were opened. And another book was opened, which is the Book of Life. And the dead were judged according to their works, by the things which were written in the books.
Who judges, and what spirit world does the Bible describe?
John 5:22: the Father gives all judgment to the Son. He says the Court also missed God as Spirit, the Holy Spirit, ministering angels, cherubim and seraphim, demons and Satan.
Who judges, and what spirit world does the Bible describe?

In John 5:22, the Father judges no one but gives all judgment to the Son. So Jesus is what the Bible talks about. Jesus is the door to eternal life, and Jesus is the one we are going to have to give an account to of the words that we speak and the lifestyle that we lead. They also missed that the Bible talks about the spirit world. For instance, God is a Spirit, an invisible Spirit; the Holy Spirit is a Spirit; angels are ministering spirits; cherubim and seraphim are creatures of the spirit world; demons and Satan are spirits.
Who judges, and what spirit world does the Bible describe?
John 5:22: For the Father judges no one, but has committed all judgment to the Son,
What does the Bible say about happiness the Court missed?
From Psalm 144:15, happy is the people whose God is the Lord; John 16:22, joy no one can take; Acts 5:41, apostles rejoicing after being beaten—joy circumstances cannot take away.
What does the Bible say about happiness the Court missed?

Witchcraft: except for drugs and witchcraft of the flesh, the Bible says there’s three sources of witchcraft, but one of them source is demonic. The next thing they missed is happiness. Everybody is looking for happiness, and the Bible says in Psalms 144:15, happy is the people whose God is the Lord. John 16:22: Jesus summed it up and says your joy, your happiness, no one can take from you. That’s how powerful it is in the Bible. Acts 5:41: we have proof of that. The apostles were beaten, and after they were beaten they departed rejoicing that they were counted worthy to suffer shame for His name. So we actually see a fulfillment of joy that people could not take away and circumstances could not take away.
What does the Bible say about happiness the Court missed?

Psalm 144:15: Happy are the people who are in such a state; Happy are the people whose God is the LORD! John 16:22: Therefore you now have sorrow; but I will see you again and your heart will rejoice, and your joy no one will take from you. Acts 5:41: So they departed from the presence of the council, rejoicing that they were counted worthy to suffer shame for His name.
How does the Declaration tie to Bible happiness and escaping judgment?

He reads life, liberty and the pursuit of happiness as a right to Bible happiness, then says escaping the lake of fire means faith in Jesus, confessing sin, repenting, water baptism, and adding virtue to faith—even for humanists and atheists.
How does the Declaration tie to Bible happiness and escaping judgment?

Now the Declaration of Independence, by the way, gives us the right to Bible happiness. “We hold these truths to be self-evident, that all men were created equal,” and they were endowed by their Creator with certain unchangeable rights, and among these rights are life, liberty and the pursuit of happiness. Happy is the people whose God is the Lord—a joy that no situation and nobody can take away. Another thing they missed is how to escape the lake of fire judgment. We’ve told you this before: I believe and have faith in Jesus. You’ve got to admit you’re wrong, confess your sin, confess your crimes. You’ve got to repent and turn from those wrong. You’ve got to be baptized in water. And then you need to grow. Growing to this aspect: you’ve got to add to your faith. I don’t care if you’re a humanist or an atheist—whatever you believe in, you have no excuse not to add to your faith virtue or moral excellence
What must you add to your faith, and what is the promise?
He lists moral excellence, knowledge, self-control, patience, godliness and love that does no harm. From 2 Peter 1:10, if you do these things you will never fall—responsibility after you’re saved.
What must you add to your faith, and what is the promise?

and knowledge about moral excellence, and self-control that you behave moral excellently, and patience with yourself and others while they’re attaining moral excellence, godliness—that’s such a respect for God that you obey His moral word—and a love that does no harm to his neighbor. We have to add these things because we didn’t get them when we were saved. 2 Peter 1:10 is where these “add to your faith” come from, and Peter said there, if you do these things you will never, never fall. So see, we’ve got to add these things. It’s our responsibility to add moral excellence and the knowledge of it and self-control and patience to our life.
What must you add to your faith, and what is the promise?
2 Peter 1:10: Therefore, brethren, be even more diligent to make your call and election sure, for if you do these things you will never stumble;
How do these principles apply to civil crime?
Sin violates God’s law; crime violates a nation’s law. James 5:19: turning a sinner from error saves a soul from death. 1 Peter 2:13: submit to every ordinance for the Lord’s sake.
How do these principles apply to civil crime?

Now these same principles will work in civil crimes. Sin is a violation of God’s law; crime is a violation of a nation’s law—same word, same terminology. In James 5:19 it says if anyone wanders from the truth, he who turns a sinner, a criminal, from the error of his way shall save a soul from death. And so the objective is to turn that criminal from their way and save them from a physical death possibly here, or physical destruction, and especially eternal destruction. 1 Peter chapter 2:13: submit to every ordinance, every law of man for the Lord’s sake, whether to the king as supreme, or to governors as those who are sent by the king for the punishment
How do these principles apply to civil crime?

James 5:19-20: Brethren, if anyone among you wanders from the truth, and someone turns him back, let him know that he who turns a sinner from the error of his way will save a soul from death and cover a multitude of sins. 1 Peter 2:13: Therefore submit yourselves to every ordinance of man for the Lord’s sake, whether to the king as supreme,
What is the Bible purpose of just government?
From 1 Peter 2 he says government punishes those who harm others and themselves, corrects criminals toward a moral life, and removes from society those who refuse to change.
What is the Bible purpose of just government?

of evildoers and the praise of those that do good. And so civil government is designed to correct the criminal, to turn them from the error of their ways. To sum it up: the Bible purpose of a just government is to punish those that harm others and themselves, and the purpose of punishment is to correct the criminals so they may lead a good moral life, and if they refuse to be corrected, remove them from society. If they refuse to change their ways they shouldn’t be allowed to hurt people anymore. Again, these same principles work in civil crimes, the civil world.
What is the Bible purpose of just government?
1 Peter 2:14: or to governors, as to those who are sent by him for the punishment of evildoers and for the praise of those who do good.
What if the law or officials are bad?
He first says believe in a just system, admit crime is wrong, add moral excellence and obey just laws—but then asks what to do when law or officials are bad.
What if the law or officials are bad?

We must believe and have faith in a just judicial system and its officials. We must admit that crime is wrong. We must turn from that which is wrong and add to our faith moral excellence, the knowledge of moral excellence, self-control so we can operate moral excellence, patience while we’re getting there—or to ourself and others—and a respect for government, a just government, to obey just laws, and love others by not harming them. And if the criminal will not change, they’ve got to be removed from society. What do we do when the law or officials are bad?
Who stood against bad slave and related laws in America?
He cites Declaration signers’ losses, [unclear] Lee imprisoned 25 years, Jonathan Walker branded “slave stealer,” Quakers from 1678, and Thomas Garrett fined heavily yet still helping slaves.
Who stood against bad slave and related laws in America?

We need to do good, like people did when the slave laws and the Indian laws and the separate-but-equal laws and the women-inferior laws were bad. Remember the signers of the Declaration of Independence: 12 of them lost their homes, they were burned to the ground; nine died in the war of independence; five were captured and tortured mercilessly. They paid a price for taking a stand for what was right. A person by the name of [unclear] Lee was imprisoned 25 years for helping slaves escape. Jonathan Walker was branded with SS on his hand—“slave stealer”—by, in court, a burning on an iron. He was scarred for life and fined and imprisoned. Quakers were the first in 1678 to stand up against slavery and against women inferiority, and it took over a hundred years of them preaching it and living it for America to finally catch on. Other people were fined. Thomas Garrett was fined $165,000 in today’s money and kept on helping slaves.
What Bible examples of civil disobedience does he give?

Hebrew midwives would not abort babies; Daniel prayed when prayer was banned; the apostles kept preaching Jesus despite censorship, saying obey God rather than man. He applies that to standing against Roe v. Wade.
What Bible examples of civil disobedience does he give?

So we’ve got to disobey laws and stand up against corrupt officials that want to enforce them. In the Bible the midwives would not abort Hebrew babies, and God saw that act and blessed them with a family of their own. He did good to them for not aborting babies. And we have a right to stand up against Roe versus Wade and the abortion of babies because adults lack self-control. Daniel prayed when the law said you can’t pray. When the law was passed he went and prayed publicly, and he was sentenced to be executed in the lion’s den, and God intervened. The apostles who rejected the censorship of the Scriptures and speech—they said don’t you talk about Jesus from the Scriptures anymore—they were beaten, they were killed and they were jailed, and they said whether we ought to obey God or man, you decide.
What Bible examples of civil disobedience does he give?

Exodus 1:17: But the midwives feared God, and did not do as the king of Egypt commanded them, but saved the male children alive. Daniel 6:10: Now when Daniel knew that the writing was signed, he went home. And in his upper room, with his windows open toward Jerusalem, he knelt down on his knees three times that day, and prayed and gave thanks before his God, as was his custom since early days. Acts 5:29: But Peter and the other apostles answered and said: “We ought to obey God rather than men.
Why does he mention John the Baptist and same-sex marriage?

He says John was beheaded for preaching repentance and baptism and for disapproving Herod’s marriage to his brother’s wife, and that America likewise has a right to stand against same-sex marriage and for right morality.
Why does he mention John the Baptist and same-sex marriage?

John the Baptist was beheaded because he preached salvation of repentance and water baptism, and he publicly disapproved of Herod’s marriage to his brother’s wife. And we have a right to stand against same-sex marriage in America. We need to do what other good people did both in the Bible and in our nation’s history and stand for right laws and stand for right morality in America.
Why does he mention John the Baptist and same-sex marriage?
Mark 6:18: Because John had said to Herod, “It is not lawful for you to have your brother’s wife.”
Why does he call 1980 and 1963 “two witnesses”?
He says the 1980 decision quoted the 1963 decision, so two witnesses confirm the Bible may be used in those studies.
What is animism as he defines it?
He says animism is the idea that a spirit is in the rocks and the trees and everything, and links evolutionists saying humans are part of nature.
Who is the door to eternal life?
He says not only is there eternal life, but the door to eternal life is Jesus Christ.
From Matthew 12:36 he says every idle word will be accounted for in the day of judgment, and Revelation 20:12 judges works written in the books.
How many sources of witchcraft does he mention?
He says the Bible gives three sources of witchcraft, one of them demonic, besides drugs and witchcraft of the flesh.
He says if you do these things—add to your faith—you will never, never fall.
What is the difference between sin and crime?
He says sin is a violation of God’s law; crime is a violation of a nation’s law—same word, same terminology.
What is the purpose of punishment?
He says to correct criminals so they may lead a good moral life, and if they refuse, remove them from society so they can’t hurt people anymore.
Who was Jonathan Walker in his account?
He says Walker was branded SS—“slave stealer”—with a burning iron in court, scarred for life, fined and imprisoned.
How does he link the Hebrew midwives to Roe v. Wade?
He says the midwives would not abort Hebrew babies and God blessed them, so we have a right to stand against Roe v. Wade because adults lack self-control.

items.t: Was There A Beginning Before Genesis?
items.d: A short clip gathering scriptures that point to a beginning before Genesis 1: Christ the beginning, the Lamb slain from the foundation of the world, and believers chosen in Him before it.
p: A short clip gathering scriptures that point to a beginning before Genesis 1: Christ the beginning, the Lamb slain from the foundation of the world, and believers chosen in Him before it.
Was there a beginning before Genesis 1?
Yes—Jesus is the beginning and the end, the beginning of the creation of God.
Was there a beginning before Genesis 1?

We have found scriptural evidence that there was a beginning before Genesis 1 beginning when God created the heavens and the earth we found in the scriptures that Jesus said I am the beginning and I am the end I am the first and I am the last all these are found in Revelations. These things says the amen the faithful and true witness the beginning of the creation of God Jesus was the beginning his birth foretold his death foretold for the sins of the world at the very beginning of creation in Colossians chapter 1 he says Christ is the head of the body the church who is the beginning.
Was there a beginning before Genesis 1?

Revelation 22:13: I am the Alpha and the Omega, the Beginning and the End, the First and the Last.” Revelation 3:14: “And to the angel of the church of the Laodiceans write, ‘These things says the Amen, the Faithful and True Witness, the Beginning of the creation of God: Colossians 1:18: And He is the head of the body, the church, who is the beginning, the firstborn from the dead, that in all things He may have the preeminence.
What was decided before the foundation of the world?
The Lamb slain; Christ predetermined to die for our sins, revealed in these last times.
What was decided before the foundation of the world?

Again in Revelations the lamb was slain from the foundation of the world also in Matthew 13 I shall declare things hidden before the foundation of the world. And again in first Peter 1:18. You were redeemed with the precious blood of Christ a lamb without blemish without spot. Who truly was predetermined before the foundation of the world before the foundation before the creation of the world he was predetermined to come and die for our sins he was made plain, made manifest in these last times to us.
What was decided before the foundation of the world?

Revelation 13:8: All who dwell on the earth will worship him, whose names have not been written in the Book of Life of the Lamb slain from the foundation of the world. Matthew 13:35: that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the prophet, saying: “I will open My mouth in parables; I will utter things kept secret from the foundation of the world.” 1 Peter 1:18-20: knowing that you were not redeemed with corruptible things, like silver or gold, from your aimless conduct received by tradition from your fathers, but with the precious blood of Christ, as of a lamb without blemish and without spot. He indeed was foreordained before the foundation of the world, but was manifest in these last times for you
God chose us in Christ before the foundation of the world, and the Father loved Jesus then.

He God chose us in him Christ. Before the foundation of the world Ephesians 1:4. And in John 17:24 Jesus was praying to the father and said father you loved me before the foundation of the world so there was a beginning before the Genesis 1 beginning and we have solid scriptural evidence of that.

Ephesians 1:4: just as He chose us in Him before the foundation of the world, that we should be holy and without blame before Him in love, John 17:24: “Father, I desire that they also whom You gave Me may be with Me where I am, that they may behold My glory which You have given Me; for You loved Me before the foundation of the world.
The beginning and the end, the first and the last.
The head of the body, the church, who is the beginning.
Was His birth and death foretold at the beginning?
Yes, at the very beginning of creation.
From the foundation of the world.
Things hidden from the foundation of the world.
Before the foundation of the world.
When did the Father love Jesus?
Before the foundation of the world.

items.d: In this short message on Bible morality the speaker says forgiveness of sin has four parts: repent, be water baptized, confess that Jesus and the Bible are true, and believe. He ties baptism to Romans 6 and…
p: In this short message on Bible morality the speaker says forgiveness of sin has four parts: repent, be water baptized, confess that Jesus and the Bible are true, and believe. He ties baptism to Romans 6 and Colossians 2, uses Romans 10:9, 1 John 1:9 and the burned books of Acts 19, and closes with a prayer for becoming a Christian.
What does he mean by “Bible morality,” and why does he say it is under attack?

He defines Bible morality as “the right and wrong standards by way of honesty and truth,” and says that in present-day America some want “to make it illegal.” He says the “warriors” are “courageous fighters for Bible morality” who are “not afraid of the Bible morality bullies.”
What does he mean by “Bible morality,” and why does he say it is under attack?

Bible morality again is the topic we’re going to be dealing with today. And. This Bible morality is the right and wrong standards. By way of honesty and truth. And present-day America. And how it is in present-day America it’s banned by wimps or too weak to fight against Bible morality bullies. They want to make it illegal these Bible morality bullies they want to make it so that it is not acceptable anywhere in America but the warriors carried on their shoulder the warriors are courageous fighters for Bible morality and they’re not afraid of the Bible morality bullies.
How important is water baptism, and when should a person be baptized?

He says Peter said to “repent and be baptized every one of you… for the remission of sins,” so “number one we repent number two we get water baptized.” He says the Pharisees and lawyers “rejected the will of God” by not being baptized, and in Acts 8 people were baptized “when they believe,” not after “some great spiritual growth.”
How important is water baptism, and when should a person be baptized?

We’re going to take a look today at water baptism and confession in Acts chapter 2 verse 38 remember Peter said repent and be baptized every one of you. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ for the remission of sins in Mark 1:4 John the Baptist preached the baptism of repentance for the remission of sins so number one we repent number two we get water baptized for the remission of sin how important is water baptism in Luke 7:30 the Bible says the Pharisees and lawyers rejected the will of God for themselves not being baptized by him so it is important we don’t want to reject the will of God Acts 8:12 when they believe Philip preaching the things concerning the kingdom of God and the name of Jesus Christ they were baptized both men and women when were they baptized when they believe they didn’t wait for some great spiritual growth or anything else you see they accepted the will of God for themselves in Romans chapter 6 verses 3 through 7.
How important is water baptism, and when should a person be baptized?

Acts 2:38: Then Peter said to them, “Repent, and let every one of you be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ for the remission of sins; and you shall receive the gift of the Holy Spirit. Mark 1:4: John came baptizing in the wilderness and preaching a baptism of repentance for the remission of sins. Luke 7:30: But the Pharisees and lawyers rejected the will of God for themselves, not having been baptized by him. Acts 8:12: But when they believed Philip as he preached the things concerning the kingdom of God and the name of Jesus Christ, both men and women were baptized.
What does water baptism picture? (Romans 6 and Colossians 2)

He says “we went into the grave when we went into the water” and “when we come out of the water the resurrection,” so we “should walk in newness of life.” He says baptism is “the circumcision” by Jesus, where “God does an operation in your life in water baptism.”
What does water baptism picture? (Romans 6 and Colossians 2)

The writer of Romans talks about water baptism and relating it to the death of our old sinful nature as many of us as were baptized unto Jesus Christ were baptized unto his death we went into the grave when we went into the water as Christ was raised from the dead when we come out of the water the resurrection. We should walk in newness of life. Knowing this that the old man is crucified with him that the body of sin might be destroyed that from this time forth that water baptism we should not serve sin for he that is dead is free from sin now again in Colossians it is backed up and Jesus you were circumcised without hands by putting off of the body of sins of the flesh by the circumcision of Christ how did Christ circumcise us buried with him in baptism see baptism is the circumcision raise with him by faith in the operation of God God does an operation in your life in water baptism when he circumcises you you being dead in your trespasses and uncircumcision of your flesh he has made alive haven’t forgiven you
What does water baptism picture? (Romans 6 and Colossians 2)

Romans 6:3-7: Or do you not know that as many of us as were baptized into Christ Jesus were baptized into His death? Therefore we were buried with Him through baptism into death, that just as Christ was raised from the dead by the glory of the Father, even so we also should walk in newness of life. For if we have been united together in the likeness of His death, certainly we also shall be in the likeness of His resurrection, knowing this, that our old man was crucified with Him, that the body of sin might be done away with, that we should no longer be slaves of sin. p: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer teaches from Isaiah 59:19 that the enemy comes in like a flood and the Spirit of the Lord lifts up a standard against him. He lists philosophies he says oppose God, then shows from Genesis and the flood that God makes a way of escape, and urges the church to warn people.
What does Isaiah 59:19 mean when the enemy comes in like a flood, and what defeats him?

He says there is “an enemy against God and an enemy against the Word,” and a flood “does nothing but damage.” He says the church is “trying to do this stuff on their own,” but the key to defeating the enemy is the Spirit: “the Spirit will lift up a standard against him.”
What does Isaiah 59:19 mean when the enemy comes in like a flood, and what defeats him?

We neglect, we disregard many priority doctrines, and one of these is Isaiah 59:19. Isaiah 59:19 says, “When the enemy comes in like a flood.” Number one, the enemy. We have an enemy. There is an enemy against God and an enemy against the Word, and when the enemy comes in like a flood (and all of us know a flood does nothing but damage; when you hear the word “flood,” you know there is damage, you know the water is out of control). Secondly, “the Spirit of the Lord will lift up a...” The Spirit of the Lord. Now, folks, this is where we’re missing it. The church is trying to do this stuff on their own. If we could have done it on our own, why we have needed Jesus? Why would we need the Holy Ghost? And it’s amazing, we start out right, we get saved and we start out right, and then we start leaning on ourself and on our own knowledge and understanding, but the key to defeating the enemy is what? The Spirit. The Spirit that everybody in America is arguing about, that’s the very part of God that will defeat your enemies. Good place for an amen. Amen means so be it. How many need your enemies defeated? Yeah, opposition. Yes, and they’re bigger than you are. You know, “the Spirit will lift up a standard against him.” Now, the word “standard” is not talking about a banner. There, when we worshiped God this morning and they talked about raising the banner, you notice I went over and got a banner, and the song said to raise the banner, so I, “Give me a banner.” I don’t have to wait for permission. They got the song, I just do what it says. Can I hear an amen? You say, “Well, that might not be in order.” Well, then don’t sing the song.
What does Isaiah 59:19 mean when the enemy comes in like a flood, and what defeats him?

Isaiah 59:19: So shall they fear The name of the LORD from the west, And His glory from the rising of the sun; When the enemy comes in like a flood, The Spirit of the LORD will lift up a standard against him.
What does “the Spirit will lift up a standard” mean, and does God make a way of escape?

He says “standard” has two meanings: to flee or escape, and to attack the enemy. He says whether God flees the enemy or causes you to flee, “He is going to move on your behalf,” and that “there is no temptation come upon anybody” that God will not make a way of escape from.
What does “the Spirit will lift up a standard” mean, and does God make a way of escape?

If you don’t want me lifting up a banner, then don’t sing the song. You don’t want me dancing, then don’t sing a song that says dance. Because this guy has learned the key is to obey the Scriptures, not just sing them, not just memorize them, but obey them. Is that a good place for us? So be it. Yeah. Now, the standard here has two meanings. You know, just like the word “bear,” b-e-a-r, in our language has several meanings: bear, an animal, grizzly bear, brown bear. It also means to carry: “I will bear that.” It also means falling prices: we got a bear market or a bear economy, things are falling down. Or it means to produce fruit. Jesus said, “I wish that you bear fruit and that your fruit remain.” See, it’s producing something. And so the standard here has two meanings: to flee, to escape, to take flight, to depart (and, uh, that’s us escaping from the enemy). The second meaning is different: it’s attacking the enemy. It means to fly to the attack, to put to flight. See, and the Spirit is going to lift up a standard against who? The enemy, him, the enemy. And He’s going to make a way of escape. And you know, the Bible says in the New Testament that there is no temptation come upon anybody that’s not common to man, that God will make a way of escape that you might bear up under it. You can handle it. Whether God flees the enemy or whether God causes you to flee, He is going to move on your behalf. All right, we got that part now. See, what’s the important thing in this verse? The Spirit. I can’t do this. I learned as a young believer I couldn’t do this stuff on my own. You know, as a young believer people would make fun of me because I claimed to be a Christian and I was making mistakes. Say, “I said I’m going to go to church with a bunch of hypocrites anyway.” I said, “Well, at least we’re going.” I said, “Is a Marine, when he enters the base the first day, is he really a Marine? The next week, is he a Marine? The next two weeks, is he a Marine?” No, he’s not a Marine till he passes and gets the standard, the U.S. standard, to be a Marine. He’s a Marine. I said, “Yes, we’re in church, and we’re learning how to be a Christian, but at least we’re there learning.” Can I hear an amen? Yeah. We got our flaws, we got our m— but we’re there, we’re trying to be like Him. We want that stamp to be like Him.
What does “the Spirit will lift up a standard” mean, and does God make a way of escape?

1 Corinthians 10:13: No temptation has overtaken you except such as is common to man; but God is faithful, who will not allow you to be tempted beyond what you are able, but with the temptation will also make the way of escape, that you may be able to bear it.
Is it safe to seek the Holy Ghost, and does the church help me grow? (Psalm 92:13)

He says most Pentecostals “only experience putting our finger in the socket” and did not learn to channel it, yet “at least we felt the power of God.” He says “I don’t have to be afraid of the Holy Ghost because somebody botches it up,” and that the church will cause him to grow.
Is it safe to seek the Holy Ghost, and does the church help me grow? (Psalm 92:13)

Hallelujah. And these people that want to argue about the Holy Ghost, listen, I told you last week, us Pentecostals, most of us only experience putting our finger in the socket. We didn’t learn how to channel it. But what I tell my adversaries that’s against the Holy Ghost: at least we put our finger in the socket. At least we felt the power of God, right? Amen. Hallelujah. And then we can learn how to channel it. Now, that’s good stuff. Church, I don’t have to be afraid of the Holy Ghost because somebody botches it up, and I don’t have to be afraid of God fulfilling His word that in the church I can grow. “They that be planted in the house of the Lord shall” what? Flourish “in the courts of our God.” The church will cause me to grow. It’s a principle of God. So I’m going, and I’m one of the hypocrites, but in the end we’re going to be in His likeness. Somewhere I’m going to grow up.
Is it safe to seek the Holy Ghost, and does the church help me grow? (Psalm 92:13)
Psalm 92:13: Those who are planted in the house of the LORD Shall flourish in the courts of our God.
Who do we wrestle against, and what does he say about atheists? (Ephesians 6:12)

He says we are attacking the philosophies, not the people: “we wrestle not against flesh and blood, but against principalities and powers,” the principles of men that try to capture our mind. He then lists the first opposing philosophy, atheism, saying that “when you speak something that’s against God, you are an enemy.”
Who do we wrestle against, and what does he say about atheists? (Ephesians 6:12)

Hallelujah. Now, we need that standard lifted up in America. We have more than seven opposing philosophies. It’s the philosophies that we are attacking back. It’s the philosophies that we need to lift up a standard against. It’s not the people. “We wrestle not against flesh and blood, but against principalities and powers and spiritual wickedness in high places.” We wrestle against the principles of men that try to capture our mind. Paul said a person can be a good person, but if he’s got a few flaws, he’s opposing God. We have to, with the Word, try to correct that stuff. Can I hear an amen? And so first we have the atheists, who don’t believe there is a God. They say there is no God. There’s 2% of the population is atheist. How many percent? 2%. Did they get the Bible out of public schools? Yeah. You call that a democracy? 2% got the Bible out of public schools. That’s not a democracy. A democracy is the majority rules. Just letting you think all right. They say that humanity is the absolute total source of ethics and values. Individuals themselves can resolve moral problems. We don’t need a God. There is no life after death, there is no lake of fire, there is no judgment after death, you just go to the grave, and there are some churches who believe that nonsense. All right, atheist. So that opposes God. See, when you speak something that’s against God, you are an enemy, you are opposing, you hate God, and that’s when I’m out there debating you, who hear me lift my voice and I tell them like it is: “You are haters.” Why? Because they’re opposing God. “You are bashers.” Why? They’re bashing the Bible. They’re bashing. I just tell them what they are. I’m just telling them the truth. “Well, as Christians, you shouldn’t do that.” Oh, and where do you find that twisted scripture in the Bible? Are you out there? You may not be able to reach your enemy, but those that hear you may get convicted and learn and change. All right, then we have the hedonist. Pleasure is the highest good. Whatever causes pleasure is right. Whatever makes you happy is right.
Who do we wrestle against, and what does he say about atheists? (Ephesians 6:12)

Ephesians 6:12: For we do not wrestle against flesh and blood, but against principalities, against powers, against the rulers of the darkness of this age, against spiritual hosts of wickedness in the heavenly places.
What does he say about hedonists and liberals?

He says the hedonist holds that “whatever makes you happy is right,” and he says some Christians believe that. He says “everybody should get their fair share” opposes Scripture, since “if you don’t work you don’t eat,” and that making people “a slave to welfare” takes away their drive. He says church liberals deny that Jesus is God and born of a virgin.
What does he say about hedonists and liberals?

Right. So if I want to go out on my wife, and I feel good about it, I, man, it gives me pleasure, it’s got to be right. If I want to go steal somebody’s car and take a ride down Main Street and I’m happy, it’s got to be right. Are you there? And there’s Christians that believe that. The third one is a liberalist. Now, liberals, there’s two sources of them: they’re in the church and secular. Secular means non-spiritual, no spirit in the secular. For instance, we hear it all the time, “Everybody should get their fair share.” Well, that really opposes the Scripture. If you don’t work, you don’t eat. So that’s what an enemy. Hallelujah. Sounds really humane, sounds very compassionate, but when you make people a slave to welfare and they lose their ambition, they lose their drive, and they lose that exercising of working, we’re opposing the Bible, and that’s an enemy. Are you there? And they say they care. Obama says it’s care. “We’re humanitarian, we care.” No, it’s hate. See, if you really cared for them, you would make a way for them to get a job and work. Hallelujah. Somebody’s got to teach this stuff. Then there is the church liberals. Jesus is not God, He’s not born of a virgin, there is no judgment after death because God is love and He can hurt no one. See, that’s in the church. That’s the liberal part of the church. Are you with me? And we need to understand these philosophies and not be destroyed by them and captured by them. Humanists. Humanists are much like atheists, and by the way, the liberals are 23% of the American population. 23%, and they’re running things. It’s not a democracy at all. Uh, humanists are 16%. There is no God, the universe is self-existing, it was not created, man is part of nature, he emerged by evolution. In other words, we come from a rock. Now, that sounds about as [unclear] science as Brooklyn talks like she knows what she’s doing. My two-year-old granddaughter. Just because you say something doesn’t make it science, does it? What’s the word for science? Knowledge. It’s knowledge. It’s just the word for knowledge.
What does he say about hedonists and liberals?
2 Thessalonians 3:10: For even when we were with you, we commanded you this: If anyone will not work, neither shall he eat.
What does he say about humanists and Christian children in public schools?

He says humanists believe there is no God and “no right and wrong,” and want to “get rid of all authority over anyone’s life.” He says they took their battle to the public schools, and he says Christians who put their kids there are “opening yourself up for losing your children at a very high rate.”
What does he say about humanists and Christian children in public schools?

All right, there is no right and wrong. Morals come by human experience, whatever. If it feels good to it, you don’t need a theological, a moral, or political authority. See, they want to get rid of all authority over anyone’s life telling them what to do. That’s the humanist. And they said they would take their battle to the public schools in the ‘40s, and they did, and they won in the public schools. And Christians who put their kids in public schools are insane. You are opening yourself up for losing your children at a very high rate. Christians that go to public school, 75% of them leave the faith when they get out of school. Now, 50% of them come back, but why lose it? 75% who are raised in a good example, Christian home and they go to a good Christian school and taught and learn the principles of God, 75% of them stay in the faith. A big switch. Huh. Hallelujah.
What does he mean by a “religionist”?

He says a religionist “follows their specific religious organizations or personal beliefs above the Bible and Jesus,” and “will defend their denomination above Jesus Christ Himself.” He gives his own estimate of 85% of the Christian world in America, and tells of a woman who said “I don’t care what the Bible says” and said she would follow her church leader.
What does he mean by a “religionist”?

Uh, religionist. Religionist, from my prediction (this is me, there’s no statistic on this), is 85% of the Christian world in America. A religionist is one who follows their specific religious organizations or personal beliefs above the Bible and Jesus. They will defend their personal beliefs, they will defend their denomination above Jesus Christ Himself and the Bible. I told you before, I had a woman tell me once, when I said, “The Bible says,” she said, “I don’t care what the Bible says,” because her church leader was a phony and I was telling her why that guy was doing things that was against Scripture, and she said, “I don’t care what the Bible says. That’s a man of God, and I’m going to follow him.” We’re not told to follow a man. Who are we told to follow? Jesus. Come on, church.
What does he say about evolution and people who say the Bible is a lie?

He says only 15% of Americans believe in evolution, according to a poll he cites, and that evolutionists “say the Bible’s a lie.” He says Christians “have to oppose that philosophy that destroys people’s life” and “come back with God’s philosophy that sets people free,” and that “they have a right to freedom of speech, we have a right to freedom of speech.”
What does he say about evolution and people who say the Bible is a lie?

So the evolution is, of course, there’s 15%. I did not know this, this was new to me. A Gallup poll just taken in 2012: only 15% of Americans believe in evolution. I was shocked. The way they projected, I thought 80%. Dead. Isn’t that a good one? We ought to be excited about that. Most Americans aren’t falling for that lie. Yeah. And basically they say the Bible’s a lie, that God did not create the world, it just spontaneously happened, and we don’t know where the first molecule or the first atom or the first cell came from, but this is the way it happened. And so they are opponents of God. Now, so here we are: atheists, no God; hedonists, sex, drugs, parties, feels good, do it; liberals, church and secular; humanists, no God again; evolutionists say the Bible’s a lie; homosexuals say they can’t change. They bash Jesus, they say the Bible is a book of myths. In fact, one of the big homosexual activists said the Bible is BS, it is a book of bull [expletive]. That’s what he said, and they openly say that. And then the Christians want to be nice little people. “Well, we love you.” No, we have to oppose that philosophy that destroys people’s life. We got to come back with God’s philosophy that sets people free. Amen. And I don’t have to go, “Oh, God loves you.” I can talk to them straight, just like they talk to the American people straight. They have a right to freedom of speech, we have a right to freedom of speech. We have a right to say what God said. They have a right to say their own lies if they want to. We’re in America. Are you with me?
Is there historical proof that God lifted up a standard when the enemy came in? (Genesis 2–3)

He says “Bible morality is the standard,” and that if God backed up the Scripture, “then we can possess this Scripture today.” He says God told Adam and Eve they would die if they ate of the tree, and asks whether He would kill them or “make a way of escape,” since He is “the same yesterday, today, and forever.”
Is there historical proof that God lifted up a standard when the enemy came in? (Genesis 2–3)

Religionists twist the Scriptures to their own destruction, and that’s going to be one of these doctrines we’re going to talk about, twisting Scripture. All right. They twist the Scripture to please themselves. Now, Bible morality is the standard. All right, Bible morals, Bible right, Bible truths, that is the standard that God will raise up every time. And we’re going to ask ourself this question: is there historical, scriptural proof that God lifted up a standard when the enemy came in? Is that a good question? In other words, did God back up the Scripture? Because if God backed it up, then we can possess this Scripture today. We’re going to go to Genesis, right at the beginning. God came and told them they were all going to die if they ate of the tree of knowledge of good and evil. All right, just like we’re told we’re going to die if we keep sinning, the wages of sin is death. The [unclear]. You see, all right, they went and they ate of the tree of knowledge. Now, is God going to kill them, or is He going to raise up a standard? Is He going to make a way of escape for them, and is He going to put the enemy to flight? Is He going to keep His word? How many know that God is the same yesterday, today, and forever? The same God that works in the New Testament has to be the same God that works in the Old Testament and the same God that works today. Amen. So we need historical proof. Number two, God gave a way of escape. He didn’t kill Adam and Eve like He said He would. Did He? Why?
Is there historical proof that God lifted up a standard when the enemy came in? (Genesis 2–3)

Genesis 2:16-17: And the LORD God commanded the man, saying, “Of every tree of the garden you may freely eat; but of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil you shall not eat, for in the day that you eat of it you shall surely die.” Romans 6:23: For the wages of sin is death, but the gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord. Hebrews 13:8: Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever.
How did God make a way of escape for Adam and Eve? (Genesis 3:21-24)

He says God confronted Satan, shed an animal’s blood and “covered them with the skin of the animal,” which was “the first written illustration of God’s plan.” He says God removed them from the tree of life “so they wouldn’t eat of the tree of life and live in sin, but they would have a chance to repent, ask forgiveness, and be reconciled back to God.”
How did God make a way of escape for Adam and Eve? (Genesis 3:21-24)

See, and He came and directly opposed Satan. He directly confronted Satan, who deceived them first. God shed blood for their sin. God shed an animal’s blood and covered them with the skin of the animal. Are you there? And that’s the first written illustration of God’s plan. God already knew He was going to die for the sins of the world. The Bible says His blood was shed before the foundation of the world. That was already in God’s plan. God didn’t think of it because Adam and Eve messed up, but this is our first illustration that was His plan, and He backed it up. Isn’t that beautiful, folks? That’s powerful. Now, because that way they could, what? Come to their senses, ask forgiveness, repent, and be reconciled back to God, which they did. See, Adam and Eve was reconciled back to God, and they didn’t do that anymore. Secondly, He removed them from access to the tree of life. Here’s that standard. You see, He made a way of escape. He drove them from the garden so they wouldn’t eat of the tree of life and live in sin, but they would have a chance to repent, ask forgiveness, and be reconciled back to God. Does that sound like New Testament stuff? Of course. That’s what Jesus did. Yes, He told us we would die if we sinned, and when He comes to us, He attacks sin, and He gives us the way of escape. Folks, that’s powerful. Are you out there? Are you alive? Thirdly, He said to Satan (this is His words to Satan, God comes and speaks to Satan personally and says), “Satan, there’s going to be enmity” (war, hatred) “between you and the woman, between the woman...” Now, you want to put down women? Uh, I don’t know how you’re going to do that. Here God personally said there’s going to be war between the woman and Satan. Why did He use the word “woman”? Because all through the Bible His people, God’s church, is an allegory of a bride, and He keeps that all the way through.
How did God make a way of escape for Adam and Eve? (Genesis 3:21-24)

Genesis 3:21: Also for Adam and his wife the LORD God made tunics of skin, and clothed them. Genesis 3:22-24: Then the LORD God said, “Behold, the man has become like one of Us, to know good and evil. And now, lest he put out his hand and take also of the tree of life, and eat, and live forever”— therefore the LORD God sent him out of the garden of Eden to till the ground from which he was taken. So He drove out the man; and He placed cherubim at the east of the garden of Eden, and a flaming sword which turned every way, to guard the way to the tree of life. Revelation 13:8: All who dwell on the earth will worship him, whose names have not been written in the Book of Life of the Lamb slain from the foundation of the world.
What does God say to Satan about “the woman’s seed”? (Genesis 3:15)

He says God said there would be war between Satan’s seed and “the woman’s seed,” and that He, Jesus, “will destroy your authority and your power.” He says the Bible says that “through death He destroyed Satan who had the power of death.”
What does God say to Satan about “the woman’s seed”? (Genesis 3:15)

Hallelujah. He didn’t say Adam, He said woman, “and between Satan’s seed and the woman’s seed,” and He, Jesus, will destroy your authority and your power. Do you see the standard? He made a way of escape for them, and then He attacks the enemy and says, “You know, you’re going to be put down by the woman’s seed, that God is going to be manifested in the flesh, and He is going to destroy you, the power of Satan.” The Bible says through death He destroyed Satan, who had the power of death. Hallelujah. Folks, I would highly recommend you take these notes and go home and get this into you. This stuff is basic, and yet it’s deep at the same time. It’s very revelational, and it will totally change your thinking, your faith, and your belief and your victory and your Christian living. Amen.
What does God say to Satan about “the woman’s seed”? (Genesis 3:15)

Genesis 3:15: And I will put enmity Between you and the woman, And between your seed and her Seed; He shall bruise your head, And you shall bruise His heel.” Hebrews 2:14: Inasmuch then as the children have partaken of flesh and blood, He Himself likewise shared in the same, that through death He might destroy him who had the power of death, that is, the devil,
How did God make a way of escape in Noah’s day? (Genesis 6)

He says that when the earth was filled with violence, God told Noah to build an ark, “just like we build the church,” with one door and one window. He says Noah “preached righteousness” for 100 years, and “only had seven converts,” yet “you’re not measured by numbers,” and those who listened and got involved went into the ark.
How did God make a way of escape in Noah’s day? (Genesis 6)

No matter what trouble I’m going through, God’s going to raise up a standard, He’s going to make a way of escape. I’ve got to have knowledge of how to escape, and I’ve got to be seeking Him so that He can destroy the enemy, because He will do it. Now, is more historical proof number two, Genesis 6. The earth was filled with violence and evil, the whole world, okay, and God says, “I’m going to destroy all of mankind. They’re all going to die.” Then God saw Noah. He was perfect and upright in his generation, he hated evil and loved righteousness, he was in God’s, uh, list of heroes over there in Ezekiel: Noah. God had Noah to build an ark. Okay, how many doors were in the ark? How many doors were in the ark? Yeah, good. Yeah, yeah. How many doors are there to the church? One. How many windows were in there? How many windows were in the ark? One. How many windows is there to heaven? Yeah, say prayer. We can pray to God, we can go directly to God. All right, so he built an ark, just like we build the church. Okay, Noah preached and lived righteousness. Noah preached to them for 100 years. He preached righteousness. He didn’t preach faith and grace, he preached what? Righteousness: turn and do right. He only had seven converts: his wife, his three boys, and three girls that come out of that world of violence and evil, and there were the only three girls available. So his boys met, married these girls. You want a good woman, live right. You want a good man, get into church, find one. Hallelujah. Only three people listened from the world, three from his own household: his sons, or four, his wife. He didn’t have, like these megachurch pastors, all these thousands of people. He got three, four from his house and three from the world. Was he still successful? Yes, because he did what God told him to do. You’re not measured by numbers. Now we see that Satan’s seed was destroyed by the flood, just like it said in Genesis, and we see they that listened and worked on the ark went into the ark and escaped the destruction. Did you hear that? They that listened, repented, they got involved in building the ark, they’re the ones that went into the ark. I was just telling my sons a week ago, if you don’t get involved in the church, I don’t care if you’re an usher, a musician, a, just scrubbing the toilets, mowing the lawn, greeting people, if you don’t do something in the church, you will wind up religious. You’ll be 85% of the religionist in the Christian world, a lot of verbal and no power. Are you out there? Yeah. Did Jesus choose 12 disciples from just anybody, or those that followed and served Him? Yes. Get involved, take on a responsibility, do something.
How did God make a way of escape in Noah’s day? (Genesis 6)

Genesis 6:11-13: The earth also was corrupt before God, and the earth was filled with violence. So God looked upon the earth, and indeed it was corrupt; for all flesh had corrupted their way on the earth. And God said to Noah, “The end of all flesh has come before Me, for the earth is filled with violence through them; and behold, I will destroy them with the earth. Ezekiel 14:14: Even if these three men, Noah, Daniel, and Job, were in it, they would deliver only themselves by their righteousness,” says the Lord GOD.
How does he say the Bible’s predictions prove it is from God?

He says God named Babylon, Persia and Greece and predicted what they would do “hundreds of years before they were a nation,” and described Rome without naming it. He says that “shows this Bible is God,” because “only God can tell what the future holds and bring it to pass.”
How does he say the Bible’s predictions prove it is from God?

Same with Lot and Sodom. You can look up these stories, and Moses in Egypt, same thing. God raised up a standard, God made a way of escape. It is scripturally historical. Are we clear so far? Is this good? Yes, okay. Hallelujah. Now, God starts talking about Assyria and what that nation’s going to do. He names Babylon, named it and said what it was going to do. He named Persia and predicted what it was going to do. He named Greece, Greece, and predicted what it was going to do hundreds of years before they were a nation, and they did it. Now, you young ones need to know this, because that shows this Bible is God. The Bible says only God can tell what the future holds and bring it to pass. Idols, intellects, they can’t do that. Only God can, and you need to know this. Then this last kingdom, Rome, He didn’t name, but He said it will engulf all the other nations, and it did, and it was going to be terrible, and in this nation the King of kings is going to be born, and a people’s going to be raised up in the Roman Empire, and lo and behold, Jesus was born, and Jesus lifted up a standard against the enemy, that we would not be destroyed and be reconciled to our God.
What destruction does Jesus save us from, and what must we do? (Matthew 13:40, 19:16-19, John 14:23)

He says the enemy’s result is eternal fire, citing Matthew 3:12 and 13:40 and Matthew 25:46. He says that when a man asked what to do for eternal life, Jesus said “if you will enter into life, keep the commandments,” and that Jesus said a man who loves Him will “keep My words.”
What destruction does Jesus save us from, and what must we do? (Matthew 13:40, 19:16-19, John 14:23)

Now, we asked ourselves, what destruction? What destruction did Jesus say we were going to be saved from? What is that enemy? What is the results of that? Eternal fire. Matthew 3:12 and Matthew 13:40: “The tares are gathered and burned in the fire at the end of this world. He will cast them into a furnace of fire.” The tares, the Bible says, are children of the wicked one. What did He tell Satan? This woman’s seed will be at war with your seed, they that follow you, and they will destroy, through Jesus, Jesus will destroy your authority, and they will put Satan under their feet themselves. How’s He going to do it? Bible moral laws. Okay, Matthew 25:46 and 19:16. How is He going to raise up a standard and save us from that destruction? Matthew 19: “What good thing?” The guy asked, “What shall I do that I might have eternal life?” and Jesus said, “Believe on Me.” Is that what it says? Doesn’t say that, does it? Why do they always harp on the other part of this and never this one? Because we’re just like our American government: we want everybody to have everything for nothing. We want illegals coming over here without going through the proper procedure. You see, they want to offer you eternal life with nothing from you, no requirements from you. But yet Jesus told him, “If you will enter into life, keep the commandments.” The man said, “Which commandments?” trying to trip up Jesus, and Jesus said, “You shall not murder, you shall not commit adultery” (sexual immorality), “you shall not steal, you shall not bear false witness, honor your parents, and you shall love your neighbor as yourself.” He brought in that one, which is not part of the Ten Commandments, but wraps up the last six. The last six commandments is totally my interaction with you, how I treat you. The first one is totally with God, the first four is totally between me and God of the Ten Commandments. What are the followers of Jesus responsible for? Okay, how many is a follower of Jesus Christ, okay, and profess to know Him? Okay, what are you responsible for? What’s your responsibility? John 14:23, Jesus said, “If a man loves Me, he will” what? “Keep My words.” If you don’t read the book, how you going to keep the book? And if you read, read, and you know the book and you don’t keep the book, what good does it do you? And “you read to assemble yourself even the more so as you see the day approaching,” and yet you can’t get up enough energy to even go to church and be a part of it. “Bring all the tithes into the storehouse,” and yet you cannot discipline your finances to put 10 cents of every dollar away for God. What good is it?
What destruction does Jesus save us from, and what must we do? (Matthew 13:40, 19:16-19, John 14:23)

Matthew 3:12: His winnowing fan is in His hand, and He will thoroughly clean out His threshing floor, and gather His wheat into the barn; but He will burn up the chaff with unquenchable fire.” Matthew 13:40: Therefore as the tares are gathered and burned in the fire, so it will be at the end of this age. Matthew 25:46: And these will go away into everlasting punishment, but the righteous into eternal life.” Matthew 19:16-19: Now behold, one came and said to Him, “Good Teacher, what good thing shall I do that I may have eternal life?” So He said to him, “Why do you call Me good? No one is good but One, that is, God. But if you want to enter into life, keep the commandments.” He said to Him, “Which ones?” Jesus said, “‘You shall not murder,’ ‘You shall not commit adultery,’ ‘You shall not steal,’ ‘You shall not bear false witness,’ ‘Honor your father and your mother,’ and, ‘You shall love your neighbor as yourself.’ ” John 14:23: Jesus answered and said to him, “If anyone loves Me, he will keep My word; and My Father will love him, and We will come to him and make Our home with him. Hebrews 10:25: not forsaking the assembling of ourselves together, as is the manner of some, but exhorting one another, and so much the more as you see the Day approaching. Malachi 3:10: Bring all the tithes into the storehouse, That there may be food in My house, And try Me now in this,” Says the LORD of hosts, “If I will not open for you the windows of heaven And pour out for you such blessing That there will not be room enough to receive it.
What does he say are our responsibilities, and what is the warning in the story of Lazarus and the rich man? (Luke 16)

He says our responsibility is to love and follow Jesus first: “I got to obey Jesus no matter what my pastor does.” From Luke 16 he says the rich man in torment wanted someone sent to “testify to my brothers… lest they too come into this place,” and he says “hell’s real.”
What does he say are our responsibilities, and what is the warning in the story of Lazarus and the rich man? (Luke 16)

See, our responsibility is to what? Love Jesus. Love our pastor? Yeah, but not like Jesus, not even the same degree, not even in the same ballpark. I’ve got to follow Jesus. I got to obey Jesus no matter what my pastor does. Is that correct? Yeah. Well, I got to love my husband. Yeah, but the way to love your husband is love that Man, Jesus, because He will shape you into being someone that can love when you’re not loved, without whining and crying, and behave in a manner that He wants to love you, and the same with a man. Are you there? Second thing, Luke 16:26. Let me have your attention. This is important. Lazarus died, and the angels carried him to heaven. The rich man died, and the demons carried him to hell, or, yeah, no angels. Uh, he was in hell. Somebody put him in hell, and in hell he lifted up his eyes and saw Lazarus afar off, up in heaven. Just, hallelujah, everything’s fine up there. And he said, “Send Lazarus down that he might dip his finger in water and touch my tongue, because I am tormented in these flames.” You young ones, get that, that you’re going to stand before God one of these days and be held accountable. Yeah, and hell’s real. It’s real. And then he says, “Okay, if you can’t do that, send Lazarus back, resurrecting from the dead, and send him back to my brothers, to testify to my brothers,” to teach them, instruct them, admonish them and warn them, notify them, advise them, caution them “lest they too come into this place of torment.” See, “testify” means and “warn” means to teach, to advise, to caution in regard to some future happening from a personal knowledge and experience. Do we, through the Bible, have a personal knowledge of a hell? Yes. How many don’t want to experience it? Yeah. Well, this guy experienced it, let me tell you. See, he not only had the knowledge, now he had the experience, and he wants his brothers to avoid this. Now, folks, if that is so urgent, how much more urgent should it be for us, the church, to be getting the message out and warning and telling people, so that God can raise up a standard in their life and they can escape?
What does he say are our responsibilities, and what is the warning in the story of Lazarus and the rich man? (Luke 16)

Luke 16:19-31: “There was a certain rich man who was clothed in purple and fine linen and fared sumptuously every day. But there was a certain beggar named Lazarus, full of sores, who was laid at his gate, desiring to be fed with the crumbs which fell from the rich man’s table. Moreover the dogs came and licked his sores. So it was that the beggar died, and was carried by the angels to Abraham’s bosom. The rich man also died and was buried. And being in torments in Hades, he lifted up his eyes and saw Abraham afar off, and Lazarus in his bosom. “Then he cried and said, ‘Father Abraham, have mercy on me, and send Lazarus that he may dip the tip of his finger in water and cool my tongue; for I am tormented in this flame.’ But Abraham said, ‘Son, remember that in your lifetime you received your good things, and likewise Lazarus evil things; but now he is comforted and you are tormented. And besides all this, between us and you there is a great gulf fixed, so that those who want to pass from here to you cannot, nor can those from there pass to us.’ “Then he said, ‘I beg you therefore, father, that you would send him to my father’s house, for I have five brothers, that he may testify to them, lest they also come to this place of torment.’ Abraham said to him, ‘They have Moses and the prophets; let them hear them.’ And he said, ‘No, father Abraham; but if one goes to them from the dead, they will repent.’ But he said to him, ‘If they do not hear Moses and the prophets, neither will they be persuaded though one rise from the dead.’ ”
Why must the church keep warning people, and does it matter how it is said?

He says the burden is to get the Word out and “warn them,” and that “it doesn’t matter how it’s said, it’s the message we need to listen to.” He tells a story of a police officer telling him to evacuate a fire, and says people should not turn off a message because of how it is delivered, since “it’s the message that will set you free.”
Why must the church keep warning people, and does it matter how it is said?

Amen. And so we have a burden on us to get the Word of God out, and we need, every year I’m saying this, and we’re still not getting the Word of God out like we should: the printed word, the audible word, the video word, the Internet word. We need to take on [unclear] personally and get the word out to them, warn them. And then some people say, “Well, it’s all in how you say it.” Well, let me give you a little illustration here. At this fire that came over this property, we evacuated the kids from the school. Christina was on the ball and had the kids out by 12:30 or so. We took the horses out. I had the tractor down there scraping down the brush behind the house. I didn’t want the house to burn down. That fire is coming over that mountain, and it’s moving pretty quick, you know, covering a mile in two hours is pretty fast, and that fire is about 300 feet from me, and I’m still knocking down this brush. And one of the firemen comes over and says, “Sir, you did a great job, you’ve saved the building, but it’s time to go.” And he said it with empathy, with feeling, and I already knew it. It’s time to go. I already had my exit route planned out. I, the, the, the gas, the smoke was up here in the air, it wasn’t down here where you’re breathing, so you could last a lot longer. If that smoke would have dropped, I’d have been out of there early. How many know that? But anyway, he was right. He said it nice and politely. I didn’t have to leave the property, just like Harry Truman at Mount St. Helens, when they told him to leave his property, the Mount St. Helens was going to erupt. He said, “I ain’t leaving here, I lived here all my life, I’m going to die here,” and he stayed there and he died, and I could have stayed there. Well, anyway, I go around and I drop the tractor off, and I come around, and this guy pulls up in a car, and he says, “You got to evacuate now,” and I go, “Who are you?” I said, “Are you the fire department?” He said, “No, I’m a police officer.” I go, “Oh,” and I kept on doing what I was doing, and he says, I said, “You got to leave now.” I didn’t even pay him any mind. He was grouchy, grumpy, authoritative, and anything else, but I know who I am, and I know my rights, and I know what I got to get done. I had three more things to get done. I was going to get them done. Now, I could have been stupid and said, “Well, if that’s the way he’s going to talk to me, I’m not leaving, I’ll show him,” and I could have burned with him. He didn’t talk to me right. How many know, folks, it doesn’t matter how we say it, it’s still the truth, and you better listen. You know, if your mentality is, “Well, talk to me, say please, and I’ll listen,” grow up. Not all of us are going to talk to you the sweet way: “You poor little thing, we don’t want to hurt your feelings, but you’re going to hell.” Oh God, you’re going to hell. We may say, “Idiot, turn or burn.” It doesn’t matter how it’s said, it’s the message we need to listen to. Can I hear an amen? It doesn’t matter if you’re there smiling like Joel, smiling, never, never misses a smile. I’d like to see him in real life. You got it. Folks, don’t turn off the message because a tooth is missing in someone, or they can’t say the English language right, or they may say it harshly, or they may say it whiny. The thing is, listen to the message. It’s the message that will set you free. “Smoking: Surgeon General’s warning: causes cancer, heart disease, emphysema, and may complicate pregnancy.” It doesn’t “may” now, it is affecting your baby, they know that. Now, is there a protest on Washington to take that label off? No. Is the atheist offended by that and said, “You know, get that label off, you’re offending us, you’re taking away our right to kill ourself and get cancer”? Is the homosexuals rallying to get rid of that? No. But they don’t like God telling them what to do. They don’t like God telling them that He wants to rule over their life. Amen. Now, if I was a smoker, that would be offensive to me. I mean, you know, millions of Americans don’t pay any attention to that warning, and it’s there every pack you get, it’s there every carton you get, it’s there. Church, should we keep on warning just because they don’t listen? Should we keep telling? Yes, and that’s what we got to get done this year. We got to get the word out, the word of righteousness, and let God raise up a standard and defeat the enemy in people’s life and give them a way of escape, that they can have a new life in Christ Jesus. Amen. That’s our job. That’s what we got to do. So today, are you in love with Jesus? Are you going to love Jesus, accepting and living by the standards of Bible morality? And are you going to admonish, instruct, and warn and notify and advise, the best of your ability? Don’t worry about how you say it. How many just say, “I’m going to give it a shot”? Would you raise your hand? Yeah. Your approach may be all messed up, but you’ll learn. You’ll learn by giving it a shot.
What does the “flood” mean in Isaiah 59:19?
He says “a flood does nothing but damage. When you hear the word ‘flood,’ you know there is damage, you know the water is out of control,” and the enemy comes in that way.
What does he say is the key to defeating the enemy?
He says it is “the Spirit… the very part of God that will defeat your enemies,” rather than leaning “on our own knowledge and understanding.”
What are the two meanings of “standard” in Isaiah 59:19?
He says one is “to flee, to escape, to take flight,” and the other is “attacking the enemy,” to “fly to the attack, to put to flight.”
What does he say the Bible promises about temptation?
He says there is “no temptation come upon anybody” that God will not make “a way of escape that you might bear up under it.”
What is his “finger in the socket” illustration?

He says most Pentecostals “only experience putting our finger in the socket. We didn’t learn how to channel it,” but “at least we felt the power of God, right?” and “then we can learn how to channel it.”
Who does he say we wrestle against?
He says “it’s not the people. We wrestle not against flesh and blood… we wrestle against the principles of men that try to capture our mind.”
What does he say about people who follow their denomination above the Bible?
He says a religionist “will defend their denomination above Jesus Christ Himself and the Bible,” and asks, “We’re not told to follow a man. Who are we told to follow? Jesus.”
Did God kill Adam and Eve as He said He would?
He says no: “He didn’t kill Adam and Eve like He said He would,” but gave “a way of escape.” He says he asks this to show God is the same “yesterday, today, and forever.”
Why does he say God shed an animal’s blood for Adam and Eve?

He says it was “the first written illustration of God’s plan,” and “God already knew He was going to die for the sins of the world.” He says “the Bible says His blood was shed before the foundation of the world.”
Why does he say God said “woman” in Genesis 3:15?
He says “all through the Bible His people, God’s church, is an allegory of a bride,” and that God “didn’t say Adam, He said woman.”
How many converts did Noah have?

He says Noah “only had seven converts: his wife, his three boys, and three girls,” after preaching righteousness for 100 years. He says Noah was successful “because he did what God told him to do. You’re not measured by numbers.”
How does the Bible show it is God’s word, according to him?

He says God named Babylon, Persia and Greece and predicted what they would do “hundreds of years before they were a nation, and they did it,” and that “only God can tell what the future holds and bring it to pass.”
What does he say Jesus told the man who asked about eternal life?
He says Jesus told him, “If you will enter into life, keep the commandments,” and then listed the commandments about how we treat others, ending with “you shall love your neighbor as yourself.”
What did the rich man in hell ask for?
He says he asked for Lazarus to dip his finger in water to cool his tongue, and then asked that Lazarus be sent to warn his brothers “lest they too come into this place of torment.”
Does it matter how the warning is said?
He says no: “It doesn’t matter how we say it, it’s still the truth, and you better listen.” He says to “listen to the message. It’s the message that will set you free.”

The resurrection—discussed in a Joe Rogan clip; there is historical evidence, but why look at a picture when you can meet your true love?

items.d: Michael Silla asks what we are looking for. Herod heard John gladly but would not repent and wanted Jesus to give him a show; the sinful woman loved much, Zacchaeus overcame obstacles and received Him…
p: Michael Silla asks what we are looking for. Herod heard John gladly but would not repent and wanted Jesus to give him a show; the sinful woman loved much, Zacchaeus overcame obstacles and received Him joyfully, the multitude tried to force Him to be king, and the disciples kept obeying in the storm. Seek first the kingdom of God, not a sign.

items.t: What do Good Leaders Have? — August 28, 2022
items.d: Good leaders walk in the fear of God. Nehemiah rebuked nobles who oppressed their brethren with interest and servitude; Joseph, Josiah and the Hebrew midwives feared God. Exodus 18:21 sets the standard—able…
p: Good leaders walk in the fear of God. Nehemiah rebuked nobles who oppressed their brethren with interest and servitude; Joseph, Josiah and the Hebrew midwives feared God. Exodus 18:21 sets the standard—able, truthful, hating covetousness—for government, church and family.

p: Salvation is rescue from hell and wrath to eternal life. The rich man and Lazarus show the reality of the afterlife. Faith without repentance does nothing; true trust responds with repentance, confession and baptism. God frees us from sin, keeps us through trials, and we grow into lived righteousness.

items.t: What Does God Save People From? 09/03/2017
items.d: Pastor David G. Kincer asks what Jesus saves us from: sin, this present evil world, evil people—told through a motel break-in where God’s peace kept him—fear, sickness, the wrath to come and the second death.…
p: Pastor David G. Kincer asks what Jesus saves us from: sin, this present evil world, evil people—told through a motel break-in where God’s peace kept him—fear, sickness, the wrath to come and the second death. He examines the fearful, the unbelieving, the abominable and murderers of Revelation 21:8, shows from Scripture that God hates evil, and says Christians who stand for right are not haters.
What does Jesus save us from?
From sin—a violation of God’s word—and from this present evil world, by giving us a commandment not to run with the crowd to do evil; evil companions corrupt good character.
