Yeah, these intellectuals and these educated people. Give me that uneducated. The Bible says that Peter was uneducated. So we we go to the uneducated church. Are you with me? You see now we got a lot more than four divisions in American church today. And the last group is I am of Christ. One group has got it right. And Paul proves it. He says, “Is Christ divided into Paul and Peter and Apollos?” No. See, did did Paul was Paul crucified for you? No. You see, were you baptized in Paul’s name? No. So if that’s not true, why are you divided? You should be united around Jesus Christ, his death, his burial, his resurrection. Amen. And of course, his word. So cure number one, follow that means imitate, pattern yourself after Jesus.

1 Corinthians 1:12-13: Now I say this, that each of you says, “I am of Paul,” or “I am of Apollos,” or “I am of Cephas,” or “I am of Christ.” Is Christ divided? Was Paul crucified for you? Or were you baptized in the name of Paul?
Christ, not any group or denomination—preachers aren’t sinless; many baptisms and rebaptisms show division.

People say, “Well, I’m following this group.” You better not be following any group. I don’t care if you’re a Baptist, a Catholic, a Presbyterian, an independent, a Jew, or whatever. The Bible tells us to what? Follow Christ. He was the one that died for us. He’s the one that we get baptized in. He’s the one that saved us. He’s the one that that’s God, not ministers or a church group. Some people I talk to people that defend their group even I had one person say when I told them you know their prophet prophesied it was a spiritfilled church and the prophet prophesied that this woman could leave her husband and I told that woman the Bible says not to. And she told me I don’t care what the Bible says that’s a man of God. Are you there? See, I deal with this all the time. Baptists will defend their Baptist doctrine. Presbyterian, their Presbyterian doctrine. Independence, their independence. That folks, we need to get Jesus Christ and his doctrines. Jesus is in unity with God. He said, “I only do the will of my father.” Can we say that? Is our church group only doing the will of the father? Is my preacher hero only doing the will of the father? See, Jesus only did the will of the father. He’s in unity with with God. He’s sinless. Is your preacher sinless? Your pastor, your TV evangelist, are they sinless? Boy, what I read, they’re far from it. Sexual immorality, taking the church’s money, living rich while the people live poor, died for us, and cleansed us through water baptism. Preachers today won’t even speak the truth because they don’t want to lose the the offering so that they can live good. If they have a threat of going to jail for preaching truth, forget it. But not Jesus. See, he spoke the truth and that’s why he died. And if we spoke the truth more, more people would be mad at us. More people would be persecuting us. But when we just start agreeing with everything and compromising what? There’s no threat. If a lot of these big churches actually spoke like Jesus spoke, most of the congregation would leave. Isn’t that true? It It’s true. They come to be entertained. They’ve come to be flattered. They come to be inspired with motivational speaking and so forth. So that is cure number one. How many raise your hand and say, “I agree with that cure. I agree with Paul.” Yeah. See, we got to make good choices here. Now, here’s another cause. Who baptized me? Who baptized me? You know, if you go to the Catholics, they sprinkle. If you go to the Protestants, they submerge. Most of them. In fact, the Baptists are so divisional, there’s 120 different denominations of them, the last time I counted. And one of them, I’ll never forget, was the 500gallon Baptist. You had to have 500 gallons in the baptismal tank before you could baptize because someone got baptized and a girl with long hair and her hair floated on top of the water and they couldn’t get her all the way in. So, we got to have 500 gallons of water in that tank from now on. That’s the truth. Oh, do I baptize them in the name of Jesus or in the name of the Father, Son, the Holy Ghost? Or I folks, it’s not the method. It’s the truth behind the the baptism. And Paul would not baptize but just of three people because he didn’t want people saying what he’s baptizing in his name. And I guarantee you when you go to another church and you want to join them, a lot of them are going to rebaptize you. There’s something wrong here. Cure number two, it’s not the person, it’s not the method or the church group that baptized you. It’s Jesus who the Bible says puts to death the old man of sin in water baptism and you come up a new creature. Old things passed away, all things made new. Now, how many would rather have that kind of baptism? Baptism. Yes. See, it’s not the method. We start worshiping methods. It is the truth of what God asked us to do, our response. Now, that’s good.
In preaching Christ crucified—not the messenger; Jews seek signs, Greeks seek wisdom.

Paul’s good so far. Don’t you agree with him? Yes. Okay. Another cause, selfishness limits God’s power. Okay. When we make selfish choices, we limit or we neutralize God’s power. Paul’s hitting some things that the American church needs to get. And you young believers and you young people, you need to get this in your understanding. You will save yourself and a lot of other people a lot of headaches tomorrow. If you can understand what Paul’s talking about, there’s not a Catholic baptism or wisdom. There’s not a Protestant baptism or wisdom. There’s not a Jew or a Muslim. There is one Christ, one gospel, and one cross. Amen. And we cannot promote our group. Our group has to line up with Jesus. And when a Muslim says that Jesus didn’t die on the cross, they’re saying Jesus is a liar. There’s something wrong. Because Jesus himself said, “I’m going to die.” Ain’t that right? And the Muslims will say, “Well, God can’t die.” That is true. That’s why Jesus said, “I lay down my life. No man has power to take my life. I lay it down.” Hallelujah. p: Baptisms, laying on of hands and eschatology are baby doctrines that still divide. Adulthood means responsibility. God gives growth, not ministers; the Spirit and word test our work as fire. Ministers are stewards, so don’t honor men, and judge nothing before Jesus reveals motives.

You’re either going to speak in tonesues or you’re going to speak by inspiration. You’re going to speak the mighty works of God. p: Pastor David G. Kincer answers why Christ died for sinners if people can repent by conscience. Going back to Genesis like clean water at a river’s source, he shows the law of death and life, God slaying the first animal in Adam and Eve’s place, and the promised Seed who would crush Satan. Christ, slain before the foundation of the world, bought us from sin, Satan and death, and knowing Him is far better than conscience alone.

items.t: Why is Moses’ Tabernacle important for Christians today?
items.d: A one-minute clip from Hebrews 8:5: the tabernacle Moses built was a copy and shadow pointing to heavenly realities.
p: A one-minute clip from Hebrews 8:5: the tabernacle Moses built was a copy and shadow pointing to heavenly realities.
Why does Moses’ tabernacle matter to Christians?
It was a copy and shadow of heavenly things; earthly shadows point us to the real thing.
Why does Moses’ tabernacle matter to Christians?

In Hebrews chapter 8 verse 5 the tabernacle Moses’s tabernacle served as the copy and shadow. Of heavenly things. As Moses was divinely instructed when he was about to make the tabernacle so if you look here I got a shadow right. If you follow the shadow a man but a picture or a shadow is just a representation of the real thing it is not the real thing so God makes these shadows. Or earthly things to. Point us to what the heavenly thing the real thing. For he said see that you make all things according to the pattern shown you on the mountain according to the shadow so in the New Testament he helps us understand why these things were made they are pointing us to the real thing.
Why does Moses’ tabernacle matter to Christians?

Hebrews 8:5: who serve the copy and shadow of the heavenly things, as Moses was divinely instructed when he was about to make the tabernacle. For He said, “See that you make all things according to the pattern shown you on the mountain.”
A copy and shadow of heavenly things.
Divinely, to make all things according to the pattern shown on the mountain.
Is a shadow the real thing?
No, only a representation of it.
To point us to the heavenly, real thing.
How does the New Testament help?
It explains why these things were made.
The one shown to Moses on the mountain.
Because it points to the real thing.

items.t: Why is the U.S. Church Mocked and Rejected?
items.d: In “Why Is the U.S. Church Mocked and Rejected?”, Pastor David G. Kincer reviews America’s four great spiritual awakenings and says the church fell asleep while the enemy sowed tares. He says Christians invite…
p: In “Why Is the U.S. Church Mocked and Rejected?”, Pastor David G. Kincer reviews America’s four great spiritual awakenings and says the church fell asleep while the enemy sowed tares. He says Christians invite mockery by speech that sounds insane and by behavior no different from the world, including fighting over doctrines that hurt no one. His answer is to stop shunning those who disagree, live by the two commandments of love, do good, and respond with love.
What were America’s great spiritual awakenings?

He asks why the U.S. church is mocked and rejected and says history records four great awakenings, the first in 1730 before the Revolutionary War and the second from 1800 to 1840, which addressed alcohol, tobacco, slavery and women’s rights.
What were America’s great spiritual awakenings?

And we thank you and appreciate you joining us in further pursuit of clarity on crucial choices. Today we’re going to ask the question: has the United States of America church made the best choices? Or, why is the United States church mocked and rejected today? Now, we know from history there have been four great spiritual awakenings. The first was in 1730, preceding the Revolutionary War and preparing us for it. The second was in 1800 through 1840, where alcohol, tobacco, the abolition of slavery and women’s rights was addressed.
Why does the church keep needing revival?

He describes the third and fourth awakenings and says that when you go to sleep you have to be reawakened. From Matthew 13:25 he says that while men slept the enemy sowed tares among the wheat, and that is what happens when the church goes to sleep.
Why does the church keep needing revival?

The third one was 1850 through the 1900s, and pre- and post-Civil War, and they address the social ills of the drunks, the orphans, the widows and so forth. The fourth was in 1948 through ‘80, where the Holy Spirit was poured out, miracles happened, praise and worship was introduced to the church, unity. And in the, the secular world, In God We Trust was put on our money in 1954, and One Nation Under God was put in our pledge in 1956, and throughout the ‘50s millions of Americans made a decision to serve Jesus Christ. Now, why do we need four awakenings? Well, when you go to sleep, you have to be reawakened, either by yourself naturally or an alarm. In Matthew 13:25 Jesus said, while men slept, his enemies came and sowed tares among the wheat. So the children of the wicked one, the children of Satan, among the wheat, while men slept. And so that’s what happens when the church goes to sleep: we need an awakening. In the ‘60s, Bible, prayer and Jesus was put out of public places and public schools; the sexual revolution and evolution was replacing them.
Why does the church keep needing revival?
Matthew 13:25: but while men slept, his enemy came and sowed tares among the wheat and went his way.
Why do people think Christians are crazy?

He traces what replaced the Bible in each decade since the 1960s and says the gap between awakenings has been 10, 30 and 50 years. He says Christians talk “like they’re crazy,” citing 1 Corinthians 14:9 and 14:23.
Why do people think Christians are crazy?

In the ‘70s, abortion, drugs, homosexual agenda and rock and roll was the main focus of America. In the ‘80s, corrupt activist leaders fighting against these evils, and corrupt ministers and priests were exposed; many gave up the fight and left the enemy seeds to grow by themselves. In the ‘90s, psychology, grace and faith, entertainment, seeker-friendly church, intellectual reasoning replaced the Holy Spirit’s power and the power of the Bible. It took between the previous awakenings was 10, 30 and 50 years. There is 30 years between the last awakening and the one we are looking for. Now, what are the reasons for mockery and rejection of Christians? Christians talk like crazy, like they’re crazy. First Corinthians 14:9: unless you utter by the tongue words easy to understand. Verse 23: they will, will they not say that you are out of your mind? You are, you people are nuts.
Why do people think Christians are crazy?

1 Corinthians 14:9: So likewise you, unless you utter by the tongue words easy to understand, how will it be known what is spoken? For you will be speaking into the air. 1 Corinthians 14:23: Therefore if the whole church comes together in one place, and all speak with tongues, and there come in those who are uninformed or unbelievers, will they not say that you are out of your mind?
Is it a blessing to be insulted as a Christian?

From 1 Peter 4:14 he says you are blessed if insulted for the name of Christ, but not if insulted as an evildoer. He says “once saved, always saved” is insane talk, because you got to back up your salvation with proper behavior.
Is it a blessing to be insulted as a Christian?

In First Peter 4:14, if you’re insulted because of the name of Christ, you are blessed, and happy are you. But if you’re insulted as an evildoer, you are not blessed. And so our behavior and our speech invite mockery and rejection and insults. Eternal salvation: here’s some, a list of some insane Christian speech. Once saved, always saved from sin, sin’s penalty, that they have wrath, and Satan. That’s like saying the blind man and the leper and all them that got healed from their diseases would never have to be delivered from sickness again, when Jesus said, go and sin no more, lest something worse come upon you. You don’t get something for nothing; you got to back up your salvation with proper behavior.
Is it a blessing to be insulted as a Christian?

1 Peter 4:14-15: If you are reproached for the name of Christ, blessed are you, for the Spirit of glory and of God rests upon you. On their part He is blasphemed, but on your part He is glorified. But let none of you suffer as a murderer, a thief, an evildoer, or as a busybody in other people’s matters. John 5:14: Afterward Jesus found him in the temple, and said to him, “See, you have been made well. Sin no more, lest a worse thing come upon you.”
Does faith alone make you rich or healthy?

He calls “faith only” and “pray only” talk insane: believing God will make you rich without a job skill, healthy without doctors, or employed without education. He says constantly announcing Jesus is coming any minute makes Christians sound like idiots.
Does faith alone make you rich or healthy?

Another one is faith only. All I got to do is believe God, get rich, don’t have to go to college, don’t have to learn a job skill. God, God, faith to get me rich, faith will get me healthy, faith to get me healing, don’t need medicine, I don’t need doctors. Uh, eternal life, faith is all there is, no matter how I live, I, faith is it. Pray only: pray for a job, don’t have to get in a job skill, don’t have to get an education, just pray for a job; pray for healing; pray to pass the college examination or my [unclear] test; just pray; just pray for the wicked to be saved in America, that’s all I got to do. You know, that’s insane talk. Imminent or predicted time of Jesus’ return: for hundreds of years the church world, he’s coming any minute, he’s coming soon, he’s coming in a minute, he’s coming soon, and he hasn’t come any minute and he hasn’t come soon. So we sound like a bunch of idiots.
Should Christians predict when Jesus will return?

He says authors predicted years for Christ’s coming and all missed, and that claiming to interpret Revelation, Daniel and Ezekiel, tongues without interpretation, false healings and failed prophecy invite the insults.
Should Christians predict when Jesus will return?

Then we predicted years, from LaHaye to all these other authors predicting the coming of Christ, and they all missed, including, uh, Smith of Calvary Chapel. We claim interpretation of the books in the Bible, of Revelation and Daniel and Ezekiel, when the authors didn’t even know what they meant, but oh, we know what they mean, and we sound crazy. Tongues without interpretation: First Corinthians plainly says people are going to think you’re nuts. False healings: people have been proclaimed to be healed that died. Prophecy that didn’t come to pass. And so yes, when we talk like that, when our doctrines and our speeches like that, the humanists think we are a bunch of nuts. We invite the insults.
Why do Christians divide over doctrine?

He says Christians divide over sectarian issues that hurt no one, such as water baptism, tongues, worship, women in ministry, hair and clothing, and asks why we fight over them. He says when believers sin like others, outsiders say “you’re no different than I am.”
Why do Christians divide over doctrine?

And so we’re going to look into why Christians are insulted and mocked because of their behavior. Sectarian issues that we divide over that directly hurt no one, like water baptism, tongues, worship, second coming, anointing or holy water, women in the ministry, hair, clothing, jewelry and so forth. They hurt nobody. Why in the world do we fight and argue over things that don’t physically or financially, mentally hurt anybody? And the humanists look at us and go, man, you guys are a bunch of crackpots, all of you are saying the different things. And so they insult us and they mock us, and we invite it in our behavior. We may, we commit crime or sin that humanists commit or don’t commit; as the Bible says, even the pagans don’t do this, he told the Corinthian church. And yet we say we got eternal life and they’re going to the lake of fire, and so the people outside of the church go, that’s insane, that’s nuts, you’re no different than I am.
Why do Christians divide over doctrine?
1 Corinthians 5:1: It is actually reported that there is sexual immorality among you, and such sexual immorality as is not even named among the Gentiles—that a man has his father’s wife!

From Galatians 5 and the Ten Commandments he lists what Christians must avoid, and says Christians are to work, provide for themselves and assemble one day to worship. When we violate these, he says, we invite mockery.

And Galatians 5:20 plainly tells us how Christians are supposed to be behaving: no idolatry, no sorcery, no witchcraft, no hatred, no quarreling and jealousies and outburst of anger, selfish ambition, I gotta have it my way or no way, rebellion, heresies, we invent our own doctrines, envy, murders, drunkenness, unlawful sex, whether it’s homosexuality, adultery, incest or whatever. Plus you got the Ten Commandments: thou shall not murder, steal; you’re supposed to honor your parents; you’re not supposed to be greedy; you’re not supposed to lie. And Christians are supposed to work and provide for their own self, and you put one day aside and you assemble in the church to learn about God and worship him. And so when we violate these things, the humanists, they mock us and they laugh at us, because we invite it by our behavior as well as our speech. In James 4:17:

Galatians 5:19-21: Now the works of the flesh are evident, which are: adultery, fornication, uncleanness, lewdness, idolatry, sorcery, hatred, contentions, jealousies, outbursts of wrath, selfish ambitions, dissensions, heresies, envy, murders, drunkenness, revelries, and the like; of which I tell you beforehand, just as I also told you in time past, that those who practice such things will not inherit the kingdom of God.
Quoting James 4:17 and 1 Peter 3:10, he says “Christianity is about doing good.” From 1 Peter 2:14 he says we need to be involved in politics and government to promote good.

He who knows to do good and does not do it, to him it is sin. Christianity is about doing good. First Peter 3:10: let him refrain his tongue from evil and his tongue from deceit; let him turn from evil and do good; let him seek peace and pursue it. We’re supposed to be people that do good, folks. First Peter 2:14: governors are for the punishment of evildoers and for the praise of those who do good. And so we need to be involved in politics and in government, because we need to be promoting good, and that’s what Christianity is, it’s good. Now, how do we prevent insane and insult reactions? Many theological doctrines directly hurt no one.

James 4:17: Therefore, to him who knows to do good and does not do it, to him it is sin. 1 Peter 3:10-11: For “He who would love life And see good days, Let him refrain his tongue from evil, And his lips from speaking deceit. Let him turn away from evil and do good; Let him seek peace and pursue it. 1 Peter 2:14: or to governors, as to those who are sent by him for the punishment of evildoers and for the praise of those who do good.
What two commandments sum up the Bible?

He says to stop shunning those who disagree with our petty doctrines, because the whole Bible hangs on two commandments: love God, and love your neighbor as yourself. He adds Romans 13 (love does no harm) and Matthew 7:12 (treat others as you would have them treat you).
What two commandments sum up the Bible?

So let’s stop mistreating and shunning those that disagree with our petty little doctrines. We got more important things to work on. The Bible now is summed up in two doctrines. The Bible says on these two doctrines hang all the law and the prophets, the whole book. Another scripture says it is the law and the prophets. And these two doctrines summarize the Bible, and humanists are wrong when they say the Bible is a bunch of lies, because there’s nothing wrong with these two doctrines. First one is to love God, Matthew 22:40. And Romans 13 tells us that love does no harm to his neighbor, therefore love fulfills the law, and everyone has to agree we should not be harming each other, whether you’re a humanist, an atheist or a Christian. That is a good law, and that sums up the Bible. The next one is love your neighbor as yourself, that’s the second one. And to clarify it, he says in Matthew 7:12, treat others as you would have them treat you.
What two commandments sum up the Bible?

Matthew 22:37-40: Jesus said to him, “‘You shall love the LORD your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your mind.’ This is the first and great commandment. And the second is like it: ‘You shall love your neighbor as yourself.’ On these two commandments hang all the Law and the Prophets.” Romans 13:10: Love does no harm to a neighbor; therefore love is the fulfillment of the law. Matthew 7:12: Therefore, whatever you want men to do to you, do also to them, for this is the Law and the Prophets.
What is love, according to 1 Corinthians 13?

He reads that love is patient and kind, not envious, rude or proud, doesn’t demand its own way, and never gives up. He says Bible morality, doing good, is the priority doctrine, and 1 Corinthians 5:11 deals with harmful behavior, not theology.
What is love, according to 1 Corinthians 13?

You don’t want robbed, don’t rob. You don’t want people talking bad about you, don’t talk about bad about other people, you see. And how can anyone fault that issue? First Corinthians 13 clarifies love: patience; love is kind; it’s not envious; it’s not rude; it’s not proud; it doesn’t brag about itself; doesn’t promote evil; doesn’t think evil; is not eagerly angered, easily angered; and it doesn’t demand its own way. Here it is again, I want my way. And it never quits; love never gives up. So the bottom line is, Bible morality, doing good, is the priority doctrine of the Bible and what the Bible is all about. First Corinthians 5:11 says if there’s a brother who claims to be a Christian and he is sexually immoral, he’s greedy, he’s a, he’s an idolater, a drunkard, an extortioner, don’t keep company with him. You say, there is no theology listed here, just harmful behavior by believers, how we’re supposed to react to believers who are sinning, so that they can correct themselves.
What is love, according to 1 Corinthians 13?

1 Corinthians 13:4-7: Love suffers long and is kind; love does not envy; love does not parade itself, is not puffed up; does not behave rudely, does not seek its own, is not provoked, thinks no evil; does not rejoice in iniquity, but rejoices in the truth; bears all things, believes all things, hopes all things, endures all things. 1 Corinthians 5:11: But now I have written to you not to keep company with anyone named a brother, who is sexually immoral, or covetous, or an idolater, or a reviler, or a drunkard, or an extortioner—not even to eat with such a person.
How should Christians respond to being mocked?

He says civil government is there to punish evildoers and honor the good, not to enforce theology, and God will deal with spiritual things. His conclusion: speak and behave so as not to invite mockery, and respond with love.
How should Christians respond to being mocked?

No theology at all. Romans 13 again says civil penalty of evildoers: the civil government’s there to penalize evildoers, to punish them for correction, not theology, and they’re there to honor the good. God and spiritual things, God can and will deal with them. And the conclusion is this: we need as Christians to speak and behave in a manner that doesn’t invite these things, and respond with love to love violators. That’s the way of our Creator.
How should Christians respond to being mocked?

Romans 13:3-4: For rulers are not a terror to good works, but to evil. Do you want to be unafraid of the authority? Do what is good, and you will have praise from the same. What does he say happened in the 1960s?
He says the Bible, prayer and Jesus were put out of public places and schools, replaced by the sexual revolution and evolution.
What does he say replaced the Holy Spirit’s power in the 1990s?
He names psychology, entertainment, the seeker-friendly church and intellectual reasoning.
What does 1 Corinthians 14 say about speech in church?
He says unless you speak words easy to understand, people will say you are out of your mind.
What does he say about “once saved, always saved”?
He says you don’t get something for nothing; you got to back up your salvation with proper behavior.
What is wrong with “just pray” for a job or healing?
He says praying without getting a job skill or education, or without medicine and doctors, is insane talk.
What does he say about tongues without interpretation?
He says First Corinthians plainly says people are going to think you’re nuts.
Which doctrines does he say Christians should stop fighting over?
He lists water baptism, tongues, worship, the second coming, anointing, women in the ministry, hair, clothing and jewelry, which he says hurt nobody.
Should Christians be involved in politics?
He says yes, because governors are for punishing evildoers and praising those who do good, and Christians need to be promoting good.
He quotes Matthew 7:12, treat others as you would have them treat you: if you don’t want to be robbed, don’t rob.
How should the church treat a believer living in sin?
From 1 Corinthians 5:11 he says don’t keep company with them, so that they can correct themselves.

p: In this message, Pastor David G. Kincer teaches on the “young men” stage of 1 John 2: those who have overcome the wicked one by the blood of the Lamb, the word of their testimony and sacrifice. He calls forgiveness the top weapon, tells stories of hurting young people, and ends with the armor of God, alertness, and speaking the word.
What does he say marks the “young men” stage? (1 John 2:13, John 15:5)

He says the young men have “overcome the wicked one” and are “victorious over Satan,” that “they’re not weak at all,” and that “they don’t follow a group, they’re not sectarian, they don’t quarrel, they just stand for truth.” He adds that “you don’t have to argue when you know you’re right,” and that “the word of God abides in you,” citing John 15:5, “you will be fruitful.”
What does he say marks the “young men” stage? (1 John 2:13, John 15:5)

And today we’re going to hit the stage of spiritual growth that John, in 1 John chapter 2, calls the young men stage. John gives us these stages of growth, and this is the young men stage. John calls it very powerful. Stage, 1 John 2:13: “I write unto you, young men, because you have overcome the wicked one.” Hallelujah. Or overcome evil, overcome bad, overcome harm, you’re victorious over Satan, you’re victorious over evil. Hallelujah, it’s very powerful. Now, how many Christians do you know are at the young men’s stage? “I have written unto young men because you are strong.” You are powerful, you are not weak. See, what was the problem with the newborn? They were weak, they were carnal, they were jealous, they quarreled, they followed little heroes, and they followed little groups, and they had problems in the flesh with sexual immorality and anger and hatred and heresies and so forth. But the young men’s stage, they’re not weak at all. They don’t give in to the flesh. You see, they don’t follow a group, they’re not sectarian, they don’t quarrel, they just stand for truth. You don’t have to argue when you know you’re right, you don’t have to argue, you don’t have to defend yourself. Powerful, strong. Number three: “The word of God abides in you.” And he repeats that they’ve overcome the wicked one. The word of God abides in you. The Bible tells us that Jesus is the living word, the bread that came down, the living bread that came down from heaven, so Jesus is abiding in him. In John 15:5 Jesus said, “If you abide in me and my words abide in you, you will be fruitful.” See, the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, patience, gentleness, kindness, meekness, temperance, and faith. You see, this is where God wants us to go; he wants us to grow and obtain these things, and this stage, they are obtaining.
What does he say marks the “young men” stage? (1 John 2:13, John 15:5)

1 John 2:13: I write to you, fathers, Because you have known Him who is from the beginning. I write to you, young men, Because you have overcome the wicked one. I write to you, little children, Because you have known the Father. John 15:5: “I am the vine, you are the branches. He who abides in Me, and I in him, bears much fruit; for without Me you can do nothing. Galatians 5:22-23: But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, self-control. Against such there is no law.
How does he say we overcome the wicked one? (Revelation 12:11, Romans 12:1)

He says “they overcame Satan by the blood of the Lamb,” which “cleanses us from all sin,” and that when Satan accuses, “I overcome Satan’s accusations by going back to the blood, going back to the cross, and asking for forgiveness.” He says too many Christians “fail 10 or 15 times on one issue and they quit,” and that we also overcome by the scriptures and by sacrifice, quoting Job: “Though God slay me, yet will I trust him.”
How does he say we overcome the wicked one? (Revelation 12:11, Romans 12:1)

The word of God abides in you; they not only have a desire for the word, but the word of God is alive in them, it lives in them, both Jesus and the Word. Now, let’s look at overcoming the wicked one. All right, how do you overcome the wicked one? Revelations 12:11 says they overcame Satan by the blood of the Lamb. See, what does he mean by the blood of the Lamb? Well, the blood of the Lamb cleanses us from all sin. And so, see, when I mess up as a Christian, I do something I shouldn’t do, Satan comes and he accuses me: “You are no good, you need to quit faking it, quit pretending, and just leave, and quit acting like you’re a Christian, you need to give up on this Christianity.” But see, the blood tells me as a Christian I can go to Christ, and that same blood that cleansed me at the beginning and washed my sins away and delivered me from, is the same blood that will cleanse me today. So I overcome Satan’s accusations by going back to the blood, going back to the cross, and asking for forgiveness, turning from that sin, rising up, and keep walking in God. See, overcome Satan by the blood of the Lamb. Too many Christians, they fail 10 or 15 times on one issue and they quit and give up, but you got to go back to the blood and let the blood cleanse you, however many times it takes until you’re free from that sin. Could that be an amen? Yeah. See, that’s how we overcome Satan. He accuses us, and you know, he’s got a lot to accuse us about. You, we say we’re Christians, we look in the mirror and go, “Wow, I’m a mess,” and so Satan brings these things out, but we overcome him by the blood of the Lamb. Secondly, you overcome by the word of their testimony. See, when Satan accused Jesus in the garden, Satan asked Jesus to make stones bread and jump down off the pinnacle of the temple, and, uh, Jesus always answered, “It is written.” He always answered the scriptures, and so we overcome Satan by, what? Referring to the scriptures. Hallelujah, so it’s important that that word abides in us. You see, the word of their testimony, and “they love not their lives unto death.” And remember, in the past we’ve told you, Romans 12:1: “Present your body as a living sacrifice, holy and acceptable unto God. Don’t be conformed to this world, but be transformed by the renewing of your mind.” Okay, so we offer our bodies a living sacrifice, we sacrifice to serve God and not give into sin and not follow the crowd to do evil. That’s how you love your life and death. Okay, and remember Job said, “Though God slay me, yet will I trust him.” Things may be going bad, finances may be difficult, your health may be down, the family may have problems, you know, there may be trouble all around you, like the song said, but you keep serving Christ, even though it’s a sacrifice, it’s not going easy, but you sacrifice, and that’s how we overcome Satan.
How does he say we overcome the wicked one? (Revelation 12:11, Romans 12:1)

Revelation 12:11: And they overcame him by the blood of the Lamb and by the word of their testimony, and they did not love their lives to the death. 1 John 1:7: But if we walk in the light as He is in the light, we have fellowship with one another, and the blood of Jesus Christ His Son cleanses us from all sin. Matthew 4:4: But He answered and said, “It is written, ‘Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceeds from the mouth of God.’ ” Romans 12:1: I beseech you therefore, brethren, by the mercies of God, that you present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable to God, which is your reasonable service. Job 13:15: Though He slay me, yet will I trust Him. Even so, I will defend my own ways before Him.
How do we resist the Devil? (James 4:7, 2 Corinthians 2:10)

He quotes James 4:7, “Resist the Devil and he will flee from you,” and “draw nigh to God and God will draw nigh to you,” and says we resist by praying, worshiping, going to church and reading the Bible. He says “just zip the lip,” since “even a fool is wise when he keeps his mouth shut.” From 2 Corinthians 2:10 he says “Satan doesn’t want you exercising forgiveness.”
How do we resist the Devil? (James 4:7, 2 Corinthians 2:10)

And we overcome evil. James 4:7 says, “Resist the Devil and he will flee from you.” So we got to resist him, we got to put up some resistance, and he goes on to say in the next verse that if you draw nigh to God, he tells us how to resist Satan: “Draw nigh to God and God will draw nigh to you.” So I resist Satan by what? Praying, worshiping, going to church, getting in the Bible studies, reading my Bible. I resist Satan by pursuing God. Hallelujah. And he says, “Cleanse your hands,” and don’t speak evil of one another. Don’t let Satan get you into measuring other people by you or you by other people. Just zip the lip. The Bible says even a fool is wise when he keeps his mouth shut. Learn to zip the lip. That’s how you resist the Devil. You know, you don’t got to attack everybody every time you, you know, you get opposed by somebody, especially in your home. Just zip the lip. Resist the Devil. The Devil loves for you to start speaking out. And then in 2 Corinthians 2:10, this is really good: “Whom you forgive anything,” Paul says, writing to the Corinthians, “whom you forgive anything, I forgive also. Whom you pardon anything, I pardon also. Whom you release anything, I release also, lest Satan get advantage of us, for we are not ignorant of his devices.” Satan doesn’t want you exercising forgiveness. Why? Because when you don’t forgive, you open the door to anger, you open the door to hatred, you open the door to conflict between you and the person, separation.
How do we resist the Devil? (James 4:7, 2 Corinthians 2:10)

James 4:7: Therefore submit to God. Resist the devil and he will flee from you. Proverbs 17:28: Even a fool is counted wise when he holds his peace; When he shuts his lips, he is considered perceptive. 2 Corinthians 2:10: Now whom you forgive anything, I also forgive. For if indeed I have forgiven anything, I have forgiven that one for your sakes in the presence of Christ,
Why does he call forgiveness the top weapon of the young men stage?

He says “forgiveness is a top weapon of the young men stage” and “if nothing else, you will free yourself.” He says people either forgive themselves and go on sinning or stay down defeated, but “we should forgive ourselves for doing wrong, get up and start doing right.”
Why does he call forgiveness the top weapon of the young men stage?

Forgiveness is a top weapon of the young men stage. Forgiveness is a very important weapon. Okay, forgiveness: you pardon, you give freedom. If nothing else, you will free yourself. Hallelujah. Very, very powerful weapon. People either forgive themselves and go on sinning, or they don’t forgive themselves and stay down and become defeated. But we should forgive ourselves, get up, and walk in the pathway that’s right. Amen. We should forgive ourselves for doing wrong, get up and start doing right, not just forgive myself and then go back and do it again, and go back and do it again, and knowing you’re going to go back and do it again. Or people don’t forgive themselves; there’s people that just can’t believe that God will forgive them, and they can’t forgive themselves, and so that brings guilt, that brings condemnation. But the young men stay just forgiving others, forgiving themselves, and getting up and doing what’s right and never quitting, and this is the top weapon of the young man stage: forgiveness. items.t: Does it matter if you show up?

The same. Righteousness and holy living should be what? The same.” ▶ 10:38 “Everything should be the same like McDonald’s is, but in America, do we have that? No! And so we confuse everybody.” ▶ 10:53 Paul says, “I want you all to speak the same thing” (1 Corinthians 1:10). Pastor Kincer says that in Brazil, Korea, China or any state in America, a Big Mac is identical, the fries are the same, and the Coke is the real Coke. The Holy Ghost, salvation, righteousness and holy living should be preached the same way in every church, but in America they aren’t, and it confuses everybody.
Should church be as consistent as a Big Mac?

📖 Scripture (NKJV) 1 Corinthians 1:10 — Now I plead with you, brethren, by the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that you all speak the same thing, and that there be no divisions among you, but that you be perfectly joined together in the same mind and in the same judgment.

items.d: It can feel that way. Pastor Kincer says church was boring to him as a teenager because he wasn’t involved and had lost his desire for Jesus.
p: It can feel that way. Pastor Kincer says church was boring to him as a teenager because he wasn’t involved and had lost his desire for Jesus.

Pastor Kincer contrasts that with David, who was glad when they said, “Let us go into the house of the LORD.” Pastor Kincer says the church is made up of people, and the people determine what a church is.

🎙 From the sermon “When I was 17, 16, 18, church is boring because I didn’t get involved. I wanted to do my thing.” ▶ 3:50 “Or we just lost our desire for Jesus.” ▶ 4:33 “David said, I was glad when they said unto me, let us what? Go to the house of the Lord. Man, he was excited. It’s assembly time. Oh, glory, let’s go.” ▶ 4:40 “But the church is made up of who? People. And it’s the people that are the determination of a church.” ▶ 5:00 Young people say church is boring. Pastor Kincer says he said the same thing at 16, 17 and 18, because he didn’t get involved and was a clock watcher. David said, “I was glad when they said unto me, Let us go into the house of the LORD.” Many Christians have lost that gladness and blame the church, but the church is made up of people.
📖 Scripture (NKJV) Psalm 122:1 — I was glad when they said to me, “Let us go into the house of the LORD.”

items.t: Who was really crucified for you?
items.d: Christ was — not Paul, and not any church name, group or minister.
p: Christ was — not Paul, and not any church name, group or minister.

Corinth had four groups — “I am of Paul,” “of Apollos,” “of Cephas,” “of Christ.” Pastor Kincer says only the group focused on Christ is right, because only Christ can save — not a church name, group or minister.
Who was really crucified for you?

🎙 From the sermon “You’ve got four groups here and only one is right. Can you rationally, reasonably, logically tell me which group is right? Yeah, the Christ group.” ▶ 15:48 “He says, was Paul baptized or crucified for you? See, was the Pope crucified for Catholics? Can the Pope save Catholics? No.” ▶ 16:51 “They’re focused on Christ who can do something. Not their church name, not their church group, not some minister.” ▶ 17:29 “It is Christ and the Scriptures.” ▶ 17:41 “I am of Paul; and I of Apollos; and I of Cephas; and I of Christ.” Pastor Kincer says there were four groups in Corinth, and only one was right: the Christ group. Is Christ divided? No; He is one with the Father and the Scriptures. Was Paul crucified for you? No church name, church group or minister can save anyone. It is Christ and the Scriptures.
Who was really crucified for you?

📖 Scripture (NKJV) 1 Corinthians 1:12–13 — Now I say this, that each of you says, “I am of Paul,” or “I am of Apollos,” or “I am of Cephas,” or “I am of Christ.” Is Christ divided? Was Paul crucified for you? Or were you baptized in the name of Paul?

items.t: What if a nation turns back to God?
items.d: God says He will relent from the judgment He planned. Pastor Kincer adds that Bible morality is an umbrella of protection when God judges.
p: God says He will relent from the judgment He planned. Pastor Kincer adds that Bible morality is an umbrella of protection when God judges.
Jeremiah shows both sides: a nation that won’t obey is plucked up, but one that turns from its evil is spared. That is why, Pastor Kincer says, we need to get the Word out.
What if a nation turns back to God?

🎙 From the sermon “If they will not obey, I will utterly pluck them up and destroy that nation.” ▶ 21:54 “But, Jeremiah 18:8, if that nation I have pronounced destruction, turn from their evil ways, I will repent of the evil that I thought to do unto them.” ▶ 22:19 “You see, if we get them to embrace Bible morality, it is also an umbrella of protection when God judges.” ▶ 22:54 Jeremiah 18:8 says, “If that nation, against whom I have pronounced, turn from their evil, I will repent of the evil that I thought to do unto them.” Pastor Kincer says God warns before He judges. If a nation turns from its evil ways and back to Bible morality, God can relent from the judgment He planned.
What if a nation turns back to God?

📖 Scripture (NKJV) Jeremiah 18:8 — if that nation against whom I have spoken turns from its evil, I will relent of the disaster that I thought to bring upon it. Jeremiah 12:17 — But if they do not obey, I will utterly pluck up and destroy that nation,” says the LORD.

items.t: Can a divided home still stand?
items.d: No. Jesus said a house divided against itself will not stand.
p: No. Jesus said a house divided against itself will not stand.

Pastor Kincer says husband and wife need to stand together in the same truth and moral standards, showing their children Jesus by their lives. When they go different ways, conflict follows and the kids can’t wait to get out.
Can a divided home still stand?

🎙 From the sermon “Jesus said these words. If they’re divided against themselves, they will not stand.” ▶ 12:16 “In the home, is it imperative that the husband and wife stand together with the same truth, the same moral standards? Is it important? And being an example to their children, not just telling their children about Jesus, but showing them in their life. Yes, it is. Why? Or the home isn’t going to stand.” ▶ 12:44 “Because the husband and wife go two different ways.” ▶ 13:13 Jesus said every kingdom, city and house divided against itself shall not stand (Matthew 12:25). Pastor Kincer says “stand” is a military word: an army that isn’t united loses the war. In the home, husband and wife must stand together with the same truth and moral standards, showing their children Jesus by their lives. When they go two different ways, conflict comes, and the kids can’t wait to get out.
Can a divided home still stand?

📖 Scripture (NKJV) Matthew 12:25 — But Jesus knew their thoughts, and said to them: “Every kingdom divided against itself is brought to desolation, and every city or house divided against itself will not stand.”

items.t: Do we want God’s blessings — or His rule?
items.d: God wants to rule our lives, not just bless them. Too many want heaven and His blessings without doing what He says.
p: God wants to rule our lives, not just bless them. Too many want heaven and His blessings without doing what He says.

Pastor Kincer says Israel rejected God and did what was right in their own eyes, and Jesus’ parable shows citizens refusing the king’s rule. People want God’s blessings and approval, he says, but God wants His Scriptures to rule their lives.
Do we want God’s blessings — or His rule?

🎙 From the sermon “God said to Samuel, they have rejected me that I should not rule over them. They haven’t rejected you, Samuel. They rejected me.” ▶ 10:36 “See, the people didn’t want God telling them what to do. Is that America? Yeah, we want to go to heaven. You see, we want his blessings. We want him to prosper us, but we don’t want to do what he tells us to do.” ▶ 10:45 “People want God’s blessings and God’s approval. But God wants to rule in their life. He wants the Scriptures to rule in their life, and they don’t want it.” ▶ 11:23 They rejected God, rejected the Scriptures, and did what they wanted in their own eyes. People want to go to heaven and want His blessings, but do not want to do what He tells them to do. Luke 19:14 says, “We will not have this man to reign over us.” People want God’s blessings and approval, but God wants to rule in their life — and He wants the Scriptures to rule in their life.
Do we want God’s blessings — or His rule?

📖 Scripture (NKJV) 1 Samuel 8:7 — And the LORD said to Samuel, “Heed the voice of the people in all that they say to you; for they have not rejected you, but they have rejected Me, that I should not reign over them.” Luke 19:14 — But his citizens hated him, and sent a delegation after him, saying, ‘We will not have this man to reign over us.’

items.d: No. Pastor Kincer says “be perfect” means spiritual maturity and completeness, not a life with no flaws.
p: No. Pastor Kincer says “be perfect” means spiritual maturity and completeness, not a life with no flaws.
Pastor Kincer says people hear “be perfect” and think it means never sinning. He points to Hebrews 5:14 and James 1:4 to show it is about growing up and being complete, lacking nothing.

🎙 From the sermon ““Be you therefore perfect, even as your Father which is in heaven is perfect.” This is Jesus talking.” ▶ 16:08 “And they thought perfect was just living a life that had no flaws in it. No, it’s coming to what? Spiritual maturity, spiritual completeness.” ▶ 16:24 “Let patience have her perfect work, that you may be what? Perfect and entire, lacking what? Nothing.” ▶ 16:50

📖 Scripture (NKJV) Matthew 5:48 — Therefore you shall be perfect, just as your Father in heaven is perfect. James 1:4 — But let patience have its perfect work, that you may be perfect and complete, lacking nothing. Hebrews 5:14 — But solid food belongs to those who are of full age, that is, those who by reason of use have their senses exercised to discern both good and evil.

items.t: What if my gifts are just noise?
items.d: Without love, even speaking in the languages of men and angels is just noise — a clanging cymbal.
p: Without love, even speaking in the languages of men and angels is just noise — a clanging cymbal.
Pastor Kincer explains Paul’s picture: a cymbal clanging by itself would drive you nuts in about 30 seconds. He says love is more important than both kinds of languages — men’s and angels’.
What if my gifts are just noise?

🎙 From the sermon “Though or if I speak with tongues of men and angels, but have not love, I am become a sounding brass or a clanging cymbal.” ▶ 0:23 “And if I had someone over there just clang the cymbals together, you know, in about 30 seconds, you would go, “You’re driving me nuts. What’s the point?”” ▶ 0:37 “There’s languages of men, like they spoke on the day of Pentecost. And there are languages of angels. But the key is love is more important than both of those.” ▶ 1:01
What if my gifts are just noise?

📖 Scripture (NKJV) 1 Corinthians 13:1 — Though I speak with the tongues of men and of angels, but have not love, I have become sounding brass or a clanging cymbal. 1 Corinthians 12:31 — But earnestly desire the best gifts. And yet I show you a more excellent way.

items.t: Does real love insist on its own way?
items.d: No. Real love doesn’t demand its own way. It wants the right way — the truth.
tg: love does not demand its own way
p: No. Real love doesn’t demand its own way. It wants the right way — the truth.
Pastor Kincer walks through Paul’s description of love: patient, kind, not proud or rude. Love doesn’t demand its own way in the family, the church or the community, and it keeps no record of wrongs.
Does real love insist on its own way?

🎙 From the sermon “Love does not seek its own way. Well, it’s going to be my way. I’m going to hit the highway. You know, love doesn’t demand its own way in the family, in the church, or in the community. It demands the right way, the truth.” ▶ 6:47 “Love is not easily provoked. It, you know, they’re not touchy. You know, if you don’t say the right thing or do the right thing, they’re all ticked off. And love doesn’t do that.” ▶ 7:03
Does real love insist on its own way?

📖 Scripture (NKJV) 1 Corinthians 13:4–5 — Love suffers long and is kind; love does not envy; love does not parade itself, is not puffed up; does not behave rudely, does not seek its own, is not provoked, thinks no evil.

items.t: Can I serve God and still miss knowing Him?
items.d: Yes. You can be used by God — even prophesy and do mighty works in Jesus’ name — and still miss the most important thing: love.
p: Yes. You can be used by God — even prophesy and do mighty works in Jesus’ name — and still miss the most important thing: love.

Pastor Kincer points to Jesus’ warning about people who prophesied and cast out demons in His name, yet hear “I never knew you.” He says they were used by God but missed love, which he describes as obeying God.
Can I serve God and still miss knowing Him?

🎙 From the sermon “See, love is to obey God. And he had the message, but he didn’t have the love.” ▶ 2:18 “See, they had faith to do all these things and these gifts and these spiritual manifestations were working in them. And Jesus said, “I will say to them, I never knew you.” Depart from me, you workers of iniquity.” ▶ 3:02 “You see, you didn’t have love. You might have been used of God to do things, but you missed the important thing, and that is love.” ▶ 3:14
Can I serve God and still miss knowing Him?

📖 Scripture (NKJV) Matthew 7:22–23 — Many will say to Me in that day, ‘Lord, Lord, have we not prophesied in Your name, cast out demons in Your name, and done many wonders in Your name?’ And then I will declare to them, ‘I never knew you; depart from Me, you who practice lawlessness!’ 1 Corinthians 13:2 — And though I have the gift of prophecy, and understand all mysteries and all knowledge, and though I have all faith, so that I could remove mountains, but have not love, I am nothing.

items.t: What is the real goal of God’s Word?
items.d: Love from a pure heart. Paul says that is the goal of the commandment.
p: Love from a pure heart. Paul says that is the goal of the commandment.
Pastor Kincer says “end” in this verse means goal. We tend to think the goal is eternal life or the gifts of the Spirit, he says, but it is love.
What is the real goal of God’s Word?

🎙 From the sermon “Now the end of the commandment is love out of a pure heart. The word end means the goal. You see the goal of the word of God is love out of a pure heart.” ▶ 23:10 “See, we think it’s eternal life. No, you’re going to live eternally no matter what.” ▶ 23:41 “We think that it’s the gifts of the spirit in our circles.” ▶ 24:04 “And it’s not. It’s love. And that’s why we have such phoniness in the spirit-filled world as we try to push something that God isn’t doing.” ▶ 24:14
What is the real goal of God’s Word?
📖 Scripture (NKJV) 1 Timothy 1:5 — Now the purpose of the commandment is love from a pure heart, from a good conscience, and from sincere faith.

items.t: Is God looking for fruit — or fireworks?
items.d: Fruit comes first. Love is the first fruit of the Spirit and the peak of God’s character, and you can’t have the manifestations of the Spirit without it.
p: Fruit comes first. Love is the first fruit of the Spirit and the peak of God’s character, and you can’t have the manifestations of the Spirit without it.

Pastor Kincer notes that love is listed first among the fruit of the Spirit, that God is love, and that love sits at the top of sharing in the divine nature. His point: the fruit and character of God come before the manifestations.
Is God looking for fruit — or fireworks?

🎙 From the sermon “Love, joy, peace. It’s the first fruit. 1 John 4:8 says, “God is love.” See, that is exactly what God is. He just gave us the description of God.” ▶ 8:29 “So the love is at the peak of divine character and it’s at the beginning of the fruits of the spirit. And believe me, Paul is telling us, you can’t have the manifestations of the spirit without the fruit and the divine character of God. That’s what he’s telling us. This is the way to get it.” ▶ 9:01
Is God looking for fruit — or fireworks?

📖 Scripture (NKJV) Galatians 5:22–23 — But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, self-control. Against such there is no law. 1 John 4:8 — He who does not love does not know God, for God is love.
